# Pattern 1: Equi-Width Histogram Pattern
# ============================================================================
class EquiWidthHistogram:
    """
    Equi-Width Histogram: Divides the range of values into bins of equal width
    Use Case: When you need uniform bin sizes regardless of data distribution
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_histogram(df, column_name, num_bins=5):
        """
        Create equi-width histogram by dividing value range into equal-width bins
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column_name: Column to create histogram for
            num_bins: Number of bins to create
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with histogram statistics
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("EQUI-WIDTH HISTOGRAM PATTERN")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Calculate min and max values
        stats = df.agg(
            _min(col(column_name)).alias("min_val"),
            _max(col(column_name)).alias("max_val")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        min_val = stats["min_val"]
        max_val = stats["max_val"]
        bin_width = (max_val - min_val) / num_bins
        
        print(f"Value Range: [{min_val}, {max_val}]")
        print(f"Bin Width: {bin_width:.2f}")
        print(f"Number of Bins: {num_bins}")
        
        # Create bins using floor division
        histogram_df = df.withColumn(
            "bin_id",
            when(col(column_name) == max_val, num_bins - 1)
            .otherwise(floor((col(column_name) - lit(min_val)) / lit(bin_width)))
        ).withColumn(
            "bin_start",
            lit(min_val) + col("bin_id") * lit(bin_width)
        ).withColumn(
            "bin_end",
            lit(min_val) + (col("bin_id") + 1) * lit(bin_width)
        )
        
        # Aggregate histogram statistics
        result = histogram_df.groupBy("bin_id", "bin_start", "bin_end") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("frequency"),
                avg(col(column_name)).alias("avg_value"),
                _min(col(column_name)).alias("min_value"),
                _max(col(column_name)).alias("max_value")
            ) \
            .orderBy("bin_id")
        
        result.show(truncate=False)
        return result


# ============================================================================
# Pattern 2: Equi-Depth Histogram Pattern
# ============================================================================
class EquiDepthHistogram:
    """
    Equi-Depth Histogram: Divides data into bins with approximately equal counts
    Use Case: When you need balanced bins regardless of value distribution
    Also known as Quantile-based histogram
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_histogram(df, column_name, num_bins=5):
        """
        Create equi-depth histogram with approximately equal number of records per bin
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column_name: Column to create histogram for
            num_bins: Number of bins to create
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with histogram statistics
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("EQUI-DEPTH HISTOGRAM PATTERN")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        total_count = df.count()
        target_bin_size = total_count / num_bins
        
        print(f"Total Records: {total_count}")
        print(f"Target Records per Bin: {target_bin_size:.2f}")
        print(f"Number of Bins: {num_bins}")
        
        # Use ntile to create equal-depth bins
        histogram_df = df.withColumn(
            "bin_id",
            ntile(num_bins).over(Window.orderBy(col(column_name))) - 1
        )
        
        # Calculate bin boundaries and statistics
        result = histogram_df.groupBy("bin_id") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("frequency"),
                _min(col(column_name)).alias("bin_start"),
                _max(col(column_name)).alias("bin_end"),
                avg(col(column_name)).alias("avg_value")
            ) \
            .orderBy("bin_id")
        
        result.show(truncate=False)
        return result


# ============================================================================
# Pattern 3: Frequency Histogram Pattern
# ============================================================================
class FrequencyHistogram:
    """
    Frequency Histogram: Groups by exact values and counts occurrences
    Use Case: For categorical or discrete data, or to find most common values
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_histogram(df, column_name, top_n=None, include_percentage=True):
        """
        Create frequency histogram showing count of each distinct value
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column_name: Column to create histogram for
            top_n: If specified, show only top N most frequent values
            include_percentage: Whether to include percentage column
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with frequency statistics
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("FREQUENCY HISTOGRAM PATTERN")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        total_count = df.count()
        
        # Group by value and count frequencies
        result = df.groupBy(col(column_name)) \
            .agg(count("*").alias("frequency")) \
            .orderBy(col("frequency").desc())
        
        if include_percentage:
            result = result.withColumn(
                "percentage",
                (col("frequency") / lit(total_count) * 100)
            )
            
        # Calculate cumulative percentage
        window_spec = Window.orderBy(col("frequency").desc()) \
            .rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow)
        
        result = result.withColumn(
            "cumulative_percentage",
            _sum("percentage").over(window_spec)
        )
        
        if top_n:
            print(f"Showing Top {top_n} Most Frequent Values")
            result = result.limit(top_n)
        
        print(f"Total Distinct Values: {result.count()}")
        result.show(truncate=False)
        return result

# Pattern 4: Adaptive Histogram Pattern
# ============================================================================
class AdaptiveHistogram:
    """
    Adaptive Histogram: Adjusts bin widths based on data density
    Use Case: When data has varying densities and you want more bins in dense areas
    Uses variance-based splitting
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_histogram(df, column_name, max_bins=10, variance_threshold=None):
        """
        Create adaptive histogram with variable bin widths based on data distribution
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column_name: Column to create histogram for
            max_bins: Maximum number of bins
            variance_threshold: Variance threshold for bin splitting
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with adaptive histogram statistics
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("ADAPTIVE HISTOGRAM PATTERN")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Start with equi-depth bins
        initial_bins = 5
        df_with_bins = df.withColumn(
            "temp_bin",
            ntile(initial_bins).over(Window.orderBy(col(column_name)))
        )
        
        # Calculate variance for each bin
        bin_stats = df_with_bins.groupBy("temp_bin") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("count"),
                avg(col(column_name)).alias("mean"),
                _min(col(column_name)).alias("min_val"),
                _max(col(column_name)).alias("max_val"),
                # Approximate variance calculation
                avg((col(column_name) - avg(col(column_name))) ** 2).alias("variance")
            ).collect()
        
        # Set variance threshold if not provided
        if variance_threshold is None:
            variances = [row["variance"] for row in bin_stats if row["variance"]]
            variance_threshold = sum(variances) / len(variances) if variances else 0
        
        print(f"Variance Threshold: {variance_threshold:.2f}")
        
        # Create adaptive bins by splitting high-variance bins
        bin_boundaries = []
        current_bin_id = 0
        
        for stat in sorted(bin_stats, key=lambda x: x["temp_bin"]):
            if stat["variance"] > variance_threshold and current_bin_id < max_bins - 1:
                # Split this bin into 2
                mid_point = (stat["min_val"] + stat["max_val"]) / 2
                bin_boundaries.append({
                    "bin_id": current_bin_id,
                    "start": stat["min_val"],
                    "end": mid_point
                })
                current_bin_id += 1
                bin_boundaries.append({
                    "bin_id": current_bin_id,
                    "start": mid_point,
                    "end": stat["max_val"]
                })
                current_bin_id += 1
            else:
                bin_boundaries.append({
                    "bin_id": current_bin_id,
                    "start": stat["min_val"],
                    "end": stat["max_val"]
                })
                current_bin_id += 1
        
        # Create DataFrame with boundaries
        boundaries_df = spark.createDataFrame(bin_boundaries)
        
        # Assign records to adaptive bins
        result_df = df.crossJoin(boundaries_df) \
            .filter(
                (col(column_name) >= col("start")) & 
                (col(column_name) <= col("end"))
            ) \
            .groupBy("bin_id", "start", "end") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("frequency"),
                avg(col(column_name)).alias("avg_value"),
                _min(col(column_name)).alias("min_value"),
                _max(col(column_name)).alias("max_value")
            ) \
            .orderBy("bin_id")
        
        print(f"Number of Adaptive Bins Created: {result_df.count()}")
        result_df.show(truncate=False)
        return result_df

class CompressedHistogram:
    """
    Compressed Histogram: Stores histogram with minimal space using compression
    Use Case: When memory/storage is limited or for efficient histogram transmission
    Combines similar bins and uses run-length encoding
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_histogram(df, column_name, num_bins=10, compression_ratio=0.5):
        """
        Create compressed histogram by merging similar adjacent bins
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column_name: Column to create histogram for
            num_bins: Initial number of bins
            compression_ratio: Target compression (0.5 = 50% of original bins)
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with compressed histogram
        """

        print("COMPRESSED HISTOGRAM PATTERN")
        print(f"{'='*60}")

            _min(col(column_name)).alias("min_val"),
            _max(col(column_name)).alias("max_val")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        min_val = stats["min_val"]
        max_val = stats["max_val"]
        bin_width = (max_val - min_val) / num_bins
        
        # Create initial bins
        initial_histogram = df.withColumn(
            "bin_id",
            when(col(column_name) == max_val, num_bins - 1)
            .otherwise(floor((col(column_name) - lit(min_val)) / lit(bin_width)))
        ).groupBy("bin_id") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("frequency"),
                _min(col(column_name)).alias("bin_start"),
                _max(col(column_name)).alias("bin_end")
            ) \
            .orderBy("bin_id")
        
        # Collect for compression
        bins = initial_histogram.collect()
        target_bins = max(1, int(num_bins * compression_ratio))
        
        print(f"Initial Bins: {len(bins)}")
        print(f"Target Bins: {target_bins}")
        print(f"Compression Ratio: {compression_ratio * 100}%")
        
        # Merge adjacent bins with similar frequencies
        compressed_bins = []
        current_bin = None
        
        for bin_row in bins:
            if current_bin is None:
                current_bin = {
                    "bin_id": len(compressed_bins),
                    "bin_start": bin_row["bin_start"],
                    "bin_end": bin_row["bin_end"],
                    "frequency": bin_row["frequency"],
                    "original_bins": 1
                }
            else:
                # Check if we should merge (similar frequency or need more compression)
                freq_diff_ratio = abs(current_bin["frequency"] - bin_row["frequency"]) / \
                                 max(current_bin["frequency"], bin_row["frequency"])
                
                should_merge = (len(compressed_bins) >= target
```python
                should_merge = (len(compressed_bins) >= target_bins) or (freq_diff_ratio < 0.3)
                
                if should_merge and len(compressed_bins) < target_bins:
                    # Merge with current bin
                    current_bin["bin_end"] = bin_row["bin_end"]
                    current_bin["frequency"] += bin_row["frequency"]
                    current_bin["original_bins"] += 1
                else:
                    # Save current bin and start new one
                    compressed_bins.append(current_bin)
                    current_bin = {
                        "bin_id": len(compressed_bins),
                        "bin_start": bin_row["bin_start"],

        result = spark.createDataFrame(compressed_bins)

        compression_achieved = (1 - len(compressed_bins) / num_bins) * 100
        
        print(f"Final Bins: {len(compressed_bins)}")
        print(f"Compression Achieved: {compression_achieved:.2f}%")
        
        result.show(truncate=False)

class HistogramAnalyzer:
    """
    Utility class for comparing and analyzing different histogram patterns
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def compare_histograms(df, column_name, num_bins=5):
        """
        Compare all histogram patterns side by side
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column_name: Column to analyze
            num_bins: Number of bins for applicable patterns
        """
        print(f"\n{'#'*60}")
        print("HISTOGRAM PATTERN COMPARISON")
        print(f"Column: {column_name}")
        print(f"{'#'*60}")
        
        # Generate all histograms
        equi_width = EquiWidthHistogram.create_histogram(df, column_name, num_bins)
        equi_depth = EquiDepthHistogram.create_histogram(df, column_name, num_bins)
        frequency = FrequencyHistogram.create_histogram(df, column_name, top_n=10)
        adaptive = AdaptiveHistogram.create_histogram(df, column_name, max_bins=num_bins)
        compressed = CompressedHistogram.create_histogram(df, column_name, num_bins, 0.6)
        
        return {
            "equi_width": equi_width,
            "equi_depth": equi_depth,
            "frequency": frequency,
            "adaptive": adaptive,
            "compressed": compressed
        }
    
    @staticmethod
    def calculate_histogram_quality_metrics(histogram_df, original_df, column_name):
        """
        Calculate quality metrics for a histogram
        
        Args:
            histogram_df: Histogram DataFrame
            original_df: Original data DataFrame
            column_name: Column name being analyzed
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary of quality metrics
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("HISTOGRAM QUALITY METRICS")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Calculate metrics
        total_bins = histogram_df.count()
        total_records = original_df.count()
        
        # Frequency variance (measure of balance)
        freq_stats = histogram_df.agg(
            avg("frequency").alias("avg_freq"),
            _min("frequency").alias("min_freq"),
            _max("frequency").alias("max_freq")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        balance_score = 1 - (freq_stats["max_freq"] - freq_stats["min_freq"]) / freq_stats["avg_freq"]
        
        metrics = {
            "total_bins": total_bins,
            "total_records": total_records,
            "avg_records_per_bin": freq_stats["avg_freq"],
            "min_records_per_bin": freq_stats["min_freq"],
            "max_records_per_bin": freq_stats["max_freq"],
            "balance_score": balance_score
        }
        
        print("Metrics:")
        for key, value in metrics.items():
            print(f"  {key}: {value}")
        
        return metrics

# Advanced Histogram Patterns

class MultiDimensionalHistogram:
    """
    Multi-Dimensional Histogram: Create histograms across multiple columns
    Use Case: Understanding joint distributions of multiple variables
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_2d_histogram(df, column1, column2, bins1=5, bins2=5):
        """
        Create 2D histogram for two columns
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column1: First column name
            column2: Second column name
            bins1: Number of bins for first column
            bins2: Number of bins for second column
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with 2D histogram
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("MULTI-DIMENSIONAL HISTOGRAM PATTERN (2D)")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Calculate ranges for both columns
        stats = df.agg(
            _min(col(column1)).alias("min1"),
            _max(col(column1)).alias("max1"),
            _min(col(column2)).alias("min2"),
            _max(col(column2)).alias("max2")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        min1, max1 = stats["min1"], stats["max1"]
        min2, max2 = stats["min2"], stats["max2"]
        
        bin_width1 = (max1 - min1) / bins1
        bin_width2 = (max2 - min2) / bins2
        
        # Create bins for both dimensions
        result = df.withColumn(
            "bin1",
            when(col(column1) == max1, bins1 - 1)
            .otherwise(floor((col(column1) - lit(min1)) / lit(bin_width1)))
        ).withColumn(
            "bin2",
            when(col(column2) == max2, bins2 - 1)
            .otherwise(floor((col(column2) - lit(min2)) / lit(bin_width2)))
        ).withColumn(
            "bin1_start",
            lit(min1) + col("bin1") * lit(bin_width1)
        ).withColumn(
            "bin1_end",
            lit(min1) + (col("bin1") + 1) * lit(bin_width1)
        ).withColumn(
            "bin2_start",
            lit(min2) + col("bin2") * lit(bin_width2)
        ).withColumn(
            "bin2_end",
            lit(min2) + (col("bin2") + 1) * lit(bin_width2)
        )
        
        # Aggregate 2D histogram
        histogram_2d = result.groupBy(
            "bin1", "bin1_start", "bin1_end",
            "bin2", "bin2_start", "bin2_end"
        ).agg(
            count("*").alias("frequency")
        ).orderBy("bin1", "bin2")
        
        print(f"Column 1: {column1} ({bins1} bins)")
        print(f"Column 2: {column2} ({bins2} bins)")
        print(f"Total 2D Bins: {histogram_2d.count()}")
        
        histogram_2d.show(20, truncate=False)
        return histogram_2d


class StreamingHistogram:
    """
    Streaming Histogram: Incrementally update histogram as new data arrives
    Use Case: Real-time data processing and monitoring
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_streaming_histogram(df, column_name, window_column, num_bins=5):
        """
        Create histogram that can be updated incrementally
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame with timestamp/sequence column
            column_name: Column to create histogram for
            window_column: Column to use for windowing (e.g., timestamp)
            num_bins: Number of bins
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with windowed histogram
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("STREAMING HISTOGRAM PATTERN")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Add row number for windowing
        window_spec = Window.orderBy(col(window_column))
        df_with_window = df.withColumn("row_num", row_number().over(window_spec))
        
        # Calculate global statistics for consistent binning
        stats = df.agg(
            _min(col(column_name)).alias("min_val"),
            _max(col(column_name)).alias("max_val")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        min_val = stats["min_val"]
        max_val = stats["max_val"]
        bin_width = (max_val - min_val) / num_bins
        
        # Create bins
        df_with_bins = df_with_window.withColumn(
            "bin_id",
            when(col(column_name) == max_val, num_bins - 1)
            .otherwise(floor((col(column_name) - lit(min_val)) / lit(bin_width)))
        )
        
        # Create cumulative histogram (simulating streaming)
        result = df_with_bins.groupBy("bin_id") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("cumulative_frequency"),
                avg("row_num").alias("avg_arrival_order")
            ) \
            .orderBy("bin_id")
        
        print(f"Bins created with width: {bin_width:.2f}")
        result.show(truncate=False)
        return result

## Performance Optimization Tips

```python
# ============================================================================
# Performance Optimization Techniques
# ============================================================================

class OptimizedHistogram:
    """
    Performance-optimized histogram implementations
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_histogram_with_sampling(df, column_name, num_bins=10, sample_fraction=0.1):
        """
        Create histogram using data sampling for very large datasets
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column_name: Column to analyze
            num_bins: Number of bins
            sample_fraction: Fraction of data to sample (0.0 to 1.0)
            
        Returns:
            Histogram DataFrame
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("OPTIMIZED HISTOGRAM WITH SAMPLING")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Sample data for faster processing
        sampled_df = df.sample(withReplacement=False, fraction=sample_fraction, seed=42)
        
        original_count = df.count()
        sampled_count = sampled_df.count()
        
        print(f"Original records: {original_count}")
        print(f"Sampled records: {sampled_count}")
        print(f"Sample fraction: {sample_fraction * 100}%")
        
        # Create histogram on sampled data
        stats = sampled_df.agg(
            _min(col(column_name)).alias("min_val"),
            _max(col(column_name)).alias("max_val")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        min_val = stats["min_val"]
        max_val = stats["max_val"]
        bin_width = (max_val - min_val) / num_bins
        
        # Create bins
        histogram_df = sampled_df.withColumn(
            "bin_id",
            when(col(column_name) == max_val, num_bins - 1)
            .otherwise(floor((col(column_name) - lit(min_val)) / lit(bin_width)))
        )
        
        # Scale up frequencies to represent full dataset
        scale_factor = 1.0 / sample_fraction
        
        result = histogram_df.groupBy("bin_id") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("sampled_frequency")
            ) \
            .withColumn(
                "estimated_frequency",
                (col("sampled_frequency") * lit(scale_factor)).cast(IntegerType())
            ) \
            .withColumn(
                "bin_start",
                lit(min_val) + col("bin_id") * lit(bin_width)
            ) \
            .withColumn(
                "bin_end",
                lit(min_val) + (col("bin_id") + 1) * lit(bin_width)
            ) \
            .orderBy("bin_id")
        
        result.show(truncate=False)
        return result
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_histogram_with_caching(df, column_name, num_bins=10):
        """
        Create histogram with intelligent caching for repeated operations
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column_name: Column to analyze
            num_bins: Number of bins
            
        Returns:
            Histogram DataFrame
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("OPTIMIZED HISTOGRAM WITH CACHING")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Cache the DataFrame if not already cached
        if not df.is_cached:
            df.cache()
            df.count()  # Force caching
            print("DataFrame cached for optimal performance")
        
        # Use equi-width approach with cached data
        result = EquiWidthHistogram.create_histogram(df, column_name, num_bins)
        
        return result
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_parallel_histogram(df, column_name, num_bins=10, num_partitions=None):
        """
        Create histogram with explicit partitioning for parallel processing
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column_name: Column to analyze
            num_bins: Number of bins
            num_partitions: Number of partitions for parallel processing
            
        Returns:
            Histogram DataFrame
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("OPTIMIZED HISTOGRAM WITH PARALLEL PROCESSING")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Repartition for better parallelism if specified
        if num_partitions:
            df = df.repartition(num_partitions)
            print(f"Repartitioned to {num_partitions} partitions")
        
        current_partitions = df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
        print(f"Current partitions: {current_partitions}")
        
        # Create histogram
        result = EquiWidthHistogram.create_histogram(df, column_name, num_bins)
        
        return result


# ============================================================================
# Incremental Histogram Update Pattern
# ============================================================================
class IncrementalHistogram:
    """
    Incrementally update histogram as new data arrives
    Useful for maintaining histograms in streaming scenarios
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def initialize_histogram(df, column_name, num_bins=10):
        """
        Initialize histogram structure
        
        Args:
            df: Initial DataFrame
            column_name: Column to analyze
            num_bins: Number of bins
            
        Returns:
            Initial histogram and metadata
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("INCREMENTAL HISTOGRAM - INITIALIZATION")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Calculate initial statistics
        stats = df.agg(
            _min(col(column_name)).alias("min_val"),
            _max(col(column_name)).alias("max_val"),
            count("*").alias("total_count")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        min_val = stats["min_val"]
        max_val = stats["max_val"]
        bin_width = (max_val - min_val) / num_bins
        
        # Create initial histogram
        histogram = df.withColumn(
            "bin_id",
            when(col(column_name) == max_val, num_bins - 1)
            .otherwise(floor((col(column_name) - lit(min_val)) / lit(bin_width)))
        ).groupBy("bin_id") \
            .agg(count("*").alias("frequency")) \
            .withColumn("bin_start", lit(min_val) + col("bin_id") * lit(bin_width)) \
            .withColumn("bin_end", lit(min_val) + (col("bin_id") + 1) * lit(bin_width)) \
            .orderBy("bin_id")
        
        metadata = {
            "min_val": min_val,
            "max_val": max_val,
            "bin_width": bin_width,
            "num_bins": num_bins,
            "total_count": stats["total_count"]
        }
        
        print(f"Initialized histogram with {num_bins} bins")
        print(f"Range: [{min_val}, {max_val}]")
        print(f"Bin width: {bin_width}")
        
        histogram.show(truncate=False)
        return histogram, metadata
    
    @staticmethod
    def update_histogram(current_histogram, metadata, new_data_df, column_name):
        """
        Update existing histogram with new data
        
        Args:
            current_histogram: Existing histogram DataFrame
            metadata: Histogram metadata
            new_data_df: New data to incorporate
            column_name: Column name
            
        Returns:
            Updated histogram and metadata
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("INCREMENTAL HISTOGRAM - UPDATE")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        min_val = metadata["min_val"]
        max_val = metadata["max_val"]
        bin_width = metadata["bin_width"]
        num_bins = metadata["num_bins"]
        
        # Process new data into bins
        new_histogram = new_data_df.withColumn(
            "bin_id",
            when(col(column_name) == max_val, num_bins - 1)
            .otherwise(floor((col(column_name) - lit(min_val)) / lit(bin_width)))
        ).groupBy("bin_id") \
            .agg(count("*").alias("new_frequency"))
        
        # Merge with existing histogram
        updated_histogram = current_histogram.join(
            new_histogram,
            "bin_id",
            "left"
        ).withColumn(
            "frequency",
            col("frequency") + when(col("new_frequency").isNotNull(), col("new_frequency")).otherwise(0)
        ).select("bin_id", "bin_start", "bin_end", "frequency") \
         .orderBy("bin_id")
        
        # Update metadata
        new_count = new_data_df.count()
        metadata["total_count"] += new_count
        
        print(f"Added {new_count} new records")
        print(f"Total records: {metadata['total_count']}")
        
        updated_histogram.show(truncate=False)
        return updated_histogram, metadata


# ============================================================================
# Histogram Comparison and Similarity Metrics
# ============================================================================
class HistogramComparison:
    """
    Compare two histograms and calculate similarity metrics
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def calculate_chi_square_distance(hist1, hist2):
        """
        Calculate Chi-Square distance between two histograms
        
        Args:
            hist1: First histogram DataFrame
            hist2: Second histogram DataFrame
            
        Returns:
            Chi-square distance value
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("HISTOGRAM CHI-SQUARE DISTANCE")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Join histograms
        joined = hist1.select(
            col("bin_id"),
            col("frequency").alias("freq1")
        ).join(
            hist2.select(
                col("bin_id"),
                col("frequency").alias("freq2")
            ),
            "bin_id",
            "outer"
        ).fillna(0)
        
        # Calculate chi-square distance
        chi_square_df = joined.withColumn(
            "chi_square_component",
            when((col("freq1") + col("freq2")) > 0,
                 ((col("freq1") - col("freq2")) ** 2) / (col("freq1") + col("freq2"))
            ).otherwise(0)
        )
        
        chi_square_distance = chi_square_df.agg(
            _sum("chi_square_component").alias("chi_square_distance")
        ).collect()[0]["chi_square_distance"]
        
        print(f"Chi-Square Distance: {chi_square_distance:.4f}")
        return chi_square_distance
    
    @staticmethod
    def calculate_histogram_intersection(hist1, hist2):
        """
        Calculate histogram intersection (similarity measure)
        
        Args:
            hist1: First histogram DataFrame
            hist2: Second histogram DataFrame
            
        Returns:
            Intersection value (0 to 1, higher is more similar)
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("HISTOGRAM INTERSECTION")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Normalize histograms
        total1 = hist1.agg(_sum("frequency")).collect()[0][0]
        total2 = hist2.agg(_sum("frequency")).collect()[0][0]
        
        norm_hist1 = hist1.withColumn("norm_freq", col("frequency") / lit(total1))
        norm_hist2 = hist2.withColumn("norm_freq", col("frequency") / lit(total2))
        
        # Calculate intersection
        joined = norm_hist1.select(
            col("bin_id"),
            col("norm_freq").alias("freq1")
        ).join(
            norm_hist2.select(
                col("bin_id"),
                col("norm_freq").alias("freq2")
            ),
            "bin_id",
            "outer"
        ).fillna(0)
        
        intersection_df = joined.withColumn(
            "min_freq",
            when(col("freq1") < col("freq2"), col("freq1")).otherwise(col("freq2"))
        )
        
        intersection = intersection_df.agg(
            _sum("min_freq").alias("intersection")
        ).collect()[0]["intersection"]
        
        print(f"Histogram Intersection: {intersection:.4f}")
        print(f"Similarity: {intersection * 100:.2f}%")
        return intersection

# ============================================================================
# Weighted Histogram Pattern
# ============================================================================
class WeightedHistogram:
    """
    Weighted Histogram: Create histogram where each record has a weight
    Use Case: When records have different importance/weights
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_weighted_histogram(df, column_name, weight_column, num_bins=10):
        """
        Create histogram with weighted frequencies
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column_name: Column to create histogram for
            weight_column: Column containing weights
            num_bins: Number of bins
            
        Returns:
            Weighted histogram DataFrame
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("WEIGHTED HISTOGRAM PATTERN")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Calculate statistics
        stats = df.agg(
            _min(col(column_name)).alias("min_val"),
            _max(col(column_name)).alias("max_val"),
            _sum(col(weight_column)).alias("total_weight")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        min_val = stats["min_val"]
        max_val = stats["max_val"]
        total_weight = stats["total_weight"]
        bin_width = (max_val - min_val) / num_bins
        
        print(f"Total weight: {total_weight}")
        print(f"Bin width: {bin_width:.2f}")
        
        # Create bins and aggregate weighted frequencies
        result = df.withColumn(
            "bin_id",
            when(col(column_name) == max_val, num_bins - 1)
            .otherwise(floor((col(column_name) - lit(min_val)) / lit(bin_width)))
        ).withColumn(
            "bin_start",
            lit(min_val) + col("bin_id") * lit(bin_width)
        ).withColumn(
            "bin_end",
            lit(min_val) + (col("bin_id") + 1) * lit(bin_width)
        ).groupBy("bin_id", "bin_start", "bin_end") \
         .agg(
             count("*").alias("record_count"),
             _sum(col(weight_column)).alias("weighted_frequency"),
             avg(col(weight_column)).alias("avg_weight")
         ) \
         .withColumn(
             "weight_percentage",
             (col("weighted_frequency") / lit(total_weight) * 100)
         ) \
         .orderBy("bin_id")
        
        result.show(truncate=False)
        return result


# ============================================================================
# Cumulative Histogram Pattern
# ============================================================================
class CumulativeHistogram:
    """
    Cumulative Histogram: Shows cumulative distribution
    Use Case: Understanding percentiles and cumulative distributions
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_cumulative_histogram(df, column_name, num_bins=10):
        """
        Create cumulative histogram (CDF approximation)
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column_name: Column to analyze
            num_bins: Number of bins
            
        Returns:
            Cumulative histogram DataFrame
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("CUMULATIVE HISTOGRAM PATTERN")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # First create regular histogram
        stats = df.agg(
            _min(col(column_name)).alias("min_val"),
            _max(col(column_name)).alias("max_val"),
            count("*").alias("total_count")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        min_val = stats["min_val"]
        max_val = stats["max_val"]
        total_count = stats["total_count"]
        bin_width = (max_val - min_val) / num_bins
        
        # Create bins
        histogram = df.withColumn(
            "bin_id",
            when(col(column_name) == max_val, num_bins - 1)
            .otherwise(floor((col(column_name) - lit(min_val)) / lit(bin_width)))
        ).withColumn(
            "bin_start",
            lit(min_val) + col("bin_id") * lit(bin_width)
        ).withColumn(
            "bin_end",
            lit(min_val) + (col("bin_id") + 1) * lit(bin_width)
        ).groupBy("bin_id", "bin_start", "bin_end") \
         .agg(count("*").alias("frequency")) \
         .orderBy("bin_id")
        
        # Calculate cumulative frequencies
        window_spec = Window.orderBy("bin_id") \
            .rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow)
        
        cumulative_result = histogram.withColumn(
            "cumulative_frequency",
            _sum("frequency").over(window_spec)
        ).withColumn(
            "cumulative_percentage",
            (col("cumulative_frequency") / lit(total_count) * 100)
        ).withColumn(
            "frequency_percentage",
            (col("frequency") / lit(total_count) * 100)
        )
        
        print(f"Total records: {total_count}")
        cumulative_result.show(truncate=False)
        return cumulative_result


# ============================================================================
# Logarithmic Histogram Pattern
# ============================================================================
class LogarithmicHistogram:
    """
    Logarithmic Histogram: Uses logarithmic binning for wide-range data
    Use Case: Data spanning multiple orders of magnitude (e.g., file sizes, latencies)
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_log_histogram(df, column_name, base=10, num_bins=10):
        """
        Create histogram with logarithmic bin widths
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column_name: Column to analyze
            base: Logarithm base (default: 10)
            num_bins: Number of bins
            
        Returns:
            Logarithmic histogram DataFrame
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("LOGARITHMIC HISTOGRAM PATTERN")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        from pyspark.sql.functions import log
        
        # Filter out non-positive values
        df_positive = df.filter(col(column_name) > 0)
        
        # Calculate log statistics
        stats = df_positive.agg(
            _min(log(base, col(column_name))).alias("min_log"),
            _max(log(base, col(column_name))).alias("max_log"),
            count("*").alias("total_count")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        min_log = stats["min_log"]
        max_log = stats["max_log"]
        total_count = stats["total_count"]
        log_bin_width = (max_log - min_log) / num_bins
        
        print(f"Log range: [{min_log:.2f}, {max_log:.2f}]")
        print(f"Log bin width: {log_bin_width:.2f}")
        
        # Create logarithmic bins
        result = df_positive.withColumn(
            "log_value",
            log(base, col(column_name))
        ).withColumn(
            "bin_id",
            when(col("log_value") == max_log, num_bins - 1)
            .otherwise(floor((col("log_value") - lit(min_log)) / lit(log_bin_width)))
        ).withColumn(
            "bin_start_log",
            lit(min_log) + col("bin_id") * lit(log_bin_width)
        ).withColumn(
            "bin_end_log",
            lit(min_log) + (col("bin_id") + 1) * lit(log_bin_width)
        ).withColumn(
            "bin_start",
            lit(base) ** col("bin_start_log")
        ).withColumn(
            "bin_end",
            lit(base) ** col("bin_end_log")
        ).groupBy("bin_id", "bin_start", "bin_end", "bin_start_log", "bin_end_log") \
         .agg(
             count("*").alias("frequency"),
             avg(col(column_name)).alias("avg_value")
         ) \
         .orderBy("bin_id")
        
        result.show(truncate=False)
        return result

# Hierarchical Histogram Pattern
# ============================================================================
class HierarchicalHistogram:
    """
    Hierarchical Histogram: Multi-level histogram with drill-down capability
    Use Case: Interactive data exploration with different granularities
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_hierarchical_histogram(df, column_name, levels=[5, 10, 20]):
        """
        Create multi-level histogram hierarchy
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column_name: Column to analyze
            levels: List of bin counts for each level
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary of histograms at different levels
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("HIERARCHICAL HISTOGRAM PATTERN")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        hierarchical_histograms = {}
        
        for level_idx, num_bins in enumerate(levels):
            print(f"\nLevel {level_idx + 1}: {num_bins} bins")
            print("-" * 40)
            
            histogram = EquiWidthHistogram.create_histogram(df, column_name, num_bins)
            hierarchical_histograms[f"level_{level_idx + 1}"] = histogram
        
        return hierarchical_histograms


# ============================================================================
# Conditional Histogram Pattern
# ============================================================================
class ConditionalHistogram:
    """
    Conditional Histogram: Create separate histograms for different conditions
    Use Case: Comparing distributions across categories or segments
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_conditional_histogram(df, column_name, condition_column, num_bins=10):
        """
        Create separate histograms for each condition value
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column_name: Column to create histogram for
            condition_column: Column to group by
            num_bins: Number of bins per histogram
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary of histograms per condition
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("CONDITIONAL HISTOGRAM PATTERN")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Get distinct condition values
        conditions = df.select(condition_column).distinct().collect()
        
        conditional_histograms = {}
        
        # Calculate global min/max for consistent binning
        stats = df.agg(
            _min(col(column_name)).alias("min_val"),
            _max(col(column_name)).alias("max_val")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        min_val = stats["min_val"]
        max_val = stats["max_val"]
        bin_width = (max_val - min_val) / num_bins
        
        print(f"Global range: [{min_val}, {max_val}]")
        print(f"Bin width: {bin_width:.2f}")
        
        for condition_row in conditions:
            condition_value = condition_row[0]
            print(f"\nCondition: {condition_column} = {condition_value}")
            print("-" * 40)
            
            # Filter data for this condition
            filtered_df = df.filter(col(condition_column) == condition_value)
            
            # Create histogram with consistent binning
            histogram = filtered_df.withColumn(
                "bin_id",
                when(col(column_name) == max_val, num_bins - 1)
                .otherwise(floor((col(column_name) - lit(min_val)) / lit(bin_width)))
            ).withColumn(
                "bin_start",
                lit(min_val) + col("bin_id") * lit(bin_width)
            ).withColumn(
                "bin_end",
                lit(min_val) + (col("bin_id") + 1) * lit(bin_width)
            ).groupBy("bin_id", "bin_start", "bin_end") \
             .agg(count("*").alias("frequency")) \
             .withColumn("condition", lit(condition_value)) \
             .orderBy("bin_id")
            
            histogram.show(10, truncate=False)
            conditional_histograms[str(condition_value)] = histogram
        
        return conditional_histograms

# ============================================================================
# Robust Histogram Pattern (Outlier-Resistant)
# ============================================================================
class RobustHistogram:
    """
    Robust Histogram: Creates histogram resistant to outliers
    Use Case: Data with extreme outliers that would distort regular histograms
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_robust_histogram(df, column_name, num_bins=10, 
                                outlier_percentile=0.95):
        """
        Create histogram using percentile-based range (ignoring extreme outliers)
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column_name: Column to analyze
            num_bins: Number of bins
            outlier_percentile: Percentile to use as max (e.g., 0.95 = 95th percentile)
            
        Returns:
            Robust histogram DataFrame
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("ROBUST HISTOGRAM PATTERN (OUTLIER-RESISTANT)")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        from pyspark.sql.functions import expr
        
        # Calculate percentile-based range
        lower_percentile = 1 - outlier_percentile
        
        # Use approxQuantile for percentile calculation
        quantiles = df.stat.approxQuantile(
            column_name, 
            [lower_percentile, outlier_percentile], 
            0.01
        )
        
        min_val = quantiles[0]
        max_val = quantiles[1]
        bin_width = (max_val - min_val) / num_bins
        
        # Get actual min/max for comparison
        actual_stats = df.agg(
            _min(col(column_name)).alias("actual_min"),
            _max(col(column_name)).alias("actual_max")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        print(f"Actual range: [{actual_stats['actual_min']}, {actual_stats['actual_max']}]")
        print(f"Robust range (p{lower_percentile*100:.0f}-p{outlier_percentile*100:.0f}): [{min_val}, {max_val}]")
        print(f"Bin width: {bin_width:.2f}")
        
        # Create histogram with outlier bins
        result = df.withColumn(
            "bin_id",
            when(col(column_name) < min_val, -1)  # Lower outliers
            .when(col(column_name) > max_val, num_bins)  # Upper outliers
            .when(col(column_name) == max_val, num_bins - 1)
            .otherwise(floor((col(column_name) - lit(min_val)) / lit(bin_width)))
        ).withColumn(
            "bin_type",
            when(col("bin_id") == -1, lit("lower_outlier"))
            .when(col("bin_id") == num_bins, lit("upper_outlier"))
            .otherwise(lit("normal"))
        ).withColumn(
            "bin_start",
            when(col("bin_id") == -1, lit(actual_stats['actual_min']))
            .when(col("bin_id") == num_bins, lit(max_val))
            .otherwise(lit(min_val) + col("bin_id") * lit(bin_width))
        ).withColumn(
            "bin_end",
            when(col("bin_id") == -1, lit(min_val))
            .when(col("bin_id") == num_bins, lit(actual_stats['actual_max']))
            .otherwise(lit(min_val) + (col("bin_id") + 1) * lit(bin_width))
        ).groupBy("bin_id", "bin_type", "bin_start", "bin_end") \
         .agg(
             count("*").alias("frequency"),
             avg(col(column_name)).alias("avg_value"),
             _min(col(column_name)).alias("min_value"),
             _max(col(column_name)).alias("max_value")
         ) \
         .orderBy("bin_id")
        
        result.show(truncate=False)
        return result


# ============================================================================
# Sparse Histogram Pattern
# ============================================================================
class SparseHistogram:
    """
    Sparse Histogram: Efficiently stores histograms with many empty bins
    Use Case: High-dimensional data or data with many zero-frequency bins
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_sparse_histogram(df, column_name, num_bins=100, 
                                min_frequency=1):
        """
        Create sparse histogram storing only non-empty bins
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column_name: Column to analyze
            num_bins: Total number of possible bins
            min_frequency: Minimum frequency to include bin (default: 1)
            
        Returns:
            Sparse histogram DataFrame
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("SPARSE HISTOGRAM PATTERN")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Calculate statistics
        stats = df.agg(
            _min(col(column_name)).alias("min_val"),
            _max(col(column_name)).alias("max_val")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        min_val = stats["min_val"]
        max_val = stats["max_val"]
        bin_width = (max_val - min_val) / num_bins
        
        # Create histogram with only non-empty bins
        result = df.withColumn(
            "bin_id",
            when(col(column_name) == max_val, num_bins - 1)
            .otherwise(floor((col(column_name) - lit(min_val)) / lit(bin_width)))
        ).withColumn(
            "bin_start",
            lit(min_val) + col("bin_id") * lit(bin_width)
        ).withColumn(
            "bin_end",
            lit(min_val) + (col("bin_id") + 1) * lit(bin_width)
        ).groupBy("bin_id", "bin_start", "bin_end") \
         .agg(count("*").alias("frequency")) \
         .filter(col("frequency") >= min_frequency) \
         .orderBy("bin_id")
        
        non_empty_bins = result.count()
        sparsity = (1 - non_empty_bins / num_bins) * 100
        
        print(f"Total possible bins: {num_bins}")
        print(f"Non-empty bins: {non_empty_bins}")
        print(f"Sparsity: {sparsity:.2f}%")
        print(f"Storage reduction: {sparsity:.2f}%")
        
        result.show(truncate=False)
        return result


# ============================================================================
# Bayesian Histogram Pattern
# ============================================================================
class BayesianHistogram:
    """
    Bayesian Histogram: Incorporates prior knowledge in histogram construction
    Use Case: When you have domain knowledge about expected distribution
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_bayesian_histogram(df, column_name, num_bins=10, 
                                  prior_weight=1.0, prior_distribution="uniform"):
        """
        Create histogram with Bayesian smoothing
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column_name: Column to analyze
            num_bins: Number of bins
            prior_weight: Weight of prior (higher = more smoothing)
            prior_distribution: Type of prior ("uniform" or "normal")
            
        Returns:
            Bayesian smoothed histogram DataFrame
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("BAYESIAN HISTOGRAM PATTERN")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Create base histogram
        stats = df.agg(
            _min(col(column_name)).alias("min_val"),
            _max(col(column_name)).alias("max_val"),
            count("*").alias("total_count")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        min_val = stats["min_val"]
        max_val = stats["max_val"]
        total_count = stats["total_count"]
        bin_width = (max_val - min_val) / num_bins
        
        # Create empirical histogram
        empirical_hist = df.withColumn(
            "bin_id",
            when(col(column_name) == max_val, num_bins - 1)
            .otherwise(floor((col(column_name) - lit(min_val)) / lit(bin_width)))
        ).groupBy("bin_id") \
         .agg(count("*").alias("observed_frequency")) \
         .orderBy("bin_id")
        
        # Calculate prior
        if prior_distribution == "uniform":
            prior_freq = prior_weight
        else:
            # For normal prior, weight center bins more
            prior_freq = prior_weight
        
        # Apply Bayesian smoothing
        result = empirical_hist.withColumn(
            "prior_frequency",
            lit(prior_freq)
        ).withColumn(
            "posterior_frequency",
            (col("observed_frequency") + col("prior_frequency")) / 
            (lit(1.0 + prior_weight / num_bins))
        ).withColumn(
            "bin_start",
            lit(min_val) + col("bin_id") * lit(bin_width)
        ).withColumn(
            "bin_end",
            lit(min_val) + (col("bin_id") + 1) * lit(bin_width)
        ).select(
            "bin_id", "bin_start", "bin_end",
            "observed_frequency", "posterior_frequency"
        )
        
        print(f"Prior weight: {prior_weight}")
        print(f"Prior distribution: {prior_distribution}")
        result.show(truncate=False)
        return result


# ============================================================================
# Kernel Density Histogram Pattern
# ============================================================================
class KernelDensityHistogram:
    """
    Kernel Density Histogram: Smooth histogram using kernel density estimation
    Use Case: When you need smooth probability density estimation
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_kde_histogram(df, column_name, num_bins=50, bandwidth=None):
        """
        Create smooth histogram using kernel density estimation
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column_name: Column to analyze
            num_bins: Number of evaluation points
            bandwidth: KDE bandwidth (None for auto)
            
        Returns:
            KDE histogram DataFrame
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("KERNEL DENSITY HISTOGRAM PATTERN")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Get data statistics
        stats = df.agg(
            _min(col(column_name)).alias("min_val"),
            _max(col(column_name)).alias("max_val"),
            avg(col(column_name)).alias("mean_val"),
            count("*").alias("total_count")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        min_val = stats["min_val"]
        max_val = stats["max_val"]
        
        # Auto-calculate bandwidth if not provided (Silverman's rule of thumb)
        if bandwidth is None:
            # Approximate standard deviation
            std_dev = df.agg(
                avg((col(column_name) - lit(stats["mean_val"])) ** 2)
            ).collect()[0][0] ** 0.5
            
            n = stats["total_count"]
            bandwidth = 1.06 * std_dev * (n ** (-1/5))
        
        print(f"Bandwidth: {bandwidth:.4f}")
        print(f"Number of evaluation points: {num_bins}")
        
        # Create evaluation points
        eval_points = [(min_val + i * (max_val - min_val) / (num_bins - 1),) 
                       for i in range(num_bins)]
        
        eval_df = spark.createDataFrame(eval_points, ["eval_point"])
        
        # For each evaluation point, calculate kernel density
        # This is a simplified version - full KDE would require more complex calculation
        from pyspark.sql.functions import exp
        
        # Cross join to calculate distances
        kde_result = eval_df.crossJoin(
            df.select(col(column_name).alias("data_point"))
        ).withColumn(
            "kernel_value",
            exp(-0.5 * ((col("eval_point") - col("data_point")) / lit(bandwidth)) ** 2) / 
            (lit(bandwidth) * lit(2.5066))  # 2.5066 ≈ sqrt(2*pi)
        ).groupBy("eval_point") \
         .agg(
             _sum("kernel_value").alias("density")
         ) \
         .orderBy("eval_point")
        
        # Normalize density
        total_density = kde_result.agg(_sum("density")).collect()[0][0]
        
        result = kde_result.withColumn(
            "normalized_density",
            col("density") / lit(total_density)
        ).withColumn(
            "estimated_frequency",
            col("normalized_density") * lit(stats["total_count"])
        )
        
        result.show(20, truncate=False)
        return result

                (col(column_name) >= col("bin_start")) & 
                (col(column_name) <= col("bin
```python
                (col(column_name) >= col("bin_start")) & 
                (col(column_name) <= col("bin_end"))
            ) \
            .groupBy("bin_id", "bin_start", "bin_end", "quantile_start", "quantile_end") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("frequency"),
                avg(col(column_name)).alias("avg_value"),
                _min(col(column_name)).alias("min_value"),
                _max(col(column_name)).alias("max_value")
            ) \
            .orderBy("bin_id")

# ============================================================================
# Rolling Window Histogram Pattern
# ============================================================================
class RollingWindowHistogram:
    """
    Rolling Window Histogram: Maintain histogram over sliding time window
    Use Case: Real-time monitoring with moving time windows
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_rolling_histogram(df, column_name, time_column, 
                                 window_size=100, num_bins=10):
        """
        Create histogram for rolling windows of data
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame with ordering column
            column_name: Column to analyze
            time_column: Column for ordering (timestamp or sequence)
            window_size: Number of records in each window
            num_bins: Number of bins per histogram
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with rolling window histograms
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("ROLLING WINDOW HISTOGRAM PATTERN")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Add row number for windowing
        window_spec = Window.orderBy(col(time_column))
        df_with_row = df.withColumn("row_num", row_number().over(window_spec))
        
        # Calculate global statistics for consistent binning
        stats = df.agg(
            _min(col(column_name)).alias("min_val"),
            _max(col(column_name)).alias("max_val")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        min_val = stats["min_val"]
        max_val = stats["max_val"]
        bin_width = (max_val - min_val) / num_bins
        
        print(f"Window size: {window_size} records")
        print(f"Value range: [{min_val}, {max_val}]")
        
        # Create bins
        df_with_bins = df_with_row.withColumn(
            "bin_id",
            when(col(column_name) == max_val, num_bins - 1)
            .otherwise(floor((col(column_name) - lit(min_val)) / lit(bin_width)))
        ).withColumn(
            "window_id",
            floor(col("row_num") / lit(window_size))
        )
        
        # Aggregate by window and bin
        result = df_with_bins.groupBy("window_id", "bin_id") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("frequency"),
                _min("row_num").alias("window_start_row"),
                _max("row_num").alias("window_end_row")
            ) \
            .withColumn(
                "bin_start",
                lit(min_val) + col("bin_id") * lit(bin_width)
            ) \
            .withColumn(
                "bin_end",
                lit(min_val) + (col("bin_id") + 1) * lit(bin_width)
            ) \
            .orderBy("window_id", "bin_id")
        
        num_windows = result.select("window_id").distinct().count()
        print(f"Number of windows: {num_windows}")
        
        result.show(30, truncate=False)
        return result


# ============================================================================
# Differential Histogram Pattern
# ============================================================================
class DifferentialHistogram:
    """
    Differential Histogram: Compare two histograms and show differences
    Use Case: A/B testing, before/after analysis, anomaly detection
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_differential_histogram(df1, df2, column_name, num_bins=10):
        """
        Create differential histogram showing changes between two datasets
        
        Args:
            df1: First DataFrame (baseline)
            df2: Second DataFrame (comparison)
            column_name: Column to analyze
            num_bins: Number of bins
            
        Returns:
            Differential histogram DataFrame
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("DIFFERENTIAL HISTOGRAM PATTERN")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Calculate combined statistics for consistent binning
        combined_stats = df1.union(df2).agg(
            _min(col(column_name)).alias("min_val"),
            _max(col(column_name)).alias("max_val")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        min_val = combined_stats["min_val"]
        max_val = combined_stats["max_val"]
        bin_width = (max_val - min_val) / num_bins
        
        # Create histogram for df1
        hist1 = df1.withColumn(
            "bin_id",
            when(col(column_name) == max_val, num_bins - 1)
            .otherwise(floor((col(column_name) - lit(min_val)) / lit(bin_width)))
        ).groupBy("bin_id") \
         .agg(count("*").alias("freq1"))
        
        # Create histogram for df2
        hist2 = df2.withColumn(
            "bin_id",
            when(col(column_name) == max_val, num_bins - 1)
            .otherwise(floor((col(column_name) - lit(min_val)) / lit(bin_width)))
        ).groupBy("bin_id") \
         .agg(count("*").alias("freq2"))
        
        # Join and calculate differences
        result = hist1.join(hist2, "bin_id", "outer") \
            .fillna(0, subset=["freq1", "freq2"]) \
            .withColumn(
                "absolute_difference",
                col("freq2") - col("freq1")
            ) \
            .withColumn(
                "relative_difference",
                when(col("freq1") > 0, 
                     ((col("freq2") - col("freq1")) / col("freq1") * 100))
                .otherwise(lit(None))
            ) \
            .withColumn(
                "bin_start",
                lit(min_val) + col("bin_id") * lit(bin_width)
            ) \
            .withColumn(
                "bin_end",
                lit(min_val) + (col("bin_id") + 1) * lit(bin_width)
            ) \
            .orderBy("bin_id")
        
        print(f"Dataset 1 count: {df1.count()}")
        print(f"Dataset 2 count: {df2.count()}")
        
        result.show(truncate=False)
        return result


# ============================================================================
# Comprehensive Testing and Validation
# ============================================================================
class HistogramValidator:
    """
    Validate histogram correctness and quality
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def validate_histogram(histogram_df, original_df, column_name):
        """
        Validate histogram against original data
        
        Args:
            histogram_df: Histogram DataFrame
            original_df: Original data DataFrame
            column_name: Column name
            
        Returns:
            Validation results dictionary
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("HISTOGRAM VALIDATION")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Check 1: Frequency sum matches original count
        hist_total = histogram_df.agg(_sum("frequency")).collect()[0][0]
        original_total = original_df.count()
        
        frequency_match = hist_total == original_total
        
        # Check 2: No gaps in bin IDs
        bin_ids = [row["bin_id"] for row in histogram_df.select("bin_id").collect()]
        expected_bins = list(range(min(bin_ids), max(bin_ids) + 1))
        no_gaps = sorted(bin_ids) == expected_bins
        
        # Check 3: Bins are contiguous
        bins_data = histogram_df.select("bin_id", "bin_start", "bin_end") \
            .orderBy("bin_id").collect()
        
        contiguous = True
        for i in range(len(bins_data) - 1):
            if abs(bins_data[i]["bin_end"] - bins_data[i+1]["bin_start"]) > 0.001:
                contiguous = False
                break
        
        # Check 4: All original values fall within histogram range
        hist_min = histogram_df.agg(_min("bin_start")).collect()[0][0]
        hist_max = histogram_df.agg(_max("bin_end")).collect()[0][0]
        
        data_min = original_df.agg(_min(col(column_name))).collect()[0][0]
        data_max = original_df.agg(_max(col(column_name))).collect()[0][0]
        
        coverage = (hist_min <= data_min) and (hist_max >= data_max)
        
        validation_results = {
            "frequency_sum_matches": frequency_match,
            "histogram_total": hist_total,
            "original_total": original_total,
            "no_bin_gaps": no_gaps,
            "bins_contiguous": contiguous,
            "full_coverage": coverage,
            "histogram_range": (hist_min, hist_max),
            "data_range": (data_min, data_max)
        }
        
        print("\nValidation Results:")
        print(f"  Frequency sum matches: {frequency_match}")
        print(f"  No bin gaps: {no_gaps}")
        print(f"  Bins contiguous: {contiguous}")
        print(f"  Full coverage: {coverage}")
        
        all_valid = all([frequency_match, no_gaps, contiguous, coverage])
        print(f"\n  Overall: {'VALID' if all_valid else 'INVALID'}")
        
        return validation_results

# Performance Benchmarking

class HistogramBenchmark:
    """
    Benchmark different histogram patterns for performance comparison
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def benchmark_histogram_patterns(df, column_name, num_bins=10):
        """
        Benchmark execution time of different histogram patterns
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column_name: Column to analyze
            num_bins: Number of bins
            
        Returns:
            Benchmark results dictionary
        """
        import time
        
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("HISTOGRAM PATTERN PERFORMANCE BENCHMARK")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        results = {}
        
        # Benchmark Equi-Width
        start = time.time()
        equi_width = EquiWidthHistogram.create_histogram(df, column_name, num_bins)
        equi_width.count()  # Force execution
        results['equi_width'] = time.time() - start
        
        # Benchmark Equi-Depth
        start = time.time()
        equi_depth = EquiDepthHistogram.create_histogram(df, column_name, num_bins)
        equi_depth.count()
        results['equi_depth'] = time.time() - start
        
        # Benchmark Adaptive
        start = time.time()
        adaptive = AdaptiveHistogram.create_histogram(df, column_name, num_bins)
        adaptive.count()
        results['adaptive'] = time.time() - start
        
        # Benchmark Compressed
        start = time.time()
        compressed = CompressedHistogram.create_histogram(df, column_name, num_bins)
        compressed.count()
        results['compressed'] = time.time() - start
        
        print("\nBenchmark Results (seconds):")
        print("-" * 40)
        for pattern, duration in sorted(results.items(), key=lambda x: x[1]):
            print(f"  {pattern:20s}: {duration:.4f}s")
        
        return results


# ============================================================================
# Histogram Persistence and Recovery
# ============================================================================
class HistogramPersistence:
    """
    Save and load histogram metadata for efficient reuse
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def save_histogram_metadata(histogram_df, metadata, output_path):
        """
        Save histogram and its metadata
        
        Args:
            histogram_df: Histogram DataFrame
            metadata: Dictionary of metadata
            output_path: Base path for saving
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("SAVING HISTOGRAM WITH METADATA")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Save histogram data
        histogram_df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(f"{output_path}/histogram_data")
        
        # Save metadata as JSON
        metadata_df = spark.createDataFrame([metadata])
        metadata_df.write.mode("overwrite").json(f"{output_path}/metadata")
        
        print(f"Histogram saved to: {output_path}")
        print(f"  - Data: {output_path}/histogram_data")
        print(f"  - Metadata: {output_path}/metadata")
    
    @staticmethod
    def load_histogram_metadata(input_path):
        """
        Load histogram and its metadata
        
        Args:
            input_path: Base path for loading
            
        Returns:
            Tuple of (histogram_df, metadata)
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("LOADING HISTOGRAM WITH METADATA")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Load histogram data
        histogram_df = spark.read.parquet(f"{input_path}/histogram_data")
        
        # Load metadata
        metadata_df = spark.read.json(f"{input_path}/metadata")
        metadata = metadata_df.collect()[0].asDict()
        
        print(f"Histogram loaded from: {input_path}")
        print(f"Bins: {histogram_df.count()}")
        
        return histogram_df, metadata
