class EvaluationPatternTests:
    """
    Unit tests for evaluation patterns
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
        self.test_results = []
    
    def test_eager_evaluation(self):
        """Test eager evaluation correctness"""
        print("\n🧪 Testing Eager Evaluation...")
        
        test_data = [(1, 100), (2, 200), (3, 300)]
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(test_data, ["id", "value"])
        
        # Test collect
        result = df.collect()
        assert len(result) == 3, "Eager collect failed"
        
        # Test count
        count = df.count()
        assert count == 3, "Eager count failed"
        
        print("   ✓ Eager evaluation tests passed")
        self.test_results.append(("Eager Evaluation", "PASSED"))
    
    def test_lazy_evaluation(self):
        """Test lazy evaluation optimization"""
        print("\n🧪 Testing Lazy Evaluation...")
        
        test_data = [(1, 100), (2, 200), (3, 300)]
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(test_data, ["id", "value"])
        
        # Build lazy pipeline
        lazy_df = df.filter(col("value") > 150).select("id")
        
        # Should not execute yet
        assert lazy_df.isStreaming == False, "Lazy evaluation setup failed"
        
        # Execute and verify
        result = lazy_df.collect()
        assert len(result) == 2, "Lazy evaluation result incorrect"
        
        print("   ✓ Lazy evaluation tests passed")
        self.test_results.append(("Lazy Evaluation", "PASSED"))
    
    def test_short_circuit(self):
        """Test short-circuit evaluation"""
        print("\n🧪 Testing Short-Circuit Evaluation...")
        
        test_data = [(i, i * 100) for i in range(1, 101)]
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(test_data, ["id", "value"])
        
        # Test limit
        limited = df.limit(10).collect()
        assert len(limited) == 10, "Short-circuit limit failed"
        
        # Test first
        first = df.first()
        assert first is not None, "Short-circuit first failed"
        
        print("   ✓ Short-circuit evaluation tests passed")
        self.test_results.append(("Short-Circuit Evaluation", "PASSED"))
    
    def test_memoized_evaluation(self):
        """Test memoized evaluation"""
        print("\n🧪 Testing Memoized Evaluation...")
        
        test_data = [(i, i * 100) for i in range(1, 101)]
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(test_data, ["id", "value"])
        
        # Cache and verify
        cached_df = df.cache()
        count1 = cached_df.count()
        
        # Second access should use cache
        count2 = cached_df.count()
        
        assert count1 == count2 == 100, "Memoized evaluation failed"
        
        cached_df.unpersist()
        print("   ✓ Memoized evaluation tests passed")
        self.test_results.append(("Memoized Evaluation", "PASSED"))
    
    def test_conditional_evaluation(self):
        """Test conditional evaluation"""
        print("\n🧪 Testing Conditional Evaluation...")
        
        test_data = [(1, 100), (2, 200), (3, 300)]
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(test_data, ["id", "value"])
        
        # Test conditional column
        result_df = df.withColumn(
            "category",
            when(col("value") > 250, "High")
            .when(col("value") > 150, "Medium")
            .otherwise("Low")
        )
        
        results = result_df.collect()
        assert results[0].category == "Low", "Conditional evaluation failed"
        assert results[1].category == "Medium", "Conditional evaluation failed"
        assert results[2].category == "High", "Conditional evaluation failed"
        
        print("   ✓ Conditional evaluation tests passed")
        self.test_results.append(("Conditional Evaluation", "PASSED"))
    
    def run_all_tests(self):
        """Run all tests"""
        print("\n" + "=" * 60)
        print("RUNNING ALL EVALUATION PATTERN TESTS")
        print("=" * 60)
        
        self.test_eager_evaluation()
        self.test_lazy_evaluation()
        self.test_short_circuit()
        self.test_memoized_evaluation()
        self.test_conditional_evaluation()
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 60)
        print("TEST SUMMARY")
        print("=" * 60)
        
        for test_name, status in self.test_results:
            status_icon = "✅" if status == "PASSED" else "❌"
            print(f"{status_icon} {test_name}: {status}")
        
        total_tests = len(self.test_results)
        passed_tests = sum(1 for _, status in self.test_results if status == "PASSED")
        
        print(f"\nTotal Tests: {total_tests}")
        print(f"Passed: {passed_tests}")
        print(f"Failed: {total_tests - passed_tests}")
        print(f"Success Rate: {(passed_tests/total_tests)*100:.1f}%")

# Run tests

class EvaluationPatternUtilities:
    """
    Additional utility functions for evaluation patterns
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    def analyze_query_complexity(self, df):
        """
        Analyze and report query complexity
        """
        print("\n🔍 QUERY COMPLEXITY ANALYSIS")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        # Get query plan
        plan = df._jdf.queryExecution().toString()
        
        # Count transformations
        num_filters = plan.count("Filter")
        num_projects = plan.count("Project")
        num_aggregates = plan.count("Aggregate")
        num_joins = plan.count("Join")
        num_sorts = plan.count("Sort")
        
        print(f"Filters: {num_filters}")
        print(f"Projections: {num_projects}")
        print(f"Aggregations: {num_aggregates}")
        print(f"Joins: {num_joins}")
        print(f"Sorts: {num_sorts}")
        
        total_operations = (num_filters + num_projects + num_aggregates + 
                           num_joins + num_sorts)
        
        complexity = "Low" if total_operations < 5 else \
                    "Medium" if total_operations < 10 else "High"
        
        print(f"\nComplexity Level: {complexity}")
        print(f"Total Operations: {total_operations}")
        
        return {
            'filters': num_filters,
            'projects': num_projects,
            'aggregates': num_aggregates,
            'joins': num_joins,
            'sorts': num_sorts,
            'total': total_operations,
            'complexity': complexity
        }
    
    def estimate_cache_size(self, df, sample_fraction=0.01):
        """
        Estimate memory required for caching
        """
        print("\n💾 CACHE SIZE ESTIMATION")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        # Get sample
        sample_df = df.sample(fraction=sample_fraction)
        sample_count = sample_df.count()
        
        if sample_count == 0:
            print("Sample too small for estimation")
            return None
        
        # Estimate size from sample
        sample_data = sample_df.collect()
        sample_size_bytes = len(str(sample_data))
        
        # Extrapolate to full dataset
        total_count = df.count()
        estimated_size_bytes = (sample_size_bytes / sample_count) * total_count
        
        # Convert to readable format
        size_kb = estimated_size_bytes / 1024
        size_mb = size_kb / 1024
        size_gb = size_mb / 1024
        
        print(f"Total Records: {total_count:,}")
        print(f"Sample Records: {sample_count:,}")
        print(f"Estimated Size: {size_mb:.2f} MB ({size_gb:.3f} GB)")
        
        # Recommendation
        if size_gb > 10:
            recommendation = "Consider MEMORY_AND_DISK storage level"
        elif size_gb > 1:
            recommendation = "MEMORY_ONLY should work, monitor usage"
        else:
            recommendation = "MEMORY_ONLY is safe"
        
        print(f"Recommendation: {recommendation}")
        
        return {
            'size_bytes': estimated_size_bytes,
            'size_mb': size_mb,
            'size_gb': size_gb,
            'recommendation': recommendation
        }
    
    def optimize_partitions(self, df, target_partition_size_mb=128):
        """
        Calculate optimal partition count
        """
        print("\n⚙️ PARTITION OPTIMIZATION")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        # Estimate total size
        size_info = self.estimate_cache_size(df)
        
        if not size_info:
            return df
        
        total_size_mb = size_info['size_mb']
        optimal_partitions = max(1, int(total_size_mb / target_partition_size_mb))
        current_partitions = df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
        
        print(f"Current Partitions: {current_partitions}")
        print(f"Optimal Partitions: {optimal_partitions}")
        print(f"Target Partition Size: {target_partition_size_mb} MB")
        
        if optimal_partitions < current_partitions:
            print(f"Recommendation: Coalesce to {optimal_partitions}")
            optimized_df = df.coalesce(optimal_partitions)
        elif optimal_partitions > current_partitions:
            print(f"Recommendation: Repartition to {optimal_partitions}")
            optimized_df = df.repartition(optimal_partitions)
        else:
            print("Current partitioning is optimal")
            optimized_df = df
        
        return optimized_df
    
    def profile_evaluation_pattern(self, df, pattern_name, operation):
        """
        Profile a specific evaluation pattern
        """
        print(f"\n📊 PROFILING: {pattern_name}")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        import gc
        
        # Clear memory
        gc.collect()
        
        # Profile execution
        start_time = time.time()
        start_memory = self.spark.sparkContext._jvm.Runtime.getRuntime().freeMemory()
        
        # Execute operation
        result = operation(df)
        
        end_time = time.time()
        end_memory = self.spark.sparkContext._jvm.Runtime.getRuntime().freeMemory()
        
        execution_time = end_time - start_time
        memory_used = (start_memory - end_memory) / (1024 * 1024)  # MB
        
        print(f"Execution Time: {execution_time:.4f} seconds")
        print(f"Memory Used: {memory_used:.2f} MB")
        
        # Calculate throughput if applicable
        if hasattr(result, 'count'):
            record_count = result.count() if callable(result.count) else len(result)
            throughput = record_count / execution_time if execution_time > 0 else 0
            print(f"Throughput: {throughput:.2f} records/second")
        
        return {
            'pattern': pattern_name,
            'execution_time': execution_time,
            'memory_used_mb': memory_used,
            'result': result
        }
    
    def compare_storage_levels(self, df):
        """
        Compare different storage levels for caching
        """
        print("\n💿 STORAGE LEVEL COMPARISON")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        from pyspark import StorageLevel
        
        storage_levels = [
            ("MEMORY_ONLY", StorageLevel.MEMORY_ONLY),
            ("MEMORY_AND_DISK", StorageLevel.MEMORY_AND_DISK),
            ("MEMORY_ONLY_SER", StorageLevel.MEMORY_ONLY_SER),
            ("DISK_ONLY", StorageLevel.DISK_ONLY)
        ]
        
        results = []
        
        for name, level in storage_levels:
            print(f"\nTesting {name}...")
            
            # Cache with specific storage level
            cached_df = df.persist(level)
            
            # Measure materialization time
            start = time.time()
            count = cached_df.count()
            materialization_time = time.time() - start
            
            # Measure access time
            start = time.time()
            cached_df.first()
            access_time = time.time() - start
            
            # Unpersist
            cached_df.unpersist()
            
            results.append({
                'storage_level': name,
                'materialization_time': materialization_time,
                'access_time': access_time
            })
            
            print(f"  Materialization: {materialization_time:.4f}s")
            print(f"  Access: {access_time:.4f}s")
        
        # Summary
        print("\n" + "=" * 60)
        print("STORAGE LEVEL SUMMARY")
        print("=" * 60)
        
        for result in results:
            print(f"{result['storage_level']:20s} | "
                  f"Mat: {result['materialization_time']:.4f}s | "
                  f"Access: {result['access_time']:.4f}s")
        
        return results
    
    def generate_evaluation_report(self, df, pattern_results):
        """
        Generate comprehensive evaluation report
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("COMPREHENSIVE EVALUATION REPORT")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        report = f"""
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                        EVALUATION PATTERN REPORT                          ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

Dataset Information:
  • Total Records: {df.count():,}
  • Total Columns: {len(df.columns)}
  • Partitions: {df.rdd.getNumPartitions()}
  • Schema Complexity: {len(df.dtypes)} fields

Pattern Performance Summary:
"""
        
        for pattern_name, metrics in pattern_results.items():
            report += f"""
  {pattern_name}:
    - Execution Time: {metrics.get('execution_time', 'N/A')}
    - Memory Usage: {metrics.get('memory_used_mb', 'N/A')} MB
    - Throughput: {metrics.get('throughput', 'N/A')} records/sec
"""

Recommendations:

  4. Use broadcast joins for small lookup tables

Next Steps:

  • Optimize partitioning based on data size
  • Consider checkpointing for long pipelines
  • Implement adaptive caching strategies
  
Report Generated: """ + time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
        
        print(report)
        return report

class AdvancedScenarios:
    """
    Handle advanced scenarios and edge cases
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    def handle_skewed_data(self, df, skew_column):
        """
        Handle data skew with evaluation patterns
        """
        print("\n⚖️ HANDLING SKEWED DATA")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        # Identify skew
        skew_stats = df.groupBy(skew_column).count() \
                       .orderBy(col("count").desc())
        
        print("Top 5 most frequent values:")
        skew_stats.show(5)
        
        # Strategy: Use salting for skewed keys
        from pyspark.sql.functions import rand, concat, lit
        
        salted_df = df.withColumn(
            "salted_key",
            concat(col(skew_column), lit("_"), (rand() * 10).cast("int"))
        )
        
        print("Applied salting to reduce skew")
        return salted_df
    
    def handle_memory_constraints(self, df, operation, max_memory_mb=1024):
        """
        Handle operations with memory constraints
        """
        print("\n🧠 HANDLING MEMORY CONSTRAINTS")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        # Estimate operation size
        estimated_size = utilities.estimate_cache_size(df)
        
        if estimated_size and estimated_size['size_mb'] > max_memory_mb:
            print(f"Data size ({estimated_size['size_mb']:.2f} MB) exceeds limit ({max_memory_mb} MB)")
            print("Using disk-based approach...")
            
            # Use MEMORY_AND_DISK instead of MEMORY_ONLY
            processed_df = operation(df).persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_AND_DISK)
        else:
            print("Data fits in memory, using MEMORY_ONLY")
            processed_df = operation(df).cache()
        
        return processed_df
    
    def handle_dynamic_schema(self, df, schema_changes):
        """
        Handle dynamic schema changes with conditional evaluation
        """
        print("\n🔄 HANDLING DYNAMIC SCHEMA")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        result = df
        
        for change in schema_changes:
            change_type = change.get('type')
            
            if change_type == 'add':
                col_name = change['column']
                col_expr = change['expression']
                result = result.withColumn(col_name, col_expr)
                print(f"Added column: {col_name}")
            
            elif change_type == 'rename':
                old_name = change['old_name']
                new_name = change['new_name']
                result = result.withColumnRenamed(old_name, new_name)
                print(f"Renamed column: {old_name} -> {new_name}")
            
            elif change_type == 'drop':
                col_name = change['column']
                result = result.drop(col_name)
                print(f"Dropped column: {col_name}")
        
        return result
    
    def handle_null_heavy_data(self, df):
        """
        Handle datasets with many nulls using conditional evaluation
        """
        print("\n🔍 HANDLING NULL-HEAVY DATA")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        # Analyze null distribution
        null_counts = df.select([
            (count(when(col(c).isNull(), c)) / count("*") * 100
```python
            (count(when(col(c).isNull(), c)) / count("*") * 100).alias(c)
            for c in df.columns
        ]).collect()[0]
        
        print("Null percentage by column:")
        high_null_cols = []
        for col_name in df.columns:
            null_pct = null_counts[col_name]
            print(f"  {col_name}: {null_pct:.2f}%")
            if null_pct > 50:
                high_null_cols.append(col_name)
        
        # Strategy: Different handling based on null percentage
        result = df
        
        for col_name in high_null_cols:
            print(f"\nHandling high-null column: {col_name}")
            # Option 1: Fill with default value
            result = result.fillna({col_name: "UNKNOWN"})
        
        return result
    
    def handle_streaming_evaluation(self, stream_df):
        """
        Adapt evaluation patterns for streaming data
        """
        print("\n📡 HANDLING STREAMING EVALUATION")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        # Note: This is conceptual for streaming
        print("Streaming requires different evaluation patterns:")
        print("  • Use window operations instead of global aggregations")
        print("  • Apply watermarking for late data")
        print("  • Use foreachBatch for batch-like operations")
        print("  • Avoid collect() and other eager operations")
        
        # Example pattern for streaming
        streaming_query = """
        # Streaming-compatible pattern
        stream_df.writeStream \\
            .foreachBatch(lambda batch_df, batch_id: 
                process_batch(batch_df, batch_id)) \\
            .start()
        """
        print(f"\nExample pattern:\n{streaming_query}")
    
    def handle_nested_data(self, df):
        """
        Handle nested/complex data structures
        """
        print("\n🗂️ HANDLING NESTED DATA STRUCTURES")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        # Check for nested structures
        has_nested = any(
            isinstance(field.dataType, (StructType, ArrayType))
            for field in df.schema.fields
        )
        
        if has_nested:
            print("Detected nested structures")
            print("Strategies:")
            print("  • Flatten structures for better performance")
            print("  • Use explode() for arrays")
            print("  • Use dot notation for struct access")
            
            # Example: If we had nested data
            # result = df.select("id", "nested_field.*")
        else:
            print("No nested structures detected")
        
        return df
    
    def handle_large_broadcast(self, large_df, lookup_df, threshold_mb=10):
        """
        Handle broadcast joins that might be too large
        """
        print("\n📻 HANDLING LARGE BROADCAST JOINS")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        # Estimate lookup table size
        lookup_size = utilities.estimate_cache_size(lookup_df)
        
        if lookup_size and lookup_size['size_mb'] > threshold_mb:
            print(f"Lookup table ({lookup_size['size_mb']:.2f} MB) exceeds "
                  f"broadcast threshold ({threshold_mb} MB)")
            print("Using standard join instead of broadcast")
            
            result = large_df.join(lookup_df, "customer_id", "left")
        else:
            print(f"Lookup table ({lookup_size['size_mb']:.2f} MB) is suitable for broadcast")
            result = large_df.join(broadcast(lookup_df), "customer_id", "left")
        
        return result
    
    def handle_iterative_algorithm(self, df, max_iterations=10, tolerance=0.001):
        """
        Handle iterative algorithms with memoization
        """
        print("\n🔁 HANDLING ITERATIVE ALGORITHMS")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        current_df = df.cache()
        current_df.count()  # Materialize
        
        for iteration in range(max_iterations):
            print(f"Iteration {iteration + 1}/{max_iterations}")
            
            # Perform iteration (example: update values)
            next_df = current_df.withColumn(
                "value",
                col("value") * 0.9  # Example transformation
            )
            
            # Cache new result
            next_df = next_df.cache()
            next_df.count()  # Materialize
            
            # Check convergence (example)
            diff = next_df.agg(sum("value")).collect()[0][0] - \
                   current_df.agg(sum("value")).collect()[0][0]
            
            # Unpersist old DataFrame
            current_df.unpersist()
            current_df = next_df
            
            if abs(diff) < tolerance:
                print(f"Converged at iteration {iteration + 1}")
                break
        
        print("Algorithm completed")
        return current_df

class VisualizationHelpers:
    """
    Helper functions for visualizing evaluation pattern results
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    def create_ascii_bar_chart(self, data_dict, title="Chart", max_width=50):
        """
        Create ASCII bar chart for visualization
        """
        print(f"\n{title}")
        print("=" * (max_width + 20))
        
        if not data_dict:
            print("No data to display")
            return
        
        max_value = max(data_dict.values())
        
        for label, value in sorted(data_dict.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True):
            bar_length = int((value / max_value) * max_width) if max_value > 0 else 0
            bar = "█" * bar_length
            print(f"{label:20s} | {bar} {value:.2f}")
    
    def create_performance_table(self, metrics_list):
        """
        Create formatted performance comparison table
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("PERFORMANCE COMPARISON TABLE")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # Header
        print(f"{'Pattern':<25} {'Time (s)':<12} {'Memory (MB)':<15} {'Throughput':<15}")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        # Rows
        for metrics in metrics_list:
            pattern = metrics.get('pattern', 'Unknown')
            exec_time = metrics.get('execution_time', 0)
            memory = metrics.get('memory_used_mb', 0)
            throughput = metrics.get('throughput', 0)
            
            print(f"{pattern:<25} {exec_time:<12.4f} {memory:<15.2f} {throughput:<15.2f}")
        
        print("=" * 80)
    
    def create_summary_dashboard(self, df, analysis_results):
        """
        Create a text-based dashboard summary
        """
        dashboard = f"""
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                         EVALUATION DASHBOARD                              ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

📊 DATASET OVERVIEW
{'─' * 78}
  Total Records:        {df.count():,}
  Total Columns:        {len(df.columns)}
  Partitions:           {df.rdd.getNumPartitions()}
  
📈 EVALUATION METRICS
{'─' * 78}
"""
        
        for pattern_name, metrics in analysis_results.items():
            dashboard += f"""
  {pattern_name}:
    ⏱️  Execution Time:    {metrics.get('execution_time', 'N/A')} seconds
    💾 Memory Usage:      {metrics.get('memory_used_mb', 'N/A')} MB
    ⚡ Throughput:        {metrics.get('throughput', 'N/A')} rec/sec
"""
        
        dashboard += f"""
🎯 RECOMMENDATIONS
{'─' * 78}
  ✓ Best Pattern:       {self._get_best_pattern(analysis_results)}
  ✓ Optimization:       {self._get_optimization_tip(analysis_results)}
  
📅 Generated:           {time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")}
{'═' * 78}
"""
        
        print(dashboard)
        return dashboard
    
    def _get_best_pattern(self, results):
        """Determine best performing pattern"""
        if not results:
            return "N/A"
        
        fastest = min(
            results.items(),
            key=lambda x: x[1].get('execution_time', float('inf'))
        )
        return fastest[0]
    
    def _get_optimization_tip(self, results):
        """Provide optimization tip based on results"""
        tips = [
            "Consider caching for repeated access",
            "Use broadcast for small lookup tables",
            "Apply filters early in pipeline",
            "Optimize partition count"
        ]
        return tips[hash(str(results)) % len(tips)]
    
    def export_metrics_to_dict(self, pattern_results):
        """
        Export all metrics to a structured dictionary
        """
        export_data = {
            'timestamp': time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
            'patterns': {}
        }
        
        for pattern_name, metrics in pattern_results.items():
            export_data['patterns'][pattern_name] = {
                'execution_time_seconds': metrics.get('execution_time', 0),
                'memory_used_mb': metrics.get('memory_used_mb', 0),
                'throughput_records_per_sec': metrics.get('throughput', 0)
            }
        
        print("\n📤 EXPORTED METRICS:")
        import json
        print(json.dumps(export_data, indent=2))
        
        return export_data

class RealWorldIntegrations:

    def integrate_with_data_lake(self, df, base_path="/tmp/data_lake"):

        processed_df.write \
            .mode(write_mode) \
            .partitionBy(*partition_cols) \
            .parquet(f"{base_path}/orders")
        
        print("✓ Data written to lake")
        
        # MEMOIZED: Read back and cache for downstream
        lake_df = self.spark.read.parquet(f"{base_path}/orders").cache()
        lake_df.count()  # Materialize

    def integrate_with_warehouse(self, df, table_name="orders_summary"):
        """
        Integration with data warehouse using evaluation patterns
        """
        print("\n🏢 DATA WAREHOUSE INTEGRATION")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        # LAZY + CONDITIONAL: Build warehouse-ready aggregation
        warehouse_df = df.groupBy("product", "status").agg(
            sum(col("quantity") * col("price")).alias("total_revenue"),
            count("*").alias("order_count"),
            avg(col("quantity") * col("price")).alias("avg_order_value"),
            min("order_date").alias("first_order_date"),
            max("order_date").alias("last_order_date")
        )
        
        # Add metadata columns
        warehouse_df = warehouse_df.withColumn("load_timestamp", lit(time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")))
        warehouse_df = warehouse_df.withColumn("source_system", lit("PySpark"))
        
        print(f"Preparing to write to warehouse table: {table_name}")
        
        # EAGER: Validate before write
        record_count = warehouse_df.count()
        print(f"Records to write: {record_count:,}")
        
        # Write to warehouse (simulated with parquet)
        warehouse_df.write.mode("overwrite").saveAsTable(table_name)
        
        print(f"✓ Data written to warehouse table: {table_name}")
        
        return warehouse_df
    
    def integrate_with_api(self, df, batch_size=100):
        """
        Integration with REST API using evaluation patterns
        """
        print("\n🌐 REST API INTEGRATION")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        # SHORT-CIRCUIT: Process in batches
        total_records = df.count()
        num_batches = (total_records + batch_size - 1) // batch_size
        
        print(f"Total records: {total_records:,}")
        print(f"Batch size: {batch_size}")
        print(f"Number of batches: {num_batches}")
        
        # Simulate API calls
        for batch_num in range(min(3, num_batches)):  # Demo: only first 3 batches
            offset = batch_num * batch_size
            
            # LAZY + SHORT-CIRCUIT: Get batch
            batch_df = df.orderBy("order_id").limit(batch_size).offset(offset)
            
            # EAGER: Collect batch for API call
            batch_data = batch_df.collect()
            
            # Simulate API call
            print(f"  Batch {batch_num + 1}: Sending {len(batch_data)} records to API")
            # api_client.post('/orders', batch_data)
        
        print("✓ API integration completed (demo)")
    
    def integrate_with_ml_pipeline(self, df):
        """
        Integration with ML pipeline using evaluation patterns
        """
        print("\n🤖 ML PIPELINE INTEGRATION")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        from pyspark.ml.feature import VectorAssembler
        from pyspark.ml import Pipeline
        
        # LAZY: Prepare features
        feature_df = df.withColumn("revenue", col("quantity") * col("price"))
        
        # Select numeric features
        feature_cols = ["quantity", "price", "revenue"]
        
        # CONDITIONAL: Build ML pipeline
        assembler = VectorAssembler(inputCols=feature_cols, outputCol="features")
        
        # MEMOIZED: Cache prepared data
        ml_ready_df = assembler.transform(feature_df).cache()
        ml_ready_df.count()  # Materialize
        
        print(f"✓ ML features prepared and cached")
        print(f"  Feature columns: {feature_cols}")
        print(f"  Records: {ml_ready_df.count():,}")
        
        return ml_ready_df

# streaming_df.writeStream.foreachBatch(process_streaming_batch).start()
"""

╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗

🔴 PROBLEM: Out of Memory (OOM) Errors
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
SYMPTOMS:
  • java.lang.OutOfMemoryError
  • Executor/Driver memory exceeded
  • Tasks failing repeatedly

SOLUTIONS:
  ✓ Avoid collect() on large DataFrames
  ✓ Use MEMORY_AND_DISK instead of MEMORY_ONLY
  ✓ Increase executor memory: --executor-memory 4g
  ✓ Increase driver memory: --driver-memory 4g
  ✓ Reduce partition size with repartition()
  ✓ Use iterative processing with limit()
  ✓ Unpersist() unused cached DataFrames

EXAMPLE:
  # Bad
  large_df.collect()  # DON'T DO THIS
  
  # Good
  large_df.write.parquet("output")  # Write to disk
  large_df.limit(1000).collect()    # Sample instead

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🔴 PROBLEM: Slow Query Performance

SYMPTOMS:
  • Queries taking longer than expected
  • High shuffle read/write
  • Uneven task distribution

SOLUTIONS:
  ✓ Check execution plan with explain()
  ✓ Apply filters early (predicate pushdown)
  ✓ Use broadcast() for small tables
  ✓ Optimize partition count
  ✓ Cache intermediate results
  ✓ Avoid UDFs when possible (use built-in functions)
  ✓ Use columnar formats (Parquet)

EXAMPLE:
  # Check execution plan
  df.explain(mode="formatted")
  
  # Optimize
  df.filter(col("date") >= "2024-01-01") \  # Filter early
    .join(broadcast(small_df), "key") \      # Broadcast small table
    .cache()                                  # Cache if reused

  cached_df.count()  # Materialize cache
  
  # Verify
  print(cached_df.storageLevel)

🔴 PROBLEM: Lazy Evaluation Confusion
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
SYMPTOMS:
  • Transformations not executing
  • Unexpected behavior in loops
  • Variables not updating

SOLUTIONS:
  ✓ Remember: transformations are lazy, actions are eager
  ✓ Use actions to trigger execution: count(), collect(), show()
  ✓ Check execution plan with explain()
  ✓ Use intermediate actions for debugging

EXAMPLE:
  # Lazy - nothing executes
  df2 = df.filter(col("value") > 100)
  df3 = df2.select("id", "value")
  
  # Eager - triggers execution
  count = df3.count()
  
  # Debug with show()
  df2.show()  # See intermediate results

  else:
      result = large_df.join(broadcast_df, "key")

🔴 PROBLEM: Partition Count Issues
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
SYMPTOMS:

  • Tasks taking too long
  • Shuffle overhead

SOLUTIONS:
  ✓ Use coalesce() to reduce partitions
  ✓ Use repartition() to increase partitions
  ✓ Set spark.sql.shuffle.partitions appropriately
  ✓ Target 128MB per partition

EXAMPLE:
  # Too many partitions (small tasks)
  df.rdd.getNumPartitions()  # e.g., 10000
  optimized_df = df.coalesce(200)
  
  # Too few partitions (large tasks)
  df.rdd.getNumPartitions()  # e.g., 2
  optimized_df = df.repartition(200)
  
  # Set default shuffle partitions
  spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "200")

optimization_cookbook = """
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                         OPTIMIZATION COOKBOOK                             ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

🍳 RECIPE 1: Optimize Large DataFrame Processing
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
INGREDIENTS:
  • Large DataFrame (> 1GB)
  • Multiple transformations
  • Repeated access needed

STEPS:
  1. Apply filters early (predicate pushdown)
  2. Select only needed columns (projection pushdown)
  3. Cache if accessed 3+ times
  4. Use appropriate storage level
  5. Unpersist when done

CODE:
  # Bad approach
  df.groupBy("category").agg(...).filter(col("date") >= "2024-01-01")
  
  # Good approach
  optimized = df.filter(col("date") >= "2024-01-01") \\
                .select("category", "amount", "date") \\
                .cache()
  
  optimized.count()  # Materialize
  
  # Use multiple times
  result1 = optimized.groupBy("category").agg(...)
  result2 = optimized.filter(col("amount") > 100)
  
  # Cleanup
  optimized.unpersist()

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🍳 RECIPE 2: Optimize Join Operations
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
INGREDIENTS:
  • Large fact table
  • Small dimension table (< 10MB)
  • Join operation

STEPS:
  1. Identify small table
  2. Apply broadcast hint
  3. Filter both tables before join
  4. Use appropriate join type

CODE:
  from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast
  
  # Filter before join
  large_filtered = large_df.filter(col("active") == True)
  small_filtered = small_df.filter(col("valid") == True)
  
  # Broadcast small table
  result = large_filtered.join(
      broadcast(small_filtered),
      "key",

"""
PySpark Data Boundary Patterns
Author: Code Generation Assistant
Description: Implementation of various data boundary patterns for controlling
            data processing limits in PySpark applications.
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, DataFrame, Window
from pyspark.sql.functions import (
    col, current_timestamp, unix_timestamp, size, count, lit,
    row_number, sum as spark_sum, monotonically_increasing_id
)
from pyspark.sql.types import *
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Optional, Callable
import logging

# Configure logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class TimeBoundaryPattern:
    """
    Time Boundary Pattern: Processes data within specific time windows or durations.
    Use cases: Session analysis, time-windowed aggregations, real-time processing limits
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        
    def filter_by_time_range(
        self, 
        df: DataFrame, 
        time_column: str,
        start_time: datetime,
        end_time: datetime
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Filter data based on absolute time boundaries.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            time_column: Name of the timestamp column
            start_time: Start boundary (inclusive)
            end_time: End boundary (exclusive)
            
        Returns:
            Filtered DataFrame within time boundaries
        """
        logger.info(f"Applying time boundary: {start_time} to {end_time}")
        
        return df.filter(
            (col(time_column) >= lit(start_time)) & 
            (col(time_column) < lit(end_time))
        )
    
    def filter_by_relative_time(
        self,
        df: DataFrame,
        time_column: str,
        hours_back: int = 24
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Filter data based on relative time (e.g., last N hours).
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            time_column: Name of the timestamp column
            hours_back: Number of hours to look back
            
        Returns:
            Filtered DataFrame
        """
        logger.info(f"Applying relative time boundary: last {hours_back} hours")
        
        cutoff_time = datetime.now() - timedelta(hours=hours_back)
        
        return df.filter(col(time_column) >= lit(cutoff_time))
    
    def process_with_timeout(
        self,
        df: DataFrame,
        processing_func: Callable,
        timeout_seconds: int = 300
    ) -> Optional[DataFrame]:
        """
        Process data with a timeout boundary.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            processing_func: Function to apply to DataFrame
            timeout_seconds: Maximum processing time in seconds
            
        Returns:
            Processed DataFrame or None if timeout
        """
        logger.info(f"Processing with timeout: {timeout_seconds} seconds")
        
        # Set Spark timeout configuration
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.sql.broadcastTimeout", timeout_seconds)
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.network.timeout", f"{timeout_seconds}s")
        
        try:
            result = processing_func(df)
            return result
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Processing failed or timed out: {str(e)}")
            return None
    
    def sliding_time_window(
        self,
        df: DataFrame,
        time_column: str,
        window_duration: str = "1 hour",
        slide_duration: str = "30 minutes"
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Create sliding time windows for aggregation.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            time_column: Name of the timestamp column
            window_duration: Size of the window
            slide_duration: Slide interval
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with windowed data
        """
        from pyspark.sql.functions import window
        
        logger.info(f"Creating sliding windows: {window_duration} / {slide_duration}")
        
        return df.groupBy(
            window(col(time_column), window_duration, slide_duration)
        ).agg(
            count("*").alias("event_count"),
            spark_sum(col("value")).alias("total_value") if "value" in df.columns else lit(0)
        )


class SizeBoundaryPattern:
    """
    Size Boundary Pattern: Controls data processing based on data size limits.
    Use cases: Memory management, chunk processing, batch size control
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        
    def limit_by_row_count(
        self,
        df: DataFrame,
        max_rows: int
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Limit DataFrame to maximum number of rows.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            max_rows: Maximum number of rows to process
            
        Returns:
            Limited DataFrame
        """
        logger.info(f"Applying row limit: {max_rows}")
        
        return df.limit(max_rows)
    
    def limit_by_partition_size(
        self,
        df: DataFrame,
        max_size_mb: int = 128
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Repartition data to ensure partition sizes don't exceed limit.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            max_size_mb: Maximum partition size in MB
            
        Returns:
            Repartitioned DataFrame
        """
        logger.info(f"Applying partition size limit: {max_size_mb} MB")
        
        # Estimate current size and calculate optimal partitions
        # Note: This is an approximation
        num_partitions = max(df.rdd.getNumPartitions(), 1)
        
        # Increase partitions if needed to meet size requirements
        target_partitions = int(num_partitions * 1.5)
        
        return df.repartition(target_partitions)
    
    def chunk_processing(
        self,
        df: DataFrame,
        chunk_size: int = 10000,
        processing_func: Callable = None
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Process data in chunks of specified size.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            chunk_size: Number of rows per chunk
            processing_func: Function to apply to each chunk
            
        Returns:
            Processed DataFrame
        """
        logger.info(f"Processing in chunks of {chunk_size} rows")
        
        # Add chunk identifier
        df_with_chunks = df.withColumn(
            "row_id",
            monotonically_increasing_id()
        ).withColumn(
            "chunk_id",
            (col("row_id") / chunk_size).cast("long")
        )
        
        if processing_func:
            # Process each chunk separately
            chunks = df_with_chunks.select("chunk_id").distinct().collect()
            
            processed_chunks = []
            for chunk in chunks:
                chunk_data = df_with_chunks.filter(col("chunk_id") == chunk.chunk_id)
                processed_chunk = processing_func(chunk_data)
                processed_chunks.append(processed_chunk)
            
            # Union all processed chunks
            result = processed_chunks[0]
            for chunk in processed_chunks[1:]:
                result = result.union(chunk)
            
            return result.drop("row_id", "chunk_id")
        
        return df_with_chunks
    
    def limit_by_data_size(
        self,
        df: DataFrame,
        max_size_gb: float = 1.0,
        sample_ratio: float = 0.1
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Limit DataFrame based on estimated data size.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            max_size_gb: Maximum data size in GB
            sample_ratio: Ratio for size estimation
            
        Returns:
            Size-limited DataFrame
        """
        logger.info(f"Applying data size limit: {max_size_gb} GB")
        
        # Sample data to estimate size
        sample_df = df.sample(False, sample_ratio)
        sample_count = sample_df.count()
        total_count = df.count()
        
        # Estimate if we need to limit
        if sample_count > 0:
            estimated_ratio = max_size_gb / (sample_ratio * 10)  # Rough estimation
            if estimated_ratio < 1.0:
                limit_rows = int(total_count * estimated_ratio)
                logger.info(f"Limiting to {limit_rows} rows based on size estimate")
                return df.limit(limit_rows)
        
        return df


class CountBoundaryPattern:
    """
    Count Boundary Pattern: Controls processing based on record counts and frequencies.
    Use cases: Top-N processing, frequency filtering, threshold-based filtering
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        
    def top_n_by_group(
        self,
        df: DataFrame,
        group_column: str,
        order_column: str,
        n: int = 10,
        ascending: bool = False
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Get top N records per group.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            group_column: Column to group by
            order_column: Column to order by
            n: Number of top records
            ascending: Sort order
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with top N records per group
        """
        logger.info(f"Getting top {n} records per {group_column}")
        
        window_spec = Window.partitionBy(group_column).orderBy(
            col(order_column).asc() if ascending else col(order_column).desc()
        )
        
        return df.withColumn(
            "rank",
            row_number().over(window_spec)
        ).filter(
            col("rank") <= n
        ).drop("rank")
    
    def filter_by_frequency(
        self,
        df: DataFrame,
        column: str,
        min_count: int = 10,
        max_count: Optional[int] = None
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Filter records based on value frequency.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column: Column to check frequency
            min_count: Minimum occurrence count
            max_count: Maximum occurrence count (optional)
            
        Returns:
            Filtered DataFrame
        """
        logger.info(f"Filtering by frequency: min={min_count}, max={max_count}")
        
        # Calculate frequencies
        freq_df = df.groupBy(column).agg(
            count("*").alias("frequency")
        )
        
        # Apply frequency filters
        if max_count:
            freq_df = freq_df.filter(
                (col("frequency") >= min_count) & 
                (col("frequency") <= max_count)
            )
        else:
            freq_df = freq_df.filter(col("frequency") >= min_count)
        
        # Join back to get filtered records
        return df.join(
            freq_df.select(column),
            on=column,
            how="inner"
        )
    
    def sample_by_count(
        self,
        df: DataFrame,
        target_count: int,
        stratify_column: Optional[str] = None
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Sample DataFrame to achieve target count.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            target_count: Desired number of records
            stratify_column: Column for stratified sampling
            
        Returns:
            Sampled DataFrame
        """
        logger.info(f"Sampling to target count: {target_count}")
        
        total_count = df.count()
        
        if total_count <= target_count:
            return df
        
        if stratify_column:
            # Stratified sampling
            fractions = df.groupBy(stratify_column).agg(
                count("*").alias("count")
            ).withColumn(
                "fraction",
                lit(target_count) / lit(total_count)
            ).select(
                stratify_column,
                "fraction"
            ).rdd.collectAsMap()
            
            return df.sampleBy(stratify_column, fractions)
        else:
            # Simple random sampling
            fraction = target_count / total_count
            return df.sample(False, fraction)
    
    def cumulative_count_boundary(
        self,
        df: DataFrame,
        order_column: str,
        max_cumulative: int
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Filter based on cumulative count boundary.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            order_column: Column to order by
            max_cumulative: Maximum cumulative count
            
        Returns:
            Filtered DataFrame
        """
        logger.info(f"Applying cumulative count boundary: {max_cumulative}")
        
        window_spec = Window.orderBy(col(order_column)).rowsBetween(
            Window.unboundedPreceding, 
            Window.currentRow
        )
        
        return df.withColumn(
            "cumulative_count",
            row_number().over(window_spec)
        ).filter(
            col("cumulative_count") <= max_cumulative
        ).drop("cumulative_count")

            self.spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
            self.spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true")
        
        return df.groupBy(*group_columns).agg(agg_expressions)
    
    def monitor_memory_usage(self, df: DataFrame) -> dict:
        """

        """
        logger.info("Monitoring memory usage")
        
        # Get Spark context
        sc = self.spark.sparkContext
        
        # Collect memory metrics
        metrics = {
            "num_partitions": df.rdd.getNumPartitions(),
            "storage_level": str(df.storageLevel),
            "is_cached": df.is_cached if hasattr(df, 'is_cached') else False
        }
        
        # Get executor memory info from Spark UI metrics
        try:
            status = sc.statusTracker()
            executor_info = status.getExecutorInfos()
            metrics["num_executors"] = len(executor_info)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning(f"Could not retrieve executor info: {e}")
        
        return metrics

        return filter_func(df)
    
    def composite_boundary(
        self,
        df: DataFrame,
        boundaries: list,
        combine_mode: str = "AND"
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Apply multiple boundary conditions with AND/OR logic.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            boundaries: List of (column, operator, value) tuples
            combine_mode: "AND" or "OR" for combining conditions
            
        Returns:
            Filtered DataFrame
        """
        logger.info(f"Applying composite boundary with {combine_mode} logic")
        
        if not boundaries:
            return df
        
        # Build filter condition
        conditions = []
        for column, operator, value in boundaries:
            if operator == "==":
                conditions.append(col(column) == value)
            elif operator == ">":
                conditions.append(col(column) > value)
            elif operator == "<":
                conditions.append(col(column) < value)
            elif operator == ">=":
                conditions.append(col(column) >= value)
            elif operator == "<=":
                conditions.append(col(column) <= value)
            elif operator == "!=":
                conditions.append(col(column) != value)
            elif operator == "in":
                conditions.append(col(column).isin(value))
            elif operator == "between":
                conditions.append(col(column).between(value[0], value[1]))
        
        # Combine conditions
        if combine_mode.upper() == "AND":
            final_condition = conditions[0]
            for cond in conditions[1:]:
                final_condition = final_condition & cond
        else:  # OR
            final_condition = conditions[0]
            for cond in conditions[1:]:
                final_condition = final_condition | cond
        
        return df.filter(final_condition)
    
    def percentile_boundary(
        self,
        df: DataFrame,
        column: str,
        lower_percentile: float = 0.05,
        upper_percentile: float = 0.95
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Filter data based on percentile boundaries (outlier removal).
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column: Column to apply percentile filter
            lower_percentile: Lower percentile threshold
            upper_percentile: Upper percentile threshold
            
        Returns:
            Filtered DataFrame
        """
        logger.info(f"Applying percentile boundary: {lower_percentile} to {upper_percentile}")
        
        # Calculate percentiles
        percentiles = df.approxQuantile(
            column,
            [lower_percentile, upper_percentile],
            0.01
        )
        
        lower_bound = percentiles[0]
        upper_bound = percentiles[1]
        
        logger.info(f"Percentile bounds: [{lower_bound}, {upper_bound}]")
        
        return df.filter(
            (col(column) >= lower_bound) & 
            (col(column) <= upper_bound)
        )
    
    def adaptive_boundary(
        self,
        df: DataFrame,
        metric_column: str,
        threshold_func: Callable[[float], bool],
        fallback_limit: int = 1000
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Apply adaptive boundary based on data statistics.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            metric_column: Column to compute metrics on
            threshold_func: Function that takes a metric and returns boolean
            fallback_limit: Fallback row limit if threshold not met
            
        Returns:
            Filtered DataFrame
        """
        logger.info("Applying adaptive boundary")
        
        # Compute statistics
        stats = df.agg({
            metric_column: "avg",
            metric_column: "stddev"
        }).collect()[0]
        
        avg_value = stats[f"avg({metric_column})"]
        
        # Apply threshold function
        if threshold_func(avg_value):
            logger.info(f"Threshold met with avg={avg_value}")
            return df
        else:
            logger.info(f"Threshold not met, applying fallback limit: {fallback_limit}")
            return df.limit(fallback_limit)
    
    def business_rule_boundary(
        self,
        df: DataFrame,
        rules: dict
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Apply complex business rules as boundaries.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            rules: Dictionary of rule definitions
                   Example: {
                       'min_transaction_amount': 10,
                       'allowed_categories': ['A', 'B', 'C'],
                       'max_age_days': 30
                   }
            
        Returns:
            Filtered DataFrame
        """
        logger.info(f"Applying business rule boundary: {len(rules)} rules")
        
        result_df = df
        
        for rule_name, rule_value in rules.items():
            if rule_name.startswith('min_'):
                column = rule_name.replace('min_', '')
                result_df = result_df.filter(col(column) >= rule_value)
                
            elif rule_name.startswith('max_'):
                column = rule_name.replace('max_', '')
                result_df = result_df.filter(col(column) <= rule_value)
                
            elif rule_name.startswith('allowed_'):
                column = rule_name.replace('allowed_', '')
                result_df = result_df.filter(col(column).isin(rule_value))
                
            elif rule_name.startswith('excluded_'):
                column = rule_name.replace('excluded_', '')
                result_df = result_df.filter(~col(column).isin(rule_value))
        
        return result_df
    
    def dynamic_sampling_boundary(
        self,
        df: DataFrame,
        target_size: int,
        priority_column: Optional[str] = None,
        priority_weights: Optional[dict] = None
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Apply dynamic sampling based on priorities.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            target_size: Target number of records
            priority_column: Column containing priority values
            priority_weights: Dictionary mapping priority values to sampling weights
            
        Returns:
            Sampled DataFrame
        """
        logger.info(f"Applying dynamic sampling boundary: target={target_size}")
        
        total_count = df.count()
        
        if total_count <= target_size:
            return df
        
        if priority_column and priority_weights:
            # Weighted sampling based on priorities
            sampled_dfs = []
            
            for priority, weight in priority_weights.items():
                priority_df = df.filter(col(priority_column) == priority)
                priority_count = priority_df.count()
                
                # Calculate sample size for this priority
                sample_size = int(target_size * weight)
                
                if priority_count > 0:
                    fraction = min(1.0, sample_size / priority_count)
                    sampled = priority_df.sample(False, fraction)
                    sampled_dfs.append(sampled)
            
            # Union all sampled DataFrames
            if sampled_dfs:
                result = sampled_dfs[0]
                for sdf in sampled_dfs[1:]:
                    result = result.union(sdf)
                return result.limit(target_size)
        
        # Fallback to simple sampling
        fraction = target_size / total_count
        return df.sample(False, fraction).limit(target_size)

def create_sample_data(spark: SparkSession) -> DataFrame:
    """Create sample data for testing boundary patterns."""
    
    from datetime import datetime, timedelta
    import random
    
    # Generate sample data
    data = []
    base_time = datetime.now()
    
    for i in range(10000):
        data.append({
            'id': i,
            'timestamp': base_time - timedelta(hours=random.randint(0, 72)),
            'category': random.choice(['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E']),
            'value': random.uniform(10, 1000),
            'user_id': random.randint(1, 100),
            'transaction_amount': random.uniform(5, 500),
            'age_days': random.randint(1, 90),
            'priority': random.choice(['high', 'medium', 'low']),
            'status': random.choice(['active', 'pending', 'completed'])
        })
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField('id', IntegerType(), False),
        StructField('timestamp', TimestampType(), False),
        StructField('category', StringType(), False),
        StructField('value', DoubleType(), False),
        StructField('user_id', IntegerType(), False),
        StructField('transaction_amount', DoubleType(), False),
        StructField('age_days', IntegerType(), False),
        StructField('priority', StringType(), False),
        StructField('status', StringType(), False)
    ])
    
    return spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)

def save_boundary_results(
    df: DataFrame,
    output_path: str,
    format: str = "parquet",
    mode: str = "overwrite"
):
    """
    Save boundary-filtered results to storage.
    
    Args:
        df: DataFrame to save
        output_path: Output path
        format: Output format (parquet, csv, json, etc.)
        mode: Write mode (overwrite, append, etc.)
    """
    logger.info(f"Saving results to {output_path} in {format} format")
    
    df.write.mode(mode).format(format).save(output_path)


def create_boundary_report(
    original_df: DataFrame,
    filtered_df: DataFrame,
    boundary_type: str
) -> dict:
    """
    Create a report comparing original and filtered data.
    
    Args:
        original_df: Original DataFrame
        filtered_df: Filtered DataFrame
        boundary_type: Type of boundary applied
        
    Returns:
        Dictionary with comparison statistics
    """
    original_count = original_df.count()
    filtered_count = filtered_df.count()
    reduction_pct = ((original_count - filtered_count) / original_count * 100) \
        if original_count > 0 else 0
    
    report = {
        'boundary_type': boundary_type,
        'original_count': original_count,
        'filtered_count': filtered_count,
        'reduction_percentage': f"{reduction_pct:.2f}%",
        'records_removed': original_count - filtered_count,
        'original_partitions': original_df.rdd.getNumPartitions(),
        'filtered_partitions': filtered_df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
    }
    
    logger.info(f"Boundary Report ({boundary_type}):")
    for key, value in report.items():
        logger.info(f"  {key}: {value}")
    
    return report

        print(f"\n{'='*80}")
        print("PATTERN 1: COLUMN BATCH PATTERN")
        print(f"{'='*80}")
        print(f"Creating sample data: {num_rows} rows x {num_cols} columns")
        
        # Create schema dynamically
        schema = StructType([StructField(f"col_{i}", IntegerType(), True) 
                            for i in range(num_cols)])
        
        # Generate sample data
        data = []
        for i in range(num_rows):
            row = [i * j % 100 for j in range(num_cols)]
            data.append(tuple(row))
        
        df = spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        print(f"Created DataFrame with {df.count()} rows and {len(df.columns)} columns")
        return df
    
    def process_in_batches(self, df, operation='sum'):
        """
        Process columns in batches to optimize memory usage
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            operation: Operation to perform ('sum', 'avg', 'max', 'min')
        """
        print(f"\nProcessing columns in batches of {self.batch_size}")
        
        columns = df.columns
        num_batches = (len(columns) + self.batch_size - 1) // self.batch_size
        
        results = []
        
        for batch_idx in range(num_batches):
            start_idx = batch_idx * self.batch_size
            end_idx = min((batch_idx + 1) * self.batch_size, len(columns))
            batch_cols = columns[start_idx:end_idx]
            
            print(f"  Batch {batch_idx + 1}/{num_batches}: Processing columns {start_idx} to {end_idx-1}")
            
            # Select only current batch of columns
            batch_df = df.select(batch_cols)
            
            # Perform operation on batch
            if operation == 'sum':
                batch_result = batch_df.select(
                    [_sum(col(c)).alias(f"{c}_sum") for c in batch_cols]
                ).collect()[0].asDict()
            elif operation == 'avg':
                batch_result = batch_df.select(
                    [avg(col(c)).alias(f"{c}_avg") for c in batch_cols]
                ).collect()[0].asDict()
            
            results.append(batch_result)
        
        # Combine results from all batches
        combined_results = {}
        for batch_result in results:
            combined_results.update(batch_result)
        
        print(f"\nProcessed {len(combined_results)} column aggregations")
        print(f"Sample results: {list(combined_results.items())[:3]}")
        
        return combined_results
    
    def demonstrate(self):
        """Demonstrate Column Batch Pattern"""
        # Create sample data
        df = self.create_sample_data(num_rows=1000, num_cols=50)
        
        # Process in batches
        start_time = time.time()
        results = self.process_in_batches(df, operation='sum')
        elapsed_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        print(f"\nBatch processing completed in {elapsed_time:.2f} seconds")
        print(f"Memory efficiency: Processing {len(df.columns)} columns in batches of {self.batch_size}")

# PATTERN 2: Column Pruning Pattern (Refined)
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Eliminate unnecessary columns early in the processing pipeline
# Use Case: Optimize query performance by reading only required columns

class ColumnPruningPattern:
    """
    Column Pruning Pattern: Intelligently select and prune columns to minimize
    data transfer and processing overhead.
    """
    
    def create_sample_data(self):
        """Create sample e-commerce dataset"""
        print(f"\n{'='*80}")
        print("PATTERN 2: COLUMN PRUNING PATTERN (REFINED)")
        print(f"{'='*80}")
        
        data = [
            (1, "John Doe", "john@email.com", "123 Main St", "New York", "NY", 
             "10001", "USA", "2024-01-15", 150.50, "Electronics", "Laptop", 
             "Premium", "Credit Card", "Shipped", "2024-01-16", "TRACK123", 
             "Standard", "John", "Doe"),
            (2, "Jane Smith", "jane@email.com", "456 Oak Ave", "Los Angeles", "CA",
             "90001", "USA", "2024-01-16", 75.25, "Books", "Python Guide",
             "Standard", "PayPal", "Processing", None, None,
             "Express", "Jane", "Smith"),
            (3, "Bob Johnson", "bob@email.com", "789 Pine Rd", "Chicago", "IL",
             "60601", "USA", "2024-01-17", 200.00, "Electronics", "Tablet",
             "Premium", "Credit Card", "Delivered", "2024-01-18", "TRACK456",
             "Express", "Bob", "Johnson"),
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("order_id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("customer_name", StringType(), True),
            StructField("email", StringType(), True),
            StructField("address", StringType(), True),
            StructField("city", StringType(), True),
            StructField("state", StringType(), True),
            StructField("zip", StringType(), True),
            StructField("country", StringType(), True),
            StructField("order_date", StringType(), True),
            StructField("amount", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("category", StringType(), True),
            StructField("product_name", StringType(), True),
            StructField("membership", StringType(), True),
            StructField("payment_method", StringType(), True),
            StructField("status", StringType(), True),
            StructField("ship_date", StringType(), True),
            StructField("tracking_number", StringType(), True),
            StructField("shipping_speed", StringType(), True),
            StructField("first_name", StringType(), True),
            StructField("last_name", StringType(), True),
        ])
        
        df = spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        print(f"Created sample dataset with {len(df.columns)} columns")
        df.printSchema()
        return df
    
    def analyze_column_usage(self, df, required_columns: List[str]):
        """
        Analyze and prune columns based on requirements
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            required_columns: List of columns actually needed
        """
        all_columns = df.columns
        pruned_columns = [col for col in all_columns if col not in required_columns]
        
        print(f"\nColumn Analysis:")
        print(f"  Total columns: {len(all_columns)}")
        print(f"  Required columns: {len(required_columns)}")
        print(f"  Pruned columns: {len(pruned_columns)}")
        print(f"  Reduction: {(len(pruned_columns)/len(all_columns)*100):.1f}%")
        print(f"\nPruned columns: {pruned_columns[:10]}{'...' if len(pruned_columns) > 10 else ''}")
        
        return pruned_columns
    
    def early_pruning_example(self, df):
        """Demonstrate early column pruning in query pipeline"""
        print("\n--- Example 1: Early Pruning for Sales Report ---")
        
        # Define only columns needed for sales report
        required_cols = ["order_id", "order_date", "amount", "category", "status"]
        
        # Prune early in the pipeline
        pruned_df = df.select(required_cols)
        
        # Perform analysis on pruned dataset
        result = pruned_df.filter(col("status") == "Shipped") \
            .groupBy("category") \
            .agg(
                _sum("amount").alias("total_sales"),
                count("order_id").alias("order_count"),
                avg("amount").alias("avg_order_value")
            )
        
        print("\nSales Report (with early pruning):")
        result.show()
        
        return result
    
    def lazy_pruning_example(self, df):
        """Demonstrate lazy column pruning (anti-pattern)"""
        print("\n--- Example 2: Lazy Pruning (Anti-pattern) ---")
        
        # Process full dataset first (inefficient)
        temp_df = df.filter(col("status") == "Shipped")
        
        # Prune columns late in pipeline
        result = temp_df.select("order_id", "order_date", "amount", "category") \
            .groupBy("category") \
            .agg(_sum("amount").alias("total_sales"))
        
        print("Note: This approach processes all columns before pruning (inefficient)")
        
        return result
    
    def nested_column_pruning(self, df):
        """Demonstrate pruning with nested structures"""
        print("\n--- Example 3: Nested Column Pruning ---")
        
        # Create nested structure
        nested_df = df.select(
            col("order_id"),
            struct(
                col("customer_name"),
                col("email"),
                col("address"),
                col("city"),
                col("state"),
                col("zip")
            ).alias("customer_info"),
            struct(
                col("amount"),
                col("payment_method"),
                col("status")
            ).alias("payment_info")
        )
        
        # Prune nested fields - select only specific nested columns
        pruned_nested = nested_df.select(
            col("order_id"),
            col("customer_info.customer_name"),
            col("customer_info.email"),
            col("payment_info.amount")
        )
        
        print("\nNested structure with selective field access:")
        pruned_nested.show(truncate=False)
        
        return pruned_nested
    
    def demonstrate(self):
        """Demonstrate Column Pruning Pattern"""
        df = self.create_sample_data()
        
        # Analyze column usage
        required_cols = ["order_id", "order_date", "amount", "category", "status"]
        self.analyze_column_usage(df, required_cols)
        
        # Examples
        self.early_pruning_example(df)
        self.lazy_pruning_example(df)
        self.nested_column_pruning(df)

# PATTERN 3: Column Projection Pattern
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Transform and project columns efficiently
# Use Case: Create derived columns and projections with minimal overhead

class ColumnProjectionPattern:
    """
    Column Projection Pattern: Efficiently create derived columns and 
    transformations while maintaining columnar storage benefits.
    """
    
    def create_sample_data(self):
        """Create sample financial dataset"""
        print(f"\n{'='*80}")
        print("PATTERN 3: COLUMN PROJECTION PATTERN")
        print(f"{'='*80}")
        
        data = [
            (1, "2024-01-15", 1000.00, 50.00, 25.00, 100.00, "Electronics", "Q1"),
            (2, "2024-02-20", 1500.00, 75.00, 30.00, 150.00, "Books", "Q1"),
            (3, "2024-03-10", 2000.00, 100.00, 40.00, 200.00, "Electronics", "Q1"),
            (4, "2024-04-05", 1200.00, 60.00, 28.00, 120.00, "Clothing", "Q2"),
            (5, "2024-05-15", 1800.00, 90.00, 35.00, 180.00, "Electronics", "Q2"),
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("transaction_id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("date", StringType(), True),
            StructField("revenue", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("cost", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("tax", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("shipping", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("category", StringType(), True),
            StructField("quarter", StringType(), True),
        ])
        
        df = spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        print("Created financial dataset")
        df.show()
        return df
    
    def simple_projection(self, df):
        """Simple column projections and derivations"""
        print("\n--- Example 1: Simple Projections ---")
        
        # Create multiple derived columns efficiently
        projected_df = df.select(
            col("transaction_id"),
            col("date"),
            col("revenue"),
            col("cost"),
            # Derived columns
            (col("revenue") - col("cost")).alias("gross_profit"),
            ((col("revenue") - col("cost")) / col("revenue") * 100).alias("profit_margin_pct"),
            (col("revenue") + col("tax") + col("shipping")).alias("total_amount"),
            col("category")
        )
        
        print("\nProjected DataFrame with derived columns:")
        projected_df.
```python
show()
        
        return projected_df
    
    def complex_projection(self, df):
        """Complex projections with conditional logic"""
        print("\n--- Example 2: Complex Projections with Conditionals ---")
        
        # Multiple complex derivations in single projection
        complex_df = df.select(
            col("transaction_id"),
            col("category"),
            col("revenue"),
            col("cost"),
            # Conditional projections
            when(col("revenue") > 1500, "High")
                .when(col("revenue") > 1000, "Medium")
                .otherwise("Low").alias("revenue_tier"),
            # Multiple calculations
            (col("revenue") - col("cost") - col("tax") - col("shipping")).alias("net_profit"),
            ((col("revenue") - col("cost")) / col("revenue") * 100).alias("margin_pct"),
            # Category-based calculations
            when(col("category") == "Electronics", col("revenue") * 0.15)
                .when(col("category") == "Books", col("revenue") * 0.10)
                .otherwise(col("revenue") * 0.12).alias("commission"),
            # Status flags
            (col("revenue") > col("cost") * 2).alias("high_margin_flag"),
            col("quarter")
        )
        
        print("\nComplex projections with conditional logic:")
        complex_df.show()
        
        return complex_df
    
    def chained_projection(self, df):
        """Demonstrate efficient chained projections"""
        print("\n--- Example 3: Chained Projections ---")
        
        # Stage 1: Basic calculations
        stage1 = df.select(
            col("transaction_id"),
            col("revenue"),
            col("cost"),
            col("tax"),
            col("shipping"),
            (col("revenue") - col("cost")).alias("gross_profit"),
            col("category"),
            col("quarter")
        )
        
        # Stage 2: Build on previous projections
        stage2 = stage1.select(
            col("transaction_id"),
            col("category"),
            col("quarter"),
            col("revenue"),
            col("gross_profit"),
            (col("gross_profit") / col("revenue") * 100).alias("margin_pct"),
            (col("gross_profit") - col("tax") - col("shipping")).alias("net_profit")
        )
        
        # Stage 3: Final aggregation projections
        stage3 = stage2.select(
            col("transaction_id"),
            col("category"),
            col("revenue"),
            col("net_profit"),
            col("margin_pct"),
            when(col("net_profit") > 0, "Profitable")
                .otherwise("Loss").alias("status"),
            (col("net_profit") / col("revenue") * 100).alias("net_margin_pct")
        )
        
        print("\nChained projections result:")
        stage3.show()
        
        return stage3
    
    def array_projection(self, df):
        """Project columns into array structures"""
        print("\n--- Example 4: Array Projections ---")
        
        # Project multiple columns into arrays
        array_df = df.select(
            col("transaction_id"),
            col("category"),
            # Create array of financial metrics
            array(
                col("revenue"),
                col("cost"),
                col("tax"),
                col("shipping")
            ).alias("financial_metrics"),
            # Create struct projection
            struct(
                col("revenue"),
                col("cost"),
                (col("revenue") - col("cost")).alias("profit")
            ).alias("summary")
        )
        
        print("\nArray and struct projections:")
        array_df.show(truncate=False)
        
        # Access nested projections
        expanded = array_df.select(
            col("transaction_id"),
            col("category"),
            col("financial_metrics")[0].alias("revenue"),
            col("financial_metrics")[1].alias("cost"),
            col("summary.profit")
        )
        
        print("\nExpanded nested projections:")
        expanded.show()
        
        return array_df
    
    def demonstrate(self):
        """Demonstrate Column Projection Pattern"""
        df = self.create_sample_data()
        
        # Run examples
        self.simple_projection(df)
        self.complex_projection(df)
        self.chained_projection(df)
        self.array_projection(df)
