def print_pattern_documentation():
    """Print comprehensive pattern documentation."""
    
    documentation = """
================================================================================
PYSPARK CLUSTER RESOURCE MANAGEMENT PATTERNS - DOCUMENTATION
================================================================================

1. STATIC ALLOCATION PATTERN
   Description: Pre-allocate fixed resources for predictable workloads
   
   Use Cases:
   - Regular batch ETL jobs with known data volumes
   - Scheduled reports with consistent resource needs
   - Production jobs requiring guaranteed resources
   
   Configuration:
   - spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled = false
   - spark.executor.instances = <fixed number>
   - spark.executor.cores = <cores per executor>
   - spark.executor.memory = <memory per executor>
   
   Pros:
   - Predictable performance
   - No scaling overhead
   - Simple to configure and monitor
   
   Cons:
   - Inefficient for variable workloads
   - Resources may be underutilized
   - No automatic adaptation to load changes

================================================================================

2. DYNAMIC ALLOCATION PATTERN
   Description: Automatically scale executors based on workload demand
   
   Use Cases:
   - Interactive analytics with variable query patterns
   - Development and testing environments
   - Jobs with unpredictable resource requirements
   
   Configuration:
   - spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled = true
   - spark.dynamicAllocation.minExecutors = <minimum>
   - spark.dynamicAllocation.maxExecutors = <maximum>
   - spark.shuffle.service.enabled = true
   
   Pros:
   - Efficient resource utilization
   - Automatic adaptation to workload
   - Cost-effective for variable loads
   
   Cons:
   - Scaling latency
   - Requires shuffle service
   - More complex to tune

================================================================================

3. ELASTIC SCALING PATTERN
   Description: Advanced scaling with custom metrics and policies
   
   Use Cases:
   - Complex workloads requiring fine-grained control
   - Applications with custom scaling logic
   - Integration with external monitoring systems
   
   Configuration:
   - Custom metrics collection
   - Programmatic scaling decisions
   - Integration with cluster autoscaling
   
   Pros:
   - Maximum flexibility
   - Custom optimization strategies
   - Integration with business metrics
   
   Cons:
   - Complex implementation
   - Requires monitoring infrastructure
   - Higher maintenance overhead

================================================================================

4. RESOURCE NEGOTIATION PATTERN
   Description: Negotiate resources with cluster manager for fair sharing
   
   Use Cases:
   - Shared clusters with multiple applications
   - Priority-based resource allocation
   - Multi-application environments
   
   Configuration:
   - spark.scheduler.mode = FAIR
   - Resource profiles per application type
   - Priority-based scheduling
   
   Pros:
   - Fair resource distribution
   - Support for priorities
   - Flexible resource sharing
   
   Cons:
   - Potential resource contention
   - Complex scheduling policies
   - Requires coordination

================================================================================

5. RESOURCE PREEMPTION PATTERN
   Description: Allow high-priority jobs to preempt lower-priority tasks
   
   Use Cases:
   - SLA-critical workloads
   - Production vs. development separation
   - Emergency job execution
   
   Configuration:
   - spark.speculation = true
   - Fair scheduler with preemption
   - Task failure tolerance settings
   
   Pros:
   - Guaranteed resources for critical jobs
   - SLA compliance
   - Priority enforcement
   
   Cons:
   - Wasted work from preempted tasks
   - Complexity in failure handling
   - Potential instability

================================================================================

6. RESOURCE ISOLATION PATTERN
   Description: Isolate resources between different workloads
   
   Use Cases:
   - Multi-tenant environments
   - Workload isolation requirements
   - Performance guarantees
   
   Configuration:
   - Separate scheduler pools
   - Memory fraction settings
   - Resource quotas per namespace
   
   Pros:
   - Strong isolation guarantees
   - Predictable performance
   - No interference between workloads
   
   Cons:
   - Potential resource fragmentation
   - Complex configuration
   - May underutilize resources

================================================================================

7. MULTI-TENANT RESOURCE PATTERN
   Description: Comprehensive multi-tenancy with quotas and SLAs
   
   Use Cases:
   - Enterprise data platforms
   - Multiple teams sharing infrastructure
   - Chargeback and cost allocation
   
   Configuration:
   - Per-tenant quotas and limits
   - SLA tracking and enforcement
   - Usage monitoring and reporting
   
   Pros:
   - Complete tenant isolation
   - Resource accountability
   - SLA compliance tracking
   
   Cons:
   - High complexity
   - Significant overhead
   - Requires extensive monitoring

================================================================================

CHOOSING THE RIGHT PATTERN:

Small Team, Predictable Workload:
→ Static Allocation Pattern

Variable Interactive Workloads:
→ Dynamic Allocation Pattern

Complex Requirements, Custom Logic:
→ Elastic Scaling Pattern

Shared Cluster, Multiple Apps:
→ Resource Negotiation Pattern

Critical SLA Requirements:
→ Resource Preemption Pattern

Strong Isolation Needed:
→ Resource Isolation Pattern

Enterprise Multi-Team Platform:
→ Multi-Tenant Resource Pattern

================================================================================

PERFORMANCE TUNING TIPS:

1. Executor Sizing:
   - Cores: 4-8 cores per executor (optimal for most workloads)
   - Memory: 8-16 GB per executor (balance between parallelism and overhead)
   - Rule of thumb: executor_memory = (total_data_size / num_executors) * 2-3

2. Partition Sizing:
   - Target: 128-256 MB per partition
   - Formula: num_partitions = total_cores * 2-3
   - Adjust based on operation type (joins need more)

3. Dynamic Allocation Tuning:
   - Set min to handle baseline load
   - Set max to prevent resource exhaustion
   - Tune idle timeout based on job patterns

4. Memory Management:
   - spark.memory.fraction = 0.6 (default, adjust if needed)
   - spark.memory.storageFraction = 0.5 (balance storage vs execution)
   - Enable off-heap memory for large datasets

5. Monitoring:
   - Track executor utilization
   - Monitor GC time (should be < 10% of task time)
   - Watch for data skew
   - Monitor shuffle read/write metrics

================================================================================
"""
    
    print(documentation)


def print_troubleshooting_guide():
    """Print troubleshooting guide for common issues."""
    
    guide = """
================================================================================
TROUBLESHOOTING GUIDE
================================================================================

ISSUE: Executors not scaling up (Dynamic Allocation)
SOLUTIONS:
- Verify shuffle service is enabled and running
- Check schedulerBacklogTimeout setting
- Ensure maxExecutors hasn't been reached
- Review cluster resource availability
- Check for quota limits

ISSUE: Out of Memory errors
SOLUTIONS:
- Increase executor memory
- Reduce executor cores (more memory per core)
- Increase number of partitions
- Enable off-heap memory
- Tune memory fractions
- Check for data skew

ISSUE: Poor performance with fair scheduler
SOLUTIONS:
- Review pool weights and priorities
- Check for resource contention
- Adjust minShare settings
- Monitor pool utilization
- Consider separate pools for different workload types

ISSUE: Tasks getting preempted frequently
SOLUTIONS:
- Review priority settings
- Adjust speculation settings
- Increase task failure tolerance
- Check for resource over-subscription
- Balance priorities across applications

ISSUE: Resource isolation not working
SOLUTIONS:
- Verify pool configuration
- Check memory fraction settings
- Ensure proper namespace usage
- Review scheduler mode
- Validate allocation file

ISSUE: Quota exceeded errors (Multi-tenant)
SOLUTIONS:
- Review tenant quotas
- Optimize job resource usage
- Request quota increase
- Implement job prioritization
- Schedule jobs during off-peak hours

ISSUE: High GC overhead
SOLUTIONS:
- Increase executor memory
- Reduce executor cores
- Tune GC settings
- Reduce caching
- Increase parallelism

ISSUE: Slow job startup
SOLUTIONS:
- Reduce initial executors (dynamic allocation)
- Use static allocation for fast startup
- Pre-warm executor pool
- Optimize application dependencies
- Check cluster scheduler latency

================================================================================
"""
    
    print(guide)

def comprehensive_example():
    """Comprehensive example using multiple patterns together."""
    
    logger.info("\n" + "=" * 80)
    logger.info("COMPREHENSIVE INTEGRATION EXAMPLE")
    logger.info("Demonstrating pattern combination and optimization")
    logger.info("=" * 80 + "\n")
    
    # Phase 1: Use optimizer to calculate requirements
    logger.info("=== Phase 1: Resource Planning ===")
    optimizer = ResourceOptimizer()
    
    data_size = 500  # GB
    optimal_executors = optimizer.calculate_optimal_executors(data_size)
    optimal_partitions = optimizer.calculate_optimal_partitions(
        data_size, 
        executor_cores=4,
        num_executors=optimal_executors
    )
    memory_est = optimizer.estimate_memory_requirements(data_size, "aggregation")
    
    logger.info(f"Data size: {data_size} GB")
    logger.info(f"Recommended executors: {optimal_executors}")
    logger.info(f"Recommended partitions: {optimal_partitions}")
    logger.info(f"Memory requirements: {memory_est}")
    
    # Phase 2: Cost estimation
    logger.info("\n=== Phase 2: Cost Estimation ===")
    cost_estimator = ResourceCostEstimator()
    costs = cost_estimator.compare_pattern_costs(data_size, runtime_hours=2.0)
    
    # Phase 3: Create optimized session
    logger.info("\n=== Phase 3: Creating Optimized Session ===")
    spark = DynamicAllocationPattern.create_spark_session(
        app_name="ComprehensiveExample",
        min_executors=max(2, optimal_executors // 2),
        max_executors=optimal_executors * 2,
        initial_executors=optimal_executors
    )
    
    try:
        # Phase 4: Health monitoring
        logger.info("\n=== Phase 4: Health Monitoring ===")
        health_checker = ResourceHealthChecker(spark)
        
        # Phase 5: Execute workload with monitoring
        logger.info("\n=== Phase 5: Executing Workload ===")
        
        for iteration in range(3):
            logger.info(f"\nIteration {iteration + 1}")
            
            # Check health before execution
            health = health_checker.check_health()
            logger.info(f"Health status: {health['status']} - {health['message']}")
            
            # Execute workload
            df = spark.range(1000000 * (iteration + 1))
            result = df.repartition(optimal_partitions) \
                       .selectExpr("id", "id % 1000 as bucket") \
                       .groupBy("bucket").count()
            count = result.count()
            
            logger.info(f"Processed {count} buckets")
            time.sleep(2)
        
        # Phase 6: Final health report
        logger.info("\n=== Phase 6: Final Health Report ===")
        health_report = health_checker.generate_health_report()
        logger.info(health_report)
        
        # Phase 7: Validation
        logger.info("\n=== Phase 7: Configuration Validation ===")
        validator = ResourcePatternValidator()
        validator.validate_dynamic_allocation(spark)
        
    finally:
        spark.stop()
    
    logger.info("\n=== Comprehensive Example Completed ===\n")

```python
ySpark Cluster Resource Management Patterns",

Examples:

        logger.info(f"  Executor Memory: {memory['executor_memory_gb']} GB")

    if args.estimate_cost:

        logger.info(f"\n=== Cost Estimation for {data_size} GB, {runtime} hours ===\n")

        logger.info("\nDetailed Cost Breakdown:")
        for pattern, cost_data in costs.items():

            for key, value in cost_data.items():
                logger.info(f"  {key}: ${value}")
    
    # Run validation
    if args.validate:

            scenario_batch_etl()

        elif args.pattern == "negotiation":

        elif args.pattern == "preemption":
            ResourcePreemptionPattern.run_example()
        elif args.pattern == "isolation":
            ResourceIsolationPattern.run_example()

    # Run benchmarks

        logger.info("RUNNING PERFORMANCE BENCHMARKS")
        logger.info("=" * 80 + "\n")

        # Define standard workload

            df = spark.range(1000000)
            result = df.selectExpr("id", "id % 100 as bucket") \
                       .groupBy("bucket").count()
            return result.count()

        comparison.benchmark_pattern(

        # Benchmark Dynamic Allocation

        )
        
        # Print comparison results

    # If no arguments provided, show help

def generate_sample_fairscheduler_xml():
    """Generate sample fair scheduler XML file."""
    
    xml_content = """<?xml version="1.0"?>
<allocations>
  <!-- Production Pool: High priority, guaranteed resources -->
  <pool name="production">
    <schedulingMode>FAIR</schedulingMode>
    <weight>3</weight>
    <minShare>10</minShare>
  </pool>
  
  <!-- Development Pool: Medium priority -->
  <pool name="development">
    <schedulingMode>FAIR</schedulingMode>
    <weight>2</weight>
    <minShare>5</minShare>
  </pool>
  
  <!-- Ad-hoc Pool: Low priority, FIFO within pool -->
  <pool name="adhoc">
    <schedulingMode>FIFO</schedulingMode>
    <weight>1</weight>
    <minShare>2</minShare>
  </pool>
  
  <!-- Critical Pool: Highest priority for SLA-critical jobs -->
  <pool name="critical">
    <schedulingMode>FAIR</schedulingMode>
    <weight>5</weight>
    <minShare>15</minShare>
  </pool>
  
  <!-- Multi-tenant pools -->
  <pool name="pool_premium_analytics">
    <schedulingMode>FAIR</schedulingMode>
    <weight>4</weight>
    <minShare>8</minShare>
  </pool>
  
  <pool name="pool_standard_ml">
    <schedulingMode>FAIR</schedulingMode>
    <weight>2</weight>
    <minShare>4</minShare>
  </pool>
  
  <pool name="pool_basic_batch">
    <schedulingMode>FIFO</schedulingMode>
    <weight>1</weight>
    <minShare>2</minShare>
  </pool>
  
  <!-- Isolated namespace pools -->
  <pool name="isolated_tenant1_analytics">
    <schedulingMode>FAIR</schedulingMode>
    <weight>2</weight>
    <minShare>5</minShare>
  </pool>
  
  <pool name="isolated_tenant2_ml">
    <schedulingMode>FAIR</schedulingMode>
    <weight>2</weight>
    <minShare>3</minShare>
  </pool>
  
  <pool name="isolated_tenant3_streaming">
    <schedulingMode>FAIR</schedulingMode>
    <weight>1</weight>
    <minShare>2</minShare>
  </pool>
  
  <!-- Default pool for unspecified jobs -->
  <pool name="default">
    <schedulingMode>FIFO</schedulingMode>
    <weight>1</weight>
    <minShare>0</minShare>
  </pool>
</allocations>
"""
    
    # Write to file
    with open("fairscheduler.xml", "w") as f:
        f.write(xml_content)
    
    logger.info("Generated fairscheduler.xml configuration file")
    logger.info("Place this file in a location accessible to Spark")
    logger.info("Set: spark.scheduler.allocation.file=/path/to/fairscheduler.xml")

This comprehensive PySpark program implements **7 Cluster Resource Management Patterns**:

1. **Static Allocation Pattern** - Fixed resources for predictable workloads
2. **Dynamic Allocation Pattern** - Auto-scaling based on demand
3. **Elastic Scaling Pattern** - Custom metrics-based scaling
4. **Resource Negotiation Pattern** - Fair sharing across applications
5. **Resource Preemption Pattern** - Priority-based resource allocation
6. **Resource Isolation Pattern** - Workload isolation in multi-tenant environments

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from pyspark.sql.types import *
from delta import *
import os

# Initialize Spark Session with Delta Lake support
def create_spark_session():
    """
    Create SparkSession with Delta Lake configurations
    """
    builder = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("Data Mutation Patterns") \
        .config("spark.sql.extensions", "io.delta.sql.DeltaSparkSessionExtension") \
        .config("spark.sql.catalog.spark_catalog", "org.apache.spark.sql.delta.catalog.DeltaCatalog") \
        .config("spark.sql.warehouse.dir", "/tmp/spark-warehouse") \
        .master("local[*]")
    
    spark = configure_spark_with_delta_pip(builder).getOrCreate()
    spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")
    return spark

spark = create_spark_session()

## 1. Insert Pattern

```python
"""
INSERT PATTERN
Purpose: Add new records to a table
Use Cases: 
- Loading initial data
- Appending new transactions
- Batch data ingestion
"""

def insert_pattern_demo():
    print("=" * 80)
    print("1. INSERT PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Define schema
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("customer_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("name", StringType(), True),
        StructField("email", StringType(), True),
        StructField("signup_date", DateType(), True),
        StructField("status", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    # Create initial dataset
    initial_data = [
        (1, "John Doe", "john@email.com", "2024-01-15", "active"),
        (2, "Jane Smith", "jane@email.com", "2024-01-16", "active"),
        (3, "Bob Johnson", "bob@email.com", "2024-01-17", "active")
    ]
    
    df_initial = spark.createDataFrame(initial_data, schema)
    
    # Write to Delta table
    delta_path = "/tmp/delta/customers_insert"
    df_initial.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(delta_path)
    
    print("\nInitial Data:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).show()
    
    # METHOD 1: Insert using DataFrame API
    new_customers = [
        (4, "Alice Williams", "alice@email.com", "2024-01-18", "active"),
        (5, "Charlie Brown", "charlie@email.com", "2024-01-19", "active")
    ]
    
    df_new = spark.createDataFrame(new_customers, schema)
    df_new.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(delta_path)
    
    print("\nAfter Insert (DataFrame API):")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).orderBy("customer_id").show()
    
    # METHOD 2: Insert using SQL
    df_read = spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path)
    df_read.createOrReplaceTempView("customers")
    
    spark.sql("""
        INSERT INTO customers
        VALUES (6, 'David Lee', 'david@email.com', '2024-01-20', 'active')
    """)
    
    print("\nAfter Insert (SQL):")
    spark.sql("SELECT * FROM customers ORDER BY customer_id").show()
    
    # METHOD 3: Bulk Insert with validation
    bulk_data = [
        (7, "Eva Martinez", "eva@email.com", "2024-01-21", "active"),
        (8, "Frank Wilson", "frank@email.com", "2024-01-22", "pending"),
        (9, "Grace Taylor", "grace@email.com", "2024-01-23", "active")
    ]
    
    df_bulk = spark.createDataFrame(bulk_data, schema)
    
    # Validate before insert
    df_validated = df_bulk.filter(col("email").isNotNull() & col("email").contains("@"))
    
    df_validated.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(delta_path)
    
    print("\nAfter Bulk Insert with Validation:")
    spark.sql("SELECT * FROM customers ORDER BY customer_id").show()
    
    # Show record count
    count = spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).count()
    print(f"\nTotal Records: {count}")

insert_pattern_demo()
```

## 2. Update Pattern (Refined)

```python
"""
UPDATE PATTERN
Purpose: Modify existing records based on conditions
Use Cases:
- Correcting data errors
- Status updates
- Data enrichment
- Conditional modifications
"""

def update_pattern_demo():
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("2. UPDATE PATTERN (REFINED)")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Setup test data
    delta_path = "/tmp/delta/customers_update"
    
    data = [
        (1, "John Doe", "john@email.com", "2024-01-15", "active", 100.0),
        (2, "Jane Smith", "jane@email.com", "2024-01-16", "active", 200.0),
        (3, "Bob Johnson", "bob@email.com", "2024-01-17", "pending", 150.0),
        (4, "Alice Williams", "alice@email.com", "2024-01-18", "inactive", 50.0),
        (5, "Charlie Brown", "charlie@email.com", "2024-01-19", "active", 300.0)
    ]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("customer_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("name", StringType(), True),
        StructField("email", StringType(), True),
        StructField("signup_date", StringType(), True),
        StructField("status", StringType(), True),
        StructField("balance", DoubleType(), True)
    ])
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
    df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(delta_path)
    
    print("\nInitial Data:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).show()
    
    # METHOD 1: Update using Delta Lake API
    from delta.tables import DeltaTable
    
    delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(spark, delta_path)
    
    # Simple update - change status
    delta_table.update(
        condition = "status = 'pending'",
        set = {"status": lit("active")}
    )
    
    print("\nAfter Simple Update (pending -> active):")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).show()
    
    # METHOD 2: Conditional update with multiple columns
    delta_table.update(
        condition = "balance < 100",
        set = {
            "status": lit("inactive"),
            "balance": col("balance") * 0.5  # Apply 50% reduction
        }
    )
    
    print("\nAfter Conditional Update (balance < 100):")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).show()
    
    # METHOD 3: Complex update with expressions
    delta_table.update(
        condition = expr("status = 'active' AND balance > 200"),
        set = {
            "balance": expr("balance * 1.1"),  # 10% bonus
            "status": lit("premium")
        }
    )
    
    print("\nAfter Complex Update (active customers with balance > 200):")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).show()
    
    # METHOD 4: Update with timestamp tracking
    delta_table.update(
        condition = "status = 'inactive'",
        set = {
            "status": lit("reactivated"),
            "signup_date": expr("current_date()")
        }
    )
    
    print("\nAfter Update with Timestamp:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).show()
    
    # METHOD 5: SQL-based update
    delta_table.toDF().createOrReplaceTempView("customers_update")
    
    spark.sql("""
        UPDATE customers_update
        SET balance = balance + 50
        WHERE customer_id IN (1, 2, 3)
    """)
    
    print("\nAfter SQL Update (bonus for customers 1,2,3):")
    spark.sql("SELECT * FROM customers_update ORDER BY customer_id").show()

update_pattern_demo()
```

```python
"""
DELETE PATTERN
Purpose: Remove records from table based on conditions
Use Cases:
- Data cleanup
- GDPR compliance (right to be forgotten)
- Archival processes
- Data retention policies
"""

def delete_pattern_demo():
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("3. DELETE PATTERN (REFINED)")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Setup test data
    delta_path = "/tmp/delta/customers_delete"
    
    data = [
        (1, "John Doe", "john@email.com", "2022-01-15", "active", True),
        (2, "Jane Smith", "jane@email.com", "2023-01-16", "active", True),
        (3, "Bob Johnson", "bob@email.com", "2024-01-17", "inactive", False),
        (4, "Alice Williams", "alice@email.com", "2021-01-18", "deleted", False),
        (5, "Charlie Brown", "charlie@email.com", "2024-01-19", "active", True),
        (6, "David Lee", "david@email.com", "2020-01-20", "inactive", False),
        (7, "Eva Martinez", "eva@email.com", "2024-01-21", "active", True)
    ]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("customer_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("name", StringType(), True),
        StructField("email", StringType(), True),
        StructField("signup_date", StringType(), True),
        StructField("status", StringType(), True),
        StructField("is_active", BooleanType(), True)
    ])
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
    df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(delta_path)
    
    print("\nInitial Data:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).show()
    
    from delta.tables import DeltaTable
    delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(spark, delta_path)
    
    # METHOD 1: Simple delete by condition
    delta_table.delete("status = 'deleted'")
    
    print("\nAfter Simple Delete (status = 'deleted'):")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).show()
    
    # METHOD 2: Delete with date-based condition
    delta_table.delete("signup_date < '2022-01-01'")
    
    print("\nAfter Date-based Delete (signup before 2022):")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).show()
    
    # METHOD 3: Delete with complex condition
    delta_table.delete("status = 'inactive' AND is_active = false")
    
    print("\nAfter Complex Delete (inactive and not active):")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).show()
    
    # METHOD 4: SQL-based delete
    delta_table.toDF().createOrReplaceTempView("customers_delete")
    
    spark.sql("""
        DELETE FROM customers_delete
        WHERE customer_id = 1
    """)
    
    print("\nAfter SQL Delete (customer_id = 1):")
    spark.sql("SELECT * FROM customers_delete ORDER BY customer_id").show()
    
    # METHOD 5: Soft delete pattern (mark as deleted instead of removing)
    # Recreate table for soft delete demo
    df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(delta_path)
    delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(spark, delta_path)
    
    # Instead of deleting, update status
    delta_table.update(
        condition = "customer_id IN (3, 4)",
        set = {
            "status": lit("soft_deleted"),
            "is_active": lit(False)
        }
    )
    
    print("\nAfter Soft Delete Pattern:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).show()
    
    # Show only active records
    print("\nActive Records Only (excluding soft deleted):")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path) \
        .filter("status != 'soft_deleted'") \
        .show()

delete_pattern_demo()

## 4. Upsert Pattern

```python
"""
UPSERT PATTERN (Update + Insert)
Purpose: Insert new records or update existing ones
Use Cases:
- CDC (Change Data Capture) processing
- Incremental data loads
- Synchronizing data from external sources
- Maintaining current state
"""

def upsert_pattern_demo():
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("4. UPSERT PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Setup target table
    delta_path = "/tmp/delta/customers_upsert"
    
    target_data = [
        (1, "John Doe", "john@email.com", 100.0, "2024-01-15"),
        (2, "Jane Smith", "jane@email.com", 200.0, "2024-01-16"),
        (3, "Bob Johnson", "bob@email.com", 150.0, "2024-01-17")
    ]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("customer_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("name", StringType(), True),
        StructField("email", StringType(), True),
        StructField("balance", DoubleType(), True),
        StructField("last_updated", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    df_target = spark.createDataFrame(target_data, schema)
    df_target.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(delta_path)
    
    print("\nTarget Table (Before Upsert):")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).show()
    
    # Source data with updates and new records
    source_data = [
        (2, "Jane Smith-Updated", "jane.new@email.com", 250.0, "2024-01-20"),  # Update
        (3, "Bob Johnson", "bob.new@email.com", 175.0, "2024-01-20"),          # Update
        (4, "Alice Williams", "alice@email.com", 300.0, "2024-01-20"),         # Insert
        (5, "Charlie Brown", "charlie@email.com", 125.0, "2024-01-20")         # Insert
    ]
    
    df_source = spark.createDataFrame(source_data, schema)
    
    print("\nSource Data (Updates + New Records):")
    df_source.show()
    
    # METHOD 1: Basic
```python
    # METHOD 1: Basic Upsert using MERGE
    from delta.tables import DeltaTable
    
    delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(spark, delta_path)
    
    delta_table.alias("target").merge(
        df_source.alias("source"),
        "target.customer_id = source.customer_id"
    ).whenMatchedUpdate(set = {
        "name": col("source.name"),
        "email": col("source.email"),
        "balance": col("source.balance"),
        "last_updated": col("source.last_updated")
    }).whenNotMatchedInsert(values = {
        "customer_id": col("source.customer_id"),
        "name": col("source.name"),
        "email": col("source.email"),
        "balance": col("source.balance"),
        "last_updated": col("source.last_updated")
    }).execute()
    
    print("\nAfter Basic Upsert:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).orderBy("customer_id").show()
    
    # METHOD 2: Conditional Upsert (update only if balance increased)
    source_data_2 = [
        (1, "John Doe", "john.updated@email.com", 90.0, "2024-01-21"),   # Lower balance - should not update
        (2, "Jane Smith", "jane@email.com", 300.0, "2024-01-21"),        # Higher balance - should update
        (6, "David Lee", "david@email.com", 400.0, "2024-01-21")         # New record - should insert
    ]
    
    df_source_2 = spark.createDataFrame(source_data_2, schema)
    
    delta_table.alias("target").merge(
        df_source_2.alias("source"),
        "target.customer_id = source.customer_id"
    ).whenMatchedUpdate(
        condition = "source.balance > target.balance",
        set = {
            "name": col("source.name"),
            "email": col("source.email"),
            "balance": col("source.balance"),
            "last_updated": col("source.last_updated")
        }
    ).whenNotMatchedInsert(values = {
        "customer_id": col("source.customer_id"),
        "name": col("source.name"),
        "email": col("source.email"),
        "balance": col("source.balance"),
        "last_updated": col("source.last_updated")
    }).execute()
    
    print("\nAfter Conditional Upsert (only if balance increased):")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).orderBy("customer_id").show()
    
    # METHOD 3: Upsert with computed columns
    source_data_3 = [
        (3, "Bob Johnson Jr", "bob@email.com", 200.0, "2024-01-22"),
        (7, "Eva Martinez", "eva@email.com", 500.0, "2024-01-22")
    ]
    
    df_source_3 = spark.createDataFrame(source_data_3, schema)
    
    delta_table.alias("target").merge(
        df_source_3.alias("source"),
        "target.customer_id = source.customer_id"
    ).whenMatchedUpdate(set = {
        "name": col("source.name"),
        "email": col("source.email"),
        "balance": expr("target.balance + source.balance"),  # Add to existing balance
        "last_updated": col("source.last_updated")
    }).whenNotMatchedInsert(values = {
        "customer_id": col("source.customer_id"),
        "name": col("source.name"),
        "email": col("source.email"),
        "balance": col("source.balance"),
        "last_updated": col("source.last_updated")
    }).execute()
    
    print("\nAfter Upsert with Computed Columns (balance addition):")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).orderBy("customer_id").show()
    
    # METHOD 4: SQL-based Upsert
    df_source_3.createOrReplaceTempView("source_customers")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).createOrReplaceTempView("target_customers")
    
    spark.sql("""
        MERGE INTO target_customers AS target
        USING source_customers AS source
        ON target.customer_id = source.customer_id
        WHEN MATCHED THEN
            UPDATE SET 
                target.name = source.name,
                target.email = source.email,
                target.balance = source.balance,
                target.last_updated = source.last_updated
        WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN
            INSERT (customer_id, name, email, balance, last_updated)
            VALUES (source.customer_id, source.name, source.email, source.balance, source.last_updated)
    """)
    
    print("\nAfter SQL-based Upsert:")
    spark.sql("SELECT * FROM target_customers ORDER BY customer_id").show()

        StructField("status", StringType(), True),
        StructField("balance", DoubleType(), True)
    ])
    
    df_source = spark.createDataFrame(source_data, source_schema)
    
    print("\nSource Data:")
    df_source.show()
    
    from delta.tables import DeltaTable
    delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(spark, delta_path)
    
    # METHOD 1: Multi-condition Merge
    delta_table.alias("target").merge(
        df_source.alias("source"),
        "target.customer_id = source.customer_id AND target.is_current = true"
    ).whenMatchedUpdate(
        condition = "target.email != source.email OR target.status != source.status OR target.balance != source.balance",
        set = {
            "email": col("source.email"),
            "status": col("source.status"),
            "balance": col("source.balance"),
            "valid_from": current_date().cast("string")
        }
    ).whenMatchedUpdate(
        condition = "target.email = source.email AND target.status = source.status AND target.balance = source.balance",
        set = {}  # No update needed
    ).whenNotMatchedInsert(values = {
        "customer_id": col("source.customer_id"),
        "name": col("source.name"),
        "email": col("source.email"),
        "status": col("source.status"),
        "balance": col("source.balance"),
        "valid_from": current_date().cast("string"),
        "valid_to": lit("9999-12-31"),
        "is_current": lit(True)
    }).execute()
    
    print("\nAfter Multi-condition Merge:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).orderBy("customer_id", "valid_from").show()
    
    # METHOD 2: Merge with Delete condition
    source_data_delete = [
        (1, "John Doe", "john.new@email.com", "deleted", 0.0),
        (6, "David Lee", "david@email.com", "active", 250.0)
    ]
    
    df_source_delete = spark.createDataFrame(source_data_delete, source_schema)
    
    delta_table.alias("target").merge(
        df_source_delete.alias("source"),
        "target.customer_id = source.customer_id AND target.is_current = true"
    ).whenMatchedDelete(
        condition = "source.status = 'deleted'"
    ).whenMatchedUpdate(
        condition = "source.status != 'deleted'",
        set = {
            "email": col("source.email"),
            "status": col("source.status"),
            "balance": col("source.balance"),
            "valid_from": current_date().cast("string")
        }
    ).whenNotMatchedInsert(values = {
        "customer_id": col("source.customer_id"),
        "name": col("source.name"),
        "email": col("source.email"),
        "status": col("source.status"),
        "balance": col("source.balance"),
        "valid_from": current_date().cast("string"),
        "valid_to": lit("9999-12-31"),
        "is_current": lit(True)
    }).execute()
    
    print("\nAfter Merge with Delete:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).orderBy("customer_id", "valid_from").show()
    
    # METHOD 3: SCD Type 2 Merge Pattern
    # Reset data for SCD demo
    df_target.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(delta_path)
    delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(spark, delta_path)
    
    scd_source_data = [
        (2, "Jane Smith-Updated", "jane.updated@email.com", "premium", 500.0),
        (7, "Frank Wilson", "frank@email.com", "active", 175.0)
    ]
    
    df_scd_source = spark.createDataFrame(scd_source_data, source_schema)
    
    # Step 1: Expire old records
    delta_table.alias("target").merge(
        df_scd_source.alias("source"),
        "target.customer_id = source.customer_id AND target.is_current = true"
    ).whenMatchedUpdate(
        condition = "target.email != source.email OR target.status != source.status",
        set = {
            "valid_to": current_date().cast("string"),
            "is_current": lit(False)
        }
    ).execute()
    
    # Step 2: Insert new versions
    df_scd_new_versions = df_scd_source \
        .withColumn("valid_from", current_date().cast("string")) \
        .withColumn("valid_to", lit("9999-12-31")) \
        .withColumn("is_current", lit(True))
    
    # Get existing customer IDs that were updated
    existing_updates = spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path) \
        .filter("is_current = false") \
        .select("customer_id").distinct()
    
    df_new_versions_only = df_scd_new_versions.join(
        existing_updates,
        "customer_id",
        "inner"
    )
    
    df_new_versions_only.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(delta_path)
    
    # Insert truly new records
    existing_ids = spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).select("customer_id").distinct()
    df_new_customers = df_scd_new_versions.join(
        existing_ids,
        "customer_id",
        "left_anti"
    )
    
    df_new_customers.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(delta_path)
    
    print("\nAfter SCD Type 2 Merge:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path) \
        .orderBy("customer_id", "valid_from") \
        .show(truncate=False)
    
    # Show only current records
    print("\nCurrent Records Only:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path) \
        .filter("is_current = true") \
        .orderBy("customer_id") \
        .show()

merge_pattern_demo()

## 6. Replace Pattern

```python
"""
REPLACE PATTERN
Purpose: Completely replace table contents or partitions
Use Cases:
- Full refresh scenarios
- Partition replacement
- Snapshot replacements
- Complete data reloads
"""

def replace_pattern_demo():
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("6. REPLACE PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Setup partitioned table
    delta_path = "/tmp/delta/sales_replace"
    
    initial_data = [
        ("2024-01-01", "North", "Product A", 100.0, 5),
        ("2024-01-01", "South", "Product B", 150.0, 3),
        ("2024-01-02", "North", "Product A", 120.0, 6),
        ("2024-01-02", "East", "Product C", 200.0, 4),
        ("2024-01-03", "West", "Product A", 90.0, 2),
        ("2024-01-03", "North", "Product B", 110.0, 3)
    ]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("sale_date", StringType(), True),
        StructField("region", StringType(), True),
        StructField("product", StringType(), True),
        StructFiel
```python
        StructField("amount", DoubleType(), True),
        StructField("quantity", IntegerType(), True)
    ])
    
    df_initial = spark.createDataFrame(initial_data, schema)
    df_initial.write.format("delta") \
        .mode("overwrite") \
        .partitionBy("sale_date") \
        .save(delta_path)
    
    print("\nInitial Data (Partitioned by sale_date):")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).orderBy("sale_date", "region").show()
    
    # METHOD 1: Complete Table Replace
    replacement_data = [
        ("2024-01-04", "North", "Product D", 300.0, 10),
        ("2024-01-04", "South", "Product D", 250.0, 8),
        ("2024-01-05", "East", "Product E", 400.0, 12)
    ]
    
    df_replacement = spark.createDataFrame(replacement_data, schema)
    df_replacement.write.format("delta") \
        .mode("overwrite") \
        .partitionBy("sale_date") \
        .save(delta_path)
    
    print("\nAfter Complete Table Replace:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).orderBy("sale_date", "region").show()
    
    # Restore initial data for next examples
    df_initial.write.format("delta") \
        .mode("overwrite") \
        .partitionBy("sale_date") \
        .save(delta_path)
    
    # METHOD 2: Dynamic Partition Replace
    new_partition_data = [
        ("2024-01-02", "North", "Product A", 999.0, 99),  # Replace 2024-01-02 partition
        ("2024-01-02", "South", "Product X", 888.0, 88)
    ]
    
    df_new_partition = spark.createDataFrame(new_partition_data, schema)
    
    # Use dynamic partition overwrite mode
    df_new_partition.write.format("delta") \
        .mode("overwrite") \
        .option("replaceWhere", "sale_date = '2024-01-02'") \
        .save(delta_path)
    
    print("\nAfter Dynamic Partition Replace (sale_date = '2024-01-02'):")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).orderBy("sale_date", "region").show()
    
    # METHOD 3: Replace with condition (multiple partitions)
    multi_partition_data = [
        ("2024-01-01", "Central", "Product Z", 500.0, 15),
        ("2024-01-03", "Central", "Product Z", 600.0, 20)
    ]
    
    df_multi = spark.createDataFrame(multi_partition_data, schema)
    
    df_multi.write.format("delta") \
        .mode("overwrite") \
        .option("replaceWhere", "sale_date IN ('2024-01-01', '2024-01-03')") \
        .save(delta_path)
    
    print("\nAfter Multi-Partition Replace (dates 01-01 and 01-03):")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).orderBy("sale_date", "region").show()
    
    # METHOD 4: Replace using DELETE + INSERT pattern
    from delta.tables import DeltaTable
    
    # Restore initial data
    df_initial.write.format("delta") \
        .mode("overwrite") \
        .partitionBy("sale_date") \
        .save(delta_path)
    
    delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(spark, delta_path)
    
    # Delete specific partition
    delta_table.delete("sale_date = '2024-01-01'")
    
    # Insert new data for that partition
    new_data = [
        ("2024-01-01", "Global", "Product Premium", 1000.0, 50)
    ]
    
    df_new = spark.createDataFrame(new_data, schema)
    df_new.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(delta_path)
    
    print("\nAfter DELETE + INSERT Replace Pattern:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).orderBy("sale_date", "region").show()
    
    # METHOD 5: SQL-based Replace
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).createOrReplaceTempView("sales")
    
    spark.sql("""
        INSERT OVERWRITE TABLE sales
        PARTITION (sale_date = '2024-01-02')
        VALUES ('2024-01-02', 'Premium', 'Product VIP', 2000.0, 100)
    """)
    
    print("\nAfter SQL-based Partition Replace:")
    spark.sql("SELECT * FROM sales ORDER BY sale_date, region").show()
    
    # METHOD 6: Replace entire table with schema evolution
    evolved_data = [
        ("2024-01-06", "North", "Product F", 150.0, 7, "USD", "John Doe"),
        ("2024-01-06", "South", "Product F", 175.0, 8, "USD", "Jane Smith")
    ]
    
    evolved_schema = StructType([
        StructField("sale_date", StringType(), True),
        StructField("region", StringType(), True),
        StructField("product", StringType(), True),
        StructField("amount", DoubleType(), True),
        StructField("quantity", IntegerType(), True),
        StructField("currency", StringType(), True),
        StructField("sales_person", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    df_evolved = spark.createDataFrame(evolved_data, evolved_schema)
    
    df_evolved.write.format("delta") \
        .mode("overwrite") \
        .option("overwriteSchema", "true") \
        .partitionBy("sale_date") \
        .save(delta_path)
    
    print("\nAfter Replace with Schema Evolution:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).show(truncate=False)
    
    # Show table history
    print("\nTable History (Replace operations):")
    delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(spark, delta_path)
    delta_table.history(5).select("version", "operation", "operationMetrics").show(truncate=False)

replace_pattern_demo()

## 7. Append Pattern

```python
"""
APPEND PATTERN
Purpose: Add new records without modifying existing data
Use Cases:
- Event logging
- Time-series data ingestion
- Incremental loads
- Audit trails
- Streaming data ingestion
"""

def append_pattern_demo():
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("7. APPEND PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Setup initial table
    delta_path = "/tmp/delta/events_append"
    
    initial_data = [
        (1, "2024-01-01 10:00:00", "login", "user_001", "success"),
        (2, "2024-01-01 10:05:00", "purchase", "user_002", "success"),
        (3, "2024-01-01 10:10:00", "logout", "user_001", "success")
    ]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("event_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("timestamp", StringType(), True),
        StructField("event_type", StringType(), True),
        StructField("user_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("status", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    df_initial = spark.createDataFrame(initial_data, schema)
    df_initial.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(delta_path)
    
    print("\nInitial Events:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).show()
    
    # METHOD 1: Simple Append
    new_events_1 = [
        (4, "2024-01-01 10:15:00", "login", "user_003", "success"),
        (5, "2024-01-01 10:20:00", "view_product", "user_002", "success")
    ]
    
    df_new_1 = spark.createDataFrame(new_events_1, schema)
    df_new_1.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(delta_path)
    
    print("\nAfter Simple Append:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).orderBy("event_id").show()
    
    # METHOD 2: Append with Deduplication
    new_events_2 = [
        (5, "2024-01-01 10:20:00", "view_product", "user_002", "success"),  # Duplicate
        (6, "2024-01-01 10:25:00", "add_to_cart", "user_003", "success"),
        (7, "2024-01-01 10:30:00", "purchase", "user_003", "success")
    ]
    
    df_new_2 = spark.createDataFrame(new_events_2, schema)
    
    # Read existing data
    df_existing = spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path)
    
    # Deduplicate based on event_id
    df_deduplicated = df_new_2.join(
        df_existing.select("event_id"),
        "event_id",
        "left_anti"  # Keep only records not in existing data
    )
    
    df_deduplicated.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(delta_path)
    
    print("\nAfter Append with Deduplication:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).orderBy("event_id").show()
    
    # METHOD 3: Append with Data Validation
    new_events_3 = [
        (8, "2024-01-01 10:35:00", "logout", "user_002", "success"),
        (9, "2024-01-01 10:40:00", "login", None, "failed"),  # Invalid - null user_id
        (10, "2024-01-01 10:45:00", "purchase", "user_004", "success")
    ]
    
    df_new_3 = spark.createDataFrame(new_events_3, schema)
    
    # Validate data before append
    df_validated = df_new_3.filter(
        col("user_id").isNotNull() & 
        col("timestamp").isNotNull() &
        col("event_type").isin(["login", "logout", "purchase", "view_product", "add_to_cart"])
    )
    
    print("\nValidated Events (before append):")
    df_validated.show()
    
    df_validated.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(delta_path)
    
    print("\nAfter Append with Validation:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).orderBy("event_id").show()
    
    # METHOD 4: Partitioned Append
    delta_path_partitioned = "/tmp/delta/events_append_partitioned"
    
    partitioned_data = [
        (1, "2024-01-01", "10:00:00", "login", "user_001", "success"),
        (2, "2024-01-01", "10:05:00", "purchase", "user_002", "success"),
        (3, "2024-01-02", "09:00:00", "login", "user_003", "success")
    ]
    
    partitioned_schema = StructType([
        StructField("event_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("event_date", StringType(), True),
        StructField("event_time", StringType(), True),
        StructField("event_type", StringType(), True),
        StructField("user_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("status", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    df_partitioned = spark.createDataFrame(partitioned_data, partitioned_schema)
    df_partitioned.write.format("delta") \
        .mode("overwrite") \
        .partitionBy("event_date") \
        .save(delta_path_partitioned)
    
    # Append to specific partition
    new_partitioned_events = [
        (4, "2024-01-02", "09:30:00", "purchase", "user_003", "success"),
        (5, "2024-01-03", "08:00:00", "login", "user_004", "success")
    ]
    
    df_new_partitioned = spark.createDataFrame(new_partitioned_events, partitioned_schema)
    df_new_partitioned.write.format("delta") \
        .mode("append") \
        .partitionBy("event_date") \
        .save(delta_path_partitioned)
    
    print("\nAfter Partitioned Append:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path_partitioned) \
        .orderBy("event_date", "event_id") \
        .show()
    
    # METHOD 5: Append with Transformation
    raw_events = [
        (11, "2024-01-01T10:50:00Z", "LOGOUT", "user_002", 1),
        (12, "2024-01-01T10:55:00Z", "LOGIN", "user_005", 1)
    ]
    
    raw_schema = StructType([
        StructField("event_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("timestamp_iso", StringType(), True),
        StructField("event_type_raw", StringType(), True),
        StructField("user_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("status_code", IntegerType(), True)
    ])
    
    df_raw = spark.createDataFrame(raw_events, raw_schema)
    
    # Transform before append
    df_transformed = df_raw.select(
        col("event_id"),
        col("timestamp_iso").alias("timestamp"),
        lower(col("event_type_raw")).alias("event_type"),
        col("user_id"),
        when(col("status_code") == 1, "success")
            .otherwise("failed").alias("status")
    )
    
    print("\nTransformed Events (before append):")
    df_transformed.show()
    
    df_transformed.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(delta_path)
    
    print("\nAfter Append with Transformation:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).orderBy("event_id").show()
    
    # METHOD 6: Batch Append with Metrics
    batch_events = [
        (13, "2024-01-01 11:00:00", "login", "user_006", "success"),
        (14, "2024-01-01 11:05:00", "view_product", "user_006", "success"),
        (15, "2024-01-01 11:10:00", "purchase", "user_006", "success"),
        (16, "2024-01-01 11:15:00", "logout", "user_006", "success")
    ]
    
    df_batch = spark.createDataFrame(batch_events, schema)
    
    # Calculate metrics before append
    batch_count = df_batch.count()
    batch_users = df_batch.select("user_id").distinct().count()
    
    
```python
    print(f"\nBatch Append Metrics:")
    print(f"  Records to append: {batch_count}")

    df_batch.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(delta_path)
    
    # Verify append
    total_count = spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path).count()

## Complete Integration Example

```python
"""
COMPLETE INTEGRATION EXAMPLE
Demonstrates all patterns working together in a realistic scenario
"""

def complete_integration_demo():
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("COMPLETE INTEGRATION EXAMPLE - E-Commerce Order Processing")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Initialize orders table
    orders_path = "/tmp/delta/orders_complete"
    
    # Day 1: Initial load (INSERT)
    print("\n--- Day 1: Initial Load (INSERT PATTERN) ---")
    day1_orders = [
        (1001, "2024-01-01", "customer_A", "pending", 150.0, "2024-01-01 09:00:00"),
        (1002, "2024-01-01", "customer_B", "pending", 200.0, "2024-01-01 09:30:00"),
        (1003, "2024-01-01", "customer_C", "pending", 100.0, "2024-01-01 10:00:00")
    ]
    
    orders_schema = StructType([
        StructField("order_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("order_date", StringType(), True),
        StructField("customer_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("status", StringType(), True),
        StructField("amount", DoubleType(), True),
        StructField("last_updated", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    df_day1 = spark.createDataFrame(day1_orders, orders_schema)
    df_day1.write.format("delta") \
        .mode("overwrite") \
        .partitionBy("order_date") \
        .save(orders_path)
    
    print("Day 1 Orders:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(orders_path).show()
    
    # Day 2: Process orders (UPDATE PATTERN)
    print("\n--- Day 2: Process Orders (UPDATE PATTERN) ---")
    from delta.tables import DeltaTable
    delta_orders = DeltaTable.forPath(spark, orders_path)
    
    # Update order statuses
    delta_orders.update(
        condition = "order_id IN (1001, 1002)",
        set = {
            "status": lit("processing"),
            "last_updated": lit("2024-01-02 10:00:00")
        }
    )
    
    print("After processing orders 1001, 1002:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(orders_path).orderBy("order_id").show()
    
    # Day 2: New orders (APPEND PATTERN)
    print("\n--- Day 2: New Orders (APPEND PATTERN) ---")
    day2_new_orders = [
        (1004, "2024-01-02", "customer_D", "pending", 300.0, "2024-01-02 11:00:00"),
        (1005, "2024-01-02", "customer_E", "pending", 175.0, "2024-01-02 11:30:00")
    ]
    
    df_day2 = spark.createDataFrame(day2_new_orders, orders_schema)
    df_day2.write.format("delta") \
        .mode("append") \
        .partitionBy("order_date") \
        .save(orders_path)
    
    print("After appending new orders:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(orders_path).orderBy("order_id").show()
    
    # Day 3: Complete some orders, cancel others (UPDATE + DELETE PATTERN)
    print("\n--- Day 3: Complete/Cancel Orders (UPDATE + DELETE PATTERN) ---")
    
    # Complete orders
    delta_orders.update(
        condition = "order_id IN (1001, 1004)",
        set = {
            "status": lit("completed"),
            "last_updated": lit("2024-01-03 14:00:00")
        }
    )
    
    # Cancel and delete fraudulent order
    delta_orders.delete("order_id = 1003")
    
    print("After completing orders and deleting fraudulent order:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(orders_path).orderBy("order_id").show()
    
    # Day 4: Receive updates from external system (UPSERT PATTERN)
    print("\n--- Day 4: External System Updates (UPSERT PATTERN) ---")
    
    external_updates = [
        (1002, "2024-01-01", "customer_B", "shipped", 200.0, "2024-01-04 09:00:00"),  # Update
        (1005, "2024-01-02", "customer_E", "processing", 175.0, "2024-01-04 09:00:00"), # Update
        (1006, "2024-01-04", "customer_F", "pending", 250.0, "2024-01-04 09:30:00")    # Insert
    ]
    
    df_external = spark.createDataFrame(external_updates, orders_schema)
    
    delta_orders.alias("target").merge(
        df_external.alias("source"),
        "target.order_id = source.order_id"
    ).whenMatchedUpdate(set = {
        "status": col("source.status"),
        "amount": col("source.amount"),
        "last_updated": col("source.last_updated")
    }).whenNotMatchedInsert(values = {
        "order_id": col("source.order_id"),
        "order_date": col("source.order_date"),
        "customer_id": col("source.customer_id"),
        "status": col("source.status"),
        "amount": col("source.amount"),
        "last_updated": col("source.last_updated")
    }).execute()
    
    print("After external system upsert:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(orders_path).orderBy("order_id").show()
    
    # Day 5: Complex merge with business rules (MERGE PATTERN)
    print("\n--- Day 5: Complex Business Rules (MERGE PATTERN) ---")
    
    payment_updates = [
        (1004, "2024-01-01", "customer_D", "delivered", 300.0, "2024-01-05 10:00:00"),
        (1005, "2024-01-02", "customer_E", "cancelled", 0.0, "2024-01-05 10:00:00"),
        (1007, "2024-01-05", "customer_G", "pending", 400.0, "2024-01-05 10:30:00")
    ]
    
    df_payments = spark.createDataFrame(payment_updates, orders_schema)
    
    delta_orders.alias("target").merge(
        df_payments.alias("source"),
        "target.order_id = source.order_id"
    ).whenMatchedUpdate(
        condition = "source.status = 'delivered'",
        set = {
            "status": lit("delivered"),
            "last_updated": col("source.last_updated")
        }
    ).whenMatchedDelete(
        condition = "source.status = 'cancelled'"
    ).whenNotMatchedInsert(values = {
        "order_id": col("source.order_id"),
        "order_date": col("source.order_date"),
        "customer_id": col("source.customer_id"),
        "status": col("source.status"),
        "amount": col("source.amount"),
        "last_updated": col("source.last_updated")
    }).execute()
    
    print("After complex merge (delivered/cancelled/new):")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(orders_path).orderBy("order_id").show()
    
    # Day 6: Replace old partition data (REPLACE PATTERN)
    print("\n--- Day 6: Correct Historical Data (REPLACE PATTERN) ---")
    
    corrected_day1_data = [
        (1001, "2024-01-01", "customer_A", "delivered", 150.0, "2024-01-06 08:00:00"),
        (1002, "2024-01-01", "customer_B", "shipped", 220.0, "2024-01-06 08:00:00")  # Corrected amount
    ]
    
    df_corrected = spark.createDataFrame(corrected_day1_data, orders_schema)
    df_corrected.write.format("delta") \
        .mode("overwrite") \
        .option("replaceWhere", "order_date = '2024-01-01'") \
        .save(orders_path)
    
    print("After replacing 2024-01-01 partition with corrected data:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(orders_path).orderBy("order_id").show()
    
    # Final Analytics
    print("\n--- Final Analytics ---")
    
    df_final = spark.read.format("delta").load(orders_path)
    
    print("\nOrders by Status:")
    df_final.groupBy("status") \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("order_count"),
            sum("amount").alias("total_amount")
        ) \
        .orderBy("status") \
        .show()
    
    print("\nOrders by Date:")
    df_final.groupBy("order_date") \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("order_count"),
            sum("amount").alias("total_amount"),
            avg("amount").alias("avg_amount")
        ) \
        .orderBy("order_date") \
        .show()
    
    print("\nCustomer Order Summary:")
    df_final.groupBy("customer_id") \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("total_orders"),
            sum("amount").alias("total_spent"),
            max("last_updated").alias("last_order_date")
        ) \
        .orderBy(desc("total_spent")) \
        .show()
    
    # Show complete history
    print("\nComplete Table History:")
    delta_orders.history().select(
        "version", 
        "timestamp", 
        "operation", 
        "operationParameters"
    ).show(truncate=False)
    
    # Time travel example
    print("\nTime Travel - View data at version 2:")
    spark.read.format("delta") \
        .option("versionAsOf", 2) \
        .load(orders_path) \
        .orderBy("order_id") \
        .show()

```python
"""
UTILITY FUNCTIONS AND BEST PRACTICES
Helper functions for common mutation operations
"""

class DeltaMutationHelper:
    """
    Helper class for Delta Lake mutation operations
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    def safe_insert(self, df, delta_path, partition_cols=None, 
                   dedup_cols=None, mode="append"):
        """
        Safely insert data with optional deduplication
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame to insert
            delta_path: Path to Delta table
            partition_cols: List of partition columns
            dedup_cols: List of columns to use for deduplication
            mode: Write mode (append/overwrite)
        """
        print(f"\n--- Safe Insert to {delta_path} ---")
        
        # Deduplicate if specified
        if dedup_cols:
            print(f"Deduplicating on columns: {dedup_cols}")
            df = df.dropDuplicates(dedup_cols)
        
        # Validate data
        initial_count = df.count()
        df_validated = df.dropna(how='all')
        validated_count = df_validated.count()
        
        print(f"Initial records: {initial_count}")
        print(f"After validation: {validated_count}")
        print(f"Dropped records: {initial_count - validated_count}")
        
        # Write data
        writer = df_validated.write.format("delta").mode(mode)
        
        if partition_cols:
            writer =
```python
            writer = writer.partitionBy(*partition_cols)
        
        writer.save(delta_path)
        
        print(f"Successfully inserted {validated_count} records")
        return validated_count
    
    def safe_update(self, delta_path, condition, updates, dry_run=False):
        """
        Safely update records with preview option
        
        Args:
            delta_path: Path to Delta table
            condition: Update condition
            updates: Dictionary of column updates
            dry_run: If True, only show what would be updated
        """
        from delta.tables import DeltaTable
        
        print(f"\n--- Safe Update on {delta_path} ---")
        print(f"Condition: {condition}")
        print(f"Updates: {updates}")
        
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, delta_path)
        
        if dry_run:
            print("\n[DRY RUN] Records that would be updated:")
            df = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path)
            df.filter(condition).show()
            return
        
        # Get count before update
        df_before = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path)
        count_before = df_before.filter(condition).count()
        
        # Perform update
        delta_table.update(condition=condition, set=updates)
        
        print(f"Updated {count_before} records")
    
    def safe_delete(self, delta_path, condition, soft_delete=False, 
                   soft_delete_column="is_deleted"):
        """
        Safely delete records with soft delete option
        
        Args:
            delta_path: Path to Delta table
            condition: Delete condition
            soft_delete: If True, mark as deleted instead of removing
            soft_delete_column: Column name for soft delete flag
        """
        from delta.tables import DeltaTable
        
        print(f"\n--- Safe Delete from {delta_path} ---")
        print(f"Condition: {condition}")
        
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, delta_path)
        df = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path)
        
        # Get count of records to delete
        count_to_delete = df.filter(condition).count()
        
        if count_to_delete == 0:
            print("No records match the delete condition")
            return 0
        
        print(f"Records matching condition: {count_to_delete}")
        
        if soft_delete:
            print(f"Performing SOFT DELETE (setting {soft_delete_column}=true)")
            delta_table.update(
                condition=condition,
                set={soft_delete_column: lit(True)}
            )
        else:
            print("Performing HARD DELETE (removing records)")
            delta_table.delete(condition)
        
        return count_to_delete
    
    def safe_upsert(self, delta_path, source_df, join_keys, 
                   update_condition=None, insert_condition=None):
        """
        Safely perform upsert with optional conditions
        
        Args:
            delta_path: Path to Delta table
            source_df: Source DataFrame
            join_keys: List of columns to join on
            update_condition: Optional condition for updates
            insert_condition: Optional condition for inserts
        """
        from delta.tables import DeltaTable
        
        print(f"\n--- Safe Upsert to {delta_path} ---")
        print(f"Join keys: {join_keys}")
        
        # Build join condition
        join_condition = " AND ".join([
            f"target.{key} = source.{key}" for key in join_keys
        ])
        
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, delta_path)
        
        # Get source statistics
        source_count = source_df.count()
        print(f"Source records: {source_count}")
        
        # Build merge
        merge_builder = delta_table.alias("target").merge(
            source_df.alias("source"),
            join_condition
        )
        
        # Prepare update set
        update_set = {
            col_name: col(f"source.{col_name}") 
            for col_name in source_df.columns
        }
        
        # Prepare insert values
        insert_values = {
            col_name: col(f"source.{col_name}") 
            for col_name in source_df.columns
        }
        
        # Apply conditions
        if update_condition:
            merge_builder = merge_builder.whenMatchedUpdate(
                condition=update_condition,
                set=update_set
            )
        else:
            merge_builder = merge_builder.whenMatchedUpdate(set=update_set)
        
        if insert_condition:
            merge_builder = merge_builder.whenNotMatchedInsert(
                condition=insert_condition,
                values=insert_values
            )
        else:
            merge_builder = merge_builder.whenNotMatchedInsert(values=insert_values)
        
        # Execute merge
        merge_builder.execute()
        
        print("Upsert completed successfully")
    
    def vacuum_table(self, delta_path, retention_hours=168, dry_run=True):
        """
        Vacuum Delta table to remove old files
        
        Args:
            delta_path: Path to Delta table
            retention_hours: Retention period in hours (default 7 days)
            dry_run: If True, only show files that would be deleted
        """
        from delta.tables import DeltaTable
        
        print(f"\n--- Vacuum {delta_path} ---")
        print(f"Retention hours: {retention_hours}")
        
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, delta_path)
        
        if dry_run:
            print("[DRY RUN] Files that would be deleted:")
            result = delta_table.vacuum(retention_hours, dryRun=True)
            return result
        else:
            print("Vacuuming table...")
            delta_table.vacuum(retention_hours)
            print("Vacuum completed")
    
    def optimize_table(self, delta_path, where_condition=None, z_order_cols=None):
        """
        Optimize Delta table with optional Z-ordering
        
        Args:
            delta_path: Path to Delta table
            where_condition: Optional partition filter
            z_order_cols: List of columns for Z-ordering
        """
        from delta.tables import DeltaTable
        
        print(f"\n--- Optimize {delta_path} ---")
        
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, delta_path)
        
        if where_condition:
            optimize_builder = delta_table.optimize().where(where_condition)
        else:
            optimize_builder = delta_table.optimize()
        
        if z_order_cols:
            print(f"Z-ordering by: {z_order_cols}")
            optimize_builder.executeZOrderBy(z_order_cols)
        else:
            optimize_builder.executeCompaction()
        
        print("Optimization completed")
    
    def get_table_stats(self, delta_path):
        """
        Get comprehensive table statistics
        
        Args:
            delta_path: Path to Delta table
        """
        from delta.tables import DeltaTable
        
        print(f"\n--- Table Statistics for {delta_path} ---")
        
        delta_table = DeltaTable.forPath(self.spark, delta_path)
        df = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path)
        
        # Basic stats
        record_count = df.count()
        column_count = len(df.columns)
        
        print(f"Total records: {record_count}")
        print(f"Total columns: {column_count}")
        
        # History
        history_df = delta_table.history(5)
        print("\nRecent operations:")
        history_df.select("version", "timestamp", "operation").show()
        
        # Detail
        print("\nTable details:")
        delta_table.detail().select(
            "format", "partitionColumns", "numFiles", "sizeInBytes"
        ).show(truncate=False)
        
        return {
            "record_count": record_count,
            "column_count": column_count
        }

# Demonstrate utility functions
def demonstrate_utilities():
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("UTILITY FUNCTIONS DEMONSTRATION")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    helper = DeltaMutationHelper(spark)
    
    # Setup test data
    test_path = "/tmp/delta/utilities_demo"
    
    test_data = [
        (1, "Product A", 100.0, "2024-01-01", False),
        (2, "Product B", 200.0, "2024-01-01", False),
        (3, "Product C", 150.0, "2024-01-02", False)
    ]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("product_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("product_name", StringType(), True),
        StructField("price", DoubleType(), True),
        StructField("date", StringType(), True),
        StructField("is_deleted", BooleanType(), True)
    ])
    
    df_test = spark.createDataFrame(test_data, schema)
    
    # Test safe insert
    helper.safe_insert(
        df_test, 
        test_path, 
        partition_cols=["date"],
        dedup_cols=["product_id"],
        mode="overwrite"
    )
    
    # Test safe update with dry run
    helper.safe_update(
        test_path,
        condition="price < 150",
        updates={"price": expr("price * 1.1")},
        dry_run=True
    )
    
    # Actual update
    helper.safe_update(
        test_path,
        condition="price < 150",
        updates={"price": expr("price * 1.1")},
        dry_run=False
    )
    
    # Test soft delete
    helper.safe_delete(
        test_path,
        condition="product_id = 3",
        soft_delete=True
    )
    
    # Test upsert
    upsert_data = [
        (2, "Product B Updated", 250.0, "2024-01-01", False),
        (4, "Product D", 300.0, "2024-01-03", False)
    ]
    
    df_upsert = spark.createDataFrame(upsert_data, schema)
    
    helper.safe_upsert(
        test_path,
        df_upsert,
        join_keys=["product_id"]
    )
    
    # Get table stats
    stats = helper.get_table_stats(test_path)
    
    # Show final state
    print("\nFinal Table State:")
    spark.read.format("delta").load(test_path).orderBy("product_id").show()
    
    # Optimize table
    helper.optimize_table(test_path, z_order_cols=["product_id"])
    
    # Vacuum (dry run)
    helper.vacuum_table(test_path, retention_hours=0, dry_run=True)

1. INSERT PATTERN
