# Role-based access
physician_view = app_enc.implement_data_masking(df, "ssn", "partial", "admin")
researcher_view = app_enc.implement_data_masking(df, "ssn", "hash", "analyst")

Scenario 2: Financial Services (PCI-DSS Compliance)
----------------------------------------------------
Requirements:
• Tokenize credit card numbers
• Encrypt CVV and expiry dates
• Mask card numbers for display
• 90-day data retention

Implementation:
# Setup
tokenizer = TokenizationPattern(spark)
col_enc = ColumnLevelEncryptionPattern(spark)

# Tokenize card numbers
tokenized_df = tokenizer.tokenize_column(df, "card_number", "ALPHANUMERIC")

# Encrypt sensitive data
pci_key = Fernet.generate_key()
encrypted_df = col_enc.encrypt_column(tokenized_df, "cvv", pci_key)
encrypted_df = col_enc.encrypt_column(encrypted_df, "expiry_date", pci_key)

# Mask for display
@udf(StringType())
def mask_card(card_num):
    return "**** **** **** " + card_num[-4:]

display_df = encrypted_df.withColumn("card_display", mask_card(col("card_number")))

# Export token vault
tokenizer.export_token_vault("/secure/token_vault.json")

Scenario 3: E-Commerce (GDPR Compliance)
-----------------------------------------
Requirements:
• Encrypt customer PII
• Right to access (data portability)
• Right to erasure (right to be forgotten)
• Consent management

Implementation:
# Setup
col_enc = ColumnLevelEncryptionPattern(spark)
compliance = EncryptionComplianceManager()

# Encrypt PII
gdpr_keys = {
    "email": Fernet.generate_key(),
    "address": Fernet.generate_key()
}
encrypted_df = col_enc.encrypt_multiple_columns(df, gdpr_keys)

# Data export (Right to Access)
def export_customer_data(customer_id):
    customer_df = encrypted_df.filter(col("customer_id") == customer_id)
    decrypted_df = col_enc.selective_decryption(customer_df, ["email", "address"])
    return decrypted_df.toJSON().collect()

# Data erasure (Right to be Forgotten)
def erase_customer_data(customer_id):
    erased_df = encrypted_df.withColumn(
        "email_enc",
        when(col("customer_id") == customer_id, lit("ERASED")).otherwise(col("email_enc"))
    )
    return erased_df

Optimization Techniques
-----------------------

1. Partitioning Strategy
   # Optimize number of partitions
   optimal_partitions = max(spark.sparkContext.defaultParallelism, 8)
   df = df.repartition(optimal_partitions)

2. Caching
   # Cache frequently accessed data
   df.cache()
   df.count()  # Force cache

3. Pandas UDF for Vectorization
   from pyspark.sql.functions import pandas_udf
   import pandas as pd
   
   @pandas_udf(StringType())
   def vectorized_encrypt(series: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
       return series.apply(lambda x: encrypt(x) if x else None)

4. Batch Processing
   # Process in batches for large datasets
   batch_size = 10000
   for i in range(0, total_records, batch_size):
       batch_df = df.filter((col("id") > i) & (col("id") <= i + batch_size))
       # Process batch

5. Compression
   # Use efficient compression
   df.write.option("compression", "snappy").parquet("/path")

6. Column Projection
   # Select only needed columns
   df.select("id", "encrypted_field", "metadata")

# ============================================================================
# 1. FIFO (First-In-First-Out) Task Scheduling Pattern
# ============================================================================

def fifo_task_scheduling_pattern():
    """
    FIFO Scheduling: Tasks are executed in the order they are submitted.
    This is the default scheduling mode in Spark.
    
    Use Case: Batch processing where order matters and all jobs have equal priority
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("1. FIFO TASK SCHEDULING PATTERN")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Create Spark session with FIFO scheduler (default)
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("FIFO_Task_Scheduling") \
        .config("spark.scheduler.mode", "FIFO") \
        .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "4") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    try:
        # Create sample data representing tasks
        tasks_data = [
            (1, "Task_A", "2024-01-01 10:00:00", 100),
            (2, "Task_B", "2024-01-01 10:01:00", 200),
            (3, "Task_C", "2024-01-01 10:02:00", 150),
            (4, "Task_D", "2024-01-01 10:03:00", 300),
            (5, "Task_E", "2024-01-01 10:04:00", 250)
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("task_id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("task_name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("submission_time", StringType(), False),
            StructField("data_size", IntegerType(), False)
        ])
        
        tasks_df = spark.createDataFrame(tasks_data, schema)
        
        print("\nOriginal Tasks (Submission Order):")
        tasks_df.show()
        
        # Simulate FIFO processing - tasks execute in submission order
        print("\nProcessing tasks in FIFO order...")
        
        # Process each task sequentially
        for row in tasks_df.collect():
            print(f"\nProcessing: {row['task_name']}")
            print(f"  Submission Time: {row['submission_time']}")
            print(f"  Data Size: {row['data_size']} MB")
            
            # Simulate processing with data transformation
            task_data = spark.range(0, row['data_size'] * 1000) \
                .withColumn("task_id", lit(row['task_id'])) \
                .withColumn("task_name", lit(row['task_name']))
            
            result = task_data.agg(
                count("*").alias("records_processed"),
                max("id").alias("max_value")
            ).collect()[0]
            
            print(f"  Records Processed: {result['records_processed']}")
            print(f"  Status: Completed")
        
        print("\nFIFO Scheduling Complete!")
        print("Characteristics:")
        print("  - Simple and predictable")
        print("  - No starvation for long-running jobs")
        print("  - May cause head-of-line blocking")
        
    finally:
        spark.stop()

def fair_task_scheduling_pattern():
    """
    Fair Scheduling: Resources are shared equally among all active jobs.
    Jobs are organized into pools with configurable weights.
    
    Use Case: Multi-tenant environments, interactive queries alongside batch jobs
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("2. FAIR TASK SCHEDULING PATTERN")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Create Spark session with FAIR scheduler
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("Fair_Task_Scheduling") \
        .config("spark.scheduler.mode", "FAIR") \
        .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "4") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    try:
        # Create sample data for different job pools
        jobs_data = [
            (1, "interactive_query_1", "interactive", 1, 50),
            (2, "batch_job_1", "batch", 3, 500),
            (3, "interactive_query_2", "interactive", 1, 75),
            (4, "batch_job_2", "batch", 3, 600),
            (5, "critical_job_1", "critical", 2, 200)
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("job_id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("job_name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("pool", StringType(), False),
            StructField("weight", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("data_size", IntegerType(), False)
        ])
        
        jobs_df = spark.createDataFrame(jobs_data, schema)
        
        print("\nJobs with Pool Assignments:")
        jobs_df.show()
        
        # Demonstrate fair sharing across pools
        print("\nPool Configuration:")
        pool_config = jobs_df.groupBy("pool") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("job_count"),
                avg("weight").alias("avg_weight"),
                sum("data_size").alias("total_data_size")
            )
        pool_config.show()
        
        # Simulate fair scheduling by processing jobs from different pools
        print("\nProcessing jobs with Fair Scheduling...")
        
        # Set scheduler pool for each job
        for row in jobs_df.collect():
            # In real implementation, each thread would set its pool
            print(f"\nJob: {row['job_name']} (Pool: {row['pool']}, Weight: {row['weight']})")
            
            # Simulate job execution with resource allocation based on pool weight
            job_data = spark.range(0, row['data_size'] * 100) \
                .withColumn("job_id", lit(row['job_id'])) \

            # Calculate resource share based on weight

            print(f"  Resource Share: {resource_share:.2%}")
            
            result = job_data.agg(count("*").alias("records")).collect()[0]
            print(f"  Records Processed: {result['records']}")
        
        print("\nFair Scheduling Benefits:")
        print("  - Prevents resource starvation")
        print("  - Better for multi-tenant environments")
        print("  - Configurable pool weights for priority")
        print("  - Interactive queries don't wait for batch jobs")
        
    finally:
        spark.stop()

def priority_task_scheduling_pattern():
    """
    Priority Scheduling: Tasks are executed based on assigned priority levels.
    Higher priority tasks are processed before lower priority ones.
    
    Use Case: SLA-based processing, critical jobs need faster execution
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("3. PRIORITY TASK SCHEDULING PATTERN")
    print("="*80)
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("Priority_Task_Scheduling") \
        .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "4") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    try:
        # Create sample data with priority levels
        tasks_data = [
            (1, "Low_Priority_Report", 1, "2024-01-01 10:00:00", 200),

            (6, "Critical_Transaction", 5, "2024-01-01 10:05:00", 75),
            (7, "Medium_ETL", 2, "2024-01-01 10:06:00", 250)
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("task_id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("task_name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("priority", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("submission_time", StringType(), False),
            StructField("data_size", IntegerType(), False)
        ])
        
        tasks_df = spark.createDataFrame(tasks_data, schema)
        
        print("\nOriginal Tasks (Submission Order):")

        # Sort by priority (descending) and submission time
        prioritized_tasks = tasks_df.orderBy(

        )
        
        print("\nTasks Ordered by Priority:")

        # Add priority queue position
        prioritized_with_queue = prioritized_tasks.withColumn(
            "queue_position",
            row_number().over(Window.orderBy(col("priority").desc(), col("submission_time")))
        )

        ).show()
        
        # Process tasks in priority order

        for row in prioritized_with_queue.collect():

        print("\nPriority Scheduling Benefits:")

        print("  - SLA compliance for high-priority jobs")
        print("  - Flexible priority assignment")
        print("  - Risk: Low-priority tasks may starve")
        
    finally:
        spark.stop()

# ============================================================================
# 5. Speculative Task Scheduling Pattern
# ============================================================================

def speculative_task_scheduling_pattern():
    """
    Speculative Execution: Launches backup copies of slow-running tasks
    to prevent stragglers from delaying job completion.
    
    Use Case: Handling heterogeneous clusters, mitigating slow nodes
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("5. SPECULATIVE TASK SCHEDULING PATTERN")
    print("="*80)
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("Speculative_Task_Scheduling") \
        .config("spark.speculation", "true") \
        .config("spark.speculation.interval", "100ms") \
        .config("spark.speculation.multiplier", "1.5") \
        .config("spark.speculation.quantile", "0.75") \
        .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "8") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    try:
        # Create sample data representing task execution times
        tasks_data = [
            (1, "task_1", "node_1", 100, 105, "COMPLETED", False),
            (2, "task_2", "node_2", 100, 98, "COMPLETED", False),
            (3, "task_3", "node_3", 100, 350, "RUNNING", True),  # Straggler
            (4, "task_4", "node_1", 100, 102, "COMPLETED", False),
            (5, "task_5", "node_2", 100, 97, "COMPLETED", False),
            (6, "task_6", "node_4", 100, 280, "RUNNING", True),  # Straggler
            (7, "task_7", "node_1", 100, 103, "COMPLETED", False),
            (8, "task_8", "node_2", 100, 101, "COMPLETED", False)
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("task_id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("task_name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("node", StringType(), False),
            StructField("expected_time_ms", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("actual_time_ms", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("status", StringType(), False),
            StructField("is_straggler", BooleanType(), False)
        ])
        
        tasks_df = spark.createDataFrame(tasks_data, schema)
        
        print("\nTask Execution Status:")
        tasks_df.show()
        
        # Identify stragglers (tasks taking significantly longer)
        print("\nStraggler Detection:")
        
        # Calculate median execution time
        median_time = tasks_df.approxQuantile("actual_time_ms", [0.5], 0.01)[0]
        threshold_time = median_time * 1.5  # 1.5x median
        
        print(f"  Median Execution Time: {median_time} ms")
        print(f"  Straggler Threshold (1.5x median): {threshold_time} ms")
        
        # Identify and show stragglers
        stragglers = tasks_df.filter(
            (col("actual_time_ms") > threshold_time) & 
            (col("status") == "RUNNING")
        )
        
        print(f"\nDetected Stragglers: {stragglers.count()}")
        stragglers.select("task_name", "node", "actual_time_ms", "expected_time_ms").show()
        
        # Simulate speculative execution
        print("\nLaunching Speculative Tasks...")
        
        speculative_tasks = []
        for row in stragglers.collect():
            spec_task = (
                row['task_id'] * 100,  # New task ID
                f"{row['task_name']}_speculative",
                "node_backup",  # Different node
                row['expected_time_ms'],
                row['expected_time_ms'] + 10,  # Slightly longer than expected
                "COMPLETED",
                False
            )
            speculative_tasks.append(spec_task)
            
            print(f"\nOriginal Task: {row['task_name']} on {row['node']}")
            print(f"  Status: {row['status']} (Running for {row['actual_time_ms']} ms)")
            print(f"Speculative Task: {spec_task[1]} on {spec_task[2]}")
            print(f"  Status: {spec_task[5]} (Completed in {spec_task[4]} ms)")
            print(f"  Action: Using speculative result, killing original task")
        
        # Create DataFrame with speculative tasks
        if speculative_tasks:
            spec_df = spark.createDataFrame(speculative_tasks, schema)
            
            print("\nSpeculative Tasks Summary:")
            spec_df.select("task_name", "node", "actual_time_ms", "status").show()
        
        # Calculate performance improvement
        print("\nPerformance Analysis:")
        
        original_max_time = tasks_df.agg(max("actual_time_ms")).collect()[0][0]
        
        # Simulated completion time with speculation
        completed_tasks = tasks_df.filter(col("status") == "COMPLETED")
        if speculative_tasks:
            spec_completion_time = max(
                completed_tasks.agg(max("actual_time_ms")).collect()[0][0],
                max([t[4] for t in speculative_tasks])
            )
        else:
            spec_completion_time = original_max_time
        
        print(f"  Without Speculation: {original_max_time} ms")
        print(f"  With Speculation: {spec_completion_time} ms")
        improvement = ((original_max_time - spec_completion_time) / original_max_time) * 100
        print(f"  Performance Improvement: {improvement:.2f}%")
        
        # Show task distribution
        print("\nTask Execution Distribution:")
        task_stats = tasks_df.groupBy("node") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("task_count"),
                avg("actual_time_ms").alias("avg_time_ms"),
                max("actual_time_ms").alias("max_time_ms")
            )
        task_stats.show()
        
        print("\nSpeculative Execution Benefits:")
        print("  - Mitigates impact of slow nodes")
        print("  - Reduces overall job completion time")
        print("  - Handles heterogeneous hardware")
        print("  - Automatic straggler detection")
        print("\nConsiderations:")
        print("  - Increases resource usage")
        print("  - May waste computation on duplicate tasks")
        print("  - Configure thresholds carefully")
        
    finally:
        spark.stop()


# ============================================================================
# 6. Delay Scheduling Pattern
# ============================================================================

def delay_scheduling_pattern():
    """
    Delay Scheduling: Waits for a short time to achieve better data locality
    instead of immediately launching tasks on any available node.
    
    Use Case: Optimizing for data locality in shared clusters
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("6. DELAY SCHEDULING PATTERN")
    print("="*80)
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("Delay_Scheduling_Pattern") \
        .config("spark.locality.wait", "3s") \
        .config("spark.locality.wait.node", "5s") \
        .config("spark.locality.wait.process", "10s") \
        .config("spark.locality.wait.rack", "2s") \
        .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "6") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    try:
        # Create sample data representing scheduling decisions
        scheduling_events = [
            (1, "task_1", "node_1", "node_1", 0, "PROCESS_LOCAL", "immediate"),
            (2, "task_2", "node_2", "node_3", 500, "NODE_LOCAL", "delayed_500ms"),
            (3, "task_3", "node_1", "node_1", 0, "PROCESS_LOCAL", "immediate"),
            (4, "task_4", "node_3", "node_3", 1000, "PROCESS_LOCAL", "delayed_1s"),
            (5, "task_5", "node_2", "node_4", 3000, "RACK_LOCAL", "delayed_3s"),
            (6, "task_6", "node_1", "node_2", 2000, "NODE_LOCAL", "delayed_2s"),
            (7, "task_7", "node_3", "node_3", 0, "PROCESS_LOCAL", "immediate"),
            (8, "task_8", "node_2", "node_5", 5000, "ANY", "delayed_5s_timeout")
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("task_id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("task_name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("preferred_node", StringType(), False),
            StructField("actual_node", StringType(), False),
            StructField("delay_ms", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("locality_achieved", StringType(), False),
            StructField("scheduling_decision", StringType(), False)
        ])
        
        events_df = spark.createDataFrame(scheduling_events, schema)
        
        print("\nScheduling Events with Delay Decisions:")
        events_df.show(truncate=False)
        
        # Analyze delay scheduling effectiveness
        print("\nDelay Scheduling Analysis:")
        
        # Locality achievement rates
        locality_stats = events_df.groupBy("locality_achieved") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("count"),
                avg("delay_ms").alias("avg_delay_ms")
            ) \
            .orderBy("locality_achieved")
        
        print("\nLocality Achievement:")
        locality_stats.show()
        
        # Decision type distribution
        decision_stats = events_df.groupBy("scheduling_decision") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("count")
            )
        
        print("\nScheduling Decisions:")
        decision_stats.show(truncate=False)
        
        # Simulate delay scheduling algorithm
        print("\nDelay Scheduling Algorithm Simulation:")
        print("-" * 60)
        
        # Configuration
        max_wait_times = {
            "PROCESS_LOCAL": 10000,  # 10 seconds
            "NODE_LOCAL": 5000,      # 5 seconds
            "RACK_LOCAL": 2000,      # 2 seconds
            "ANY": 0                 # No wait
        }
        
        print("\nConfiguration:")
        for level, wait_time in max_wait_times.items():
            print(f"  {level}: {wait_time} ms max wait")
        
        print("\nTask Scheduling Simulation:")
        
        for row in events_df.collect():
            print(f"\n{'='*60}")
            print(f"Task: {row['task_name']}")
            print(f"  Preferred Node: {row['preferred_node']}")
            print(f"  Available Node: {row['actual_node']}")
            
            # Determine if nodes match
            if row['preferred_node'] == row['actual_node']:
                print(f"  Decision: Schedule immediately (PROCESS_LOCAL)")
                print(f"  Delay: 0 ms")
            else:
                print(f"  Decision: Wait for preferred node")
                print(f"  Delay: {row['delay_ms']} ms")
                
                # Check if delay was worth it
                if row['delay_ms'] < max_wait_times.get(row['locality_achieved'], 0):
                    print(f"  Result: Achieved {row['locality_achieved']} within timeout")
                else:
                    print(f"  Result: Timeout - scheduled on {row['actual_node']}")
            
            print(f"  Final Locality: {row['locality_achieved']}")
        
        # Calculate efficiency metrics
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("Efficiency Metrics:")
        
        # Locality improvement rate
        process_local_count = events_df.filter(
            col("locality_achieved") == "PROCESS_LOCAL"
        ).count()
        total_count = events_df.count()
        
        print(f"\n  Process Local Rate: {(process_local_count/total_count)*100:.2f}%")
        
        # Average delay for better locality
        avg_delay = events_df.filter(col("delay_ms") > 0).agg(
            avg("delay_ms")
        ).collect()[0][0]
        
        print(f"  Average Delay for Better Locality: {avg_delay:.2f} ms")
        
        # Create a detailed scheduling timeline
        print("\nScheduling Timeline:")
        timeline_df = events_df.select(
            "task_name",
            "delay_ms",
            "locality_achieved",
            "scheduling_decision"
        ).orderBy("delay_ms")
        
        timeline_df.show(truncate=False)
        
        # Performance comparison
        print("\nPerformance Comparison:")
        
        # Calculate data transfer costs (simulated)
        transfer_costs = events_df.withColumn(
            "data_transfer_cost",
            when(col("locality_achieved") == "PROCESS_LOCAL", lit(0))
            .when(col("locality_achieved") == "NODE_LOCAL", lit(10))
            .when(col("locality_achieved") == "RACK_LOCAL", lit(50))
            .otherwise(lit(100))
        )
        
        avg_transfer_cost = transfer_costs.agg(
            avg("data_transfer_cost")
        ).collect()[0][0]
        
        print(f"  Average Data Transfer Cost: {avg_transfer_cost:.2f} units")
        
        # Total cost (delay + transfer)
        total_cost_df = transfer_costs.withColumn(
            "total_cost",
            col("delay_ms") / 10 + col("data_transfer_cost")  # Normalize delay
        )
        
        avg_total_cost = total_cost_df.agg(
            avg("total_cost")
        ).collect()[0][0]
        
        print(f"  Average Total Cost (Delay + Transfer): {avg_total_cost:.2f} units")
        
        #
```python
        # Compare with no-delay scheduling
        print("\nComparison with No-Delay Scheduling:")
        
        # Simulate immediate scheduling (worst locality)
        immediate_transfer_cost = 100 * 0.5 + 50 * 0.3 + 10 * 0.2  # Weighted average
        print(f"  No-Delay Average Transfer Cost: {immediate_transfer_cost:.2f} units")
        print(f"  Delay Scheduling Transfer Cost: {avg_transfer_cost:.2f} units")
        
        improvement = ((immediate_transfer_cost - avg_transfer_cost) / immediate_transfer_cost) * 100
        print(f"  Improvement: {improvement:.2f}%")
        
        # Show delay distribution
        print("\nDelay Distribution:")
        delay_buckets = events_df.withColumn(
            "delay_bucket",
            when(col("delay_ms") == 0, lit("0ms (immediate)"))
            .when(col("delay_ms") <= 1000, lit("1-1000ms"))
            .when(col("delay_ms") <= 3000, lit("1001-3000ms"))
            .otherwise(lit(">3000ms"))
        )
        
        delay_distribution = delay_buckets.groupBy("delay_bucket") \
            .agg(count("*").alias("count")) \
            .orderBy("delay_bucket")
        
        delay_distribution.show(truncate=False)
        
        # Advanced: Show node utilization
        print("\nNode Utilization:")
        node_util = events_df.groupBy("actual_node") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("tasks_executed"),
                avg("delay_ms").alias("avg_delay")
            ) \
            .orderBy("tasks_executed", ascending=False)
        
        node_util.show()
        
        print("\nDelay Scheduling Benefits:")
        print("  - Improved data locality")
        print("  - Reduced network traffic")
        print("  - Better cluster resource utilization")
        print("  - Configurable wait times per locality level")
        
        print("\nBest Practices:")
        print("  - Set appropriate wait times based on cluster size")
        print("  - Monitor locality metrics")
        print("  - Balance delay vs. resource utilization")
        print("  - Consider job characteristics (I/O vs CPU bound)")
        
        # Create a comprehensive summary
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("DELAY SCHEDULING SUMMARY")
        print("="*60)
        
        summary_stats = events_df.agg(
            count("*").alias("total_tasks"),
            sum(when(col("locality_achieved") == "PROCESS_LOCAL", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("process_local"),
            sum(when(col("locality_achieved") == "NODE_LOCAL", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("node_local"),
            sum(when(col("locality_achieved") == "RACK_LOCAL", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("rack_local"),
            sum(when(col("locality_achieved") == "ANY", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("any_locality"),
            avg("delay_ms").alias("avg_delay_ms"),
            max("delay_ms").alias("max_delay_ms")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        print(f"\nTotal Tasks: {summary_stats['total_tasks']}")
        print(f"\nLocality Distribution:")
        print(f"  PROCESS_LOCAL: {summary_stats['process_local']} ({(summary_stats['process_local']/summary_stats['total_tasks'])*100:.1f}%)")
        print(f"  NODE_LOCAL: {summary_stats['node_local']} ({(summary_stats['node_local']/summary_stats['total_tasks'])*100:.1f}%)")
        print(f"  RACK_LOCAL: {summary_stats['rack_local']} ({(summary_stats['rack_local']/summary_stats['total_tasks'])*100:.1f}%)")
        print(f"  ANY: {summary_stats['any_locality']} ({(summary_stats['any_locality']/summary_stats['total_tasks'])*100:.1f}%)")
        print(f"\nDelay Statistics:")
        print(f"  Average Delay: {summary_stats['avg_delay_ms']:.2f} ms")
        print(f"  Maximum Delay: {summary_stats['max_delay_ms']} ms")
        
    finally:
        spark.stop()

def compare_all_scheduling_patterns():
    """
    Comprehensive comparison of all task scheduling patterns
    with performance metrics and use case recommendations.
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("COMPREHENSIVE SCHEDULING PATTERNS COMPARISON")

    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("Scheduling_Patterns_Comparison") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    try:
        # Create comparison data
        comparison_data = [
            ("FIFO", "Simple", "High", "Low", "Batch Processing", "Head-of-line blocking"),
            ("Fair", "Medium", "Medium", "Medium", "Multi-tenant", "Complex configuration"),
            ("Priority", "Medium", "Low", "High", "SLA-critical jobs", "Potential starvation"),
            ("Locality-Aware", "Complex", "High", "Medium", "Large datasets", "May delay execution"),
            ("Speculative", "Complex", "Medium", "Low", "Heterogeneous clusters", "Resource overhead"),
            ("Delay", "Complex", "High", "Medium", "Data-intensive jobs", "Increased latency")
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("pattern", StringType(), False),
            StructField("complexity", StringType(), False),
            StructField("efficiency", StringType(), False),
            StructField("predictability", StringType(), False),
            StructField("best_for", StringType(), False),
            StructField("main_drawback", StringType(), False)
        ])
        
        comparison_df = spark.createDataFrame(comparison_data, schema)
        
        print("\nScheduling Patterns Overview:")
        comparison_df.show(truncate=False)
        
        # Performance characteristics
        performance_data = [
            ("FIFO", 100, 90, 50, 70, 80),
            ("Fair", 85, 95, 70, 80, 85),
            ("Priority", 90, 70, 90, 75, 75),
            ("Locality-Aware", 95, 85, 60, 90, 80),
            ("Speculative", 85, 80, 65, 85, 70),
            ("Delay", 90, 90, 55, 95, 75)
        ]
        
        perf_schema = StructType([
            StructField("pattern", StringType(), False),
            StructField("throughput", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("fairness", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("latency", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("resource_efficiency", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("scalability", IntegerType(), False)
        ])

             col("resource_efficiency") + col("scalability")) / 5

        overall_scores.show()
        
        # Use case recommendations

        use_cases = [

            ("Big Data Processing", "Locality-Aware", "Minimize network data transfer"),
            ("Unreliable Infrastructure", "Speculative", "Handle slow/failing nodes"),

        for use_case, pattern, reason in use_cases:

        # Configuration examples

        print("CONFIGURATION EXAMPLES")

        configs = {
            "FIFO": [
                ("spark.scheduler.mode", "FIFO"),
                ("spark.scheduler.revive.interval", "1s")

            "Fair": [

                ("spark.scheduler.pool", "production")
            ],
            "Priority": [

            "Locality-Aware": [

                ("spark.locality.wait.node", "5s"),

            ],
            "Speculative": [

            ],

        print("""
        1. Do you have multiple concurrent users/jobs?
           YES -> Consider FAIR scheduling

        2. Do you have strict SLA requirements?
           YES -> Consider PRIORITY scheduling

        best_practices = [

            "Tune locality wait times based on cluster characteristics",
            "Consider combining multiple patterns for complex workloads",
            "Test configuration changes in staging environment",

        ]
        
        for i, practice in enumerate(best_practices, 1):

def create_fair_scheduler_xml():
    """
    Creates a sample fairscheduler.xml configuration file
    for Fair scheduling pattern.
    """
    xml_content = """<?xml version="1.0"?>
<allocations>
  <!-- Pool for interactive queries -->
  <pool name="interactive">
    <schedulingMode>FAIR</schedulingMode>
    <weight>2</weight>
    <minShare>2</minShare>
  </pool>
  
  <!-- Pool for batch jobs -->
  <pool name="batch">
    <schedulingMode>FIFO</schedulingMode>
    <weight>1</weight>
    <minShare>1</minShare>
  </pool>
  
  <!-- Pool for critical jobs -->
  <pool name="critical">
    <schedulingMode>FAIR</schedulingMode>
    <weight>3</weight>
    <minShare>4</minShare>
  </pool>
  
  <!-- Default pool -->
  <pool name="default">
    <schedulingMode>FAIR</schedulingMode>
    <weight>1</weight>
    <minShare>0</minShare>
  </pool>
</allocations>
"""
    
    with open("fairscheduler.xml", "w") as f:
        f.write(xml_content)
    
    print("Created fairscheduler.xml configuration file")

def simulate_workload(spark, num_tasks=100, pattern="FIFO"):
    """
    Simulates a realistic workload for testing scheduling patterns.
    
    Args:
        spark: SparkSession instance
        num_tasks: Number of tasks to simulate
        pattern: Scheduling pattern to use
    """
    print(f"\nSimulating {num_tasks} tasks with {pattern} scheduling...")
    
    # Generate random task data
    import random
    
    tasks = []
    for i in range(num_tasks):
        task = (
            i,
            f"task_{i}",
            random.randint(1, 5),  # priority
            random.randint(100, 1000),  # data size
            random.choice(["node_1", "node_2", "node_3", "node_4"])  # preferred node
        )
        tasks.append(task)
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("task_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("task_name", StringType(), False),
        StructField("priority", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("data_size", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("preferred_node", StringType(), False)
    ])
    
    tasks_df = spark.createDataFrame(tasks, schema)
    
    # Process based on pattern
    if pattern == "FIFO":
        ordered_tasks = tasks_df.orderBy("task_id")
    elif pattern == "Priority":
        ordered_tasks = tasks_df.orderBy(col("priority").desc(), "task_id")
    elif pattern == "Fair":
        ordered_tasks = tasks_df.orderBy("task_id")  # Fair shares resources
    else:
        ordered_tasks = tasks_df
    
    # Execute tasks
    start_time = time.time()
    
    result = ordered_tasks.agg(
        count("*").alias("total_tasks"),
        sum("data_size").alias("total_data_size"),
        avg("priority").alias("avg_priority")
    ).collect()[0]
    
    end_time = time.time()
    
    print(f"\nWorkload Simulation Results:")
    print(f"  Total Tasks: {result['total_tasks']}")
    print(f"  Total Data Size: {result['total_data_size']} MB")
    print(f"  Average Priority: {result['avg_priority']:.2f}")
    print(f"  Execution Time: {(end_time - start_time):.2f} seconds")
    
    return ordered_tasks

def hybrid_scheduling_pattern():
    """
    Demonstrates a hybrid approach combining multiple scheduling patterns
    for optimal performance in production environments.
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("HYBRID SCHEDULING PATTERN (ADVANCED)")
    print("="*80)
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("Hybrid_Scheduling") \
        .config("spark.scheduler.mode", "FAIR") \
        .config("spark.speculation", "true") \
        .config("spark.speculation.multiplier", "1.5") \
        .config("spark.locality.wait", "3s") \
        .config("spark.locality.wait.node", "5s") \
        .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "8") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    try:
        print("\nHybrid Configuration:")
        print("  Base: FAIR scheduling for multi-tenancy")
        print("  + Speculative execution for fault tolerance")
        print("  + Locality-aware scheduling for efficiency")
        print("  + Dynamic resource allocation")
        
        # Create mixed workload
        workload_data = [
            (1, "interactive_query", "interactive", 5, 100, "node_1", 50),
            (2, "batch_etl", "batch", 2, 1000, "node_2", 500),
            (3, "ml_training", "ml", 4, 2000, "node_3", 1200),
            (4, "interactive_dashboard", "interactive", 5, 150, "node_1", 75),
            (5, "batch_report", "batch", 2, 800, "node_2", 400),
            (6, "ml_inference", "ml", 3, 300, "node_3", 150),
            (7, "critical_alert", "critical", 5, 50, "node_1", 25),
            (8, "batch_archive", "batch", 1, 1500, "node_4", 750)
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("job_id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("job_name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("pool", StringType(), False),
            StructField("priority", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("data_size_mb", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("preferred_node", StringType(), False),
            StructField("estimated_runtime_ms", IntegerType(), False)
        ])
        
        workload_df = spark.createDataFrame(workload_data, schema)
        
        print("\nMixed Workload:")
        workload_df.show(truncate=False)
        
        # Apply hybrid scheduling logic
        print("\nApplying Hybrid Scheduling Strategy:")
        
        # 1. Group by pool (Fair scheduling)
        print("\n1. Fair Scheduling - Pool Distribution:")
        pool_stats = workload_df.groupBy("pool") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("job_count"),
                sum("data_size_mb").alias("total_data_mb"),
                avg("priority").alias("avg_priority")
            )
        pool_stats.show()
        
        # 2. Within each pool, apply priority
        print("\n2. Priority Within Pools:")
        prioritized = workload_df.withColumn(
            "execution_order",
            row_number().over(
                Window.partitionBy("pool")
                .orderBy(col("priority").desc(), "job_id")
            )
        )
        prioritized.select("job_name", "pool", "priority", "execution_order").show(truncate=False)
        
        # 3. Apply locality awareness
        print("\n3. Locality-Aware Assignment:")
        locality_assigned = prioritized.withColumn(
            "locality_level",
            when(col("preferred_node").isNotNull(), lit("PROCESS_LOCAL"))
            .otherwise(lit("ANY"))
        )
        
        locality_assigned.select(
            "job_name", "preferred_node", "locality_level"
        ).show(truncate=False)
        
        # 4. Identify candidates for speculative execution
        print("\n4. Speculative Execution Candidates:")
        median_runtime = workload_df.approxQuantile("estimated_runtime_ms", [0.5], 0.01)[0]
        speculation_threshold = median_runtime * 1.5
        
        speculation_candidates = workload_df.filter(
            col("estimated_runtime_ms") > speculation_threshold
        )
        
        print(f"  Median Runtime: {median_runtime} ms")
        print(f"  Speculation Threshold: {speculation_threshold} ms")
        print(f"  Candidates: {speculation_candidates.count()} jobs")
        speculation_candidates.select("job_name", "estimated_runtime_ms").show()
        
        # 5. Calculate resource allocation
        print("\n5. Dynamic Resource Allocation:")
        
        # Pool weights
        pool_weights = {
            "critical": 5,
            "interactive": 3,
            "ml": 2,
            "batch": 1
        }
        
        total_weight = sum(pool_weights.values())
        
        resource_allocation = workload_df.withColumn(
            "pool_weight",
            when(col("pool") == "critical", lit(pool_weights["critical"]))
            .when(col("pool") == "interactive", lit(pool_weights["interactive"]))
            .when(col("pool") == "ml", lit(pool_weights["ml"]))
            .otherwise(lit(pool_weights["batch"]))
        ).withColumn(
            "resource_share_pct",
            (col("pool_weight") / total_weight * 100)
        )
        
        resource_summary = resource_allocation.groupBy("pool") \
            .agg(
                first("resource_share_pct").alias("resource_share_pct"),
                count("*").alias("jobs")
            )
        
        resource_summary.show()
        
        # 6. Execution simulation
        print("\n6. Simulated Execution Timeline:")
        
        execution_timeline = []
        current_time = 0
        
        for row in prioritized.orderBy("pool", "execution_order").collect():
            exec_start = current_time
            exec_end = current_time + row['estimated_runtime_ms']
            
            execution_timeline.append({
                "job_name": row['job_name'],
                "pool": row['pool'],
                "start_ms": exec_start,
                "end_ms": exec_end,
                "duration_ms": row['estimated_runtime_ms']
            })
            
            # Fair scheduling - don't wait for completion in same pool
            if row['pool'] in ['interactive', 'critical']:
                current_time += row['estimated_runtime_ms'] // 2  # Parallel execution
            else:
                current_time += row['estimated_runtime_ms']
        
        timeline_schema = StructType([
            StructField("job_name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("pool", StringType(), False),
            StructField("start_ms", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("end_ms", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("duration_ms", IntegerType(), False)
        ])
        
        timeline_df = spark.createDataFrame(execution_timeline, timeline_schema)
        timeline_df.show(truncate=False)
        
        # Performance metrics
        print("\nHybrid Scheduling Performance Metrics:")
        
        total_duration = timeline_df.agg(max("end_ms")).collect()[0][0]
        sequential_duration = workload_df.agg(sum("estimated_runtime_ms")).collect()[0][0]
        
        print(f"  Sequential Execution Time: {sequential_duration} ms")
        print(f"  Hybrid Execution Time: {total_duration} ms")
        print(f"  Time Saved: {sequential_duration - total_duration} ms")
        print(f"  Efficiency Gain: {((sequential_duration - total_duration) / sequential_duration * 100):.2f}%")
        
        # Job completion by pool
        print("\nJob Completion by Pool:")
        completion_stats = timeline_df.groupBy("pool") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("jobs_completed"),
                avg("duration_ms").alias("avg_duration"),
                max("end_ms").alias("completion_time")
            )
        completion_stats.show()
        
        print("\nHybrid Scheduling Benefits:")
        print("  ✓ Fair resource sharing across pools")
        print("  ✓ Priority-based execution within pools")
        print("  ✓ Data locality optimization")
        print("  ✓ Automatic handling of stragglers")
        print("  ✓ Dynamic resource allocation")
        print("  ✓ Optimal for production workloads")
        
    finally:
        spark.stop()

def benchmark_scheduling_patterns():
    """
    Benchmarks different scheduling patterns with identical workloads
    to compare performance characteristics.
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("SCHEDULING PATTERNS PERFORMANCE BENCHMARK")
    print("="*80)
    
    patterns = ["FIFO", "FAIR"]
    results = []
    
    # Standard workload for benchmarking
    workload_size = 1000
    
    for pattern in patterns:
        print(f"\nBenchmarking {pattern} scheduling...")
        
        # Configure Spark for pattern
        spark = SparkSession.builder \
            .appName(f"Benchmark_{pattern}") \
            .config("spark.scheduler.mode", pattern) \
            .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "4") \
            .master("local[*]") \
            .getOrCreate()
        
        try:
            start_time = time.time()
            
            # Create workload
            df = spark.range(0, workload_size * 1000) \
                .withColumn("value", col("id") * 2) \
                .withColumn("category", col("id") % 10)
            
            # Perform operations
            result = df.groupBy("category") \
                .agg(
                    count("*").alias("count"),
                    sum("value").alias("sum"),
                    avg("value").alias("avg")
                ) \
                .collect()
            
            end_time = time.time()
            execution_time = end_time - start_time
            
            results.append({
                "pattern": pattern,
                "execution_time": execution_time,
                "records_processed": workload_size * 1000,
                "throughput": (workload_size * 1000) / execution_time
            })
            
            print(f"  Execution Time: {execution_time:.2f} seconds")
            print(f"  Throughput: {(workload_size * 1000) / execution_time:.2f} records/sec")
            
        finally:
            spark.stop()
    
    # Display benchmark results
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("BENCHMARK RESULTS")
    print("="*80)
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("Benchmark_Results") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    try:
        results_schema = StructType([
            StructField("pattern", StringType(), False),
            StructField("execution_time", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("records_processed", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("throughput", DoubleType(), False)
        ])
        
        results_data = [(r["pattern"], r["execution_time"], 
                        r["records_processed"], r["throughput"]) 
                       for r in results]
        
        results_df = spark.createDataFrame(results_data, results_schema)
        results_df.show()
        
        # Find best performer
        best = min(results, key=lambda x: x["execution_time"])
        print(f"\nBest Performer: {best['pattern']}")
        print(f"  Execution Time: {best['execution_time']:.2f} seconds")
        
    finally:
        spark.stop()

def create_scheduling_examples():
    """
    Creates practical code examples for each scheduling pattern.
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PRACTICAL CODE EXAMPLES")
    print("="*80)
    
    examples = {
        "FIFO": '''
# FIFO Scheduling Example
spark = SparkSession.builder \\
    .appName("FIFO_Example") \\
    .config("spark.scheduler.mode", "FIFO") \\
    .getOrCreate()

# Jobs execute in submission order
job1 = spark.range(1000000).count()  # Executes first
job2 = spark.range(2000000).count()  # Waits for job1
job3 = spark.range(1500000).count()  # Waits for job2
''',
        "FAIR": '''
# Fair Scheduling Example
spark = SparkSession.builder \\
    .appName("Fair_Example") \\
    .config("spark.scheduler.mode", "FAIR") \\
    .config("spark.scheduler.allocation.file", "fairscheduler.xml") \\
    .getOrCreate()

# Set pool for each job
spark.sparkContext.setLocalProperty("spark.scheduler.pool", "interactive")
interactive_query = spark.sql("SELECT * FROM table WHERE condition")

spark.sparkContext.setLocalProperty("spark.scheduler.pool", "batch")
batch_job = spark.sql("SELECT * FROM large_table")
''',
        "PRIORITY": '''
# Priority Scheduling Example (using Fair pools with weights)
spark = SparkSession.builder \\
    .appName("Priority_Example") \\
    .config("spark.scheduler.mode", "FAIR") \\
    .getOrCreate()

# High priority job
spark.sparkContext.setLocalProperty("spark.scheduler.pool", "high_priority")
critical_job = spark.sql("SELECT * FROM alerts WHERE severity = 'CRITICAL'")

# Low priority job
spark.sparkContext.setLocalProperty("spark.scheduler.pool", "low_priority")
report_job = spark.sql("SELECT * FROM logs WHERE date = '2024-01-01'")
''',
        "LOCALITY_AWARE": '''
# Locality-Aware Scheduling Example

    .appName("Locality_Example") \\
    .config("spark.locality.wait", "3s") \\
    .config("spark.locality.wait.node", "5s") \\
    .config("spark.locality.wait.process", "10s") \\
    .getOrCreate()

# Read data from HDFS - Spark will schedule tasks on data nodes
df = spark.read.parquet("hdfs:///data/large_dataset")
result = df.groupBy("category").agg(sum("amount"))
''',
        "SPECULATIVE": '''
# Speculative Execution Example

    .appName("Speculative_Example") \\

    .config("spark.speculation.multiplier", "1.5") \\
    .config("spark.speculation.quantile", "0.75") \\
    .getOrCreate()

# Long-running job - stragglers will be detected and re-executed

result = large_df.groupBy("key").agg(complex_aggregation())
''',
        "DELAY": '''

    .config("spark.locality.wait.rack", "2s") \\
    .config("spark.scheduler.minRegisteredResourcesRatio", "0.8") \\
    .getOrCreate()

# Spark waits for better locality before scheduling
df = spark.read.parquet("hdfs:///data/partitioned_data")
result = df.filter("date >= '2024-01-01'").groupBy("region").count()
'''

    for pattern, code in examples.items():

def create_monitoring_dashboard():
    """
    Creates a monitoring dashboard for tracking scheduling metrics.
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("SCHEDULING MONITORING DASHBOARD")
    print("="*80)
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("Monitoring_Dashboard") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    try:
        # Simulate monitoring data
        monitoring_data = [
            ("2024-01-01 10:00:00", "FIFO", 10, 5, 2, 95.5, 1200),
            ("2024-01-01 10:05:00", "FIFO", 12, 6, 3, 92.3, 1350),
            ("2024-01-01 10:10:00", "FAIR", 15, 8, 1, 98.1, 980),
            ("2024-01-01 10:15:00", "FAIR", 14, 7, 2, 96.7, 1050),
            ("2024-01-01 10:20:00", "FAIR", 16, 9, 1, 97.8, 920),
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("timestamp", StringType(), False),
            StructField("scheduler_mode", StringType(), False),
            StructField("active_jobs", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("completed_jobs", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("failed_jobs", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("cpu_utilization", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("avg_task_duration_ms", IntegerType(), False)
        ])
        
        monitoring_df = spark.createDataFrame(monitoring_data, schema)
        
        print("\nReal-time Scheduling Metrics:")
        monitoring_df.show(truncate=False)
        
        # Calculate KPIs
        print("\nKey Performance Indicators:")
        
        kpis = monitoring_df.agg(
            avg("active_jobs").alias("avg_active_jobs"),
            sum("completed_jobs").alias("total_completed"),
            sum("failed_jobs").alias("total_failed"),
            avg("cpu_utilization").alias("avg_cpu_utilization"),
            avg("avg_task_duration_ms").alias("avg_task_duration")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        print(f"  Average Active Jobs: {kpis['avg_active_jobs']:.2f}")
        print(f"  Total Completed Jobs: {kpis['total_completed']}")
        print(f"  Total Failed Jobs: {kpis['total_failed']}")
        print(f"  Average CPU Utilization: {kpis['avg_cpu_utilization']:.2f}%")
        print(f"  Average Task Duration: {kpis['avg_task_duration']:.2f} ms")
        
        # Success rate
        success_rate = (kpis['total_completed'] / 
                       (kpis['total_completed'] + kpis['total_failed'])) * 100
        print(f"  Job Success Rate: {success_rate:.2f}%")
        
        # Compare schedulers
        print("\nScheduler Comparison:")
        scheduler_comparison = monitoring_df.groupBy("scheduler_mode") \
            .agg(
                avg("cpu_utilization").alias("avg_cpu"),
                avg("avg_task_duration_ms").alias("avg_duration"),
                sum("completed_jobs").alias("completed")
            )
        scheduler_comparison.show()
        
        # Alerts and recommendations
        print("\nAlerts and Recommendations:")
        
        for row in monitoring_df.collect():
            if row['failed_jobs'] > 2:
                print(f"  ⚠ HIGH FAILURE RATE at {row['timestamp']}")
            if row['cpu_utilization'] < 80:
                print(f"  ℹ LOW CPU UTILIZATION at {row['timestamp']}: {row['cpu_utilization']:.1f}%")
            if row['avg_task_duration_ms'] > 1200:
                print(f"  ⚠ SLOW TASKS at {row['timestamp']}: {row['avg_task_duration_ms']} ms")
        
    finally:
        spark.stop()

╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                    PYSPARK SCHEDULING PATTERNS SUMMARY                       ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

This comprehensive guide covered 6 essential task scheduling patterns:

1. FIFO (First-In-First-Out)
   → Best for: Single-user batch processing, development
   → Key benefit: Simplicity and predictability

2. FAIR Scheduling
   → Best for: Multi-tenant environments, shared clusters
   → Key benefit: Resource sharing and fairness

3. PRIORITY Scheduling
   → Best for: SLA-critical applications, time-sensitive jobs
   → Key benefit: Business-driven execution order

4. LOCALITY-AWARE Scheduling
   → Best for: Large-scale data processing, HDFS-based workloads
   → Key benefit: Minimized network transfer

5. SPECULATIVE Execution
   → Best for: Heterogeneous clusters, handling stragglers
   → Key benefit: Fault tolerance and reduced tail latency

6. DELAY Scheduling
   → Best for: Data-intensive workloads, optimizing locality
   → Key benefit: Better data locality with controlled delay

║                         COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID                             ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

1. Using FIFO in multi-tenant environments
   → Switch to FAIR scheduling

2. Not setting locality wait times
   → Configure based on cluster characteristics

3. Aggressive speculation without monitoring
   → Tune parameters and monitor resource usage

4. Ignoring data locality metrics
   → Optimize data placement and locality settings

5. Not configuring pool weights properly
   → Review and adjust based on business priorities

6. Disabling speculation on heterogeneous clusters
   → Enable and tune for better fault tolerance

7. Setting partition count too low
   → Use at least 2-3x number of cores

8. Not using dynamic allocation
   → Enable for better resource utilization

9. Ignoring Spark UI metrics
   → Regular monitoring is essential

10. One-size-fits-all configuration
    → Tune per workload type

def interactive_pattern_selector():
    """
    Interactive tool to help select the right scheduling pattern.
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("INTERACTIVE SCHEDULING PATTERN SELECTOR")
    print("="*80)
    
    print("\nAnswer the following questions to get a recommendation:\n")
    
    # Simulated questions and answers (in real implementation, use input())
    questions = {
        "multi_user": {
            "question": "Do you have multiple concurrent users/applications?",
            "answer": "yes",  # Simulated
            "weight": {"FAIR": 3, "FIFO": -2}
        },
        "sla": {
            "question": "Do you have strict SLA requirements?",
            "answer": "yes",  # Simulated
            "weight": {"PRIORITY": 3, "FAIR": 2}
        },
        "data_size": {
            "question": "Are you processing large datasets (>1TB)?",
            "answer": "yes",  # Simulated
            "weight": {"LOCALITY_AWARE": 3, "DELAY": 2}
        },
        "reliability": {
            "question": "Do you have heterogeneous or unreliable nodes?",
            "answer": "yes",  # Simulated
            "weight": {"SPECULATIVE": 3}
        },
        "latency": {
            "question": "Is low latency critical?",
            "answer": "no",  # Simulated
            "weight": {"DELAY": -1, "FIFO": 1}
        }
    }
    
    scores = {
        "FIFO": 0,
        "FAIR": 0,
        "PRIORITY": 0,
        "LOCALITY_AWARE": 0,
        "SPECULATIVE": 0,
        "DELAY": 0
    }
    
    print("Simulated Answers:")
    for key, q_data in questions.items():
        print(f"Q: {q_data['question']}")
        print(f"A: {q_data['answer']}")
        
        if q_data['answer'].lower() == 'yes':
            for pattern, weight in q_data['weight'].items():
                scores[pattern] += weight
        print()
    
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("RECOMMENDATION")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Sort by score
    sorted_patterns = sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    
    print("\nPattern Scores:")
    for pattern, score in sorted_patterns:
        if score > 0:
            print(f"  {pattern}: {'★' * score} ({score} points)")
    
    print("\nRecommended Configuration:")
    top_patterns = [p for p, s in sorted_patterns if s > 0][:3]
    
    if len(top_patterns) > 1:
        print(f"  Primary: {top_patterns[0]}")
        print(f"  Combine with: {', '.join(top_patterns[1:])}")
    else:
        print(f"  Pattern: {top_patterns[0] if top_patterns else 'FIFO (default)'}")
    
    print("\nSuggested Spark Configuration:")
    if "FAIR" in top_patterns:
        print("  spark.scheduler.mode = FAIR")
        print("  spark.scheduler.allocation.file = fairscheduler.xml")
    
    if "LOCALITY_AWARE" in top_patterns or "DELAY" in top_patterns:
        print("  spark.locality.wait = 3s")
        print("  spark.locality.wait.node = 5s")
    
    if "SPECULATIVE" in top_patterns:
        print("  spark.speculation = true")
        print("  spark.speculation.multiplier = 1.5")
        print("  spark.speculation.quantile = 0.75")

## Sample fairscheduler.xml Configuration File

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<allocations>
  <!-- Interactive queries pool -->
  <pool name="interactive">
    <schedulingMode>FAIR</schedulingMode>
    <weight>3</weight>
    <minShare>4</minShare>
  </pool>
  
  <!-- Batch processing pool -->
  <pool name="batch">
    <schedulingMode>FIFO</schedulingMode>
    <weight>1</weight>
    <minShare>2</minShare>
  </pool>
  
  <!-- Critical/high-priority jobs pool -->
  <pool name="critical">
    <schedulingMode>FAIR</schedulingMode>
    <weight>5</weight>
    <minShare>6</minShare>
  </pool>
  
  <!-- Machine learning pool -->
  <pool name="ml">
    <schedulingMode>FAIR</schedulingMode>
    <weight>2</weight>
    <minShare>3</minShare>
  </pool>
  
  <!-- Default pool for unassigned jobs -->
  <pool name="default">
    <schedulingMode>FAIR</schedulingMode>
    <weight>1</weight>
    <minShare>1</minShare>
  </pool>
</allocations>
```

# ============================================================================
# ADDITIONAL HELPER FUNCTIONS FOR PRODUCTION USE
# ============================================================================

def validate_scheduler_config(spark):
    """
    Validates the current scheduler configuration.
    
    Args:
        spark: SparkSession instance
    
    Returns:
        dict: Validation results
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("SCHEDULER CONFIGURATION VALIDATION")
    print("="*80)
    
    config = spark.sparkContext.getConf()
    
    validation_results = {
        "scheduler_mode": config.get("spark.scheduler.mode", "FIFO"),
        "issues": [],
        "warnings": [],
        "recommendations": []
    }
    
    # Check scheduler mode
    scheduler_mode = validation_results["scheduler_mode"]
    print(f"\nScheduler Mode: {scheduler_mode}")
    
    # Validate FAIR scheduling configuration
    if scheduler_mode == "FAIR":
        allocation_file = config.get("spark.scheduler.allocation.file", None)
        
        if not allocation_file:
            validation_results["warnings"].append(
                "FAIR mode enabled but no allocation file specified"
            )
            validation_results["recommendations"].append(
                "Set spark.scheduler.allocation.file to fairscheduler.xml"
            )
        else:
            print(f"Allocation File: {allocation_file}")
            
            # Check if file exists
            import os
            if not os.path.exists(allocation_file):
                validation_results["issues"].append(
                    f"Allocation file not found: {allocation_file}"
                )
    
    # Check speculation settings
    speculation = config.get("spark.speculation", "false")
    print(f"\nSpeculation Enabled: {speculation}")
    
    if speculation == "true":
        multiplier = config.get("spark.speculation.multiplier", "1.5")
        quantile = config.get("spark.speculation.quantile", "0.75")
        
        print(f"  Multiplier: {multiplier}")
        print(f"  Quantile: {quantile}")
        
        if float(multiplier) < 1.2:
            validation_results["warnings"].append(
                "Speculation multiplier is low, may trigger too frequently"
            )
        
        if float(quantile) < 0.5:
            validation_results["warnings"].append(
                "Speculation quantile is low, may cause excessive speculation"
            )
    
    # Check locality settings
    locality_wait = config.get("spark.locality.wait", "3s")
    print(f"\nLocality Wait: {locality_wait}")
    
    # Check dynamic allocation
    dynamic_allocation = config.get("spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled", "false")
    print(f"Dynamic Allocation: {dynamic_allocation}")
    
    if dynamic_allocation == "true":
        min_executors = config.get("spark.dynamicAllocation.minExecutors", "0")
        max_executors = config.get("spark.dynamicAllocation.maxExecutors", "infinity")
        
        print(f"  Min Executors: {min_executors}")
        print(f"  Max Executors: {max_executors}")
        
        if max_executors == "infinity":
            validation_results["warnings"].append(
                "No maximum executor limit set, may consume all cluster resources"
            )
            validation_results["recommendations"].append(
                "Set spark.dynamicAllocation.maxExecutors to a reasonable limit"
            )
    
    # Print validation summary
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("VALIDATION SUMMARY")
    print("="*80)
    
    if validation_results["issues"]:
        print("\n❌ ISSUES FOUND:")
        for issue in validation_results["issues"]:
            print(f"  • {issue}")
    
    if validation_results["warnings"]:
        print("\n⚠ WARNINGS:")
        for warning in validation_results["warnings"]:
            print(f"  • {warning}")
    
    if validation_results["recommendations"]:
        print("\n💡 RECOMMENDATIONS:")
        for rec in validation_results["recommendations"]:
            print(f"  • {rec}")
    
    if not validation_results["issues"] and not validation_results["warnings"]:
        print("\n✅ Configuration looks good!")
    
    return validation_results


def export_scheduling_metrics(spark, output_path="scheduling_metrics.json"):
    """
    Exports scheduling metrics to a JSON file.
    
    Args:
        spark: SparkSession instance
        output_path: Path to output file
    """
    import json
    from datetime import datetime
    
    print(f"\n[INFO] Exporting scheduling metrics to {output_path}...")
    
    sc = spark.sparkContext
    config = sc.getConf()
    
    metrics = {
        "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
        "configuration": {
            "scheduler_mode": config.get("spark.scheduler.mode", "FIFO"),
            "speculation": config.get("spark.speculation", "false"),
            "locality_wait": config.get("spark.locality.wait", "3s"),
            "dynamic_allocation": config.get("spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled", "false")
        },
        "runtime_metrics": {
            "active_jobs": len(sc.statusTracker().getActiveJobIds()),
            "active_stages": len(sc.statusTracker().getActiveStageIds())
        }
    }
    
    with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
        json.dump(metrics, f, indent=2)
    
    print(f"[SUCCESS] Metrics exported to {output_path}")

def run_performance_test(pattern_name, spark_config, workload_func):
    """
    Runs a performance test for a specific scheduling pattern.
    
    Args:
        pattern_name: Name of the pattern being tested
        spark_config: Dictionary of Spark configuration
        workload_func: Function that executes the workload
    
    Returns:
        dict: Performance metrics
    """
    print(f"\n[INFO] Running performance test for {pattern_name}...")
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName(f"PerfTest_{pattern_name}")
    
    for key, value in spark_config.items():
        spark = spark.config(key, value)
    
    spark = spark.master("local[*]").getOrCreate()
    
    try:
        start_time = time.time()
        
        # Run workload
        result = workload_func(spark)
        
        end_time = time.time()
        execution_time = end_time - start_time
        
        metrics = {
            "pattern": pattern_name,
            "execution_time_seconds": execution_time,
            "result_count": result if
```python
            "result_count": result if isinstance(result, int) else len(result),
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat()
        }
        
        print(f"[SUCCESS] {pattern_name} completed in {execution_time:.2f} seconds")
        
        return metrics
        
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"[ERROR] Performance test failed: {str(e)}")
        return {
            "pattern": pattern_name,
            "execution_time_seconds": -1,
            "error": str(e)
        }
    finally:
        spark.stop()


def compare_pattern_performance():
    """
    Compares performance across different scheduling patterns.
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("SCHEDULING PATTERN PERFORMANCE COMPARISON")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Define test workload
    def test_workload(spark):
        df = spark.range(0, 10000000) \
            .withColumn("value", col("id") * 2) \
            .withColumn("category", col("id") % 100)
        
        result = df.groupBy("category") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("count"),
                sum("value").alias("sum"),
                avg("value").alias("avg"),
                max("value").alias("max"),
                min("value").alias("min")
            ).count()
        
        return result
    
    # Test configurations
    test_configs = {
        "FIFO_Default": {
            "spark.scheduler.mode": "FIFO",
            "spark.sql.shuffle.partitions": "200"
        },
        "FAIR_Basic": {
            "spark.scheduler.mode": "FAIR",
            "spark.sql.shuffle.partitions": "200"
        },
        "FAIR_Optimized": {
            "spark.scheduler.mode": "FAIR",
            "spark.sql.shuffle.partitions": "200",
            "spark.locality.wait": "3s",
            "spark.speculation": "true"
        }
    }
    
    results = []
    
    for config_name, config in test_configs.items():
        metrics = run_performance_test(config_name, config, test_workload)
        results.append(metrics)
        time.sleep(2)  # Brief pause between tests
    
    # Display results
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PERFORMANCE TEST RESULTS")
    print("="*80)
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("Results_Display") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    try:
        results_schema = StructType([
            StructField("pattern", StringType(), False),
            StructField("execution_time_seconds", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("result_count", IntegerType(), False)
        ])
        
        valid_results = [r for r in results if r.get("execution_time_seconds", -1) > 0]
        
        if valid_results:
            results_data = [(r["pattern"], r["execution_time_seconds"], 
                           r.get("result_count", 0)) for r in valid_results]
            
            results_df = spark.createDataFrame(results_data, results_schema)
            
            print("\nExecution Times:")
            results_df.orderBy("execution_time_seconds").show()
            
            # Calculate speedup
            baseline = max([r["execution_time_seconds"] for r in valid_results])
            
            print("\nSpeedup vs Slowest:")
            for result in valid_results:
                speedup = baseline / result["execution_time_seconds"]
                print(f"  {result['pattern']}: {speedup:.2f}x")
        
    finally:
        spark.stop()

def setup_scheduling_logger(log_file="scheduling_audit.log"):
    """
    Sets up logging for scheduling decisions and metrics.
    
    Args:
        log_file: Path to log file
    """
    import logging
    
    logger = logging.getLogger("SchedulingAudit")
    logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)
    
    # File handler
    fh = logging.FileHandler(log_file)
    fh.setLevel(logging.INFO)
    
    # Console handler
    ch = logging.StreamHandler()
    ch.setLevel(logging.INFO)
    
    # Formatter
    formatter = logging.Formatter(
        '%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s'
    )
    fh.setFormatter(formatter)
    ch.setFormatter(formatter)
    
    logger.addHandler(fh)
    logger.addHandler(ch)
    
    logger.info("Scheduling audit logger initialized")
    
    return logger


def log_scheduling_decision(logger, job_name, pool, priority, decision):
    """
    Logs a scheduling decision for audit purposes.
    
    Args:
        logger: Logger instance
        job_name: Name of the job
        pool: Scheduler pool
        priority: Job priority
        decision: Scheduling decision made
    """
    logger.info(
        f"JOB_SCHEDULED | Job: {job_name} | Pool: {pool} | "
        f"Priority: {priority} | Decision: {decision}"
    )

def comprehensive_production_example():
    """
    Comprehensive example showing production-ready scheduling setup.
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("COMPREHENSIVE PRODUCTION EXAMPLE")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Setup logger
    logger = setup_scheduling_logger()
    
    # Create Spark session with production configuration
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("Production_Scheduling_Example") \
        .config("spark.scheduler.mode", "FAIR") \
        .config("spark.scheduler.allocation.file", "fairscheduler.xml") \
        .config("spark.locality.wait", "3s") \
        .config("spark.locality.wait.node", "5s") \
        .config("spark.locality.wait.process", "10s") \
        .config("spark.speculation", "true") \
        .config("spark.speculation.interval", "100ms") \
        .config("spark.speculation.multiplier", "1.5") \
        .config("spark.speculation.quantile", "0.75") \
        .config("spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled", "true") \
        .config("spark.dynamicAllocation.minExecutors", "5") \
        .config("spark.dynamicAllocation.maxExecutors", "100") \
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true") \
        .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "200") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    try:
        # Validate configuration
        validation_results = validate_scheduler_config(spark)
        
        # Create sample jobs for different pools
        jobs = [
            {
                "name": "critical_alert_processing",
                "pool": "critical",
                "priority": 5,
                "data_size": 100
            },
            {
                "name": "interactive_dashboard_query",
                "pool": "interactive",
                "priority": 4,
                "data_size": 500
            },
            {
                "name": "batch_etl_job",
                "pool": "batch",
                "priority": 2,
                "data_size": 5000
            },
            {
                "name": "ml_model_training",
                "pool": "ml",
                "priority": 3,
                "data_size": 10000
            }
        ]
        
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("EXECUTING PRODUCTION WORKLOAD")
        print("="*80)
        
        for job in jobs:
            # Set scheduler pool
            spark.sparkContext.setLocalProperty(
                "spark.scheduler.pool", 
                job["pool"]
            )
            
            # Log scheduling decision
            log_scheduling_decision(
                logger,
                job["name"],
                job["pool"],
                job["priority"],
                f"Assigned to {job['pool']} pool"
            )
            
            print(f"\n[INFO] Executing: {job['name']}")
            print(f"  Pool: {job['pool']}")
            print(f"  Priority: {job['priority']}")
            print(f"  Data Size: {job['data_size']} MB")
            
            # Execute job
            start_time = time.time()
            
            df = spark.range(0, job['data_size'] * 1000) \
                .withColumn("job_name", lit(job['name'])) \
                .withColumn("pool", lit(job['pool'])) \
                .withColumn("value", col("id") * 2)
            
            result = df.groupBy("pool") \
                .agg(
                    count("*").alias("records"),
                    sum("value").alias("total_value"),
                    avg("value").alias("avg_value")
                ).collect()
            
            execution_time = time.time() - start_time
            
            print(f"  Execution Time: {execution_time:.2f} seconds")
            print(f"  Records Processed: {result[0]['records']:,}")
            
            # Log completion
            logger.info(
                f"JOB_COMPLETED | Job: {job['name']} | "
                f"Time: {execution_time:.2f}s | "
                f"Records: {result[0]['records']:,}"
            )
        
        # Export metrics
        export_scheduling_metrics(spark, "production_metrics.json")
        
        # Create dashboard
        create_scheduling_dashboard_html("production_dashboard.html")
        
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("PRODUCTION EXAMPLE COMPLETED")
        print("="*80)
        
        print("\n[SUCCESS] Generated files:")
        print("  - scheduling_audit.log (Audit trail)")
        print("  - production_metrics.json (Performance metrics)")
        print("  - production_dashboard.html (Monitoring dashboard)")
        
        print("\n[INFO] Key metrics:")
        print(f"  Scheduler Mode: FAIR")
        print(f"  Jobs Executed: {len(jobs)}")
        print(f"  Pools Used: {len(set(j['pool'] for j in jobs))}")
        
    finally:
        spark.stop()
        logger.info("Production example completed - Spark session closed")
