# 6. RESOURCE OPTIMIZATION PATTERN
# ============================================================================

class ResourceOptimizationPattern:
    """
    Analyzes resource usage patterns and provides optimization recommendations.
    Identifies underutilized resources and optimization opportunities.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark):
        self.spark = spark
    
    def analyze_resource_efficiency(self, monitoring_df):
        """Analyze resource efficiency and identify optimization opportunities"""
        
        # Calculate resource efficiency metrics
        df_efficiency = monitoring_df.withColumn(
            "memory_used_percent",
            (col("memory_used_gb") / col("memory_total_gb")) * 100
        ).withColumn(
            "cpu_efficiency",
            when(col("cpu_percent") < 20, "Underutilized")
            .when(col("cpu_percent") < 60, "Optimal")
            .when(col("cpu_percent") < 80, "High")
            .otherwise("Overutilized")
        ).withColumn(
            "memory_efficiency",
            when(col("memory_used_percent") < 30, "Underutilized")
            .when(col("memory_used_percent") < 70, "Optimal")
            .when(col("memory_used_percent") < 85, "High")
            .otherwise("Overutilized")
        ).withColumn(
            "disk_efficiency",
            when(col("disk_used_percent") < 40, "Underutilized")
            .when(col("disk_used_percent") < 75, "Optimal")
            .when(col("disk_used_percent") < 85, "High")
            .otherwise("Overutilized")
        )
        
        # Identify underutilized resources
        underutilized = df_efficiency.filter(
            (col("cpu_percent") < 20) |
            (col("memory_used_percent") < 30) |
            (col("disk_used_percent") < 40)
        ).groupBy("server_id", "environment") \
         .agg(
             avg("cpu_percent").alias("avg_cpu"),
             avg("memory_used_percent").alias("avg_memory"),
             avg("disk_used_percent").alias("avg_disk"),
             count("*").alias("sample_count")
         ).withColumn(
             "optimization_potential",
             when(
                 (col("avg_cpu") < 20) & 
                 (col("avg_memory") < 30), 
                 "High - Consider downsizing"
             ).when(
                 (col("avg_cpu") < 30) | 
                 (col("avg_memory") < 40),
                 "Medium - Review resource allocation"
             ).otherwise("Low")
         )
        
        # Resource right-sizing recommendations
        window_spec = Window.partitionBy("server_id").orderBy("timestamp")
        
        rightsizing = df_efficiency.withColumn(
            "cpu_p95",
            percentile_approx("cpu_percent", 0.95).over(
                Window.partitionBy("server_id")
            )
        ).withColumn(
            "memory_p95",
            percentile_approx("memory_used_percent", 0.95).over(
                Window.partitionBy("server_id")
            )
        ).select(
            "server_id", "environment", "cpu_cores", "memory_total_gb",
            "cpu_p95", "memory_p95"
        ).distinct() \
         .withColumn(
             "recommended_cpu_cores",
             when(col("cpu_p95") < 25, (col("cpu_cores") / 2).cast("int"))
             .when(col("cpu_p95") > 80, (col("cpu_cores") * 1.5).cast("int"))
             .otherwise(col("cpu_cores"))
         ).withColumn(
             "recommended_memory_gb",
             when(col("memory_p95") < 30, (col("memory_total_gb") * 0.5).cast("int"))
             .when(col("memory_p95") > 80, (col("memory_total_gb") * 1.5).cast("int"))
             .otherwise(col("memory_total_gb"))
         ).withColumn(
             "potential_savings_percent",
             ((col("cpu_cores") - col("recommended_cpu_cores")) / col("cpu_cores") * 50 +
              (col("memory_total_gb") - col("recommended_memory_gb")) / col("memory_total_gb") * 50)
         )
        
        # Cost optimization analysis
        cost_optimization = df_efficiency.withColumn(
            "estimated_hourly_cost",
            (col("cpu_cores") * 0.05 + col("memory_total_gb") * 0.01)
        ).groupBy("server_id", "environment") \
         .agg(
             first("cpu_cores").alias("cpu_cores"),
             first("memory_total_gb").alias("memory_total_gb"),
             avg("cpu_percent").alias("avg_cpu_util"),
             avg("memory_used_percent").alias("avg_memory_util"),
             first("estimated_hourly_cost").alias("current_hourly_cost")
         ).withColumn(
             "waste_score",
             (100 - col("avg_cpu_util")) * 0.5 + 
             (100 - col("avg_memory_util")) * 0.5
         ).withColumn(
             "potential_monthly_savings",
             col("current_hourly_cost") * col("waste_score") / 100 * 730
         ).orderBy(desc("potential_monthly_savings"))
        
        # Workload consolidation opportunities
        consolidation = df_efficiency.groupBy("environment", "region") \
            .agg(
                count("server_id").alias("server_count"),
                avg("cpu_percent").alias("avg_cpu"),
                avg("memory_used_percent").alias("avg_memory"),
                sum(col("cpu_cores")).alias("total_cores"),
                sum(col("memory_total_gb")).alias("total_memory_gb")
            ).withColumn(
                "consolidation_ratio",
                when(col("avg_cpu") < 30, 2)
                .when(col("avg_cpu") < 50, 1.5)
                .otherwise(1)
            ).withColumn(
                "recommended_server_count",
                (col("server_count") / col("consolidation_ratio")).cast("int")
            ).withColumn(
                "servers_to_decommission",
                col("server_count") - col("recommended_server_count")
            )
        
        # Performance vs. resource usage analysis
        performance_efficiency = df_efficiency.withColumn(
            "efficiency_ratio",
            col("request_rate") / 
            ((col("cpu_percent") + col("memory_used_percent")) / 2 + 1)
        ).groupBy("server_id") \
         .agg(
             avg("efficiency_ratio").alias("avg_efficiency_ratio"),
             avg("request_rate").alias("avg_request_rate"),
             avg("response_time_ms").alias("avg_response_time")
         ).withColumn(
             "performance_rating",
             when(
                 (col("avg_efficiency_ratio") > 100) & 
                 (col("avg_response_time") < 200),
                 "Excellent"
             ).when(
                 (col("avg_efficiency_ratio") > 50) & 
                 (col("avg_response_time") < 500),
                 "Good"
             ).when(
                 col("avg_efficiency_ratio") > 25,
                 "Fair"
             ).otherwise("Poor")
         )
        
        return {
            'underutilized': underutilized,
            'rightsizing': rightsizing,
            'cost_optimization': cost_optimization,
            'consolidation': consolidation,
            'performance_efficiency': performance_efficiency
        }
    
    def generate_optimization_recommendations(self, monitoring_df):
        """Generate actionable optimization recommendations"""
        
        df_enriched = monitoring_df.withColumn(
            "memory_used_percent",
            (col("memory_used_gb") / col("memory_total_gb")) * 100
        )
        
        # Analyze patterns over time
        daily_stats = df_enriched.withColumn(
            "date", to_date(col("timestamp"))
        ).groupBy("server_id", "date") \
         .agg(
             avg("cpu_percent").alias("daily_avg_cpu"),
             max("cpu_percent").alias("daily_max_cpu"),
             avg("memory_used_percent").alias("daily_avg_memory"),
             max("memory_used_percent").alias("daily_max_memory")
         )
        
        # Generate recommendations
        recommendations = daily_stats.groupBy("server_id") \
            .agg(
                avg("daily_avg_cpu").alias("overall_avg_cpu"),
                avg("daily_max_cpu").alias("overall_max_cpu"),
                avg("daily_avg_memory").alias("overall_avg_memory"),
                avg("daily_max_memory").alias("overall_max_memory")
            ).withColumn(
                "recommendation",
                when(
                    (col("overall_avg_cpu") < 20) & 
                    (col("overall_avg_memory") < 30),
                    "DOWNSIZE: Server is significantly underutilized. " +
                    "Consider reducing resources by 50%."
                ).when(
                    (col("overall_max_cpu") > 90) | 
                    (col("overall_max_memory") > 90),
                    "UPSIZE: Server frequently hits resource limits. " +
                    "Consider increasing resources by 50%."
                ).when(
                    (col("overall_avg_cpu") < 40) & 
                    (col("overall_max_cpu") < 60),
                    "CONSOLIDATE: Low average utilization. " +
                    "Consider consolidating workloads."
                ).when(
                    col("overall_max_cpu") - col("overall_avg_cpu") > 40,
                    "AUTOSCALE: High variance in utilization. " +
                    "Consider implementing auto-scaling."
                ).otherwise(
                    "OPTIMAL: Resource allocation appears appropriate."
                )
            ).withColumn(
                "priority",
                when(col("recommendation").contains("DOWNSIZE"), "High")
                .when(
```python
col("recommendation").contains("UPSIZE"), "Critical")
                .when(col("recommendation").contains("CONSOLIDATE"), "Medium")
                .when(col("recommendation").contains("AUTOSCALE"), "Medium")
                .otherwise("Low")
            ).withColumn(
                "estimated_impact",
                when(col("recommendation").contains("DOWNSIZE"), "30-50% cost reduction")
                .when(col("recommendation").contains("UPSIZE"), "Improved performance and stability")
                .when(col("recommendation").contains("CONSOLIDATE"), "20-40% cost reduction")
                .when(col("recommendation").contains("AUTOSCALE"), "15-30% cost reduction")
                .otherwise("Maintain current state")
            )
        
        return recommendations
    
    def calculate_resource_waste(self, monitoring_df):
        """Calculate resource waste and potential savings"""
        
        df_enriched = monitoring_df.withColumn(
            "memory_used_percent",
            (col("memory_used_gb") / col("memory_total_gb")) * 100
        )
        
        # Calculate waste metrics
        waste_analysis = df_enriched.groupBy("server_id", "environment") \
            .agg(
                avg("cpu_percent").alias("avg_cpu_util"),
                avg("memory_used_percent").alias("avg_memory_util"),
                first("cpu_cores").alias("cpu_cores"),
                first("memory_total_gb").alias("memory_total_gb")
            ).withColumn(
                "cpu_waste_percent", 100 - col("avg_cpu_util")
            ).withColumn(
                "memory_waste_percent", 100 - col("avg_memory_util")
            ).withColumn(
                "wasted_cpu_cores",
                col("cpu_cores") * col("cpu_waste_percent") / 100
            ).withColumn(
                "wasted_memory_gb",
                col("memory_total_gb") * col("memory_waste_percent") / 100
            ).withColumn(
                "estimated_monthly_waste_cost",
                (col("wasted_cpu_cores") * 0.05 + 
                 col("wasted_memory_gb") * 0.01) * 730
            ).withColumn(
                "waste_category",
                when(col("estimated_monthly_waste_cost") > 500, "High")
                .when(col("estimated_monthly_waste_cost") > 200, "Medium")
                .otherwise("Low")
            )
        
        # Total waste summary
        waste_summary = waste_analysis.groupBy("environment", "waste_category") \
            .agg(
                count("server_id").alias("server_count"),
                sum("estimated_monthly_waste_cost").alias("total_monthly_waste"),
                avg("cpu_waste_percent").alias("avg_cpu_waste"),
                avg("memory_waste_percent").alias("avg_memory_waste")
            ).orderBy(desc("total_monthly_waste"))
        
        return {
            'waste_analysis': waste_analysis,
            'waste_summary': waste_summary
        }

    # Forecast resource exhaustion

    window_spec = Window.partitionBy("server_id").orderBy("timestamp")
    
    resource_forecast = monitoring_df.withColumn(
        "disk_used_gb",
        col("disk_used_percent") / 100 * 100  # Assuming 100GB disk
    ).withColumn(
        "disk_growth_rate",
        col("disk_used_gb") - lag("disk_used_gb", 1).over(window_spec)
    ).withColumn(
        "memory_growth_rate",
        col("memory_used_gb") - lag("memory_used_gb", 1).over(window_spec)
    ).groupBy("server_id") \
     .agg(
         avg("disk_growth_rate").alias("avg_disk_growth_per_min"),
         avg("memory_growth_rate").alias("avg_memory_growth_per_min"),
         max("disk_used_percent").alias("current_disk_used_percent"),
         max("memory_used_gb").alias("current_memory_used_gb"),
         first("memory_total_gb").alias("memory_total_gb")
     ).withColumn(
         "disk_days_to_full",
         when(col("avg_disk_growth_per_min") > 0,
              (100 - col("current_disk_used_percent")) / 
              (col("avg_disk_growth_per_min") * 1440)  # Minutes per day
         ).otherwise(lit(999))
     ).withColumn(
         "memory_days_to_full",
         when(col("avg_memory_growth_per_min") > 0,
              (col("memory_total_gb") - col("current_memory_used_gb")) / 
              (col("avg_memory_growth_per_min") * 1440)
         ).otherwise(lit(999))
     ).withColumn(
         "urgent_action_needed",
         when(
             (col("disk_days_to_full") < 30) | 
             (col("memory_days_to_full") < 30),
             "YES"
         ).otherwise("NO")
     ).filter(col("urgent_action_needed") == "YES")
    
    resource_forecast.show(10, truncate=False)

        "response_efficiency",

     .agg(
         avg("requests_per_cpu_percent").alias("avg_req_per_cpu"),

    # ========================================================================

    # Define SLA thresholds
    SLA_CPU_THRESHOLD = 85
    SLA_MEMORY_THRESHOLD = 85
    SLA_RESPONSE_TIME_THRESHOLD = 500
    SLA_ERROR_RATE_THRESHOLD = 1.0
    
    sla_compliance = monitoring_df.withColumn(
        "memory_used_percent",
        (col("memory_used_gb") / col("memory_total_gb")) * 100
    ).withColumn(
        "cpu_sla_met",
        when(col("cpu_percent") <= SLA_CPU_THRESHOLD, 1).otherwise(0)
    ).withColumn(
        "memory_sla_met",
        when(col("memory_used_percent") <= SLA_MEMORY_THRESHOLD, 1).otherwise(0)
    ).withColumn(
        "response_sla_met",
        when(col("response_time_ms") <= SLA_RESPONSE_TIME_THRESHOLD, 1).otherwise(0)
    ).withColumn(
        "error_sla_met",
        when(col("error_rate") <= SLA_ERROR_RATE_THRESHOLD, 1).otherwise(0)
    ).withColumn(
        "overall_sla_met",
        when(
            (col("cpu_sla_met") == 1) & 
            (col("memory_sla_met") == 1) & 
            (col("response_sla_met") == 1) & 
            (col("error_sla_met") == 1),
            1
        ).otherwise(0)
    )
    
    # Calculate SLA compliance percentage
    print("\nSLA Compliance by Server:")
    
    sla_summary = sla_compliance.groupBy("server_id", "environment") \
        .agg(
            (sum("cpu_sla_met") / count("*") * 100).alias("cpu_sla_percent"),
            (sum("memory_sla_met") / count("*") * 100).alias("memory_sla_percent"),
            (sum("response_sla_met") / count("*") * 100).alias("response_sla_percent"),
            (sum("error_sla_met") / count("*") * 100).alias("error_sla_percent"),
            (sum("overall_sla_met") / count("*") * 100).alias("overall_sla_percent")
        ).withColumn(
            "sla_status",
            when(col("overall_sla_percent") >= 99.9, "Gold")
            .when(col("overall_sla_percent") >= 99.0, "Silver")
            .when(col("overall_sla_percent") >= 95.0, "Bronze")
            .otherwise("Below Target")
        )
    
    sla_summary.orderBy(desc("overall_sla_percent")).show(10, truncate=False)
    
    # SLA violations
    print("\nSLA Violations:")

            "timestamp", "server_id", "environment",

            "response_time_ms", "error_rate",

     .agg(
         avg("cpu_percent").alias("avg_cpu"),
         avg("memory_used_gb").alias("avg_memory"),
         avg("network_in_mbps").alias("avg_network"),

     ).orderBy("day_of_week", "hour")
    
    print("\nHourly Usage Patterns by Day of Week:")

    # ========================================================================
    # ANOMALY DETECTION SUMMARY
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("COMPREHENSIVE ANOMALY DETECTION")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Calculate z-scores for multiple metrics
    from pyspark.sql.functions import mean as _mean, stddev as _stddev
    
    # Get global statistics
    stats = monitoring_df.agg(
        _mean("cpu_percent").alias("mean_cpu"),
        _stddev("cpu_percent").alias("stddev_cpu"),
        _mean("memory_used_gb").alias("mean_memory"),
        _stddev("memory_used_gb").alias("stddev_memory"),
        _mean("response_time_ms").alias("mean_response"),
        _stddev("response_time_ms").alias("stddev_response")
    ).collect()[0]
    
    anomalies = monitoring_df.withColumn(
        "cpu_z_score",
        (col("cpu_percent") - lit(stats["mean_cpu"])) / 
        (lit(stats["stddev_cpu"]) + 0.01)
    ).withColumn(
        "memory_z_score",
        (col("memory_used_gb") - lit(stats["mean_memory"])) / 
        (lit(stats["stddev_memory"]) + 0.01)
    ).withColumn(
        "response_z_score",
        (col("response_time_ms") - lit(stats["mean_response"])) / 
        (lit(stats["stddev_response"]) + 0.01)
    ).withColumn(
        "is_anomaly",
        when(
            (abs(col("cpu_z_score")) > 3) |
            (abs(col("memory_z_score")) > 3) |
            (abs(col("response_z_score")) > 3),
            True
        ).otherwise(False)
    ).withColumn(
        "anomaly_type",
        when(abs(col("cpu_z_score")) > 3, "CPU Anomaly")
        .when(abs(col("memory_z_score")) > 3, "Memory Anomaly")
        .when(abs(col("response_z_score")) > 3, "Performance Anomaly")
        .otherwise("Normal")
    ).filter(col("is_anomaly") == True)
    
    print("\nDetected Anomalies:")
    anomalies.select(
        "timestamp", "server_id", "anomaly_type",
        "cpu_z_score", "memory_z_score", "response_z_score",
        "cpu_percent", "memory_used_gb", "response_time_ms"
    ).show(20, truncate=False)
    
    # Anomaly summary
    print("\nAnomaly Summary:")
    anomaly_summary = anomalies.groupBy("server_id", "anomaly_type") \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("anomaly_count")
        ).orderBy(desc("anomaly_count"))
    
    anomaly_summary.show(10)
    
    # ========================================================================
    # FINAL EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("EXECUTIVE SUMMARY - KEY FINDINGS")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Overall infrastructure health

        "waste_category"
    ).limit(5).show(truncate=False)
    
    # Performance leaders
    print("\nTop 5 Best Performing Servers:")

    performance_benchmark.orderBy(

    ).limit(5).show(truncate=False)

# ============================================================================
# UTILITY FUNCTIONS FOR ADVANCED ANALYSIS
# ============================================================================

def generate_resource_report(spark, monitoring_df, output_path="/tmp/resource_report"):
    """
    Generate comprehensive resource utilization report
    """
    print("\nGenerating Comprehensive Resource Report...")
    
    # Create report dataframes
    report_data = {}
    
    # 1. Executive Summary
    report_data['executive_summary'] = monitoring_df.withColumn(
        "memory_used_percent",
        (col("memory_used_gb") / col("memory_total_gb")) * 100
    ).agg(
        countDistinct("server_id").alias("total_servers"),
        countDistinct("environment").alias("total_environments"),
        avg("cpu_percent").alias("avg_cpu"),
        avg("memory_used_percent").alias("avg_memory"),
        avg("disk_used_percent").alias("avg_disk"),
        avg("response_time_ms").alias("avg_response_time"),
        sum(when(col("error_rate") > 1, 1).otherwise(0)).alias("servers_with_errors")
    )
    
    # 2. Resource Trends
    report_data['resource_trends'] = monitoring_df.withColumn(
        "date", to_date(col("timestamp"))
    ).groupBy("date") \
     .agg(
         avg("cpu_percent").alias("daily_avg_cpu"),
         max("cpu_percent").alias("daily_max_cpu"),
         avg("memory_used_gb").alias("daily_avg_memory"),
         avg("disk_used_percent").alias("daily_avg_disk"),
         avg("response_time_ms").alias("daily_avg_response")
     ).orderBy("date")
    
    # 3. Server Rankings
    report_data['server_rankings'] = monitoring_df.groupBy("server_id") \
        .agg(
            avg("cpu_percent").alias("avg_cpu"),
            avg("response_time_ms").alias("avg_response"),
            avg("error_rate").alias("avg_error_rate"),
            count("*").alias("sample_count")
        ).withColumn(
            "rank_score",
            (100 - col("avg_cpu")) * 0.3 +
            (1000 / (col("avg_response") + 1)) * 0.4 +
            (10 - col("avg_error_rate")) * 0.3
        ).orderBy(desc("rank_score"))
    
    # 4. Alert Summary
    report_data['alert_summary'] = monitoring_df.withColumn(
        "memory_used_percent",
        (col("memory_used_gb") / col("memory_total_gb")) * 100
    ).withColumn(
        "alert_level",
        when(
            (col("cpu_percent") > 90) | 
            (col("memory_used_percent") > 90) |
            (col("disk_used_percent") > 90),
            "Critical"
        ).when(
            (col("cpu_percent") > 80) | 
            (col("memory_used_percent") > 80) |
            (col("disk_used_percent") > 80),
            "Warning"
        ).otherwise("Normal")
    ).groupBy("alert_level") \
     .agg(
         count("*").alias("occurrence_count"),
         countDistinct("server_id").alias("affected_servers")
     )
    
    # Display report sections
    print("\n--- EXECUTIVE SUMMARY ---")
    report_data['executive_summary'].show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\n--- RESOURCE TRENDS ---")
    report_data['resource_trends'].show(10, truncate=False)
    
    print("\n--- TOP 10 SERVER RANKINGS ---")
    report_data['server_rankings'].show(10, truncate=False)
    
    print("\n--- ALERT SUMMARY ---")
    report_data['alert_summary'].show(truncate=False)
    
    # Save report to files
    try:
        for report_name, report_df in report_data.items():
            report_df.write.mode("overwrite") \
                .parquet(f"{output_path}/{report_name}")
        print(f"\nReport saved to {output_path}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Could not save report: {e}")
    
    return report_data


def create_capacity_planning_model(monitoring_df):
    """
    Create capacity planning model based on historical data
    """
    print("\nCreating Capacity Planning Model...")
    
    # Calculate growth rates
    window_spec = Window.partitionBy("server_id").orderBy("timestamp")
    
    capacity_model = monitoring_df.withColumn(
        "memory_used_percent",
        (col("memory_used_gb") / col("memory_total_gb")) * 100
    ).withColumn(
        "prev_cpu", lag("cpu_percent", 1).over(window_spec)
    ).withColumn(
        "prev_memory", lag("memory_used_percent", 1).over(window_spec)
    ).withColumn(
        "prev_disk", lag("disk_used_percent", 1).over(window_spec)
    ).withColumn(
        "cpu_growth", col("cpu_percent") - col("prev_cpu")
    ).withColumn(
        "memory_growth", col("memory_used_percent") - col("prev_memory")
    ).withColumn(
        "disk_growth", col("disk_used_percent") - col("prev_disk")
    ).groupBy("server_id", "environment") \
     .agg(
         avg("cpu_growth").alias("avg_cpu_growth_per_sample"),
         avg("memory_growth").alias("avg_memory_growth_per_sample"),
         avg("disk_growth").alias("avg_disk_growth_per_sample"),
         max("cpu_percent").alias("current_cpu"),
         max("memory_used_percent").alias("current_memory"),
         max("disk_used_percent").alias("current_disk"),
         first("cpu_cores").alias("cpu_cores"),
         first("memory_total_gb").alias("memory_total_gb")
     ).withColumn(
         "months_to_cpu_capacity",
         when(col("avg_cpu_growth_per_sample") > 0,
              (85 - col("current_cpu")) / 
              (col("avg_cpu_growth_per_sample") * 1440 * 30)  # Convert to monthly
         ).otherwise(lit(999))
     ).withColumn(
         "months_to_memory_capacity",
         when(col("avg_memory_growth_per_sample") > 0,
              (85 - col("current_memory")) / 
              (col("avg_memory_growth_per_sample") * 1440 * 30)
         ).otherwise(lit(999))
     ).withColumn(
         "months_to_disk_capacity",
         when(col("avg_disk_growth_per_sample") > 0,
              (85 - col("current_disk")) / 
              (col("avg_disk_growth_per_sample") * 1440 * 30)
         ).otherwise(lit(999))
     ).withColumn(
         "earliest_capacity_constraint",
         least("months_to_cpu_capacity", "months_to_memory_capacity", 
               "months_to_disk_capacity")
     ).withColumn(
         "capacity_action_needed",
         when(col("earliest_capacity_constraint") < 3, "Immediate")
         .when(col("earliest_capacity_constraint") < 6, "Short-term")
         .when(col("earliest_capacity_constraint") < 12, "Medium-term")
         .otherwise("Long-term")
     )
    
    print("\nCapacity Planning Forecast:")
    capacity_model.orderBy("earliest_capacity_constraint") \
        .show(20, truncate=False)
    
    return capacity_model


def analyze_workload_patterns(monitoring_df):
    """
    Analyze workload patterns for better resource allocation
    """
    print("\nAnalyzing Workload Patterns...")
    
    # Classify workload types
    workload_analysis = monitoring_df.withColumn(
        "memory_used_percent",
        (col("memory_used_gb") / col("memory_total_gb")) * 100
    ).withColumn(
        "cpu_to_memory_ratio",
        col("cpu_percent") / (col("memory_used_percent") + 1)
    ).withColumn(
        "io_intensity",
        (col("disk_read_mbps") + col("disk_write_mbps")) / 100
    ).withColumn(
        "network_intensity",
        (col("network_in_mbps") + col("network_out_mbps")) / 100
    ).withColumn(
        "workload_type",
        when(
            (col("cpu_percent") > 70) & (col("memory_used_percent") < 50),
            "CPU-Intensive"
        ).when(
            (col("memory_used_percent") > 70) & (col("cpu_percent") < 50),
            "Memory-Intensive"
        ).when(
            (col("io_intensity") > 5),
            "I/O-Intensive"
        ).when(
            (col("network_intensity") > 5),
            "Network-Intensive"
        ).when(
            (col("cpu_percent") > 60) & (col("memory_used_percent") > 60),
            "Balanced-Heavy"
        ).otherwise("Balanced-Light")
    )
    
    # Workload distribution
    workload_distribution = workload_analysis.groupBy(
        "environment", "workload_type"
    ).agg(
        count("*").alias("occurrence_count"),
        countDistinct("server_id").alias("server_count"),
        avg("cpu_percent").alias("avg_cpu"),
        avg("memory_used_percent").alias("avg_memory"),
        avg("response_time_ms").alias("avg_response_time")
    ).orderBy("environment", desc("occurrence_count"))
    
    print("\nWorkload Distribution:")
    workload_distribution.show(20, truncate=False)
    
    # Workload recommendations
    workload_recommendations = workload_analysis.groupBy(
        "server_id", "workload_type"
    ).agg(
        count("*").alias("pattern_frequency")
    ).groupBy("server_id") \
     .agg(
         first("workload_type").alias("primary_workload"),
         max("pattern_frequency").alias("max_frequency")
     ).join(
         monitoring_df.groupBy("server_id").agg(
             first("cpu_cores").alias("cpu_cores"),
             first("memory_total_gb").alias("memory_total_gb")
         ),
         "server_id"
     ).withColumn(
         "optimization_recommendation",
         when(
             col("primary_workload") == "CPU-Intensive",
             "Consider increasing CPU cores or using compute-optimized instances"
         ).when(
             col("primary_workload") == "Memory-Intensive",
             "Consider increasing memory or using memory-optimized instances"
         ).when(
             col("primary_workload") == "I/O-Intensive",
             "Consider using SSD storage or I/O-optimized instances"
         ).when(
             col("primary_workload") == "Network-Intensive",
             "Consider using enhanced networking or network-optimized instances"
         ).otherwise(
             "Current configuration appears balanced"
         )
     )
    
    print("\nWorkload-Based Optimization Recommendations:")
    workload_recommendations.show(10, truncate=False)
    
    return {
        'workload_distribution': workload_distribution,
        'workload_recommendations': workload_recommendations
    }


def create_resource_utilization_scorecard(monitoring_df):
    """
    Create a comprehensive scorecard for resource utilization
    """
    print("\nCreating Resource Utilization Scorecard...")
    
    scorecard = monitoring_df.withColumn(
        "memory_used_percent",
        (col("memory_used_gb") / col("memory_total_gb")) * 100
    ).groupBy("server_id", "environment") \
     .agg(
         # Utilization metrics
         avg("cpu_percent").alias("avg_cpu"),
         avg("memory_used_percent").alias("avg_memory"),
         avg("disk_used_percent").alias("avg_disk"),
         # Performance metrics
         avg("response_time_ms").alias("avg_response_time"),
         percentile_approx("response_time_ms", 0.95).alias("p95_response_time"),
         avg("error_rate").alias("avg_error_rate"),
         # Stability metrics
         stddev("cpu_percent").alias("cpu_stability"),
         stddev("memory_used_percent").alias("memory_stability"),
         # Capacity metrics
         max("cpu_percent").alias("peak_cpu"),
         max("memory_used_percent").alias("peak_memory")
     ).withColumn(
         # Utilization score (0-100, higher is better balance)
         "utilization_score",
         when(
             (col("avg_cpu") >= 40) & (col("avg_cpu") <= 70) &
             (col("avg_memory") >= 40) & (col("avg_memory") <= 70),
             100
         ).when(
             (col("avg_cpu") >= 30) & (col("avg_cpu") <= 80) &
             (col("avg_memory") >= 30) & (col("avg_memory") <= 80),
             80
         ).when(
             (col("avg_cpu") >= 20) & (col("avg_cpu") <= 90) &
             (col("avg_memory") >= 20) & (col("avg_memory") <= 90),
             60
         ).otherwise(40)
     ).withColumn(
         # Performance score (0-100)
         "performance_score",
         when(col("avg_response_time") < 100, 100)
         .when(col("avg_response_time") < 200, 90)
         .when(col("avg_response_time") < 300, 80)
         .when(col("avg_response_time") < 500, 60)
         .otherwise(40)
     ).withColumn(
         # Stability score (0-100, lower variance is better)
         "stability_score",
         when(
             (col("cpu_stability") < 10) & (col("memory_stability") < 10),
             100
         ).when(
             (col("cpu_stability") < 20) & (col("memory_stability") < 20),
             80
         ).when(
             (col("cpu_stability") < 30) & (col("memory_stability") < 30),
             60
         ).otherwise(40)
```python
    ).withColumn(
         # Capacity score (0-100, based on headroom)
         "capacity_score",
         when(
             (col("peak_cpu") < 70) & (col("peak_memory") < 70),
             100
         ).when(
             (col("peak_cpu") < 80) & (col("peak_memory") < 80),
             80
         ).when(
             (col("peak_cpu") < 90) & (col("peak_memory") < 90),
             60
         ).otherwise(40)
     ).withColumn(
         # Overall health score (weighted average)
         "overall_score",
         (col("utilization_score") * 0.25 +
          col("performance_score") * 0.35 +
          col("stability_score") * 0.20 +
          col("capacity_score") * 0.20)
     ).withColumn(
         # Grade assignment
         "grade",
         when(col("overall_score") >= 90, "A")
         .when(col("overall_score") >= 80, "B")
         .when(col("overall_score") >= 70, "C")
         .when(col("overall_score") >= 60, "D")
         .otherwise("F")
     ).withColumn(
         # Status indicator
         "status",
         when(col("grade").isin(["A", "B"]), "Healthy")
         .when(col("grade") == "C", "Needs Attention")
         .otherwise("Critical")
     )
    
    print("\nResource Utilization Scorecard:")
    scorecard.orderBy(desc("overall_score")).show(20, truncate=False)
    
    # Grade distribution
    print("\nGrade Distribution:")
    grade_dist = scorecard.groupBy("environment", "grade") \
        .agg(count("*").alias("server_count")) \
        .orderBy("environment", "grade")
    grade_dist.show()
    
    # Status summary
    print("\nStatus Summary:")
    status_summary = scorecard.groupBy("status") \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("server_count"),
            avg("overall_score").alias("avg_score")
        ).orderBy(desc("server_count"))
    status_summary.show()
    
    return scorecard


def generate_time_series_analysis(monitoring_df):
    """
    Perform time series analysis on resource metrics
    """
    print("\nPerforming Time Series Analysis...")
    
    # Add time-based features
    time_series = monitoring_df.withColumn(
        "hour", hour(col("timestamp"))
    ).withColumn(
        "day_of_week", dayofweek(col("timestamp"))
    ).withColumn(
        "is_weekend", 
        when(col("day_of_week").isin([1, 7]), 1).otherwise(0)
    ).withColumn(
        "is_business_hours",
        when((col("hour") >= 9) & (col("hour") <= 17), 1).otherwise(0)
    )
    
    # Hourly patterns
    hourly_analysis = time_series.groupBy("hour") \
        .agg(
            avg("cpu_percent").alias("avg_cpu"),
            avg("memory_used_gb").alias("avg_memory"),
            avg("request_rate").alias("avg_requests"),
            avg("response_time_ms").alias("avg_response_time"),
            stddev("cpu_percent").alias("cpu_variance")
        ).orderBy("hour")
    
    print("\nHourly Resource Patterns:")
    hourly_analysis.show(24, truncate=False)
    
    # Business hours vs. off-hours comparison
    business_comparison = time_series.groupBy("is_business_hours") \
        .agg(
            avg("cpu_percent").alias("avg_cpu"),
            avg("memory_used_gb").alias("avg_memory"),
            avg("request_rate").alias("avg_requests"),
            avg("response_time_ms").alias("avg_response_time"),
            count("*").alias("sample_count")
        ).withColumn(
            "period",
            when(col("is_business_hours") == 1, "Business Hours")
            .otherwise("Off Hours")
        )
    
    print("\nBusiness Hours vs Off-Hours Comparison:")
    business_comparison.select(
        "period", "avg_cpu", "avg_memory", 
        "avg_requests", "avg_response_time", "sample_count"
    ).show(truncate=False)
    
    # Weekend vs. weekday comparison
    weekend_comparison = time_series.groupBy("is_weekend") \
        .agg(
            avg("cpu_percent").alias("avg_cpu"),
            avg("memory_used_gb").alias("avg_memory"),
            avg("request_rate").alias("avg_requests"),
            avg("response_time_ms").alias("avg_response_time")
        ).withColumn(
            "period",
            when(col("is_weekend") == 1, "Weekend").otherwise("Weekday")
        )
    
    print("\nWeekend vs Weekday Comparison:")
    weekend_comparison.select(
        "period", "avg_cpu", "avg_memory", 
        "avg_requests", "avg_response_time"
    ).show(truncate=False)
    
    # Identify peak and off-peak hours
    peak_hours = hourly_analysis.withColumn(
        "load_category",
        when(col("avg_cpu") > 70, "Peak")
        .when(col("avg_cpu") > 40, "Medium")
        .otherwise("Off-Peak")
    )
    
    print("\nPeak Hours Identification:")
    peak_hours.show(24, truncate=False)
    
    return {
        'hourly_analysis': hourly_analysis,
        'business_comparison': business_comparison,
        'weekend_comparison': weekend_comparison,
        'peak_hours': peak_hours
    }


def create_cost_analysis_report(monitoring_df):
    """
    Create detailed cost analysis and optimization report
    """
    print("\nCreating Cost Analysis Report...")
    
    # Define cost parameters (example rates)
    CPU_COST_PER_CORE_HOUR = 0.05
    MEMORY_COST_PER_GB_HOUR = 0.01
    STORAGE_COST_PER_GB_MONTH = 0.10
    NETWORK_COST_PER_GB = 0.09
    
    cost_analysis = monitoring_df.withColumn(
        "memory_used_percent",
        (col("memory_used_gb") / col("memory_total_gb")) * 100
    ).withColumn(
        # Hourly costs
        "cpu_cost_hourly",
        col("cpu_cores") * CPU_COST_PER_CORE_HOUR
    ).withColumn(
        "memory_cost_hourly",
        col("memory_total_gb") * MEMORY_COST_PER_GB_HOUR
    ).withColumn(
        "total_hourly_cost",
        col("cpu_cost_hourly") + col("memory_cost_hourly")
    ).withColumn(
        # Calculate waste
        "cpu_waste_cost_hourly",
        col("cpu_cost_hourly") * (100 - col("cpu_percent")) / 100
    ).withColumn(
        "memory_waste_cost_hourly",
        col("memory_cost_hourly") * (100 - col("memory_used_percent")) / 100
    ).withColumn(
        "total_waste_hourly",
        col("cpu_waste_cost_hourly") + col("memory_waste_cost_hourly")
    )
    
    # Aggregate cost metrics by server
    server_costs = cost_analysis.groupBy("server_id", "environment") \
        .agg(
            first("cpu_cores").alias("cpu_cores"),
            first("memory_total_gb").alias("memory_total_gb"),
            avg("cpu_percent").alias("avg_cpu_util"),
            avg("memory_used_percent").alias("avg_memory_util"),
            first("total_hourly_cost").alias("hourly_cost"),
            avg("total_waste_hourly").alias("avg_waste_hourly")
        ).withColumn(
            "monthly_cost",
            col("hourly_cost") * 730
        ).withColumn(
            "monthly_waste",
            col("avg_waste_hourly") * 730
        ).withColumn(
            "annual_cost",
            col("monthly_cost") * 12
        ).withColumn(
            "annual_waste",
            col("monthly_waste") * 12
        ).withColumn(
            "efficiency_percent",
            ((col("avg_cpu_util") + col("avg_memory_util")) / 2)
        ).withColumn(
            "potential_annual_savings",
            when(col("efficiency_percent") < 50,
                 col("annual_waste") * 0.8  # 80% recoverable
            ).when(col("efficiency_percent") < 70,
                 col("annual_waste") * 0.5  # 50% recoverable
            ).otherwise(
                 col("annual_waste") * 0.2  # 20% recoverable
            )
        )
    
    print("\nServer Cost Analysis:")
    server_costs.orderBy(desc("monthly_waste")).show(20, truncate=False)
    
    # Environment-level cost summary
    env_costs = server_costs.groupBy("environment") \
        .agg(
            count("server_id").alias("server_count"),
            sum("monthly_cost").alias("total_monthly_cost"),
            sum("monthly_waste").alias("total_monthly_waste"),
            sum("potential_annual_savings").alias("total_potential_savings"),
            avg("efficiency_percent").alias("avg_efficiency")
        ).withColumn(
            "waste_percentage",
            (col("total_monthly_waste") / col("total_monthly_cost")) * 100
        )
    
    print("\nEnvironment Cost Summary:")
    env_costs.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Total cost summary
    total_summary = server_costs.agg(
        sum("monthly_cost").alias("total_monthly_cost"),
        sum("monthly_waste").alias("total_monthly_waste"),
        sum("annual_cost").alias("total_annual_cost"),
        sum("annual_waste").alias("total_annual_waste"),
        sum("potential_annual_savings").alias("total_potential_savings")
    )
    
    print("\nTotal Cost Summary:")
    total_summary.show(truncate=False)
    
    # ROI opportunities
    roi_opportunities = server_costs.filter(
        col("potential_annual_savings") > 1000
    ).select(
        "server_id", "environment",
        "monthly_cost", "monthly_waste",
        "efficiency_percent", "potential_annual_savings"
    ).withColumn(
        "roi_priority",
        when(col("potential_annual_savings") > 10000, "High")
        .when(col("potential_annual_savings") > 5000, "Medium")
        .otherwise("Low")
    ).orderBy(desc("potential_annual_savings"))
    
    print("\nTop ROI Opportunities:")
    roi_opportunities.show(20, truncate=False)
    
    return {
        'server_costs': server_costs,
        'env_costs': env_costs,
        'total_summary': total_summary,
        'roi_opportunities': roi_opportunities
    }

def export_to_csv(df, filename, output_path="/tmp"):
    """
    Export DataFrame to CSV file
    """
    try:
        full_path = f"{output_path}/{filename}"
        df.coalesce(1).write.mode("overwrite") \
            .option("header", "true") \
            .csv(full_path)
        print(f"Exported to {full_path}")
        return True
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Failed to export {filename}: {e}")
        return False

def generate_executive_dashboard_data(monitoring_df, scorecard, cost_analysis):
    """
    Generate data for executive dashboard visualization
    """
    print("\nGenerating Executive Dashboard Data...")
    
    dashboard_data = {}
    
    # KPI Summary
    dashboard_data['kpi_summary'] = monitoring_df.agg(
        countDistinct("server_id").alias("total_servers"),
        avg("cpu_percent").alias("avg_cpu_utilization"),
        avg("response_time_ms").alias("avg_response_time"),
        sum(when(col("error_rate") > 1, 1).otherwise(0)).alias("servers_with_errors")
    )
    
    # Health Distribution
    dashboard_data['health_distribution'] = scorecard.groupBy("status") \
        .agg(count("*").alias("count")) \
        .withColumn("percentage", col("count") / scorecard.count() * 100)
    
    # Cost Breakdown
    dashboard_data['cost_breakdown'] = cost_analysis['env_costs']
    
    # Top Issues
    dashboard_data['top_issues'] = scorecard.filter(
        col("overall_score") < 70
    ).orderBy("overall_score").limit(10)
    
    # Trends
    dashboard_data['trends'] = monitoring_df.withColumn(
        "hour", hour(col("timestamp"))
    ).groupBy("hour") \
     .agg(
         avg("cpu_percent").alias("cpu"),
         avg("memory_used_gb").alias("memory"),
         avg("response_time_ms").alias("response_time")
     ).orderBy("hour")
    
    print("\nExecutive Dashboard Data Generated:")
    print("  - KPI Summary")
    print("  - Health Distribution")
    print("  - Cost Breakdown")
    print("  - Top Issues")
    print("  - Hourly Trends")
    
    return dashboard_data

# PATTERN 1: Cross-Column Correlation Pattern
# Purpose: Analyze correlations between multiple columns/features
# ============================================================================

class CrossColumnCorrelationPattern:
    """
    Analyzes correlations between different columns in a dataset.
    Useful for feature selection, multicollinearity detection, and understanding
    relationships between variables.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    def create_sample_data(self):
        """Create sample sales and customer data"""
        data = [
            (1, 100, 5000, 45, 3, 85, 120000),
            (2, 150, 7500, 52, 5, 90, 150000),
            (3, 80, 4000, 38, 2, 75, 95000),
            (4, 200, 10000, 48, 7, 95, 180000),
            (5, 120, 6000, 41, 4, 80, 110000),
            (6, 180, 9000, 55, 6, 88, 165000),
            (7, 90, 4500, 35, 2, 72, 88000),
            (8, 160, 8000, 50, 5, 92, 155000),
            (9, 110, 5500, 43, 3, 78, 105000),
            (10, 190, 9500, 58, 8, 94, 175000)
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("customer_id", IntegerType(), True),
            StructField("num_purchases", IntegerType(), True),
            StructField("total_revenue", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("age", IntegerType(), True),
            StructField("years_customer", IntegerType(), True),
            StructField("satisfaction_score", IntegerType(), True),
            StructField("annual_income", DoubleType(), True)
        ])
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
    
    def calculate_pearson_correlation_matrix(self, df, columns):
        """
        Calculate Pearson correlation matrix for specified columns
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            columns: List of column names to correlate
            
        Returns:
            Correlation matrix as DataFrame
        """
        # Assemble features into a vector
        assembler = VectorAssembler(
            inputCols=columns,
            outputCol="features"
        )
        
        df_vector = assembler.transform(df).select("features")
        
        # Calculate correlation matrix
        correlation_matrix = Correlation.corr(df_vector, "features", "pearson")
        correlation_values = correlation_matrix.collect()[0][0].toArray()
        
        # Convert to readable format
        correlation_data = []
        for i, col1 in enumerate(columns):
            for j, col2 in enumerate(columns):
                correlation_data.append((
                    col1,
                    col2,
                    float(correlation_values[i][j])
                ))
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("column1", StringType(), True),
            StructField("column2", StringType(), True),
            StructField("correlation", DoubleType(), True)
        ])
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(correlation_data, schema)
    
    def calculate_pairwise_correlations(self, df, columns):
        """
        Calculate pairwise correlations using SQL functions
        More flexible for streaming or incremental calculations
        """
        correlations = []
        
        for i, col1 in enumerate(columns):
            for j, col2 in enumerate(columns[i:], start=i):
                correlation_df = df.select(
                    corr(col1, col2).alias("correlation")
                )
                corr_value = correlation_df.collect()[0]["correlation"]
                
                correlations.append({
                    "column1": col1,
                    "column2": col2,
                    "correlation": corr_value if corr_value else 0.0
                })
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(correlations)
    
    def find_highly_correlated_pairs(self, df, columns, threshold=0.7):
        """
        Identify pairs of columns with correlation above threshold
        Useful for detecting multicollinearity
        """
        corr_matrix = self.calculate_pearson_correlation_matrix(df, columns)
        
        high_corr = corr_matrix.filter(
            (col("column1") != col("column2")) &
            (_abs(col("correlation")) >= threshold)
        ).orderBy(col("correlation").desc())
        
        return high_corr
    
    def calculate_correlation_with_target(self, df, feature_columns, target_column):
        """
        Calculate correlation of all features with a target variable
        Useful for feature selection
        """
        correlations = []
        
        for feature in feature_columns:
            corr_value = df.select(
                corr(feature, target_column).alias("correlation")
            ).collect()[0]["correlation"]
            
            correlations.append({
                "feature": feature,
                "target": target_column,
                "correlation": corr_value if corr_value else 0.0,
                "abs_correlation": abs(corr_value) if corr_value else 0.0
            })
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(correlations).orderBy(
            col("abs_correlation").desc()
        )
    
    def run_example(self):
        """Execute Cross-Column Correlation Pattern example"""
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("PATTERN 1: Cross-Column Correlation Pattern")
        print("="*80)
        
        df = self.create_sample_data()
        
        print("\n1. Sample Data:")
        df.show()
        
        # Define columns for correlation analysis
        numeric_columns = [
            "num_purchases", "total_revenue", "age",
            "years_customer", "satisfaction_score", "annual_income"
        ]
        
        print("\n2. Full Correlation Matrix:")
        corr_matrix = self.calculate_pearson_correlation_matrix(df, numeric_columns)
        corr_matrix.filter(
            col("column1") <= col("column2")
        ).orderBy("column1", "column2").show(30, truncate=False)
        
        print("\n3. Highly Correlated Pairs (|r| >= 0.7):")
        high_corr = self.find_highly_correlated_pairs(df, numeric_columns, 0.7)
        high_corr.show(truncate=False)
        
        print("\n4. Feature Correlation with Total Revenue:")
        feature_cols = [c for c in numeric_columns if c != "total_revenue"]
        target_corr = self.calculate_correlation_with_target(
            df, feature_cols, "total_revenue"
        )
        target_corr.show(truncate=False)

# PATTERN 2: Temporal Correlation Pattern
# Purpose: Analyze correlations across time periods and identify time-based patterns
# ============================================================================

class TemporalCorrelationPattern:
    """
    Analyzes correlations in time-series data, including lag correlations,
    autocorrelation, and cross-correlation between time-shifted series.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    def create_sample_data(self):
        """Create sample time-series data"""
        data = [
            ("2024-01-01", 100, 50, 25),
            ("2024-01-02", 105, 52, 26),
            ("2024-01-03", 110, 55, 28),
            ("2024-01-04", 108, 54, 27),
            ("2024-01-05", 115, 58, 30),
            ("2024-01-06", 120, 60, 32),
            ("2024-01-07", 118, 59, 31),
            ("2024-01-08", 125, 63, 34),
            ("2024-01-09", 130, 65, 36),
            ("2024-01-10", 128, 64, 35),
            ("2024-01-11", 135, 68, 38),
            ("2024-01-12", 140, 70, 40),
            ("2024-01-13", 138, 69, 39),
            ("2024-01-14", 145, 73, 42),
            ("2024-01-15", 150, 75, 45)
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("date", StringType(), True),
            StructField("sales", IntegerType(), True),
            StructField("website_visits", IntegerType(), True),
            StructField("marketing_spend", IntegerType(), True)
        ])
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        return df.withColumn("date", to_date(col("date")))
    
    def calculate_lag_correlation(self, df, date_col, value_col, max_lag=5):
        """
        Calculate autocorrelation at different lag periods
        Helps identify cyclical patterns and dependencies
        """
        window_spec = Window.orderBy(date_col)
        
        # Create lagged columns
        df_lagged = df
        for i in range(1, max_lag + 1):
            df_lagged = df_lagged.withColumn(
                f"{value_col}_lag_{i}",
                lag(col(value_col), i).over(window_spec)
            )
        
        # Calculate correlations for each lag
        lag_correlations = []
        for i in range(1, max_lag + 1):
            lag_col = f"{value_col}_lag_{i}"
            corr_value = df_lagged.select(
                corr(value_col, lag_col).alias("correlation")
            ).collect()[0]["correlation"]
            
            lag_correlations.append({
                "variable": value_col,
                "lag": i,
                "correlation": corr_value if corr_value else 0.0
            })
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(lag_correlations)
    
    def calculate_cross_lag_correlation(self, df, date_col, col1, col2, max_lag=5):
        """
        Calculate correlation between one series and lagged values of another
        Useful for identifying leading/lagging indicators
        """
        window_spec = Window.orderBy(date_col)
        
        # Create lagged columns for col2
        df_lagged = df
        for i in range(-max_lag, max_lag + 1):
            if i < 0:
                # Lead values
                df_lagged = df_lagged.withColumn(
                    f"{col2}_lead_{abs(i)}",
                    lead(col(col2), abs(i)).over(window_spec)
                )
            elif i > 0:
                # Lag values
                df_lagged = df_lagged.withColumn(
                    f"{col2}_lag_{i}",
                    lag(col(col2), i).over(window_spec)
                )
        
        # Calculate correlations
        correlations = []
        
        # Negative lags (col2 leads col1)
        for i in range(1, max_lag + 1):
            lead_col = f"{col2}_lead_{i}"
            corr_value = df_lagged.select(
                corr(col1, lead_col).alias("correlation")
            ).collect()[0]["correlation"]
            
            correlations.append({
                "series1": col1,
                "series2": col2,
                "lag": -i,
                "correlation": corr_value if corr_value else 0.0,
                "interpretation": f"{col2} leads {col1} by {i} periods"
            })
        
        # Zero lag (concurrent)
        corr_value = df.select(
            corr(col1, col2).alias("correlation")
        ).collect()[0]["correlation"]
        
        correlations.append({
            "series1": col1,
            "series2": col2,
            "lag": 0,
            "correlation": corr_value if corr_value else 0.0,
            "interpretation": "Concurrent correlation"
        })
        
        # Positive lags (col1 leads col2)
        for i in range(1, max_lag + 1):
            lag_col = f"{col2}_lag_{i}"
            corr_value = df_lagged.select(
                corr(col1, lag_col).alias("correlation")
            ).collect()[0]["correlation"]
            
            correlations.append({
                "series1": col1,
                "series2": col2,
                "lag": i,
                "correlation": corr_value if corr_value else 0.0,
                "interpretation": f"{col1} leads {col2} by {i} periods"
            })
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(correlations)
    
    def calculate_rolling_correlation(self, df, date_col, col1, col2, window_size=7):
        """
        Calculate correlation over rolling time windows
        Helps identify changing relationships over time
        """
        window_spec = Window.orderBy(date_col).rowsBetween(
            -(window_size - 1), 0
        )
        
        # Collect values in rolling windows
        df_windowed = df.withColumn(
            f"{col1}_window",
            collect_list(col(col1)).over(window_spec)
        ).withColumn(
            f"{col2}_window",
            collect_list(col(col2)).over(window_spec)
        )
        
        # Filter to windows with full size
        df_windowed = df_windowed.withColumn(
            "window_size_check",
            size(col(f"{col1}_window"))
        ).filter(col("window_size_check") >= window_size)
        
        # Calculate correlation
```python
        # Calculate correlation for each window using UDF
        from pyspark.sql.functions import udf
        from pyspark.sql.types import DoubleType
        
        def calculate_window_correlation(values1, values2):
            """Calculate Pearson correlation for two lists"""
            if not values1 or not values2 or len(values1) != len(values2):
                return None
            
            n = len(values1)
            if n < 2:
                return None
            
            mean1 = sum(values1) / n
            mean2 = sum(values2) / n
            
            numerator = sum((values1[i] - mean1) * (values2[i] - mean2) for i in range(n))
            
            var1 = sum((values1[i] - mean1) ** 2 for i in range(n))
            var2 = sum((values2[i] - mean2) ** 2 for i in range(n))
            
            if var1 == 0 or var2 == 0:
                return None
            
            denominator = (var1 * var2) ** 0.5
            
            return numerator / denominator if denominator != 0 else None
        
        corr_udf = udf(calculate_window_correlation, DoubleType())
        
        result = df_windowed.withColumn(
            "rolling_correlation",
            corr_udf(col(f"{col1}_window"), col(f"{col2}_window"))
        ).select(
            date_col,
            col1,
            col2,
            "rolling_correlation"
        )
        
        return result
    
    def detect_temporal_patterns(self, df, date_col, value_col):
        """
        Detect temporal patterns like seasonality and trends
        """
        df_temporal = df.withColumn("year", year(col(date_col))) \
            .withColumn("month", month(col(date_col))) \
            .withColumn("day", dayofmonth(col(date_col)))
        
        # Calculate day-of-week patterns
        df_temporal = df_temporal.withColumn(
            "day_of_week",
            dayofmonth(col(date_col)) % 7
        )
        
        # Group by temporal components
        monthly_pattern = df_temporal.groupBy("month").agg(
            avg(value_col).alias("avg_value"),
            stddev(value_col).alias("stddev_value"),
            count(value_col).alias("count")
        ).orderBy("month")
        
        return monthly_pattern
    
    def run_example(self):
        """Execute Temporal Correlation Pattern example"""
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("PATTERN 2: Temporal Correlation Pattern")
        print("="*80)
        
        df = self.create_sample_data()
        
        print("\n1. Sample Time-Series Data:")
        df.show()
        
        print("\n2. Autocorrelation Analysis (Sales):")
        autocorr = self.calculate_lag_correlation(df, "date", "sales", max_lag=5)
        autocorr.show(truncate=False)
        
        print("\n3. Cross-Lag Correlation (Marketing Spend vs Sales):")
        cross_corr = self.calculate_cross_lag_correlation(
            df, "date", "sales", "marketing_spend", max_lag=3
        )
        cross_corr.orderBy("lag").show(truncate=False)
        
        print("\n4. Rolling Correlation (Sales vs Website Visits, 5-day window):")
        rolling_corr = self.calculate_rolling_correlation(
            df, "date", "sales", "website_visits", window_size=5
        )
        rolling_corr.show(truncate=False)

# PATTERN 3: Statistical Correlation Pattern
# Purpose: Advanced statistical correlation analysis including covariance,
#          rank correlation, and statistical significance testing
# ============================================================================

class StatisticalCorrelationPattern:
    """
    Performs comprehensive statistical correlation analysis including
    Pearson, Spearman rank correlation, covariance, and significance testing.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    def create_sample_data(self):
        """Create sample data with various distributions"""
        data = [
            (1, 23, 45000, 3.2, 85, "A"),
            (2, 35, 65000, 4.1, 92, "B"),
            (3, 28, 52000, 3.5, 78, "A"),
            (4, 42, 78000, 4.5, 95, "A"),
            (5, 31, 58000, 3.8, 88, "B"),
            (6, 26, 48000, 3.3, 82, "C"),
            (7, 38, 72000, 4.3, 91, "A"),
            (8, 29, 54000, 3.6, 86, "B"),
            (9, 45, 85000, 4.7, 97, "A"),
            (10, 33, 61000, 3.9, 89, "C"),
            (11, 27, 50000, 3.4, 84, "B"),
            (12, 40, 75000, 4.4, 93, "A"),
            (13, 30, 56000, 3.7, 87, "C"),
            (14, 36, 68000, 4.2, 90, "B"),
            (15, 25, 47000, 3.1, 80, "A")
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("employee_id", IntegerType(), True),
            StructField("age", IntegerType(), True),
            StructField("salary", IntegerType(), True),
            StructField("performance_rating", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("satisfaction_score", IntegerType(), True),
            StructField("department", StringType(), True)
        ])
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
    
    def calculate_covariance_matrix(self, df, columns):
        """
        Calculate covariance matrix for specified columns
        Covariance measures how two variables change together
        """
        covariances = []
        
        for col1 in columns:
            for col2 in columns:
                # Calculate population covariance
                cov_pop = df.select(
                    covar_pop(col1, col2).alias("covariance")
                ).collect()[0]["covariance"]
                
                # Calculate sample covariance
                cov_samp = df.select(
                    covar_samp(col1, col2).alias("covariance")
                ).collect()[0]["covariance"]
                
                covariances.append({
                    "variable1": col1,
                    "variable2": col2,
                    "covariance_population": cov_pop if cov_pop else 0.0,
                    "covariance_sample": cov_samp if cov_samp else 0.0
                })
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(covariances)
    
    def calculate_spearman_rank_correlation(self, df, col1, col2):
        """
        Calculate Spearman's rank correlation coefficient
        Non-parametric measure of monotonic relationship
        """
        # Assign ranks to both columns
        window_spec1 = Window.orderBy(col(col1))
        window_spec2 = Window.orderBy(col(col2))
        
        df_ranked = df.withColumn(
            f"{col1}_rank",
            row_number().over(window_spec1)
        ).withColumn(
            f"{col2}_rank",
            row_number().over(window_spec2)
        )
        
        # Calculate Pearson correlation on ranks (Spearman correlation)
        spearman_corr = df_ranked.select(
            corr(f"{col1}_rank", f"{col2}_rank").alias("spearman_correlation")
        ).collect()[0]["spearman_correlation"]
        
        return spearman_corr
    
    def calculate_correlation_with_statistics(self, df, col1, col2):
        """
        Calculate comprehensive correlation statistics
        """
        # Basic statistics
        stats = df.select(
            count(col1).alias("n"),
            mean(col1).alias("mean_x"),
            mean(col2).alias("mean_y"),
            stddev(col1).alias("std_x"),
            stddev(col2).alias("std_y"),
            variance(col1).alias("var_x"),
            variance(col2).alias("var_y"),
            corr(col1, col2).alias("pearson_r"),
            covar_samp(col1, col2).alias("covariance")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        # Calculate Spearman correlation
        spearman_r = self.calculate_spearman_rank_correlation(df, col1, col2)
        
        # Calculate coefficient of determination (R²)
        r_squared = stats["pearson_r"] ** 2 if stats["pearson_r"] else 0.0
        
        # Create result dictionary
        result = {
            "variable1": col1,
            "variable2": col2,
            "n_observations": stats["n"],
            "mean_x": stats["mean_x"],
            "mean_y": stats["mean_y"],
            "std_x": stats["std_x"],
            "std_y": stats["std_y"],
            "pearson_correlation": stats["pearson_r"],
            "spearman_correlation": spearman_r,
            "covariance": stats["covariance"],
            "r_squared": r_squared,
            "correlation_strength": self._interpret_correlation(stats["pearson_r"])
        }
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame([result])
    
    def _interpret_correlation(self, r):
        """Interpret correlation strength"""
        if r is None:
            return "undefined"
        
        abs_r = abs(r)
        if abs_r >= 0.9:
            return "very strong"
        elif abs_r >= 0.7:
            return "strong"
        elif abs_r >= 0.5:
            return "moderate"
        elif abs_r >= 0.3:
            return "weak"
        else:
            return "very weak"
    
    def calculate_partial_correlation(self, df, x_col, y_col, control_cols):
        """
        Calculate partial correlation controlling for other variables
        Shows relationship between x and y after removing effect of control variables
        """
        # This is a simplified implementation
        # For production, consider using more sophisticated methods
        
        # Calculate residuals after regressing on control variables
        # Here we use a simple approach with correlation adjustments
        
        # Get correlations
        r_xy = df.select(corr(x_col, y_col)).collect()[0][0]
        
        if len(control_cols) == 1:
            z_col = control_cols[0]
            r_xz = df.select(corr(x_col, z_col)).collect()[0][0]
            r_yz = df.select(corr(y_col, z_col)).collect()[0][0]
            
            # Partial correlation formula for one control variable
            if r_xz and r_yz:
                numerator = r_xy - (r_xz * r_yz)
                denominator = ((1 - r_xz**2) * (1 - r_yz**2)) ** 0.5
                partial_r = numerator / denominator if denominator != 0 else None
            else:
                partial_r = None
            
            return {
                "variable_x": x_col,
                "variable_y": y_col,
                "control_variable": z_col,
                "zero_order_correlation": r_xy,
                "partial_correlation": partial_r
            }
        
        return None
    
    def calculate_correlation_by_group(self, df, group_col, col1, col2):
        """
        Calculate correlations within different groups
        Useful for stratified analysis
        """
        result = df.groupBy(group_col).agg(
            corr(col1, col2).alias("correlation"),
            count(col1).alias("n_observations"),
            mean(col1).alias(f"mean_{col1}"),
            mean(col2).alias(f"mean_{col2}")
        ).orderBy(group_col)
        
        return result
    
    def detect_correlation_outliers(self, df, col1, col2, z_threshold=2.5):
        """
        Detect outliers that may be influencing correlation
        Uses standardized residuals approach
        """
        # Calculate means and standard deviations
        stats = df.select(
            mean(col1).alias("mean_x"),
            mean(col2).alias("mean_y"),
            stddev(col1).alias("std_x"),
            stddev(col2).alias("std_y")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        # Calculate standardized values
        df_standardized = df.withColumn(
            "z_score_x",
            (col(col1) - lit(stats["mean_x"])) / lit(stats["std_x"])
        ).withColumn(
            "z_score_y",
            (col(col2) - lit(stats["mean_y"])) / lit(stats["std_y"])
        ).withColumn(
            "combined_z_score",
            sqrt(_pow(col("z_score_x"), 2) + _pow(col("z_score_y"), 2))
        ).withColumn(
            "is_outlier",
            when(col("combined_z_score") > z_threshold, True).otherwise(False)
        )
        
        return df_standardized.select(
            col1, col2, "z_score_x", "z_score_y",
            "combined_z_score", "is_outlier"
        )
    
    def run_example(self):
        """Execute Statistical Correlation Pattern example"""
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("PATTERN 3: Statistical Correlation Pattern")
        print("="*80)
        
        df = self.create_sample_data()
        
        print("\n1. Sample Data:")
        df.show()
        
        print("\n2. Covariance Matrix:")
        numeric_cols = ["age", "salary", "performance_rating", "satisfaction_score"]
        cov_matrix = self.calculate_covariance_matrix(df, numeric_cols)
        cov_matrix.filter(col("variable1") == "salary").show(truncate=False)
        
        print("\n3. Comprehensive Correlation Statistics (Age vs Salary):")
        detailed_corr = self.calculate_correlation_with_statistics(df, "age", "salary")
        detailed_corr.show(truncate=False)
        
        print("\n4. Correlation by Department:")
        group_corr = self.calculate_correlation_by_group(
            df, "department", "age", "salary"
        )
        group_corr.show(truncate=False)
        
        print("\n5. Correlation Outlier Detection (Age vs Salary):")
        outliers = self.detect_correlation_outliers(df, "age", "salary", z_threshold=2.0)
        outliers.orderBy(col("combined_z_score").desc()).show(truncate=False)
        
        print("\n6. Partial Correlation (Age vs Salary, controlling for Performance):")
        partial_corr = self
