def demonstrate_database_normalization():
    """Demonstrate Database Normalization Forms (1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF)"""
    
    normalizer = DataNormalizationPatterns("DatabaseNormalization")
    
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("DATABASE NORMALIZATION PATTERNS DEMONSTRATION")
    print("="*80)
    
    # ========================================================================
    # 1NF Example: Unnormalized Student Data
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n--- First Normal Form (1NF) ---")
    
    # Create sample data with multi-valued attributes (violates 1NF)
    unnormalized_data = [
        (1, "John Doe", "Math,Physics,Chemistry", "A,B,A"),
        (2, "Jane Smith", "English,History", "A,A"),
        (3, "Bob Johnson", "Math,English,Physics", "B,A,B")
    ]
    
    schema_unnormalized = StructType([
        StructField("student_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("student_name", StringType(), False),
        StructField("courses", StringType(), False),
        StructField("grades", StringType(), False)
    ])
    
    df_unnormalized = normalizer.spark.createDataFrame(
        unnormalized_data, 
        schema_unnormalized
    )
    
    print("\nUnnormalized Data (Violates 1NF):")
    df_unnormalized.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Apply 1NF - separate multi-valued attributes
    df_1nf = normalizer.first_normal_form(
        df_unnormalized, 
        multi_valued_columns=['courses', 'grades']
    )
    
    print("\nAfter 1NF Transformation:")
    df_1nf.show(truncate=False)
    
    # ========================================================================
    # 2NF Example: Remove Partial Dependencies
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n--- Second Normal Form (2NF) ---")
    
    # Create data with partial dependencies (violates 2NF)
    # Composite key: (student_id, course_id)
    # instructor_name depends only on course_id (partial dependency)
    data_2nf = [
        (1, "John Doe", 101, "Math", "Dr. Smith", "A"),
        (1, "John Doe", 102, "Physics", "Dr. Jones", "B"),
        (2, "Jane Smith", 101, "Math", "Dr. Smith", "A"),
        (2, "Jane Smith", 103, "Chemistry", "Dr. Brown", "A"),
        (3, "Bob Johnson", 102, "Physics", "Dr. Jones", "B")
    ]
    
    schema_2nf = StructType([
        StructField("student_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("student_name", StringType(), False),
        StructField("course_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("course_name", StringType(), False),
        StructField("instructor_name", StringType(), False),
        StructField("grade", StringType(), False)
    ])
    
    df_pre_2nf = normalizer.spark.createDataFrame(data_2nf, schema_2nf)
    
    print("\nData with Partial Dependencies (Violates 2NF):")
    df_pre_2nf.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Apply 2NF
    dependent_cols_map = {
        'main_table': ['student_id', 'course_id', 'grade'],
        'student_table': ['student_id', 'student_name'],
        'course_table': ['course_id', 'course_name', 'instructor_name']
    }
    
    tables_2nf = normalizer.second_normal_form(
        df_pre_2nf,
        primary_key_cols=['student_id', 'course_id'],
        dependent_cols_map=dependent_cols_map
    )
    
    print("\nAfter 2NF Transformation:")
    for table_name, table_df in tables_2nf.items():
        print(f"\n{table_name}:")
        table_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # ========================================================================
    # 3NF Example: Remove Transitive Dependencies
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n--- Third Normal Form (3NF) ---")
    
    # Create data with transitive dependencies (violates 3NF)
    # student_id -> city -> state -> country (transitive)
    data_3nf = [
        (1, "John Doe", "New York", "NY", "USA"),
        (2, "Jane Smith", "Los Angeles", "CA", "USA"),
        (3, "Bob Johnson", "New York", "NY", "USA"),
        (4, "Alice Brown", "Chicago", "IL", "USA")
    ]
    
    schema_3nf = StructType([
        StructField("student_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("student_name", StringType(), False),
        StructField("city", StringType(), False),
        StructField("state", StringType(), False),
        StructField("country", StringType(), False)
    ])
    
    df_pre_3nf = normalizer.spark.createDataFrame(data_3nf, schema_3nf)
    
    print("\nData with Transitive Dependencies (Violates 3NF):")
    df_pre_3nf.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Apply 3NF
    transitive_deps = {
        'city_lookup': {
            'determinant': 'city',
            'dependent': ['state', 'country']
        }
    }
    
    tables_3nf = normalizer.third_normal_form(
        df_pre_3nf,
        primary_key_cols=['student_id'],
        transitive_deps=transitive_deps
    )
    
    print("\nAfter 3NF Transformation:")
    for table_name, table_df in tables_3nf.items():
        print(f"\n{table_name}:")
        table_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # ========================================================================
    # BCNF Example: Every determinant is a candidate key
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n--- Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF) ---")
    
    # Create data that violates BCNF
    # A professor teaches only one subject, but a subject can have multiple professors
    # student_id, subject -> professor (violates BCNF if professor -> subject)
    data_bcnf = [
        (1, "Math", "Dr. Smith"),
        (2, "Math", "Dr. Jones"),
        (1, "Physics", "Dr. Brown"),
        (3, "Math", "Dr. Smith"),
        (2, "Chemistry", "Dr. White")
    ]
    
    schema_bcnf = StructType([
        StructField("student_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("subject", StringType(), False),
        StructField("professor", StringType(), False)
    ])
    
    df_pre_bcnf = normalizer.spark.createDataFrame(data_bcnf, schema_bcnf)
    
    print("\nData Violating BCNF:")
    df_pre_bcnf.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Apply BCNF
    functional_dependencies = [
        {
            'determinant': ['professor'],
            'dependent': ['subject'],
            'table_name': 'professor_subject'
        }
    ]
    
    tables_bcnf = normalizer.boyce_codd_normal_form(
        df_pre_bcnf,
        functional_dependencies=functional_dependencies
    )
    
    print("\nAfter BCNF Transformation:")
    for table_name, table_df in tables_bcnf.items():
        print(f"\n{table_name}:")
        table_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    normalizer.cleanup()

def demonstrate_normalization_use_cases():

    reconstructed.show(truncate=False)

        ("A", 1, 100, 85),
        ("A", 2, 150, 90),
        ("A", 3, 120, 88),
        ("B", 4, 200, 75),
        ("B", 5, 250, 80),

    ]

    ])

    print("\nData with Multiple Categories:")
    df_groups.show()
    
    # Group-wise Z-Score normalization using window functions
    from pyspark.sql.window import Window
    
    window_spec = Window.partitionBy("category")
    
    # Calculate group-wise mean and stddev
    df_group_norm = df_groups \

        .withColumn(
            "value_normalized",
            (col("value") - col("group_mean")) / col("group_stddev")
        )
    
    print("\nGroup-wise Z-Score Normalization:")
    df_group_norm.select(
        "category", "id", "value", "group_mean", 
        "group_stddev", "value_normalized"
    ).show()
    
    # ========================================================================
    # Pattern 4: Decimal Scaling Normalization

    decimal_data = [
        (1, 12345, 987),
        (2, 54321, 456),
        (3, 98765, 123),
        (4, 23456, 789)
    ]
    
    decimal_schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("large_value", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("small_value", IntegerType(), False)
    ])
    
    df_decimal = normalizer.spark.createDataFrame(decimal_data, decimal_schema)
    
    print("\nOriginal Data:")
    df_decimal.show()
    
    # Decimal scaling: divide by 10^j where j is smallest integer 
    # such that max(|value|) < 1
    from pyspark.sql.functions import log10, ceil, pow as spark_pow, abs as spark_abs
    
    # Find the scaling factor
    max_val = df_decimal.agg(spark_max(spark_abs(col("large_value")))).collect()[0][0]
    j = int(len(str(max_val)))
    scaling_factor = 10 ** j
    
    df_decimal_scaled = df_decimal.withColumn(
        "large_value_scaled",
        col("large_value") / lit(scaling_factor)
    )
    
    print(f"\nDecimal Scaling (dividing by 10^{j}):")
    df_decimal_scaled.select("id", "large_value", "large_value_scaled").show()
    
    # ========================================================================

    print("\n--- Pattern 5: Log Transformation for Skewed Data ---")

        (2, 100, 1000),
        (3, 1000, 10000),
        (4, 10000, 100000),
        (5, 100000, 1000000)
    ]

        StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("exponential_value", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("power_value", IntegerType(), False)
    ])
    
    df_skewed = normalizer.spark.createDataFrame(skewed_data, skewed_schema)
    
    print("\nHighly Skewed Data:")
    df_skewed.show()
    
    from pyspark.sql.functions import log as spark_log, log10 as spark_log10
    
    df_log_transformed = df_skewed \
        .withColumn("exp_log", spark_log(col("exponential_value"))) \
        .withColumn("exp_log10", spark_log10(col("exponential_value"))) \
        .withColumn("power_log", spark_log(col("power_value")))
    
    print("\nLog Transformed Data:")
    df_log_transformed.select(
        "id", "exponential_value", "exp_log", "exp_log10"
    ).show()
    
    # Now apply normalization on log-transformed data
    df_log_normalized = normalizer.z_score_normalization(
        df_log_transformed,
        columns_to_normalize=["exp_log", "power_log"],
        output_col_suffix="_zscore"
    )
    
    print("\nZ-Score after Log Transformation:")
    df_log_normalized.select(
        "id", "exp_log", "exp_log_zscore", "power_log", "power_log_zscore"
    ).show()
    
    # ========================================================================
    # Pattern 6: Unit Vector Normalization (L2 Normalization)
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n--- Pattern 6: Unit Vector Normalization (L2 Norm) ---")
    
    vector_data = [
        (1, 3.0, 4.0, 5.0),
        (2, 1.0, 2.0, 2.0),
        (3, 5.0, 12.0, 13.0),
        (4, 8.0, 15.0, 17.0)
    ]
    
    vector_schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("x", DoubleType(), False),
        StructField("y", DoubleType(), False),
        StructField("z", DoubleType(), False)
    ])
    
    df_vector = normalizer.spark.createDataFrame(vector_data, vector_schema)
    
    print("\nOriginal Vectors:")
    df_vector.show()
    
    from pyspark.sql.functions import sqrt
    
    # Calculate L2 norm (Euclidean length)
    df_l2_norm = df_vector \
        .withColumn(
            "l2_norm",
            sqrt(col("x")**2 + col("y")**2 + col("z")**2)
        ) \
        .withColumn("x_normalized", col("x") / col("l2_norm")) \
        .withColumn("y_normalized", col("y") / col("l2_norm")) \
        .withColumn("z_normalized", col("z") / col("l2_norm"))
    
    print("\nUnit Vector Normalization (L2 Norm):")
    df_l2_norm.select(
        "id", "l2_norm", 
        "x_normalized", "y_normalized", "z_normalized"
    ).show()
    
    # Verify that normalized vectors have length 1
    df_verification = df_l2_norm.withColumn(
        "normalized_length",
        sqrt(
            col("x_normalized")**2 + 
            col("y_normalized")**2 + 
            col("z_normalized")**2
        )
    )
    
    print("\nVerification (all lengths should be 1.0):")
    df_verification.select("id", "normalized_length").show()
    
    # ========================================================================
    # Pattern 7: Quantile Normalization
    # ========================================================================
    print("\n--- Pattern 7: Quantile-based Normalization ---")
    
    quantile_data = [
        (1, 23, 45, 67),
        (2, 45, 78, 89),
        (3, 12, 34, 56),
        (4, 67, 90, 100),
        (5, 34, 56, 78),
        (6, 89, 100, 120),
        (7, 56, 67, 89)
    ]
    
    quantile_schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("feature1", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("feature2", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("feature3", IntegerType(), False)
    ])
    
    df_quantile = normalizer.spark.createDataFrame(quantile_data, quantile_schema)
    
    print("\nOriginal Data:")
    df_quantile.show()
    
    # Calculate quantiles and create bins
    quantiles = df_quantile.approxQuantile("feature1", [0.25, 0.5, 0.75], 0.01)
    
    from pyspark.sql.functions import when
    
    df_quantile_binned = df_quantile.withColumn(
        "feature1_quantile",
        when(col("feature1") <= quantiles[0], 0)
        .when(col("feature1") <= quantiles[1], 1)
        .when(col("feature1") <= quantiles[2], 2)
        .otherwise(3)
    )
    
    print(f"\nQuantile Bins (Q1={quantiles[0]}, Q2={quantiles[1]}, Q3={quantiles[2]}):")
    df_quantile_binned.select("id", "feature1", "feature1_quantile").show()
    
    normalizer.cleanup()

    DATABASE NORMALIZATION FORMS:
    1. First Normal Form (1NF)
       - Eliminates repeating groups
       - Ensures atomic values
       
```python
       - Ensures atomic values
       - Each column contains single type
    
    2. Second Normal Form (2NF)
       - Must be in 1NF
       - Eliminates partial dependencies
       - Non-key attributes fully dependent on primary key
    
    3. Third Normal Form (3NF)
       - Must be in 2NF
       - Eliminates transitive dependencies
       - Non-key attributes depend only on primary key
    
    4. Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF)
       - Stricter version of 3NF
       - Every determinant must be a candidate key
       - Eliminates all anomalies based on functional dependencies
    
    STATISTICAL NORMALIZATION TECHNIQUES:
    1. Min-Max Normalization
       - Scales to fixed range [min, max]
       - Formula: (X - X_min) / (X_max - X_min)
       - Best for: Neural networks, bounded values
       - Sensitive to outliers
    
    2. Z-Score Normalization (Standardization)
       - Centers around mean with unit variance
       - Formula: (X - μ) / σ
       - Best for: Gaussian distributions, SVM, Linear Regression
       - Mean = 0, Std = 1
    
    3. Robust Normalization
       - Uses median and IQR
       - Formula: (X - median) / IQR
       - Best for: Data with outliers
       - More resistant to extreme values
    
    4. L2 Normalization (Unit Vector)
       - Scales to unit length
       - Formula: X / ||X||
       - Best for: Text analysis, cosine similarity
    
    5. Log Transformation
       - Reduces skewness
       - Formula: log(X) or log10(X)
       - Best for: Highly skewed data, exponential distributions
    
    WHEN TO USE WHICH NORMALIZATION:
    
    Database Design:
    - Use 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF for relational database design
    - Reduces redundancy and improves data integrity
    
    Machine Learning:
    - Neural Networks → Min-Max [0,1] or [-1,1]
    - SVM, Linear/Logistic Regression → Z-Score
    - Tree-based models (Random Forest, XGBoost) → No normalization needed
    - K-Means Clustering → Z-Score or Min-Max
    - Distance-based algorithms → Z-Score
    
    Data with Outliers:
    - Use Robust Normalization or Log Transformation
    - Avoid Min-Max (sensitive to outliers)
    
    Text/NLP:
    - TF-IDF → L2 Normalization
    - Word embeddings → Often pre-normalized
    
    Time Series:
    - Min-Max for visualization
    - Z-Score for anomaly detection
    - Differencing for stationarity
    """)
    
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("BEST PRACTICES")
    print("="*80)

def create_normalization_report(df, normalized_df, columns, normalization_type):
    """
    Create a comprehensive report comparing original and normalized data
    
    Args:
        df: Original DataFrame
        normalized_df: Normalized DataFrame
        columns: List of columns that were normalized
        normalization_type: Type of normalization applied
    
    Returns:
        Report DataFrame
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print(f"NORMALIZATION REPORT: {normalization_type}")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    for col_name in columns:
        normalized_col = f"{col_name}_{normalization_type.lower()}"
        
        print(f"\nColumn: {col_name}")
        print("-" * 40)
        
        # Original statistics
        orig_stats = df.select(col_name).describe().collect()
        print("\nOriginal Statistics:")
        for stat in orig_stats:
            print(f"  {stat['summary']:>10}: {stat[col_name]}")
        
        # Normalized statistics
        if normalized_col in normalized_df.columns:
            norm_stats = normalized_df.select(normalized_col).describe().collect()
            print(f"\nNormalized Statistics ({normalization_type}):")
            for stat in norm_stats:
                print(f"  {stat['summary']:>10}: {stat[normalized_col]}")


def save_normalization_parameters(df, columns, output_path, normalization_type):
    """
    Save normalization parameters for later use in production
    
    Args:
        df: DataFrame
        columns: Columns to save parameters for
        output_path: Path to save parameters
        normalization_type: Type of normalization
    """
    import json
    
    parameters = {
        'normalization_type': normalization_type,
        'columns': {}
    }
    
    for col_name in columns:
        if normalization_type.lower() == 'minmax':
            stats = df.agg(
                spark_min(col(col_name)).alias('min'),
                spark_max(col(col_name)).alias('max')
            ).collect()[0]
            
            parameters['columns'][col_name] = {
                'min': float(stats['min']),
                'max': float(stats['max'])
            }
            
        elif normalization_type.lower() == 'zscore':
            stats = df.agg(
                mean(col(col_name)).alias('mean'),
                stddev(col(col_name)).alias('std')
            ).collect()[0]
            
            parameters['columns'][col_name] = {
                'mean': float(stats['mean']),
                'std': float(stats['std'])
            }
    
    # Save to JSON file
    with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
        json.dump(parameters, f, indent=2)
    
    print(f"\nNormalization parameters saved to: {output_path}")
    return parameters


def load_and_apply_normalization(df, parameters_path):
    """
    Load saved normalization parameters and apply to new data
    
    Args:
        df: DataFrame to normalize
        parameters_path: Path to saved parameters
    
    Returns:
        Normalized DataFrame
    """
    import json
    
    with open(parameters_path, 'r') as f:
        parameters = json.load(f)
    
    result_df = df
    normalization_type = parameters['normalization_type']
    
    for col_name, params in parameters['columns'].items():
        if normalization_type.lower() == 'minmax':
            min_val = params['min']
            max_val = params['max']
            
            normalized_col = (col(col_name) - lit(min_val)) / (lit(max_val) - lit(min_val))
            result_df = result_df.withColumn(f"{col_name}_normalized", normalized_col)
            
        elif normalization_type.lower() == 'zscore':
            mean_val = params['mean']
            std_val = params['std']
            
            normalized_col = (col(col_name) - lit(mean_val)) / lit(std_val)
            result_df = result_df.withColumn(f"{col_name}_normalized", normalized_col)
    
    print(f"\nApplied {normalization_type} normalization from saved parameters")
    return result_df


def inverse_transform_minmax(df, col_name, min_val, max_val, 
                             feature_range=(0, 1)):
    """
    Inverse Min-Max transformation to get original values
    
    Args:
        df: DataFrame with normalized values
        col_name: Column name to inverse transform
        min_val: Original minimum value
        max_val: Original maximum value
        feature_range: Range used in normalization
    
    Returns:
        DataFrame with original scale values
    """
    range_min, range_max = feature_range
    
    original_col = (
        (col(col_name) - range_min) / (range_max - range_min)
        * (max_val - min_val) + min_val
    )
    
    return df.withColumn(f"{col_name}_original", original_col)


def inverse_transform_zscore(df, col_name, mean_val, std_val):
    """
    Inverse Z-Score transformation to get original values
    
    Args:
        df: DataFrame with normalized values
        col_name: Column name to inverse transform
        mean_val: Original mean value
        std_val: Original standard deviation
    
    Returns:
        DataFrame with original scale values
    """
    original_col = col(col_name) * lit(std_val) + lit(mean_val)
    
    return df.withColumn(f"{col_name}_original", original_col)


# ========================================================================
# ADDITIONAL EXAMPLE: Complete ML Pipeline with Normalization
# ========================================================================

def complete_ml_pipeline_example():
    """
    Demonstrate a complete ML pipeline with proper normalization
    """
    normalizer = DataNormalizationPatterns("MLPipeline")
    
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("COMPLETE ML PIPELINE WITH NORMALIZATION")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Create sample dataset
    ml_data = [
        (1, 25, 50000, 5, 1),
        (2, 30, 60000, 3, 0),
        (3, 35, 75000, 8, 1),
        (4, 28, 55000, 2, 0),
        (5, 45, 90000, 12, 1),
        (6, 22, 45000, 1, 0),
        (7, 50, 120000, 15, 1),
        (8, 33, 70000, 6, 1),
        (9, 27, 52000, 4, 0),
        (10, 40, 85000, 10, 1)
    ]
    
    ml_schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("age", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("salary", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("experience", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("target", IntegerType(), False)
    ])
    
    df_ml = normalizer.spark.createDataFrame(ml_data, ml_schema)
    
    print("\nOriginal Dataset:")
    df_ml.show()
    
    # Step 1: Train-Test Split (70-30)
    print("\nStep 1: Train-Test Split")
    train_df, test_df = df_ml.randomSplit([0.7, 0.3], seed=42)
    
    print(f"Training samples: {train_df.count()}")
    print(f"Test samples: {test_df.count()}")
    
    # Step 2: Fit normalization on training data only
    print("\nStep 2: Fit Normalization on Training Data")
    
    feature_cols = ["age", "salary", "experience"]
    
    # Calculate normalization parameters from training data
    train_stats = {}
    for col_name in feature_cols:
        stats = train_df.agg(
            spark_min(col(col_name)).alias('min'),
            spark_max(col(col_name)).alias('max'),
            mean(col(col_name)).alias('mean'),
            stddev(col(col_name)).alias('std')
        ).collect()[0]
        
        train_stats[col_name] = {
            'min': stats['min'],
            'max': stats['max'],
            'mean': stats['mean'],
            'std': stats['std']
        }
    
    print("\nTraining Data Statistics:")
    for col_name, stats in train_stats.items():
        print(f"\n{col_name}:")
        for stat_name, value in stats.items():
            print(f"  {stat_name}: {value:.2f}")
    
    # Step 3: Apply normalization to both train and test using training parameters
    print("\nStep 3: Apply Normalization")
    
    # Normalize training data
    train_normalized = train_df
    for col_name in feature_cols:
        stats = train_stats[col_name]
        # Using Z-Score normalization
        normalized_col = (col(col_name) - lit(stats['mean'])) / lit(stats['std'])
        train_normalized = train_normalized.withColumn(
            f"{col_name}_norm", 
            normalized_col
        )
    
    # Normalize test data using SAME parameters from training
    test_normalized = test_df
    for col_name in feature_cols:
        stats = train_stats[col_name]
        normalized_col = (col(col_name) - lit(stats['mean'])) / lit(stats['std'])
        test_normalized = test_normalized.withColumn(
            f"{col_name}_norm", 
            normalized_col
        )
    
    print("\nNormalized Training Data:")
    train_normalized.select(
        "id", "age", "age_norm", "salary", "salary_norm", "target"
    ).show()
    
    print("\nNormalized Test Data:")
    test_normalized.select(
        "id", "age", "age_norm", "salary", "salary_norm", "target"
    ).show()
    
    # Step 4: Save normalization parameters
    print("\nStep 4: Save Normalization Parameters")
    save_normalization_parameters(
        train_df,
        feature_cols,
        "/tmp/normalization_params.json",
        "zscore"
    )
    
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("ML PIPELINE COMPLETE")
    print("="*80)
    print("""
    Key Points:
    1. ✓ Split data BEFORE normalization
    2. ✓ Fit normalization on training data only
    3. ✓ Apply same parameters to test data
    4. ✓ Save parameters for production use
    5. ✓ No data leakage occurred
    """)
    
    normalizer.cleanup()


# Run the complete ML pipeline example
if __name__ == "__main__":
    complete_ml_pipeline_example()

```

## Summary

This comprehensive PySpark implementation covers all requested normalization patterns:

### **Database Normalization Forms:**
1. **1NF** - Eliminates multi-valued attributes
2. **2NF** - Removes partial dependencies
3. **3NF** - Eliminates transitive dependencies
4. **
```python
4. **BCNF** - Ensures every determinant is a candidate key

### **Statistical Normalization Techniques:**
5. **Min-Max Normalization** - Scales to [0,1] or custom range
6. **Z-Score Normalization** - Standardizes to mean=0, std=1

### **Additional Patterns Included:**
- Robust Normalization (using median and IQR)
- L2 Normalization (Unit Vector)
- Log Transformation
- Decimal Scaling
- Group-wise Normalization
- Quantile-based Normalization

### **Performance Considerations:**

1. **Custom implementations** - Better for:
   - Small to medium datasets
   - When you need fine control
   - Simple transformations

2. **ML-based implementations** - Better for:
   - Large datasets
   - Multiple features
   - Production pipelines
   - When using Spark ML library

### **When to Use Each Normalization:**

| Scenario | Recommended Normalization |
|----------|--------------------------|
| Neural Networks | Min-Max [0,1] or [-1,1] |
| SVM, Linear Regression | Z-Score |
| Tree-based Models | None (not needed) |
| Data with Outliers | Robust or Log Transform |
| Distance-based Algorithms | Z-Score or Min-Max |
| Text/NLP | L2 Normalization |
| Database Design | 1NF → 2NF → 3NF → BCNF |

### **Customization:**

You can easily extend the class with additional normalization methods:

```python
class DataNormalizationPatterns:
    # ... existing methods ...
    
    def custom_normalization(self, df, columns, custom_func):
        """
        Apply custom normalization function
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            columns: Columns to normalize
            custom_func: Custom transformation function
        """
        result_df = df
        for col_name in columns:
            result_df = result_df.withColumn(
                f"{col_name}_custom",
                custom_func(col(col_name))
            )
        return result_df

```python
def validate_normalization(original_df, normalized_df, 
                          col_name, norm_type):
    """Validate normalization results"""
    
    if norm_type == "minmax":
        # Check range [0, 1]
        min_val = normalized_df.agg(
            spark_min(col(f"{col_name}_normalized"))
        ).collect()[0][0]
        max_val = normalized_df.agg(
            spark_max(col(f"{col_name}_normalized"))
        ).collect()[0][0]
        
        assert min_val >= 0 and max_val <= 1, \
            f"Min-Max values out of range: [{min_val}, {max_val}]"
        print(f"✓ Min-Max validation passed: [{min_val:.4f}, {max_val:.4f}]")
    
    elif norm_type == "zscore":
        # Check mean ≈ 0, std ≈ 1
        stats = normalized_df.agg(
            mean(col(f"{col_name}_zscore")).alias('mean'),
            stddev(col(f"{col_name}_zscore")).alias('std')
        ).collect()[0]
        
        assert abs(stats['mean']) < 0.01, \
            f"Mean not close to 0: {stats['mean']}"
        assert abs(stats['std'] - 1) < 0.01, \
            f"Std not close to 1: {stats['std']}"
        print(f"✓ Z-Score validation passed: mean={stats['mean']:.4f}, std={stats['std']:.4f}")
```

    def test_first_normal_form(self):

    def test_min_max_normalization_range(self):

        schema = StructType([

            StructField("value", IntegerType(), False)
        ])
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)

        ).collect()[0]
        
        self.assertAlmostEqual(stats["min"], 0.0, places=5)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(stats["max"], 1.0, places=5)
        
        print("✓ Test Min-Max range passed")

        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("value", DoubleType(), False)
        ])
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)

        result = self.normalizer.z_score_normalization(df, ["value"])
        
        # Check mean and std

        ).collect()[0]
        
        self.assertAlmostEqual(stats["mean"], 0.0, places=5)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(stats["std"], 1.0, places=5)

    def test_zero_variance_handling(self):
        """Test handling of zero variance features"""
        data = [(i, 100, i * 10) for i in range(1, 11)]  # constant_col = 100
        schema = StructType([

        ])

        """Test inverse Min-Max transformation"""
        data = [(i, float(i * 10)) for i in range(1, 11)]
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("value", DoubleType(), False)
        ])

        stats = df.agg(
            spark_min("value").alias("min"),

        ).collect()[0]
        
        # Normalize
        normalized = self.normalizer.min_max_normalization(
            df,

            feature_range=(0, 1)
        )

        )
        
        # Compare original and restored values

            restored.select("id", "value_normalized_original"),
            "id"
        )
        
        for row in comparison.collect():
            self.assertAlmostEqual(
                row["value"], 
                row["value_normalized_original"],
                places=5
            )
        
        print("✓ Test inverse Min-Max transform passed")

            )

    def test_second_normal_form(self):
        """Test 2NF transformation"""
        data = [
            (1, "John", 101, "Math", "A"),
            (1, "John", 102, "Physics", "B"),
            (2, "Jane", 101, "Math", "A")
        ]
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("student_id", IntegerType(), False),

            StructField("course_id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("course_name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("grade", StringType(), False)
        ])
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        
        # Apply 2NF
        dependent_cols_map = {
            'main_table': ['student_id', 'course_id', 'grade'],
            'student_table': ['student_id', 'student_name'],
            'course_table': ['course_id', 'course_name']
        }
        
        result = self.normalizer.second_normal_form(
            df,
            primary_key_cols=['student_id', 'course_id'],
            dependent_cols_map=dependent_cols_map
        )
        
        # Verify tables were created
        self.assertIn('main_table', result)
        self.assertIn('student_table', result)
        self.assertIn('course_table', result)
        
        # Verify student table has no duplicates
        student_count = result['student_table'].count()
        distinct_students = result['student_table'].select('student_id').distinct().count()
        self.assertEqual(student_count, distinct_students)
        
        print("✓ Test 2NF passed")

    def test_ml_minmax_scaler(self):
        """Test ML-based Min-Max scaler"""
        data = [(i, float(i), float(i * 10)) for i in range(1, 11)]
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("col1", DoubleType(), False),

        ])
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        
        # Apply ML-based Min-Max

            spark_min("col1_scaled").alias("min"),
            spark_max("col1_scaled").alias("max")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        self.assertAlmostEqual(stats["min"], 0.0, places=5)
        self.assertAlmostEqual(stats["max"], 1.0, places=5)
        
        print("✓ Test ML Min-Max scaler passed")

        data = [(i, float(i), float(i * 10)) for i in range(1, 101)]

        # Apply ML-based Z-Score

        )

        ).collect()[
```python
        ).collect()[0]

        self.assertAlmostEqual(stats["std"], 1.0, places=5)

    def test_data_leakage_prevention(self):
        """Test that normalization prevents data leakage"""
        # Create train/test split
        data = [(i, float(i * 10)) for i in range(1, 21)]
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("value", DoubleType(), False)
        ])
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        
        train_df, test_df = df.randomSplit([0.7, 0.3], seed=42)
        
        # Calculate stats from training data only
        train_stats = train_df.agg(
            mean("value").alias("mean"),
            stddev("value").alias("std")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        # Apply same normalization to both sets
        train_norm = train_df.withColumn(
            "value_norm",
            (col("value") - lit(train_stats["mean"])) / lit(train_stats["std"])
        )
        
        test_norm = test_df.withColumn(
            "value_norm",
            (col("value") - lit(train_stats["mean"])) / lit(train_stats["std"])
        )
        
        # Test set should use training parameters (not its own)
        test_stats = test_norm.agg(
            mean("value_norm").alias("mean")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        # Test mean should NOT be exactly 0 (would indicate data leakage)
        self.assertNotAlmostEqual(test_stats["mean"], 0.0, places=1)
        
        print("✓ Test data leakage prevention passed")
    
    def test_empty_dataframe_handling(self):
        """Test handling of empty DataFrames"""
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("value", DoubleType(), False)
        ])
        empty_df = self.spark.createDataFrame([], schema)
        
        # Should handle empty DataFrame gracefully
        try:
            result = self.normalizer.min_max_normalization(
                empty_df,
                ["value"]
            )
            # If it doesn't raise an error, check it returns empty
            self.assertEqual(result.count(), 0)
            print("✓ Test empty DataFrame handling passed")
        except Exception as e:
            # Expected behavior - log and pass
            print(f"✓ Test empty DataFrame handling passed (raised: {type(e).__name__})")
    
    def test_null_value_handling(self):
        """Test handling of null values"""
        data = [
            (1, 10.0),
            (2, None),
            (3, 30.0),
            (4, 40.0)
        ]
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("value", DoubleType(), True)
        ])
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        
        # Normalization should handle nulls
        result = self.normalizer.z_score_normalization(df, ["value"])
        
        # Check that null remains null
        null_row = result.filter(col("id") == 2).collect()[0]
        self.assertIsNone(null_row["value_zscore"])
        
        # Check that non-null values are normalized
        non_null_count = result.filter(col("value_zscore").isNotNull()).count()
        self.assertEqual(non_null_count, 3)
        
        print("✓ Test null value handling passed")

def benchmark_normalization_methods():
    """
    Comprehensive performance benchmarking of different normalization methods
    """
    normalizer = DataNormalizationPatterns("Benchmarking")
    
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PERFORMANCE BENCHMARKING")
    print("="*80)
    
    import time
    
    # Test different dataset sizes
    sizes = [1000, 10000, 100000]
    results = []
    
    for size in sizes:
        print(f"\n--- Dataset Size: {size:,} rows ---")
        
        # Generate test data
        data = [(i, float(i), float(i * 10), float(i * 100)) 
                for i in range(1, size + 1)]
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("col1", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("col2", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("col3", DoubleType(), False)
        ])
        df = normalizer.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        df.cache()
        df.count()  # Materialize cache
        
        cols = ["col1", "col2", "col3"]
        
        # Benchmark 1: Custom Min-Max
        start = time.time()
        df_minmax = normalizer.min_max_normalization(df, cols)
        df_minmax.count()
        time_minmax = time.time() - start
        
        # Benchmark 2: ML Min-Max
        start = time.time()
        df_ml_minmax = normalizer.min_max_normalization_ml(df, cols)
        df_ml_minmax.count()
        time_ml_minmax = time.time() - start
        
        # Benchmark 3: Custom Z-Score
        start = time.time()
        df_zscore = normalizer.z_score_normalization(df, cols)
        df_zscore.count()
        time_zscore = time.time() - start
        
        # Benchmark 4: ML Z-Score
        start = time.time()
        df_ml_zscore = normalizer.z_score_normalization_ml(df, cols)
        df_ml_zscore.count()
        time_ml_zscore = time.time() - start
        
        # Benchmark 5: Robust Normalization
        start = time.time()
        df_robust = normalizer.robust_normalization(df, cols)
        df_robust.count()
        time_robust = time.time() - start
        
        # Store results
        results.append({
            'size': size,
            'custom_minmax': time_minmax,
            'ml_minmax': time_ml_minmax,
            'custom_zscore': time_zscore,
            'ml_zscore': time_ml_zscore,
            'robust': time_robust
        })
        
        # Display results
        print(f"Custom Min-Max:    {time_minmax:.4f}s")
        print(f"ML Min-Max:        {time_ml_minmax:.4f}s")
        print(f"Custom Z-Score:    {time_zscore:.4f}s")
        print(f"ML Z-Score:        {time_ml_zscore:.4f}s")
        print(f"Robust:            {time_robust:.4f}s")
        
        df.unpersist()
    
    # Summary table
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PERFORMANCE SUMMARY (seconds)")
    print("="*80)
    print(f"{'Size':<10} {'Custom MM':<12} {'ML MM':<12} {'Custom ZS':<12} {'ML ZS':<12} {'Robust':<12}")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    for r in results:
        print(f"{r['size']:<10,} {r['custom_minmax']:<12.4f} {r['ml_minmax']:<12.4f} "
              f"{r['custom_zscore']:<12.4f} {r['ml_zscore']:<12.4f} {r['robust']:<12.4f}")
    
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("RECOMMENDATIONS")
    print("="*80)
    print("""
    Based on benchmarks:
    
    1. For small datasets (< 10K rows):
       - Custom implementations are often faster
       - More control and flexibility
    
    2. For large datasets (> 100K rows):
       - ML-based implementations scale better
       - Optimized for distributed processing
    
    3. For multiple features:
       - ML implementations more efficient
       - Single pass over data
    
    4. For production pipelines:
       - Use ML implementations
       - Better integration with Spark ML
    """)
    
    normalizer.cleanup()

def real_world_example_customer_segmentation():
    """
    Real-world example: Customer segmentation with normalization
    """
    normalizer = DataNormalizationPatterns("CustomerSegmentation")
    
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("REAL-WORLD EXAMPLE: CUSTOMER SEGMENTATION")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Simulated customer data
    customer_data = [
        (1, "Alice", 25, 50000, 5, 1200, 15),
        (2, "Bob", 35, 75000, 10, 3500, 45),
        (3, "Charlie", 45, 120000, 20, 8000, 120),
        (4, "Diana", 28, 60000, 3, 1800, 20),
        (5, "Eve", 52, 150000, 25, 12000, 200),
        (6, "Frank", 31, 68000, 7, 2400, 30),
        (7, "Grace", 38, 85000, 12, 4200, 60),
        (8, "Henry", 42, 95000, 15, 5500, 80),
        (9, "Ivy", 29, 62000, 4, 2000, 25),
        (10, "Jack", 48, 110000, 18, 7000, 100)
    ]
    
    customer_schema = StructType([
        StructField("customer_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("name", StringType(), False),
        StructField("age", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("income", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("years_customer", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("total_purchases", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("num_transactions", IntegerType(), False)
    ])
    
    df_customers = normalizer.spark.createDataFrame(customer_data, customer_schema)
    
    print("\nOriginal Customer Data:")
    df_customers.show()
    
    print("\nData Statistics:")
    df_customers.select(
        "age", "income", "years_customer", "total_purchases", "num_transactions"
    ).describe().show()
    
    # Step 1: Normalize features for clustering
    print("\nStep 1: Normalize Features for K-Means Clustering")
    
    features = ["age", "income", "years_customer", "total_purchases", "num_transactions"]
    
    # Use Z-Score normalization for clustering
    df_normalized = normalizer.z_score_normalization(
        df_customers,
        columns_to_normalize=features,
        output_col_suffix="_norm"
    )
    
    print("\nNormalized Features:")
    df_normalized.select(
        "customer_id", "name",
        "age", "age_norm",
        "income", "income_norm"
    ).show()
    
    # Step 2: Create feature vector for ML
    print("\nStep 2: Create Feature Vector")
    
    from pyspark.ml.feature import VectorAssembler
    
    normalized_features = [f"{f}_norm" for f in features]
    assembler = VectorAssembler(
        inputCols=normalized_features,
        outputCol="features"
    )
    
    df_features = assembler.transform(df_normalized)
    
    print("\nFeature Vectors:")
    df_features.select("customer_id", "name", "features").show(truncate=False)
    
    # Step 3: Apply K-Means clustering
    print("\nStep 3: Apply K-Means Clustering")
    
    from pyspark.ml.clustering import KMeans
    
    kmeans = KMeans(k=3, seed=42, featuresCol="features", predictionCol="segment")
    model = kmeans.fit(df_features)
    
    df_segmented = model.transform(df_features)
    
    print("\nCustomer Segments:")
    df_segmented.select(
        "customer_id", "name", "age", "income", 
        "total_purchases", "segment"
    ).orderBy("segment").show()
    
    # Step 4: Analyze segments
    print("\nStep 4: Segment Analysis")
    
    segment_analysis = df_segmented.groupBy("segment").agg(
        count("*").alias("num_customers"),
        mean("age").alias("avg_age"),
        mean("income").alias("avg_income"),
        mean("total_purchases").alias("avg_purchases"),
        mean("num_transactions").alias("avg_transactions")
    ).orderBy("segment")
    
    print("\nSegment Characteristics:")
    segment_analysis.show()
    
    # Step 5: Segment profiling
    print("\nStep 5: Segment Profiling")
    
    for segment_id in range(3):
        print(f"\n--- Segment {segment_id} Profile ---")
        segment_df = df_segmented.filter(col("segment") == segment_id)
        
        stats = segment_df.agg(
            count("*").alias("count"),
            mean("age").alias("avg_age"),
            mean("income").alias("avg_income"),
            mean("years_customer").alias("avg_tenure"),
            mean("total_purchases").alias("avg_purchases")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        print(f"Customers: {stats['count']}")
        print(f"Avg Age: {stats['avg_age']:.1f}")
        print(f"Avg Income: ${stats['avg_income']:,.0f}")
        print(f"Avg Tenure: {stats['avg_tenure']:.1f} years")
        print(f"Avg Purchases: ${stats['avg_purchases']:,.0f}")
        
        # Assign segment label
        if stats['avg_income'] > 100000:
            label = "Premium Customers"
        elif stats['avg_purchases'] > 4000:
            label = "High Value Customers"
        else:
            label = "Standard Customers"
        
        print(f"Label: {label}")
    
    normalizer.cleanup()


def real_world_example_fraud_detection():
    """

    """

    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("REAL-WORLD EXAMPLE: FRAUD DETECTION")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Simulated transaction data
    transaction_data = [
        (1, 1001, 50.0, 1, 10.5, 0),
        (2, 1001, 75.0, 1, 15.2, 0),
        (3, 1002, 5000.0, 10, 2.3, 1),
```python
        (3, 1002, 5000.0, 10, 2.3, 1),  # Fraud
        (4, 1003, 120.0, 2, 20.1, 0),
        (5, 1001, 65.0, 1, 12.8, 0),
        (6, 1004, 8000.0, 15, 1.5, 1),  # Fraud
        (7, 1005, 200.0, 3, 25.0, 0),
        (8, 1002, 4500.0, 8, 3.1, 1),   # Fraud
        (9, 1006, 85.0, 1, 18.5, 0),
        (10, 1003, 150.0, 2, 22.3, 0),
        (11, 1007, 10000.0, 20, 0.8, 1), # Fraud
        (12, 1008, 95.0, 1, 16.7, 0),
        (13, 1009, 3000.0, 5, 4.2, 1),   # Fraud
        (14, 1010, 110.0, 2, 19.8, 0),
        (15, 1001, 55.0, 1, 11.2, 0)
    ]
    
    transaction_schema = StructType([
        StructField("transaction_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("user_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("amount", DoubleType(), False),
        StructField("num_items", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("time_since_last_txn", DoubleType(), False),
        StructField("is_fraud", IntegerType(), False)
    ])
    
    df_transactions = normalizer.spark.createDataFrame(
        transaction_data, 
        transaction_schema
    )
    
    print("\nTransaction Data:")
    df_transactions.show()
    
    # Analyze fraud vs normal transactions
    print("\nFraud Analysis:")
    df_transactions.groupBy("is_fraud").agg(
        count("*").alias("count"),
        mean("amount").alias("avg_amount"),
        mean("num_items").alias("avg_items"),
        mean("time_since_last_txn").alias("avg_time_gap")
    ).show()
    
    # Step 1: Feature Engineering
    print("\nStep 1: Feature Engineering")
    
    # Calculate additional features
    df_features = df_transactions.withColumn(
        "amount_per_item",
        col("amount") / col("num_items")
    ).withColumn(
        "is_high_amount",
        (col("amount") > 1000).cast(IntegerType())
    ).withColumn(
        "is_fast_transaction",
        (col("time_since_last_txn") < 5).cast(IntegerType())
    )
    
    print("\nEngineered Features:")
    df_features.select(
        "transaction_id", "amount", "num_items", 
        "amount_per_item", "is_high_amount", "is_fraud"
    ).show()
    
    # Step 2: Handle class imbalance - show distribution
    print("\nStep 2: Class Distribution")
    fraud_count = df_features.filter(col("is_fraud") == 1).count()
    normal_count = df_features.filter(col("is_fraud") == 0).count()
    total = df_features.count()
    
    print(f"Normal transactions: {normal_count} ({normal_count/total*100:.1f}%)")
    print(f"Fraudulent transactions: {fraud_count} ({fraud_count/total*100:.1f}%)")
    
    # Step 3: Split data before normalization
    print("\nStep 3: Train-Test Split (before normalization)")
    train_df, test_df = df_features.randomSplit([0.7, 0.3], seed=42)
    
    print(f"Training set: {train_df.count()} transactions")
    print(f"Test set: {test_df.count()} transactions")
    
    # Step 4: Normalize features using training data statistics
    print("\nStep 4: Feature Normalization (Robust - handles outliers)")
    
    numeric_features = ["amount", "num_items", "time_since_last_txn", "amount_per_item"]
    
    # Calculate robust statistics from training data
    train_params = {}
    for feature in numeric_features:
        quantiles = train_df.approxQuantile(feature, [0.25, 0.5, 0.75], 0.01)
        train_params[feature] = {
            'q1': quantiles[0],
            'median': quantiles[1],
            'q3': quantiles[2],
            'iqr': quantiles[2] - quantiles[0]
        }
    
    print("\nTraining Data Statistics (Robust):")
    for feature, params in train_params.items():
        print(f"\n{feature}:")
        print(f"  Median: {params['median']:.2f}")
        print(f"  IQR: {params['iqr']:.2f}")
    
    # Apply robust normalization to train and test
    train_normalized = train_df
    test_normalized = test_df
    
    for feature in numeric_features:
        params = train_params[feature]
        median = params['median']
        iqr = params['iqr'] if params['iqr'] != 0 else 1.0
        
        # Apply to training data
        train_normalized = train_normalized.withColumn(
            f"{feature}_norm",
            (col(feature) - lit(median)) / lit(iqr)
        )
        
        # Apply to test data using SAME parameters
        test_normalized = test_normalized.withColumn(
            f"{feature}_norm",
            (col(feature) - lit(median)) / lit(iqr)
        )
    
    print("\nNormalized Training Data:")
    train_normalized.select(
        "transaction_id", "amount", "amount_norm", 
        "is_fraud"
    ).show(10)
    
    # Step 5: Prepare features for ML model
    print("\nStep 5: Prepare Feature Vectors")
    
    from pyspark.ml.feature import VectorAssembler
    
    feature_cols = [f"{f}_norm" for f in numeric_features] + \
                   ["is_high_amount", "is_fast_transaction"]
    
    assembler = VectorAssembler(
        inputCols=feature_cols,
        outputCol="features"
    )
    
    train_ml = assembler.transform(train_normalized)
    test_ml = assembler.transform(test_normalized)
    
    print("\nFeature Vector Sample:")
    train_ml.select("transaction_id", "features", "is_fraud").show(5, truncate=False)
    
    # Step 6: Train Random Forest model
    print("\nStep 6: Train Random Forest Classifier")
    
    from pyspark.ml.classification import RandomForestClassifier
    from pyspark.ml.evaluation import BinaryClassificationEvaluator
    
    rf = RandomForestClassifier(
        featuresCol="features",
        labelCol="is_fraud",
        numTrees=10,
        maxDepth=5,
        seed=42
    )
    
    model = rf.fit(train_ml)
    
    # Step 7: Make predictions
    print("\nStep 7: Make Predictions on Test Set")
    
    predictions = model.transform(test_ml)
    
    print("\nPredictions:")
    predictions.select(
        "transaction_id", "amount", "is_fraud", 
        "prediction", "probability"
    ).show(truncate=False)
    
    # Step 8: Evaluate model
    print("\nStep 8: Model Evaluation")
    
    evaluator = BinaryClassificationEvaluator(
        labelCol="is_fraud",
        rawPredictionCol="rawPrediction",
        metricName="areaUnderROC"
    )
    
    auc = evaluator.evaluate(predictions)
    print(f"\nAUC-ROC: {auc:.4f}")
    
    # Confusion matrix
    from pyspark.sql.functions import sum as spark_sum
    
    tp = predictions.filter((col("is_fraud") == 1) & (col("prediction") == 1)).count()
    tn = predictions.filter((col("is_fraud") == 0) & (col("prediction") == 0)).count()
    fp = predictions.filter((col("is_fraud") == 0) & (col("prediction") == 1)).count()
    fn = predictions.filter((col("is_fraud") == 1) & (col("prediction") == 0)).count()
    
    print("\nConfusion Matrix:")
    print(f"                Predicted")
    print(f"              0      1")
    print(f"Actual 0    {tn:3d}    {fp:3d}")
    print(f"       1    {fn:3d}    {tp:3d}")
    
    # Calculate metrics
    accuracy = (tp + tn) / (tp + tn + fp + fn) if (tp + tn + fp + fn) > 0 else 0
    precision = tp / (tp + fp) if (tp + fp) > 0 else 0
    recall = tp / (tp + fn) if (tp + fn) > 0 else 0
    f1 = 2 * (precision * recall) / (precision + recall) if (precision + recall) > 0 else 0
    
    print(f"\nMetrics:")
    print(f"Accuracy:  {accuracy:.4f}")
    print(f"Precision: {precision:.4f}")
    print(f"Recall:    {recall:.4f}")
    print(f"F1-Score:  {f1:.4f}")
    
    # Feature importance
    print("\nFeature Importance:")
    feature_importance = model.featureImportances.toArray()
    for i, importance in enumerate(feature_importance):
        print(f"{feature_cols[i]:30s}: {importance:.4f}")
    
    normalizer.cleanup()


def real_world_example_time_series_forecasting():
    """
    Real-world example: Time series forecasting with normalization
    """
    normalizer = DataNormalizationPatterns("TimeSeriesForecasting")
    
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("REAL-WORLD EXAMPLE: TIME SERIES SALES FORECASTING")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Simulated daily sales data
    from datetime import datetime, timedelta
    
    start_date = datetime(2024, 1, 1)
    sales_data = []
    
    for i in range(90):  # 90 days of data
        date = start_date + timedelta(days=i)
        # Simulate sales with trend and seasonality
        trend = 1000 + i * 10
        seasonal = 200 * (1 if date.weekday() < 5 else 0.5)  # Weekday vs weekend
        noise = (i % 7) * 50
        sales = trend + seasonal + noise
        
        sales_data.append((
            date.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"),
            int(sales),
            date.weekday(),
            1 if date.weekday() < 5 else 0
        ))
    
    sales_schema = StructType([
        StructField("date", StringType(), False),
        StructField("sales", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("day_of_week", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("is_weekday", IntegerType(), False)
    ])
    
    df_sales = normalizer.spark.createDataFrame(sales_data, sales_schema)
    
    print("\nSales Data (First 14 days):")
    df_sales.show(14)
    
    # Step 1: Feature Engineering
    print("\nStep 1: Feature Engineering")
    
    # Add rolling statistics
    from pyspark.sql.window import Window
    
    window_7 = Window.orderBy("date").rowsBetween(-6, 0)
    window_30 = Window.orderBy("date").rowsBetween(-29, 0)
    
    df_features = df_sales \
        .withColumn("sales_7day_avg", mean("sales").over(window_7)) \
        .withColumn("sales_30day_avg", mean("sales").over(window_30)) \
        .withColumn("sales_7day_std", stddev("sales").over(window_7))
    
    print("\nEngineered Features:")
    df_features.select(
        "date", "sales", "sales_7day_avg", "sales_30day_avg"
    ).show(14)
    
    # Step 2: Train-Test Split (temporal split)
    print("\nStep 2: Temporal Train-Test Split")
    
    # Use first 70 days for training, last 20 for testing
    train_df = df_features.limit(70)
    test_df = df_features.subtract(train_df)
    
    print(f"Training period: {train_df.count()} days")
    print(f"Test period: {test_df.count()} days")
    
    # Step 3: Normalize features
    print("\nStep 3: Normalize Features")
    
    features_to_normalize = ["sales", "sales_7day_avg", "sales_30day_avg"]
    
    # Use Min-Max normalization for time series
    train_normalized = normalizer.min_max_normalization(
        train_df,
        columns_to_normalize=features_to_normalize,
        feature_range=(0, 1),
        output_col_suffix="_norm"
    )
    
    # Get normalization parameters from training data
    norm_params = {}
    for feature in features_to_normalize:
        stats = train_df.agg(
            spark_min(feature).alias("min"),
            spark_max(feature).alias("max")
        ).collect()[0]
        norm_params[feature] = {'min': stats['min'], 'max': stats['max']}
    
    # Apply same normalization to test data
    test_normalized = test_df
    for feature in features_to_normalize:
        min_val = norm_params[feature]['min']
        max_val = norm_params[feature]['max']
        
        test_normalized = test_normalized.withColumn(
            f"{feature}_norm",
            (col(feature) - lit(min_val)) / (lit(max_val) - lit(min_val))
        )
    
    print("\nNormalized Training Data:")
    train_normalized.select(
        "date", "sales", "sales_norm", "sales_7day_avg_norm"
    ).show(10)
    
    # Step 4: Visualize normalization effect
    print("\nStep 4: Compare Original vs Normalized Sales")
    
    comparison = train_normalized.select(
        "date", "sales", "sales_norm"
    ).orderBy("date")
    
    print("\nOriginal vs Normalized (First 10 days):")
    comparison.show(10)
    
    # Step 5: Denormalization for predictions
    print("\nStep 5: Denormalization Example")
    
    # Simulate a prediction (normalized value)
    sample_prediction = 0.75  # Normalized prediction
    
    # Denormalize
    sales_min = norm_params['sales']['min']
    sales
```python
    sales_min = norm_params['sales']['min']
    sales_max = norm_params['sales']['max']
    
    actual_prediction = sample_prediction * (sales_max - sales_min) + sales_min
    
    print(f"\nNormalized prediction: {sample_prediction}")
    print(f"Denormalized prediction: ${actual_prediction:,.2f}")
    print(f"(Range: ${sales_min:,.2f} - ${sales_max:,.2f})")
    
    # Step 6: Calculate forecast accuracy metrics
    print("\nStep 6: Forecast Accuracy Metrics")
    
    # Simple baseline: use 7-day average as prediction
    test_with_baseline = test_normalized.withColumn(
        "baseline_prediction_norm",
        col("sales_7day_avg_norm")
    )
    
    # Denormalize predictions
    test_with_baseline = test_with_baseline.withColumn(
        "baseline_prediction",
        col("baseline_prediction_norm") * (sales_max - sales_min) + sales_min
    )
    
    # Calculate errors
    test_with_errors = test_with_baseline.withColumn(
        "error",
        col("sales") - col("baseline_prediction")
    ).withColumn(
        "absolute_error",
        abs(col("error"))
    ).withColumn(
        "squared_error",
        col("error") ** 2
    ).withColumn(
        "percentage_error",
        abs(col("error") / col("sales")) * 100
    )
    
    print("\nForecast Results:")
    test_with_errors.select(
        "date", "sales", "baseline_prediction", 
        "error", "percentage_error"
    ).show(10)
    
    # Calculate metrics
    metrics = test_with_errors.agg(
        mean("absolute_error").alias("MAE"),
        sqrt(mean("squared_error")).alias("RMSE"),
        mean("percentage_error").alias("MAPE")
    ).collect()[0]
    
    print("\nForecast Accuracy Metrics:")
    print(f"MAE (Mean Absolute Error):      ${metrics['MAE']:,.2f}")
    print(f"RMSE (Root Mean Squared Error): ${metrics['RMSE']:,.2f}")
    print(f"MAPE (Mean Absolute % Error):   {metrics['MAPE']:.2f}%")
    
    normalizer.cleanup()

def advanced_edge_cases():
    """
    Demonstrate handling of advanced edge cases
    """
    normalizer = DataNormalizationPatterns("EdgeCases")
    
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("ADVANCED EDGE CASES")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Edge Case 1: Highly Skewed Data
    print("\n--- Edge Case 1: Highly Skewed Data ---")
    
    skewed_data = [
        (1, 10), (2, 15), (3, 12), (4, 18), (5, 20),
        (6, 14), (7, 16), (8, 11), (9, 19), (10, 10000)  # Extreme outlier
    ]
    
    skewed_schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("value", IntegerType(), False)
    ])
    
    df_skewed = normalizer.spark.createDataFrame(skewed_data, skewed_schema)
    
    print("\nOriginal Skewed Data:")
    df_skewed.show()
    
    # Compare normalization techniques
    print("\nMin-Max Normalization (sensitive to outliers):")
    df_minmax_skewed = normalizer.min_max_normalization(
        df_skewed, ["value"], feature_range=(0, 1)
    )
    df_minmax_skewed.select("id", "value", "value_normalized").show()
    
    print("\nRobust Normalization (resistant to outliers):")
    df_robust_skewed = normalizer.robust_normalization(
        df_skewed, ["value"]
    )
    df_robust_skewed.select("id", "value", "value_robust").show()
    
    print("\nLog Transformation + Z-Score:")
    from pyspark.sql.functions import log as spark_log
    
    df_log = df_skewed.withColumn("value_log", spark_log(col("value")))
    df_log_norm = normalizer.z_score_normalization(df_log, ["value_log"])
    df_log_norm.select("id", "value", "value_log", "value_log_zscore").show()
    
    # Edge Case 2: Categorical Features with Normalization
    print("\n--- Edge Case 2: Mixed Categorical and Numerical Features ---")
    
    mixed_data = [
        (1, "A", 100, 50),
        (2, "B", 200, 60),
        (3, "A", 150, 55),
        (4, "C", 300, 70),
        (5, "B", 250, 65)
    ]
    
    mixed_schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("category", StringType(), False),
        StructField("numeric1", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("numeric2", IntegerType(), False)
    ])
    
    df_mixed = normalizer.spark.createDataFrame(mixed_data, mixed_schema)
    
    print("\nMixed Data:")
    df_mixed.show()
    
    # One-hot encode categorical, normalize numerical
    from pyspark.ml.feature import StringIndexer, OneHotEncoder
    
    indexer = StringIndexer(inputCol="category", outputCol="category_index")
    encoder = OneHotEncoder(inputCol="category_index", outputCol="category_vec")
    
    df_indexed = indexer.fit(df_mixed).transform(df_mixed)
    df_encoded = encoder.fit(df_indexed).transform(df_indexed)
    
    # Normalize numerical features
    df_final = normalizer.z_score_normalization(
        df_encoded, 
        ["numeric1", "numeric2"]
    )
    
    print("\nProcessed Mixed Features:")
    df_final.select(
        "id", "category", "category_vec", 
        "numeric1_zscore", "numeric2_zscore"
    ).show(truncate=False)
    
    # Edge Case 3: Missing Values in Normalization
    print("\n--- Edge Case 3: Missing Values ---")
    
    missing_data = [
        (1, 100.0, 50.0),
        (2, None, 60.0),
        (3, 150.0, None),
        (4, 200.0, 70.0),
        (5, None, None)
    ]
    
    missing_schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("col1", DoubleType(), True),
        StructField("col2", DoubleType(), True)
    ])
    
    df_missing = normalizer.spark.createDataFrame(missing_data, missing_schema)
    
    print("\nData with Missing Values:")
    df_missing.show()
    
    # Strategy 1: Normalize with nulls (nulls remain null)
    print("\nStrategy 1: Keep Nulls")
    df_norm_nulls = normalizer.z_score_normalization(
        df_missing, 
        ["col1", "col2"]
    )
    df_norm_nulls.select("id", "col1", "col1_zscore", "col2", "col2_zscore").show()
    
    # Strategy 2: Impute then normalize
    print("\nStrategy 2: Impute Mean, Then Normalize")
    
    # Calculate mean excluding nulls
    col1_mean = df_missing.agg(mean("col1")).collect()[0][0]
    col2_mean = df_missing.agg(mean("col2")).collect()[0][0]
    
    df_imputed = df_missing \
        .fillna({'col1': col1_mean, 'col2': col2_mean})
    
    print("\nAfter Imputation:")
    df_imputed.show()
    
    df_imputed_norm = normalizer.z_score_normalization(
        df_imputed, 
        ["col1", "col2"]
    )
    
    print("\nAfter Normalization:")
    df_imputed_norm.select("id", "col1_zscore", "col2_zscore").show()
    
    # Edge Case 4: Very Large Numbers
    print("\n--- Edge Case 4: Very Large Numbers ---")
    
    large_data = [
        (1, 1e10, 1e15),
        (2, 2e10, 2e15),
        (3, 3e10, 3e15),
        (4, 4e10, 4e15)
    ]
    
    large_schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("big_num1", DoubleType(), False),
        StructField("big_num2", DoubleType(), False)
    ])
    
    df_large = normalizer.spark.createDataFrame(large_data, large_schema)
    
    print("\nVery Large Numbers:")
    df_large.show()
    
    # Normalize to prevent numerical instability
    df_large_norm = normalizer.min_max_normalization(
        df_large, 
        ["big_num1", "big_num2"]
    )
    
    print("\nNormalized Large Numbers:")
    df_large_norm.select(
        "id", "big_num1_normalized", "big_num2_normalized"
    ).show()
    
    # Edge Case 5: Single Value (Zero Variance)
    print("\n--- Edge Case 5: Single Unique Value ---")
    
    single_data = [
        (1, 100, 50),
        (2, 100, 60),
        (3, 100, 70),
        (4, 100, 80)
    ]
    
    single_schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("constant", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("variable", IntegerType(), False)
    ])
    
    df_single = normalizer.spark.createDataFrame(single_data, single_schema)
    
    print("\nData with Constant Column:")
    df_single.show()
    
    df_single_norm = normalizer.z_score_normalization(
        df_single, 
        ["constant", "variable"]
    )
    
    print("\nNormalized (constant column becomes 0):")
    df_single_norm.select("id", "constant_zscore", "variable_zscore").show()
    
    # Edge Case 6: Negative Values
    print("\n--- Edge Case 6: Negative Values ---")
    
    negative_data = [
        (1, -100, 50),
        (2, -50, 100),
        (3, 0, 150),
        (4, 50, 200),
        (5, 100, 250)
    ]
    
    negative_schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("negative_vals", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("positive_vals", IntegerType(), False)
    ])
    
    df_negative = normalizer.spark.createDataFrame(negative_data, negative_schema)
    
    print("\nData with Negative Values:")
    df_negative.show()
    
    # Min-Max handles negative values correctly
    df_neg_minmax = normalizer.min_max_normalization(
        df_negative, 
        ["negative_vals", "positive_vals"],
        feature_range=(0, 1)
    )
    
    print("\nMin-Max Normalized (0 to 1):")
    df_neg_minmax.select(
        "id", "negative_vals", "negative_vals_normalized"
    ).show()
    
    # Can also normalize to [-1, 1]
    df_neg_custom = normalizer.min_max_normalization(
        df_negative, 
        ["negative_vals"],
        feature_range=(-1, 1),
        output_col_suffix="_custom"
    )
    
    print("\nMin-Max Normalized (-1 to 1):")
    df_neg_custom.select(
        "id", "negative_vals", "negative_vals_custom"
    ).show()
    
    normalizer.cleanup()

def interactive_mode():
    """
    Interactive mode for testing normalization patterns
    """
    normalizer = DataNormalizationPatterns("InteractiveMode")
    
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("INTERACTIVE NORMALIZATION MODE")
    print("="*80)
    print("""
    Available commands:
    1. demo_db       - Database normalization demo
    2. demo_stats    - Statistical normalization demo
    3. demo_ml       - ML pipeline demo
    4. demo_fraud    - Fraud detection demo
    5. demo_segment  - Customer segmentation demo
    6. demo_ts       - Time series demo
    7. test          - Run unit tests
    8. benchmark     - Performance benchmarks
    9. help          - Show this help
    10. exit         - Exit interactive mode
    """)
    
    while True:
        try:
            command = input("\nEnter command: ").strip().lower()
            
            if command == 'demo_db':
                demonstrate_database_normalization()
            elif command == 'demo_stats':
                demonstrate_statistical_normalization()
            elif command == 'demo_ml':
                complete_ml_pipeline_example()
            elif command == 'demo_fraud':
                real_world_example_fraud_detection()
            elif command == 'demo_segment':
                real_world_example_customer_segmentation()
            elif command == 'demo_ts':
                real_world_example_time_series_forecasting()
            elif command == 'test':
                loader = unittest.TestLoader()
                suite = loader.loadTestsFromTestCase(TestDataNormalizationPatterns)
                runner = unittest.TextTestRunner(verbosity=2)
                runner.run(suite)
            elif command == 'benchmark':
                benchmark_normalization_methods()
            elif command == 'help':
                print("""
                Available commands:
                1. demo_db       - Database normalization demo
                2. demo_stats    - Statistical normalization demo
                3. demo_ml       - ML pipeline demo
                4. demo_fraud    - Fraud detection demo
                5. demo_segment  - Customer segmentation demo
                6. demo_ts       - Time series demo
                7. test          - Run unit tests
                8. benchmark     - Performance benchmarks
                9. help          - Show this help
                10. exit         - Exit interactive mode
                """)
            elif command == 'exit':
                print("\nExiting interactive mode...")
                break
            else:
                print(f"Unknown command: {command}")
                print("Type 'help' for available commands")
                
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            print("\n\nExiting interactive mode...")
            break
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error: {str(e)}")
            import traceback
            traceback.print_exc()
    
    normalizer.cleanup()

# PATTERN 1: Event Time Extraction Pattern
# =============================================================================
# Purpose: Extract event time from various data formats and sources
# Use Case: Parsing timestamps from JSON, CSV, or custom formats

class EventTimeExtractionPattern:
    """
    Extracts event time from different data formats and normalizes them
    to a standard timestamp format for processing.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    def extract_from_json_field(self, df, json_column, timestamp_field):
        """
        Extract event time from a JSON string field.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            json_column: Column containing JSON data
            timestamp_field: Field name in JSON containing timestamp
        
        Returns:
            DataFrame with extracted event_time column
        """
        # Define schema for JSON parsing
        json_schema = StructType([
            StructField("event_id", StringType(), True),
            StructField("timestamp", StringType(), True),
            StructField("user_id", StringType(), True),
            StructField("value", DoubleType(), True)
        ])
        
        # Parse JSON and extract timestamp
        result_df = df \
            .withColumn("parsed_data", from_json(col(json_column), json_schema)) \
            .withColumn("event_time", 
                       to_timestamp(col(f"parsed_data.{timestamp_field}"))) \
            .withColumn("event_id", col("parsed_data.event_id")) \
            .withColumn("user_id", col("parsed_data.user_id")) \
            .withColumn("value", col("parsed_data.value"))
        
        return result_df
    
    def extract_from_epoch_milliseconds(self, df, epoch_column):
        """
        Convert epoch milliseconds to timestamp.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            epoch_column: Column containing epoch time in milliseconds
        
        Returns:
            DataFrame with converted event_time
        """
        result_df = df \
            .withColumn("event_time", 
                       (col(epoch_column) / 1000).cast(TimestampType()))
        
        return result_df
    
    def extract_from_multiple_formats(self, df, timestamp_column):
        """
        Handle multiple timestamp formats in the same column.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            timestamp_column: Column containing timestamps in various formats
        
        Returns:
            DataFrame with normalized event_time
        """
        result_df = df \
            .withColumn("event_time",
                coalesce(
                    # Try ISO 8601 format
                    to_timestamp(col(timestamp_column), "yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'Z'"),
                    # Try standard format
                    to_timestamp(col(timestamp_column), "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss"),
                    # Try Unix timestamp
                    to_timestamp(col(timestamp_column).cast("long")),
                    # Default to current timestamp if all fail
                    current_timestamp()
                )
            ) \
            .withColumn("extraction_method",
                when(to_timestamp(col(timestamp_column), 
                                 "yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'Z'").isNotNull(), 
                     "ISO8601")
                .when(to_timestamp(col(timestamp_column), 
                                  "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss").isNotNull(), 
                      "STANDARD")
                .when(to_timestamp(col(timestamp_column).cast("long")).isNotNull(), 
                      "UNIX")
                .otherwise("DEFAULT")
            )
        
        return result_df
