# =============================================================================
# 1. FIXED-SIZE CHUNKING PATTERN
# =============================================================================
# Splits data into chunks of fixed number of records
# Use Case: Batch processing, parallel processing with equal workloads

def fixed_size_chunking(df, chunk_size=1000):
    """
    Divides DataFrame into fixed-size chunks
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame
        chunk_size: Number of records per chunk
    
    Returns:
        DataFrame with chunk_id column
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print("PATTERN 1: FIXED-SIZE CHUNKING")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    # Add monotonically increasing ID
    df_with_id = df.withColumn("row_id", monotonically_increasing_id())
    
    # Calculate chunk_id based on row position
    df_chunked = df_with_id.withColumn(
        "chunk_id",
        (col("row_id") / chunk_size).cast("long")
    )
    
    # Get chunk statistics
    chunk_stats = df_chunked.groupBy("chunk_id").count().orderBy("chunk_id")
    
    print(f"\nChunk Size: {chunk_size}")
    print(f"Total Records: {df.count()}")
    print(f"Number of Chunks: {chunk_stats.count()}")
    print("\nChunk Distribution:")
    chunk_stats.show(10)
    
    return df_chunked

# =============================================================================
# 2. VARIABLE-SIZE CHUNKING PATTERN
# =============================================================================
# Creates chunks based on cumulative size/weight with variable boundaries
# Use Case: Memory-efficient processing, load balancing

def variable_size_chunking(df, target_chunk_weight=10000, weight_column="amount"):
    """
    Creates variable-size chunks based on cumulative weight
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame
        target_chunk_weight: Target cumulative weight per chunk
        weight_column: Column to use for weight calculation
    
    Returns:
        DataFrame with chunk_id column
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print("PATTERN 2: VARIABLE-SIZE CHUNKING")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    # Sort data for consistent chunking
    df_sorted = df.withColumn("row_id", monotonically_increasing_id()) \
                  .orderBy("row_id")
    
    # Calculate cumulative sum of weights
    window_spec = Window.orderBy("row_id").rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)
    
    df_with_cumsum = df_sorted.withColumn(
        "cumulative_weight",
        _sum(col(weight_column)).over(window_spec)
    )
    
    # Assign chunk based on cumulative weight
    df_chunked = df_with_cumsum.withColumn(
        "chunk_id",
        (col("cumulative_weight") / target_chunk_weight).cast("long")
    )
    
    # Get chunk statistics
    chunk_stats = df_chunked.groupBy("chunk_id").agg(
        _sum(weight_column).alias("total_weight"),
        _sum(lit(1)).alias("record_count")
    ).orderBy("chunk_id")
    
    print(f"\nTarget Chunk Weight: {target_chunk_weight}")
    print(f"Weight Column: {weight_column}")
    print(f"Number of Chunks: {chunk_stats.count()}")
    print("\nChunk Distribution:")
    chunk_stats.show(10)
    
    return df_chunked

# =============================================================================
# 3. TIME-BASED CHUNKING PATTERN
# =============================================================================
# Splits data into chunks based on time intervals
# Use Case: Time-series analysis, temporal data processing

def time_based_chunking(df, timestamp_column="timestamp", interval_seconds=3600):
    """
    Creates chunks based on time intervals
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame
        timestamp_column: Column containing timestamp
        interval_seconds: Time interval in seconds (default: 1 hour)
    
    Returns:
        DataFrame with chunk_id and chunk_timestamp columns
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print("PATTERN 3: TIME-BASED CHUNKING")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    # Convert timestamp to unix timestamp if needed
    df_with_unix = df.withColumn(
        "unix_time",
        unix_timestamp(col(timestamp_column))
    )
    
    # Calculate chunk based on time interval
    df_chunked = df_with_unix.withColumn(
        "chunk_id",
        floor(col("unix_time") / interval_seconds)
    ).withColumn(
        "chunk_timestamp",
        (col("chunk_id") * interval_seconds).cast("timestamp")
    )
    
    # Get chunk statistics
    chunk_stats = df_chunked.groupBy("chunk_id", "chunk_timestamp").count() \
                            .orderBy("chunk_id")
    
    interval_minutes = interval_seconds / 60
    print(f"\nTime Interval: {interval_minutes} minutes")
    print(f"Timestamp Column: {timestamp_column}")
    print(f"Number of Time Chunks: {chunk_stats.count()}")
    print("\nTime-Based Chunk Distribution:")
    chunk_stats.show(10)
    
    return df_chunked

# =============================================================================
# 4. MEMORY-BASED CHUNKING PATTERN
# =============================================================================
# Creates chunks based on estimated memory footprint
# Use Case: Memory-constrained processing, avoiding OOM errors

def memory_based_chunking(df, max_chunk_memory_mb=100, avg_row_size_bytes=1024):
    """
    Creates chunks based on estimated memory consumption
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame
        max_chunk_memory_mb: Maximum memory per chunk in MB
        avg_row_size_bytes: Estimated average row size in bytes
    
    Returns:
        DataFrame with chunk_id column
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print("PATTERN 4: MEMORY-BASED CHUNKING")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    # Calculate estimated row size if complex columns exist
    # For demonstration, using a simple approach
    df_with_size = df.withColumn("row_id", monotonically_increasing_id())
    
    # If DataFrame has string columns, calculate actual size
    string_cols = [f.name for f in df.schema.fields if isinstance(f.dataType, StringType)]
    
    if string_cols:
        # Estimate size based on string lengths
        size_expr = sum([length(col(c)) for c in string_cols])
        df_with_size = df_with_size.withColumn("estimated_row_size", size_expr + lit(avg_row_size_bytes))
    else:
        df_with_size = df_with_size.withColumn("estimated_row_size", lit(avg_row_size_bytes))
    
    # Calculate cumulative memory
    window_spec = Window.orderBy("row_id").rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)
    
    df_with_cumsum = df_with_size.withColumn(
        "cumulative_bytes",
        _sum(col("estimated_row_size")).over(window_spec)
    )
    
    # Convert max memory to bytes
    max_chunk_bytes = max_chunk_memory_mb * 1024 * 1024
    
    # Assign chunk based on memory threshold
    df_chunked = df_with_cumsum.withColumn(
        "chunk_id",
        (col("cumulative_bytes") / max_chunk_bytes).cast("long")
    )
    
    # Get chunk statistics
    chunk_stats = df_chunked.groupBy("chunk_id").agg(
        (_sum("estimated_row_size") / 1024 / 1024).alias("chunk_size_mb"),
        _sum(lit(1)).alias("record_count")
    ).orderBy("chunk_id")
    
    print(f"\nMax Chunk Memory: {max_chunk_memory_mb} MB")
    print(f"Estimated Avg Row Size: {avg_row_size_bytes} bytes")
    print(f"Number of Memory Chunks: {chunk_stats.count()}")
    print("\nMemory-Based Chunk Distribution:")
    chunk_stats.show(10)
    
    return df_chunked

# =============================================================================
# 5. CONTENT-BASED CHUNKING PATTERN
# =============================================================================
# Creates chunks based on content characteristics (rolling hash)
# Use Case: Deduplication, change detection, distributed caching

def content_based_chunking(df, content_columns, min_chunk_size=500, max_chunk_size=2000):
    """
    Creates chunks based on content using rolling hash technique
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame
        content_columns: List of columns to use for content hashing
        min_chunk_size: Minimum records per chunk
        max_chunk_size: Maximum records per chunk
    
    Returns:
        DataFrame with chunk_id column
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print("PATTERN 5: CONTENT-BASED CHUNKING")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    # Create content hash from specified columns
    df_with_hash = df.withColumn("row_id", monotonically_increasing_id())
    
    # Concatenate content columns and create hash
    content_expr = concat_ws("|", *[col(c).cast("string") for c in content_columns])
    df_with_hash = df_with_hash.withColumn("content_hash", hash(content_expr))
    
    # Use modulo operation to create chunk boundaries
    # This simulates rolling hash chunking
    df_with_hash = df_with_hash.withColumn(
        "is_boundary",
        (_abs(col("content_hash")) % 100 < 5)  # ~5% of records are boundaries
    )
    
    # Create cumulative sum of boundaries to get chunk IDs
    window_spec = Window.orderBy("row_id").rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)
    
    df_chunked = df_with_hash.withColumn(
        "chunk_id",
        _sum(col("is_boundary").cast("long")).over(window_spec)
    )
    
    # Enforce min/max chunk sizes by merging small chunks
    chunk_sizes = df_chunked.groupBy("chunk_id").count().orderBy("chunk_id")
    
    # For simplicity, we'll use the basic chunk_id
    # In production, you'd implement logic to merge/split chunks
    
    # Get chunk statistics
    chunk_stats = df_chunked.groupBy("chunk_id").agg(
        _sum(lit(1)).alias("record_count")
    ).orderBy("chunk_id")
    
    print(f"\nContent Columns: {', '.join(content_columns)}")
    print(f"Min Chunk Size: {min_chunk_size}")
    print(f"Max Chunk Size: {max_chunk_size}")
    print(f"Number of Content Chunks: {chunk_stats.count()}")
    print("\nContent-Based Chunk Distribution:")
    chunk_stats.show(10)
    
    return df_chunked

    def process_chunks_sequentially(df_chunked, process_func, chunk_id_col="chunk_id"):
        """
        Process each chunk sequentially with a custom function
        
        Args:
            df_chunked: DataFrame with chunk_id column
            process_func: Function that takes a DataFrame and returns processed DataFrame
            chunk_id_col: Name of the chunk ID column
        """
        chunk_ids = df_chunked.select(chunk_id_col).distinct().collect()
        results = []
        
        for row in chunk_ids:
            chunk_id = row[chunk_id_col]
            chunk_data = df_chunked.filter(col(chunk_id_col) == chunk_id)
            processed = process_func(chunk_data)
            results.append(processed)
        
        # Union all results
        from functools import reduce
        final_result = reduce(lambda df1, df2: df1.union(df2), results)
        return final_result

def hash_based_chunking(df, num_chunks=10, hash_columns=None):
    """
    Hash-based chunking for consistent distribution
    Use Case: Distributed processing with consistent routing
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame
        num_chunks: Number of chunks to create
        hash_columns: Columns to use for hashing (default: all columns)
    
    Returns:
        DataFrame with chunk_id column
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print("BONUS PATTERN: HASH-BASED CHUNKING")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    if hash_columns is None:
        hash_columns = df.columns
    
    # Create hash from specified columns
    hash_expr = hash(*[col(c) for c in hash_columns])
    
    df_chunked = df.withColumn(
        "chunk_id",
        (_abs(hash_expr) % num_chunks)
    )
    
    # Get chunk statistics
    chunk_stats = df_chunked.groupBy("chunk_id").count().orderBy("chunk_id")
    
    print(f"\nNumber of Chunks: {num_chunks}")
    print(f"Hash Columns: {', '.join(hash_columns)}")
    print(f"Actual Chunks Created: {chunk_stats.count()}")
    print("\nHash-Based Chunk Distribution:")
    chunk_stats.show()
    
    return df_chunked

def percentile_based_chunking(df, num_chunks=10, sort_column="amount"):
    """
    Percentile-based chunking for even distribution by value
    Use Case: Creating balanced chunks based on sorted values
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame
        num_chunks: Number of chunks to create
        sort_column: Column to use for percentile calculation
    
    Returns:
        DataFrame with chunk_id column
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print("BONUS PATTERN: PERCENTILE-BASED CHUNKING")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    # Calculate percentiles
    percentiles = [i / num_chunks for i in range(num_chunks + 1)]
    
    # Get percentile values
    approx_percentiles = df.approxQuantile(sort_column, percentiles, 0.01)
    
    # Create chunk boundaries
    df_chunked = df.withColumn("chunk_id", lit(0))
    
    for i in range(len(approx_percentiles) - 1):
        lower_bound = approx_percentiles[i]
        upper_bound = approx_percentiles[i + 1]
        
        df_chunked = df_chunked.withColumn(
            "chunk_id",
            when(
                (col(sort_column) >= lower_bound) & 
                (col(sort_column) < upper_bound if i < len(approx_percentiles) - 2 
                 else col(sort_column) <= upper_bound),
                lit(i)
            ).otherwise(col("chunk_id"))
        )
    
    # Get chunk statistics
    chunk_stats = df_chunked.groupBy("chunk_id").agg(
        _sum(lit(1)).alias("count"),
        _sum(sort_column).alias(f"total_{sort_column}"),
        min(sort_column).alias(f"min_{sort_column}"),
        max(sort_column).alias(f"max_{sort_column}")
    ).orderBy("chunk_id")
    
    print(f"\nNumber of Chunks: {num_chunks}")
    print(f"Sort Column: {sort_column}")
    print("\nPercentile-Based Chunk Distribution:")
    chunk_stats.show()
    
    return df_chunked

def sliding_window_chunking(df, window_size=1000, slide_size=500, 
                           order_column="id"):
    """
    Sliding window chunking with overlapping chunks
    Use Case: Time-series analysis with overlapping windows
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame
        window_size: Size of each window
        slide_size: How much to slide for next window
        order_column: Column to use for ordering
    
    Returns:
        DataFrame with multiple chunk_id values per record
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print("BONUS PATTERN: SLIDING WINDOW CHUNKING")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    # Add row number
    window_spec = Window.orderBy(order_column)
    df_with_row = df.withColumn("row_num", row_number().over(window_spec))
    
    # Calculate which windows each record belongs to
    # A record can belong to multiple windows
    max_row = df_with_row.agg({"row_num": "max"}).collect()[0][0]
    num_windows = ((max_row - window_size) // slide_size) + 1
    
    print(f"\nWindow Size: {window_size}")
    print(f"Slide Size: {slide_size}")
    print(f"Number of Windows: {num_windows}")
    print(f"Overlap: {window_size - slide_size} records")
    
    # Create array of window IDs for each record
    from pyspark.sql.functions import array, explode
    
    # For each record, calculate which windows it belongs to
    window_ids_expr = array(*[
        lit(i) for i in range(num_windows)
    ])
    
    # Filter to only include windows where record falls within range
    df_windowed = df_with_row.withColumn(
        "window_id",
        explode(
            array(*[
                when(
                    (col("row_num") >= i * slide_size) & 
                    (col("row_num") < i * slide_size + window_size),
                    lit(i)
                )
                for i in range(num_windows)
            ])
        )
    ).filter(col("window_id").isNotNull())
    
    # Get window statistics
    window_stats = df_windowed.groupBy("window_id").count().orderBy("window_id")
    
    print("\nSliding Window Distribution:")
    window_stats.show(10)
    
    return df_windowed

def stratified_chunking(df, stratify_column="category", chunks_per_stratum=5):
    """
    Stratified chunking to maintain category distribution
    Use Case: ML training data splitting, balanced sampling
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame
        stratify_column: Column to stratify by
        chunks_per_stratum: Number of chunks per category
    
    Returns:
        DataFrame with chunk_id column
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print("BONUS PATTERN: STRATIFIED CHUNKING")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    # Add row number within each stratum
    window_spec = Window.partitionBy(stratify_column).orderBy(monotonically_increasing_id())
    
    df_with_row = df.withColumn(
        "row_num_in_stratum",
        row_number().over(window_spec)
    )
    
    # Get count per stratum
    stratum_counts = df.groupBy(stratify_column).count() \
                       .withColumnRenamed("count", "stratum_size")
    
    # Join back to get stratum size
    df_with_size = df_with_row.join(stratum_counts, on=stratify_column)
    
    # Calculate chunk within stratum
    df_chunked = df_with_size.withColumn(
        "chunk_in_stratum",
        ((col("row_num_in_stratum") - 1) / (col("stratum_size") / chunks_per_stratum)).cast("long")
    ).withColumn(
        "chunk_id",
        concat_ws("_", col(stratify_column), col("chunk_in_stratum").cast("string"))
    )
    
    # Get chunk statistics
    chunk_stats = df_chunked.groupBy("chunk_id", stratify_column).count() \
                            .orderBy(stratify_column, "chunk_id")
    
    print(f"\nStratify Column: {stratify_column}")
    print(f"Chunks per Stratum: {chunks_per_stratum}")
    print(f"Total Chunks: {chunk_stats.count()}")
    print("\nStratified Chunk Distribution:")
    chunk_stats.show(20)
    
    return df_chunked

def adaptive_size_chunking(df, target_processing_time_sec=60, 
                          sample_fraction=0.01, processing_rate_col="complexity"):
    """
    Adaptive chunking based on estimated processing time
    Use Case: Load balancing for variable-complexity tasks
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame
        target_processing_time_sec: Target processing time per chunk
        sample_fraction: Fraction of data to sample for estimation
        processing_rate_col: Column indicating processing complexity
    
    Returns:
        DataFrame with chunk_id column
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print("BONUS PATTERN: ADAPTIVE SIZE CHUNKING")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    # If complexity column doesn't exist, create one
    if processing_rate_col not in df.columns:
        df = df.withColumn(processing_rate_col, lit(1))
    
    # Sample data to estimate processing rate
    sample_df = df.sample(False, sample_fraction, seed=42)
    avg_complexity = sample_df.agg({processing_rate_col: "avg"}).collect()[0][0]
    
    # Calculate optimal chunk size
    # Assuming linear relationship between complexity and processing time
    estimated_records_per_sec = 1000  # Baseline estimate
    records_per_chunk = int(target_processing_time_sec * estimated_records_per_sec / avg_complexity)
    
    print(f"\nTarget Processing Time: {target_processing_time_sec} seconds")
    print(f"Average Complexity: {avg_complexity:.2f}")
    print(f"Calculated Records per Chunk: {records_per_chunk}")
    
    # Add cumulative complexity
    window_spec = Window.orderBy(monotonically_increasing_id()) \
                        .rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)
    
    df_with_cumsum = df.withColumn(
        "cumulative_complexity",
        _sum(col(processing_rate_col)).over(window_spec)
    )
    
    # Create chunks based on cumulative complexity
    target_complexity_per_chunk = records_per_chunk * avg_complexity
    
    df_chunked = df_with_cumsum.withColumn(
        "chunk_id",
        (col("cumulative_complexity") / target_complexity_per_chunk).cast("long")
    )
    
    # Get chunk statistics
    chunk_stats = df_chunked.groupBy("chunk_id").agg(
        _sum(lit(1)).alias("record_count"),
        _sum(processing_rate_col).alias("total_complexity"),
        (sum(processing_rate_col) / avg_complexity).alias("estimated_processing_time")
    ).orderBy("chunk_id")
    
    print("\nAdaptive Chunk Distribution:")
    chunk_stats.show(10)
    
    return df_chunked

class ChunkProcessor:
    """
    Framework for processing chunks with error handling and monitoring
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
        self.processing_stats = []
    
    def process_chunk_with_retry(self, chunk_df, process_func, 
                                 max_retries=3, chunk_id=None):
        """
        Process a chunk with retry logic
        
        Args:
            chunk_df: DataFrame chunk to process
            process_func: Function to apply to chunk
            max_retries: Maximum number of retry attempts
            chunk_id: Identifier for the chunk (for logging)
        
        Returns:
            Processed DataFrame or None if all retries failed
        """
        import time
        
        for attempt in range(max_retries):
            try:
                start_time = time.time()
                result = process_func(chunk_df)
                end_time = time.time()
                
                # Record stats
                stats = {
                    "chunk_id": chunk_id,
                    "attempt": attempt + 1,
                    "success": True,
                    "processing_time": end_time - start_time,
                    "record_count": chunk_df.count()
                }
                self.processing_stats.append(stats)
                
                print(f"✓ Chunk {chunk_id} processed successfully in {stats['processing_time']:.2f}s")
                return result
                
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"✗ Chunk {chunk_id} failed on attempt {attempt + 1}: {str(e)}")
                
                if attempt == max_retries - 1:
                    stats = {
                        "chunk_id": chunk_id,
                        "attempt": attempt + 1,
                        "success": False,
                        "error": str(e),
                        "record_count": chunk_df.count()
                    }
                    self.processing_stats.append(stats)
                    return None
                
                # Exponential backoff
                time.sleep(2 ** attempt)
        
        return None
    
    def process_all_chunks(self, df_chunked, process_func, 
                          chunk_id_col="chunk_id", parallel=True):
        """
        Process all chunks with monitoring
        
        Args:
            df_chunked: DataFrame with chunk_id column
            process_func: Function to apply to each chunk
            chunk_id_col: Name of chunk ID column
            parallel: Whether to process in parallel
        
        Returns:
            Combined result DataFrame
        """
        chunk_ids = df_chunked.select(chunk_id_col).distinct() \
                             .rdd.map(lambda
```python
                             .rdd.map(lambda row: row[0]).collect()
        
        print(f"\nProcessing {len(chunk_ids)} chunks...")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        results = []
        successful = 0
        failed = 0
        
        for chunk_id in chunk_ids:
            chunk_data = df_chunked.filter(col(chunk_id_col) == chunk_id)
            result = self.process_chunk_with_retry(chunk_data, process_func, chunk_id=chunk_id)
            
            if result is not None:
                results.append(result)
                successful += 1
            else:
                failed += 1
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print(f"Processing Complete: {successful} successful, {failed} failed")
        
        # Combine results
        if results:
            from functools import reduce
            final_result = reduce(lambda df1, df2: df1.union(df2), results)
            return final_result
        else:
            return None
    
    def get_processing_report(self):
        """
        Generate processing statistics report
        
        Returns:
            DataFrame with processing statistics
        """
        if not self.processing_stats:
            print("No processing statistics available")
            return None
        
        stats_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(self.processing_stats)
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("PROCESSING STATISTICS REPORT")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        stats_df.show()
        
        # Summary statistics
        summary = stats_df.filter(col("success") == True).agg(
            _sum("record_count").alias("total_records"),
            _sum("processing_time").alias("total_time"),
            (sum("processing_time") / sum("record_count")).alias("avg_time_per_record")
        ).first()
        
        if summary:
            print(f"\nTotal Records Processed: {summary['total_records']}")
            print(f"Total Processing Time: {summary['total_time']:.2f} seconds")
            print(f"Avg Time per Record: {summary['avg_time_per_record']:.6f} seconds")
        
        return stats_df

def optimize_chunk_size(df, process_func, min_size=100, max_size=10000, 
                       step=500, sample_fraction=0.1):
    """
    Find optimal chunk size through benchmarking
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame
        process_func: Processing function to benchmark
        min_size: Minimum chunk size to test
        max_size: Maximum chunk size to test
        step: Step size for testing
        sample_fraction: Fraction of data to use for testing
    
    Returns:
        Optimal chunk size
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print("CHUNK SIZE OPTIMIZATION")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    import time
    
    sample_df = df.sample(False, sample_fraction, seed=42)
    sample_count = sample_df.count()
    
    print(f"\nTesting chunk sizes from {min_size} to {max_size}")
    print(f"Using sample of {sample_count} records ({sample_fraction*100}% of data)")
    
    results = []
    
    for chunk_size in range(min_size, max_size + 1, step):
        # Create chunks
        df_chunked = fixed_size_chunking(sample_df, chunk_size)
        num_chunks = df_chunked.select("chunk_id").distinct().count()
        
        # Time the processing
        start_time = time.time()
        
        # Process first few chunks as sample
        sample_chunks = min(5, num_chunks)
        for i in range(sample_chunks):
            chunk = df_chunked.filter(col("chunk_id") == i)
            _ = process_func(chunk).count()  # Force execution
        
        end_time = time.time()
        avg_time = (end_time - start_time) / sample_chunks
        
        results.append({
            "chunk_size": chunk_size,
            "num_chunks": num_chunks,
            "avg_time_per_chunk": avg_time,
            "throughput": chunk_size / avg_time if avg_time > 0 else 0
        })
        
        print(f"Chunk size {chunk_size}: {avg_time:.4f}s per chunk, "
              f"{chunk_size / avg_time:.2f} records/sec")
    
    # Find optimal size (maximum throughput)
    optimal = max(results, key=lambda x: x['throughput'])
    
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print(f"OPTIMAL CHUNK SIZE: {optimal['chunk_size']}")
    print(f"Expected throughput: {optimal['throughput']:.2f} records/second")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    return optimal['chunk_size']

def merge_small_chunks(df_chunked, min_chunk_size=500, chunk_id_col="chunk_id"):
    """
    Merge chunks that are smaller than minimum size
    
    Args:
        df_chunked: DataFrame with chunk_id column
        min_chunk_size: Minimum acceptable chunk size
        chunk_id_col: Name of chunk ID column
    
    Returns:
        DataFrame with rebalanced chunks
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print("MERGING SMALL CHUNKS")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    # Get chunk sizes
    chunk_sizes = df_chunked.groupBy(chunk_id_col).count() \
                           .withColumnRenamed("count", "chunk_size") \
                           .orderBy(chunk_id_col)
    
    # Identify small chunks
    small_chunks = chunk_sizes.filter(col("chunk_size") < min_chunk_size)
    small_count = small_chunks.count()
    
    print(f"\nMinimum chunk size: {min_chunk_size}")
    print(f"Chunks below minimum: {small_count}")
    
    if small_count == 0:
        print("No chunks need merging")
        return df_chunked
    
    # Create mapping for merging small chunks
    # Simple strategy: merge consecutive small chunks
    window_spec = Window.orderBy(chunk_id_col)
    
    chunk_mapping = chunk_sizes.withColumn(
        "is_small",
        (col("chunk_size") < min_chunk_size).cast("int")
    ).withColumn(
        "merge_group",
        _sum("is_small").over(window_spec)
    ).withColumn(
        "new_chunk_id",
        when(col("is_small") == 1, col("merge_group"))
        .otherwise(col(chunk_id_col))
    )
    
    # Apply mapping
    df_rebalanced = df_chunked.join(
        chunk_mapping.select(chunk_id_col, "new_chunk_id"),
        on=chunk_id_col
    ).drop(chunk_id_col).withColumnRenamed("new_chunk_id", chunk_id_col)
    
    # Show new distribution
    new_sizes = df_rebalanced.groupBy(chunk_id_col).count().orderBy(chunk_id_col)
    
    print("\nNew chunk distribution after merging:")
    new_sizes.show(10)
    
    return df_rebalanced

def split_large_chunks(df_chunked, max_chunk_size=5000, chunk_id_col="chunk_id"):
    """
    Split chunks that are larger than maximum size
    
    Args:
        df_chunked: DataFrame with chunk_id column
        max_chunk_size: Maximum acceptable chunk size
        chunk_id_col: Name of chunk ID column
    
    Returns:
        DataFrame with rebalanced chunks
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print("SPLITTING LARGE CHUNKS")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    # Get chunk sizes
    chunk_sizes = df_chunked.groupBy(chunk_id_col).count() \
                           .withColumnRenamed("count", "chunk_size")
    
    # Identify large chunks
    large_chunks = chunk_sizes.filter(col("chunk_size") > max_chunk_size)
    large_count = large_chunks.count()
    
    print(f"\nMaximum chunk size: {max_chunk_size}")
    print(f"Chunks above maximum: {large_count}")
    
    if large_count == 0:
        print("No chunks need splitting")
        return df_chunked
    
    # Add row number within each chunk
    window_spec = Window.partitionBy(chunk_id_col).orderBy(monotonically_increasing_id())
    
    df_with_row = df_chunked.withColumn(
        "row_in_chunk",
        row_number().over(window_spec)
    )
    
    # Split large chunks into sub-chunks
    df_split = df_with_row.withColumn(
        "sub_chunk",
        (col("row_in_chunk") / max_chunk_size).cast("long")
    ).withColumn(
        "new_chunk_id",
        concat_ws("_", col(chunk_id_col).cast("string"), col("sub_chunk").cast("string"))
    ).drop(chunk_id_col, "row_in_chunk", "sub_chunk") \
     .withColumnRenamed("new_chunk_id", chunk_id_col)
    
    # Show new distribution
    new_sizes = df_split.groupBy(chunk_id_col).count().orderBy(chunk_id_col)
    
    print("\nNew chunk distribution after splitting:")
    new_sizes.show(10)
    
    return df_split

# =============================================================================
# CHECKPOINT AND RECOVERY UTILITIES
# =============================================================================

def checkpoint_chunks(df_chunked, checkpoint_path, chunk_id_col="chunk_id"):
    """
    Checkpoint chunks to disk for fault tolerance
    
    Args:
        df_chunked: DataFrame with chunk_id column
        checkpoint_path: Path to save checkpoints
        chunk_id_col: Name of chunk ID column
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print("CHECKPOINTING CHUNKS")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    chunk_ids = df_chunked.select(chunk_id_col).distinct().collect()
    
    print(f"\nCheckpointing {len(chunk_ids)} chunks to {checkpoint_path}")
    
    for row in chunk_ids:
        chunk_id = row[chunk_id_col]
        chunk_data = df_chunked.filter(col(chunk_id_col) == chunk_id)
        
        output_path = f"{checkpoint_path}/chunk_{chunk_id}"
        chunk_data.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(output_path)
        print(f"✓ Chunk {chunk_id} checkpointed")
    
    print(f"\nAll chunks checkpointed successfully")

def recover_from_checkpoint(spark, checkpoint_path, failed_chunks=None):
    """
    Recover chunks from checkpoint
    
    Args:
        spark: SparkSession
        checkpoint_path: Path where checkpoints are saved
        failed_chunks: List of chunk IDs to recover (None = recover all)
    
    Returns:
        Combined DataFrame from checkpoints
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print("RECOVERING FROM CHECKPOINT")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    import os
    
    # In production, use proper file system operations
    # This is a simplified example
    
    if failed_chunks is None:
        print("Recovering all chunks from checkpoint")
        # Read all checkpoints
        df_recovered = spark.read.parquet(f"{checkpoint_path}/chunk_*")
    else:
        print(f"Recovering {len(failed_chunks)} failed chunks")
        dfs = []
        for chunk_id in failed_chunks:
            chunk_path = f"{checkpoint_path}/chunk_{chunk_id}"
            df_chunk = spark.read.parquet(chunk_path)
            dfs.append(df_chunk)
            print(f"✓ Chunk {chunk_id} recovered")
        
        from functools import reduce
        df_recovered = reduce(lambda df1, df2: df1.union(df2), dfs)
    
    print(f"\nRecovered {df_recovered.count()} records")
    return df_recovered

def print_performance_tuning_guide():
    """Print comprehensive performance tuning guide"""
    
    guide = """
    
    ╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
    ║                    CHUNKING PERFORMANCE TUNING GUIDE                       ║
    ╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
    
    1. CHOOSING THE RIGHT CHUNK SIZE
    ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
    
    Too Small:
    • High overhead from task scheduling
    • Inefficient resource utilization
    • More network shuffles
    
    Too Large:
    • Memory pressure and OOM errors
    • Stragglers and uneven load distribution
    • Longer recovery time on failures
    
    Optimal Range:
    • 10MB - 128MB per chunk (for file-based processing)
    • 1,000 - 100,000 records (for record-based processing)
    • Aim for 2-4x more chunks than available cores
    
    2. SPARK CONFIGURATION FOR CHUNKING
    ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
    
    spark.sql.shuffle.partitions = <num_chunks>
        Set to match your chunk count for optimal shuffling
    
    spark.default.parallelism = <2-3x cores>
        Controls default partition count
    
    spark.executor.memory = <appropriate size>
        Ensure enough memory per executor for chunk processing
    
    spark.executor.cores = <2-5>
        Balance between parallelism and resource per task
    
    spark.memory.fraction = 0.6
        Adjust if experiencing memory pressure
    
    spark.memory.storageFraction = 0.5
        Balance between execution and storage memory
    
    3. OPTIMIZATION STRATEGIES BY PATTERN
    ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
    
    FIXED-SIZE CHUNKING:
    ✓ Use monotonically_increasing_id() sparingly (causes shuffle)
    ✓ Consider zipWithIndex() for RDDs
    ✓ Cache if reusing chunked DataFrame
    ✓ Coalesce/repartition to match chunk count
    
    VARIABLE-SIZE CHUNKING:
    ✓ Pre-calculate weights if possible
    ✓ Use approximate algorithms for large datasets
    ✓ Consider sampling for weight estimation
    ✓ Broadcast small lookup tables
    
    TIME-BASED CHUNKING:
    ✓ Ensure timestamp column is indexed
    ✓ Use partition pruning when possible
    ✓ Pre-sort data by timestamp if feasible
    ✓ Consider window functions for rolling aggregations
    
    MEMORY-BASED CHUNKING:
    ✓ Use schema inference carefully
    ✓ Compress intermediate results
    ✓ Spill to disk for large chunks
    ✓ Monitor executor memory usage
    
    CONTENT-BASED CHUNKING:
    ✓ Use efficient hash functions
    ✓ Cache hash values if reused
    ✓ Consider salting for skewed data
    ✓ Use approximate algorithms for large-scale deduplication
    
    4. COMMON PITFALLS AND SOLUTIONS
    ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
    
    PITFALL: Data Skew
    SOLUTION: Use salting, stratified sampling, or adaptive chunking
    
    PITFALL: Memory Leaks
    SOLUTION: Unpersist DataFrames, use checkpointing, limit window sizes
    
    PITFALL: Excessive Shuffling
    SOLUTION: Minimize wide transformations, use broadcast joins
    
    PITFALL: Small Files Problem
    SOLUTION: Coalesce before writing, use appropriate file formats
    
    PITFALL: Stragglers

    5. MONITORING AND DEBUGGING

def example_ml_data_preparation():
    """
    Example: ML data preparation with chunking
    """
    
    example_code = """
    
    ╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
    ║              MACHINE LEARNING DATA PREPARATION EXAMPLE                     ║
    ╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
    
    # =========================================================================
    # SCENARIO: Preparing large dataset for ML model training
    # =========================================================================
    
    from pyspark.ml.feature import VectorAssembler, StandardScaler
    from pyspark.ml import Pipeline
    
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # STEP 1: Load and Stratify Data
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    df_raw = spark.read.parquet("s3://bucket/ml_data")
    
    # Stratified chunking to maintain class distribution
    df_stratified = stratified_chunking(
        df_raw,
        stratify_column="target_class",
        chunks_per_stratum=20
    )
    
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # STEP 2: Feature Engineering per Chunk
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    def engineer_features(chunk_df):
        \"\"\"Apply feature engineering transformations\"\"\"
        
        # Numerical features
        chunk_df = chunk_df.withColumn(
            "log_amount", log1p(col("amount"))
        ).withColumn(
            "amount_squared", col("amount") ** 2
        )
        
        # Categorical encoding
        from pyspark.ml.feature import StringIndexer, OneHotEncoder
        
        indexer = StringIndexer(
            inputCol="category", 
            outputCol="category_index"
        )
        
        encoder = OneHotEncoder(
            inputCol="category_index",
            outputCol="category_vec"
        )
        
        # Apply transformations
        indexed = indexer.fit(chunk_df).transform(chunk_df)
        encoded = encoder.fit(indexed).transform(indexed)
        
        return encoded
    
    processor = ChunkProcessor(spark)
    df_featured = processor.process_all_chunks(
        df_stratified,
        engineer_features
    )
    
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # STEP 3: Memory-Based Chunking for Scaling
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    # Chunk based on memory for scaling operation
    df_memory_chunks = memory_based_chunking(
        df_featured,
        max_chunk_memory_mb=500
    )
    
    # Assemble features
    feature_cols = ["log_amount", "amount_squared", "category_vec"]
    assembler = VectorAssembler(
        inputCols=feature_cols,
        outputCol="raw_features"
    )
    
    # Scale features
    scaler = StandardScaler(
        inputCol="raw_features",
        outputCol="scaled_features",
        withMean=True,
        withStd=True
    )
    
    def scale_chunk(chunk_df):
        \"\"\"Scale features in chunk\"\"\"
        assembled = assembler.transform(chunk_df)
        scaler_model = scaler.fit(assembled)
        return scaler_model.transform(assembled)
    
    df_scaled = processor.process_all_chunks(
        df_memory_chunks,
        scale_chunk
    )
    
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # STEP 4: Train/Test Split with Stratification
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    # Split while maintaining stratification
    train_chunks = []
    test_chunks = []
    
    for target_class in df_scaled.select("target_class").distinct().collect():
        class_val = target_class["target_class"]
        class_data = df_scaled.filter(col("target_class") == class_val)
        
        # 80/20 split
        train, test = class_data.randomSplit([0.8, 0.2], seed=42)
        train_chunks.append(train)
        test_chunks.append(test)
    
    from functools import reduce
    df_train = reduce(lambda a, b: a.union(b), train_chunks)
    df_test = reduce(lambda a, b: a.union(b), test_chunks)
    
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # STEP 5: Save with Optimal Chunking
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    # Fixed-size chunks for training data
    df_train_chunked = fixed_size_chunking(df_train, chunk_size=50000)
    
    df_train_chunked \\
        .write \\
        .mode("overwrite") \\
        .partitionBy("chunk_id") \\
        .parquet("s3://bucket/ml_data/train")
    
    df_test \\
        .write \\
        .mode("overwrite") \\
        .parquet("s3://bucket/ml_data/test")
    
    print(f"Training samples: {df_train.count():,}")
    print(f"Test samples: {df_test.count():,}")
    
    """
    
    print(example_code)

def example_streaming_chunking():
    """
    Example: Streaming data with chunking
    """
    
    example_code = """
    
    ╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
    ║                    STREAMING DATA CHUNKING EXAMPLE                         ║
    ╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
    
    # =========================================================================
    # SCENARIO: Processing streaming data with micro-batches
    # =========================================================================
    
    from pyspark.sql.streaming import StreamingQuery
    
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # STEP 1: Setup Streaming Source
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    df_stream = spark.readStream \\
        .format("kafka") \\
        .option("kafka.bootstrap.servers", "localhost:9092") \\
        .option("subscribe", "transactions") \\
        .load()
    
    # Parse JSON from Kafka
    from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, DoubleType
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("transaction_id", StringType()),
        StructField("user_id", StringType()),
        StructField("amount", DoubleType()),
        StructField("timestamp", StringType())
    ])
    
    df_parsed = df_stream.select(
        from_json(col("value").cast("string"), schema).alias("data")
    ).select("data.*")
    
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # STEP 2: Time-Based Windowing (Streaming Chunks)
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    # Convert timestamp
    df_timestamped = df_parsed.withColumn(
        "event_time",
        to_timestamp(col("timestamp"))
    )
    
    # Create tumbling windows (non-overlapping chunks)
    df_windowed = df_timestamped.groupBy(
        window(col("event_time"), "5 minutes")
    ).agg(
        count("*").alias("transaction_count"),
        sum("amount").alias("total_amount"),
        avg("amount").alias("avg_amount"),
        countDistinct("user_id").alias("unique_users")
    )
    
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # STEP 3: Process Each Micro-Batch
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    def process_batch(batch_df, batch_id):
        \"\"\"Process each streaming micro-batch as a chunk\"\"\"
        
        print(f"Processing batch {batch_id}")
        
        # Apply fixed-size chunking within batch
        if batch_df.count() > 0:
            chunked = fixed_size_chunking(batch_df, chunk_size=1000)
            
            # Process each chunk
            for chunk_id in chunked.select("chunk_id").distinct().collect():
                chunk = chunked.filter(col("chunk_id") == chunk_id[0])
                
                # Apply transformations
                processed = chunk.withColumn(
                    "processed_time",
                    current_timestamp()
                ).withColumn(
                    "batch_id",
                    lit(batch_id)
                )
                
                # Write to output
                processed.write \\
                    .mode("append") \\
                    .partitionBy("batch_id", "chunk_id") \\
                    .parquet("s3://bucket/streaming_output")
            
            print(f"Batch {batch_id} completed")
    
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # STEP 4: Start Streaming Query
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    query = df_windowed.writeStream \\
        .foreachBatch(process_batch) \\
        .outputMode("update") \\
        .option("checkpointLocation", "s3://bucket/checkpoints/streaming") \\
        .trigger(processingTime="1 minute") \\
        .start()
    
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # STEP 5: Sliding Window for Real-Time Analytics
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    
    # Create sliding windows (overlapping chunks)
    df_sliding = df_timestamped.groupBy(
        window(col("event_time"), "10 minutes", "5 minutes"),
        col("user_id")
    ).agg(
        count("*").alias("transaction_count"),
        sum("amount").alias("total_spent")
    )
    
    # Detect anomalies in sliding windows
    df_anomalies = df_sliding.filter(
        (col("transaction_count") > 100) |
        (col("total_spent") > 10000)
    )
    
    # Write anomalies to separate stream
    query_anomalies = df_anomalies.writeStream \\
        .format("console") \\
        .outputMode("update") \\
        .start()
    
    # Wait for termination
    query.awaitTermination()
    
    """
    
    print(example_code)

def export_chunking_config(chunking_params, output_path="chunking_config.json"):
    """
    Export chunking configuration for reproducibility
    
    Args:
        chunking_params: Dictionary of chunking parameters
        output_path: Path to save configuration
    """
    import json
    
    config = {
        "chunking_strategy": chunking_params.get("strategy", "fixed-size"),
        "parameters": chunking_params,
        "timestamp": str(datetime.now()),
        "spark_version": spark.version
    }
    
    with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
        json.dump(config, f, indent=2)
    
    print(f"Configuration exported to {output_path}")

def load_chunking_config(config_path="chunking_config.json"):
    """
    Load chunking configuration from file
    
    Args:
        config_path: Path to configuration file
    
    Returns:
        Dictionary of chunking parameters
    """
    import json
    
    with open(config_path, 'r') as f:
        config = json.load(f)
    
    print(f"Configuration loaded from {config_path}")
    return config

def create_chunking_report(df_chunked, output_path="chunking_report.html"):
    """
    Generate HTML report of chunking statistics
    
    Args:
        df_chunked: Chunked DataFrame
        output_path: Path to save HTML report
    """
    
    stats = df_chunked.groupBy("chunk_id").count().toPandas()
    
    html_template = f"""
    <!DOCTYPE html>
    <html>
    <head>
        <title>Chunking Report</title>
        <style>
            body {{ font-family: Arial, sans-serif; margin: 20px; }}
            h1 {{ color: #333; }}
            table {{ border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; }}
            th, td {{ border: 1px solid #ddd; padding: 8px; text-align: left; }}
            th {{ background-color: #4CAF50; color: white; }}
            .stats {{ background-color: #f9f9f9; padding: 15px; margin: 20px 0; }}
        </style>
    </head>
    <body>
        <h1>Data Chunking Report</h1>
        <div class="stats">
            <h2>Summary Statistics</h2>
            <p><strong>Total Chunks:</strong> {len(stats)}</p>
            <p><strong>Total Records:</strong> {stats['count'].sum():,}</p>
            <p><strong>Min Chunk Size:</strong> {stats['count'].min():,}</p>
            <p><strong>Max Chunk Size:</strong> {stats['count'].max():,}</p>
            <p><strong>Avg Chunk Size:</strong> {stats['count'].mean():.2f}</p>
            <p><strong>Std Dev:</strong> {stats['count'].std():.2f}</p>
        </div>
        
        <h2>Chunk Distribution</h2>
        <table>
            <tr>
                <th>Chunk ID</th>
                <th>Record Count</th>
                <th>Percentage</th>
            </tr>
    """
    
    total_records = stats['count'].sum()
    for _, row in stats.iterrows():
        percentage = (row['count'] / total_records) * 100
        html_template += f"""
            <tr>
                <td>{row['chunk_id']}</td>
                <td>{row['count']:,}</td>
                <td>{percentage:.2f}%</td>
            </tr>
        """
    
    html_template += """
        </table>
    </body>
    </html>
    """
    
    with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
        f.write(html_template)
    
    print(f"Report generated: {output_path}")

def test_chunking_strategy(df, strategy_func, expected_chunks, tolerance=0.1):
    """
    Test chunking strategy meets expectations
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame
        strategy_func: Chunking function to test
        expected_chunks: Expected number of chunks
        tolerance: Acceptable deviation (0.1 = 10%)
    
    Returns:
        Boolean indicating if test passed
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print(f"TESTING CHUNKING STRATEGY: {strategy_func.__name__}")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    df_chunked = strategy_func(df)
    actual_chunks = df_chunked.select("chunk_id").distinct().count()
    
    deviation = abs(actual_chunks - expected_chunks) / expected_chunks
    
    print(f"\nExpected chunks: {expected_chunks}")
    print(f"Actual chunks: {actual_chunks}")
    print(f"Deviation: {deviation*100:.2f}%")
    
    if deviation <= tolerance:
        print("✓ TEST PASSED")
        return True
    else:
        print("✗ TEST FAILED")
        return False

def benchmark_chunking_strategies(df, strategies, iterations=3):
    """
    Benchmark multiple chunking strategies
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame
        strategies: List of (name, function, args) tuples
        iterations: Number of iterations for averaging
    
    Returns:
        DataFrame with benchmark results
    """
    import time
    
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print("BENCHMARKING CHUNKING STRATEGIES")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    results = []
    
    for name, func, args in strategies:
        print(f"\nBenchmarking: {name}")
        times = []
        
        for i in range(iterations):
            start_time = time.time()
            df_chunked = func(df, *args)
            _ = df_chunked.count()  # Force execution
            end_time = time.time()
            
            elapsed = end_time - start_time
            times.append(elapsed)
            print(f"  Iteration {i+1}: {elapsed:.4f}s")
        
        avg_time = sum(times) / len(times)
        results.append({
            "strategy": name,
            "avg_time_seconds": avg_time,
            "min_time_seconds": min(times),
            "max_time_seconds": max(times)
        })
    
    results_df = spark.createDataFrame(results)
    
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("BENCHMARK RESULTS")
    print("="*80)
    results_df.show()
    
    return results_df

def export_chunks_to_database(df_chunked, jdbc_url, table_name, 
                              connection_properties):
    """
    Export chunks to external database
    
    Args:
        df_chunked: Chunked DataFrame
        jdbc_url: JDBC connection URL
        table_name: Target table name
        connection_properties: Database connection properties
    """
    
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print(f"EXPORTING CHUNKS TO DATABASE: {table_name}")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    chunk_ids = df_chunked.select("chunk_id").distinct().collect()
    
    for row in chunk_ids:
        chunk_id = row["chunk_id"]
        chunk_data = df_chunked.filter(col("chunk_id") == chunk_id)
        
        # Write chunk to database
        chunk_data.write \
            .jdbc(url=jdbc_url,
                  table=f"{table_name}_chunk_{chunk_id}",
                  mode="overwrite",
                  properties=connection_properties)
        
        print(f"✓ Chunk {chunk_id} exported to database")
    
    print("\nAll chunks exported successfully")

def export_chunks_to_cloud_storage(df_chunked, storage_path, 
                                   storage_format="parquet"):
    """
    Export chunks to cloud storage (S3, GCS, Azure Blob)
    
    Args:
        df_chunked: Chunked DataFrame
        storage_path: Cloud storage path
        storage_format: Output format (parquet, orc, csv, json)
    """
    
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print(f"EXPORTING CHUNKS TO CLOUD STORAGE")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    print(f"Path: {storage_path}")
    print(f"Format: {storage_format}")
    
    # Write with partitioning by chunk_id
    df_chunked.write \
        .mode("overwrite") \
        .partitionBy("chunk_id") \
        .format(storage_format) \
        .save(storage_path)
    
    print("\n✓ Chunks exported to cloud storage")

def read_chunks_from_cloud_storage(storage_path, chunk_ids=None, 
                                   storage_format="parquet"):
    """
    Read specific chunks from cloud storage
    
    Args:
        storage_path: Cloud storage path
        chunk_ids: List of chunk IDs to read (None = read all)
        storage_format: Input format
    
    Returns:
        DataFrame with requested chunks
    """
    
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print(f"READING CHUNKS FROM CLOUD STORAGE")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    df = spark.read.format(storage_format).load(storage_path)
    
    if chunk_ids is not None:
        df = df.filter(col("chunk_id").isin(chunk_ids))
        print(f"Reading {len(chunk_ids)} specific chunks")
    else:
        print("Reading all chunks")
    
    count = df.count()
    print(f"✓ Loaded {count:,} records")
    
    return df

def monitor_chunk_processing(df_chunked, alert_threshold=0.3):
    """
    Monitor chunk processing and alert on imbalances
    
    Args:
        df_chunked: Chunked DataFrame
        alert_threshold: Threshold for coefficient of variation to trigger alert
    
    Returns:
        Dictionary with monitoring metrics
    """
    
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print("MONITORING CHUNK PROCESSING")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    # Calculate chunk statistics
    chunk_stats = df_chunked.groupBy("chunk_id").count().toPandas()
    
    mean_size = chunk_stats['count'].mean()
    std_size = chunk_stats['count'].std()
    cv = std_size / mean_size if mean_size > 0 else 0
    
    metrics = {
        "total_chunks": len(chunk_stats),
        "total_records": chunk_stats['count'].sum(),
        "mean_chunk_size": mean_size,
        "std_chunk_size": std_size,
        "coefficient_of_variation": cv,
        "min_chunk_size": chunk_stats['count'].min(),
        "max_chunk_size": chunk_stats['count'].max(),
        "imbalance_ratio": chunk_stats['count'].max() / chunk_stats['count'].min() 
                          if chunk_stats['count'].min() > 0 else float('inf')
    }
    
    print("\nChunk Processing Metrics:")
    print("-" * 80)
    for key, value in metrics.items():
        print(f"{key:30s}: {value:,.2f}" if isinstance(value, float) 
              else f"{key:30s}: {value:,}")
    
    # Alert if imbalanced
    if cv > alert_threshold:
        print(f"\n⚠ ALERT: High chunk imbalance detected (CV: {cv:.2f})")
        print(f"   Recommendation: Consider rebalancing chunks")
    else:
        print(f"\n✓ Chunk distribution is balanced (CV: {cv:.2f})")
    
    return metrics

def create_monitoring_dashboard_data(df_chunked, output_path="dashboard_data.json"):
    """
    Generate data for monitoring dashboard
    
    Args:
        df_chunked: Chunked DataFrame
        output_path: Path to save dashboard data
    """
    import json
    from datetime import datetime
    
    metrics = monitor_chunk_processing(df_chunked)
    
    # Get chunk distribution
    chunk_dist = df_chunked.groupBy("chunk_id").count() \
                          .orderBy("chunk_id").toPandas()
    
    dashboard_data = {
        "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
        "metrics": metrics,
        "chunk_distribution": chunk_dist.to_dict('records'),
        "alerts": []
    }
    
    # Add alerts
    if metrics['coefficient_of_variation'] > 0.3:
        dashboard_data['alerts'].append({
            "severity": "warning",
            "message": "High chunk imbalance detected",
            "metric": "coefficient_of_variation",
            "value": metrics['coefficient_of_variation']
        })
    
    if metrics['imbalance_ratio'] > 5:
        dashboard_data['alerts'].append({
            "severity": "critical",
            "message": "Extreme chunk size variation",
            "metric": "imbalance_ratio",
            "value": metrics['imbalance_ratio']
        })
    
    with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
        json.dump(dashboard_data, f, indent=2)
    
    print(f"\n✓ Dashboard data saved to {output_path}")

## Performance Characteristics

### Time Complexity
- **Best Case**: O(n)
- **Average Case**: O(n log n)
- **Worst Case**: O(n²)

### Space Complexity
- **Memory Usage**: {parameters.get('max_chunk_memory_mb', 'N/A')} MB per chunk
- **Storage Overhead**: ~5-10% for metadata

## Monitoring

### Key Metrics to Track
1. Chunk size distribution
2. Processing time per chunk
3. Memory utilization
4. Data skew indicators

### Alert Thresholds
- Coefficient of Variation > 0.3
- Imbalance Ratio > 5.0
- Processing time variance > 50%

## Troubleshooting

### Common Issues

#### Issue: Unbalanced Chunks
**Symptoms**: High variance in chunk sizes  
**Solution**: 
- Increase sample size for estimation
- Use adaptive chunking
- Implement rebalancing logic

#### Issue: Out of Memory Errors
**Symptoms**: Executor failures, GC overhead  
**Solution**:
- Reduce chunk size
- Increase executor memory
- Enable memory-based chunking

#### Issue: Slow Processing
**Symptoms**: Long execution time  
**Solution**:
- Optimize chunk size
- Increase parallelism
- Use appropriate partitioning

## Maintenance

### Regular Tasks
- [ ] Review chunk distribution weekly
- [ ] Monitor performance metrics
- [ ] Adjust parameters based on data growth
- [ ] Update documentation

### Optimization Opportunities
- Tune chunk size based on workload
- Implement caching for frequently accessed chunks
- Consider hybrid chunking strategies

def get_strategy_description(strategy_name):
    """Get detailed description for chunking strategy"""
    
    descriptions = {
        "Fixed-Size Chunking": """
This strategy divides data into chunks of equal size (by record count).
It's the simplest and most predictable chunking method.

**Advantages:**
- Simple to implement and understand
- Predictable resource usage
- Good for uniform data distribution

**Disadvantages:**
- Doesn't account for data skew
- May not be optimal for variable-size records
- Can lead to imbalanced processing times

**Best Used For:**
- Batch processing with uniform records
- Simple parallel processing
- Initial prototyping
""",
        "Variable-Size Chunking": """
This strategy creates chunks based on cumulative weight or size,
allowing for variable numbers of records per chunk.

**Advantages:**
- Adapts to data characteristics
- Better resource utilization
- Handles skewed data well

**Disadvantages:**
- More complex implementation
- Requires weight calculation
- May need tuning

**Best Used For:**
- Variable-length documents
- Mixed data types
- Memory-constrained environments
""",
        "Time-Based Chunking": """
This strategy creates chunks based on time intervals,
ideal for time-series and temporal data.

**Advantages:**
- Natural boundaries for temporal data
- Easy to understand and debug
- Supports time-based queries

**Disadvantages:**
- Can create unbalanced chunks with bursty data
- Requires timestamp column
- May not align with processing requirements

**Best Used For:**
- Time-series analysis
- Log processing
- Event stream processing
""",
        "Memory-Based Chunking": """
This strategy creates chunks based on estimated memory footprint,
preventing out-of-memory errors.

**Advantages:**
- Prevents OOM errors
- Optimizes memory usage
- Adapts to record complexity

**Disadvantages:**
- Requires size estimation
- More computational overhead
- May need calibration

**Best Used For:**
- Large object processing
- Memory-constrained environments
- Variable-size records
""",
        "Content-Based Chunking": """
This strategy uses content hashing to create chunk boundaries,
enabling deduplication and change detection.

**Advantages:**
- Content-aware boundaries
- Supports deduplication
- Good for incremental processing

**Disadvantages:**
- Complex implementation
- May create unbalanced chunks
- Higher computational cost

**Best Used For:**
- Deduplication
- Change data capture
- Distributed caching
"""
    }
    
    return descriptions.get(strategy_name, "No description available.")

# ADVANCED ANALYTICS ON CHUNKS
# =============================================================================

def analyze_chunk_characteristics(df_chunked, chunk_id_col="chunk_id"):
    """
    Perform detailed analysis of chunk characteristics
    
    Args:
        df_chunked: Chunked DataFrame
        chunk_id_col: Name of chunk ID column
    
    Returns:
        DataFrame with detailed chunk analytics
    """
    
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print("DETAILED CHUNK CHARACTERISTICS ANALYSIS")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    # Basic statistics
    chunk_stats = df_chunked.groupBy(chunk_id_col).agg(
        count("*").alias("record_count"),
        approx_count_distinct("*").alias("approx_unique_records")
    )
    
    # Calculate percentiles
    from pyspark.sql.functions import percentile_approx
    
    percentiles = chunk_stats.select(
        percentile_approx("record_count", 0.25).alias("p25"),
        percentile_approx("record_count", 0.50).alias("p50"),
        percentile_approx("record_count", 0.75).alias("p75"),
        percentile_approx("record_count", 0.90).alias("p90"),
        percentile_approx("record_count", 0.95).alias("p95"),
        percentile_approx("record_count", 0.99).alias("p99")
    ).first()
    
    print("\nChunk Size Percentiles:")
    print("-" * 80)
    print(f"25th percentile: {percentiles['p25']:,.0f}")
    print(f"50th percentile (median): {percentiles['p50']:,.0f}")
    print(f"75th percentile: {percentiles['p75']:,.0f}")
    print(f"90th percentile: {percentiles['p90']:,.0f}")
    print(f"95th percentile: {percentiles['p95']:,.0f}")
    print(f"99th percentile: {percentiles['p99']:,.0f}")
    
    # Identify outlier chunks
    from pyspark.sql.functions import mean, stddev
    
    stats = chunk_stats.select(
        mean("record_count").alias("mean"),
        stddev("record_count").alias("stddev")
    ).first()
    
    outlier_threshold = stats['mean'] + (2 * stats['stddev'])
    
    outliers = chunk_stats.filter(col("record_count") > outlier_threshold)
    outlier_count = outliers.count()
    
    if outlier_count > 0:
        print(f"\n⚠ Found {outlier_count} outlier chunks (>2 std dev from mean):")
        outliers.orderBy(col("record_count").desc()).show(10)
    else:
        print("\n✓ No significant outlier chunks detected")
    
    return chunk_stats

def predict_processing_time(df_chunked, sample_processing_time, 
                           chunk_id_col="chunk_id"):
    """
    Predict total processing time based on sample
    
    Args:
        df_chunked: Chunked DataFrame
        sample_processing_time: Time taken to process one sample chunk
        chunk_id_col: Name of chunk ID column
    
    Returns:
        Dictionary with time predictions
    """
    
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print("PROCESSING TIME PREDICTION")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    total_chunks = df_chunked.select(chunk_id_col).distinct().count()
    
    # Assume linear scaling (simplification)
    predictions = {
        "total_chunks": total_chunks,
        "sample_time_seconds": sample_processing_time,
        "sequential_time_hours": (total_chunks * sample_processing_time) / 3600,
        "parallel_time_minutes_4cores": (total_chunks * sample_processing_time) / (4 * 60),
        "parallel_time_minutes_8cores": (total_chunks * sample_processing_time) / (8 * 60),
        "parallel_time_minutes_16cores": (total_chunks * sample_processing_time) / (16 * 60)
    }
    
    print(f"\nBased on sample processing time of {sample_processing_time:.2f} seconds:")
    print("-" * 80)
    print(f"Total chunks to process: {predictions['total_chunks']:,}")
    print(f"\nEstimated completion times:")
    print(f"  Sequential: {predictions['sequential_time_hours']:.2f} hours")
    print(f"  Parallel (4 cores): {predictions['parallel_time_minutes_4cores']:.2f} minutes")
    print(f"  Parallel (8 cores): {predictions['parallel_time_minutes_8cores']:.2f} minutes")
    print(f"  Parallel (16 cores): {predictions['parallel_time_minutes_16cores']:.2f} minutes")
    
    return predictions

class ChunkingWorkflow:
    """
    Complete workflow orchestrator for chunking operations
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session, workflow_name="chunking_workflow"):
        self.spark = spark_session
        self.workflow_name = workflow_name
        self.execution_log = []
        self.start_time = None
        self.end_time = None
    
    def execute(self, df, chunking_strategy, strategy_params, 
                processing_func, output_path):
        """
        Execute complete chunking workflow
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            chunking_strategy: Chunking function to use
            strategy_params: Parameters for chunking strategy
            processing_func: Function to apply to each chunk
            output_path: Path to save results
        
        Returns:
            Final processed DataFrame
        """
        from datetime import datetime
        import time
        
        self.start_time = datetime.now()
        
        print(f"\n{'='*80}")
        print(f"EXECUTING CHUNKING WORKFLOW: {self.workflow_name}")
        print(f"{'='*80}")
        print(f"Start time: {self.start_time}")
        
        try:
            # Step 1: Apply chunking strategy
            print("\n[1/6] Applying chunking strategy...")
            step_start = time.time()
            df_chunked = chunking_strategy(df, **strategy_params)
            self._log_step("chunking", time.time() - step_start, "success")
            
            # Step 2: Analyze chunk distribution
            print("\n[2/6] Analyzing chunk distribution...")
            step_start = time.time()
            chunk_stats = analyze_chunk_characteristics(df_chunked)
            self._log_step("analysis", time.time() - step_start, "success")
            
            # Step 3: Checkpoint chunks
            print("\n[3/6] Checkpointing chunks...")
            step_start = time.time()
            checkpoint_path = f"{output_path}/checkpoints"
            df_chunked.write.mode("overwrite") \
                .partitionBy("chunk_id") \
                .parquet(checkpoint_path)
            self._log_step("checkpoint", time.time() - step_start, "success")
            
            # Step 4: Process chunks
            print("\n[4/6] Processing chunks...")
            step_start = time.time()
            processor = ChunkProcessor(self.spark)
            df_processed = processor.process_all_chunks(df_chunked, processing_func)
            self._log_step("processing", time.time() - step_start, "success")
            
            # Step 5: Save results
            print("\n[5/6] Saving results...")
            step_start = time.time()
            df_processed.write.mode("overwrite") \
                .parquet(f"{output_path}/results")
            self._log_step("save_results", time.time() - step_start, "success")
            
            # Step 6: Generate reports
            print("\n[6/6] Generating reports...")
            step_start = time.time()
            self._generate_workflow_report(output_path, chunk_stats, processor)
            self._log_step("reporting", time.time() - step_start, "success")
            
            self.end_time = datetime.now()
            duration = (self.end_time - self.start_time).total_seconds()
            
            print(f"\n{'='*80}")
            print(f"WORKFLOW COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY")
            print(f"{'='*80}")
            print(f"End time: {self.end_time}")
            print(f"Total duration: {duration:.2f} seconds ({duration/60:.2f} minutes)")
            
            return df_processed
            
        except Exception as e:
            self.end_time = datetime.now()
            print(f"\n{'='*80}")
            print(f"WORKFLOW FAILED")
            print(f"{'='*80}")
            print(f"Error: {str(e)}")
            self._log_step("workflow", 0, "failed", str(e))
            raise
    
    def _log_step(self, step_name, duration, status, error_msg=None):
        """Log workflow step execution"""
        log_entry = {
            "step": step_name,
            "duration_seconds": duration,
            "status": status,
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat()
        }
        if error_msg:
            log_entry["error"] = error_msg
        
        self.execution_log.append(log_entry)
    
    def _generate_workflow_report(self, output_path, chunk_stats, processor):
        """Generate comprehensive workflow report"""
        import json
        
        report = {
            "workflow_name": self.workflow_name,
            "start_time": self.start_time.isoformat(),
            "end_time": self.end_time.isoformat() if self.end_time else None,
            "execution_log": self.execution_log,
            "chunk_statistics": chunk_stats.toPandas().to_dict('records') if chunk_stats else [],
            "processing_statistics": processor.processing_stats if processor else []
        }
        
        report_path = f"{output_path}/workflow_report.json"
        with open(report_path, 'w') as f:
            
```python
            json.dump(report, f, indent=2)
        
        print(f"✓ Workflow report saved to {report_path}")
        
        # Also create a summary text file
        summary_path = f"{output_path}/workflow_summary.txt"
        with open(summary_path, 'w') as f:
            f.write(f"CHUNKING WORKFLOW SUMMARY\n")
            f.write(f"{'='*80}\n\n")
            f.write(f"Workflow Name: {self.workflow_name}\n")
            f.write(f"Start Time: {self.start_time}\n")
            f.write(f"End Time: {self.end_time}\n")
            f.write(f"Duration: {(self.end_time - self.start_time).total_seconds():.2f} seconds\n\n")
            f.write(f"Execution Steps:\n")
            f.write(f"{'-'*80}\n")
            for log in self.execution_log:
                f.write(f"  {log['step']:20s} - {log['status']:10s} - {log['duration_seconds']:.2f}s\n")
        
        print(f"✓ Workflow summary saved to {summary_path}")

def complete_example():
    """
    Complete end-to-end example demonstrating all patterns
    """
    
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print("COMPLETE END-TO-END CHUNKING EXAMPLE")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    # Create sample data
    df = create_sample_data()
    
    # Define processing function
    def my_processing_function(chunk_df):
        """Custom processing logic for each chunk"""
        return chunk_df.withColumn(
            "processed",
            lit(True)
        ).withColumn(
            "total_value",
            col("amount") * col("quantity")
        ).withColumn(
            "processing_timestamp",
            current_timestamp()
        )
    
    # Initialize workflow
    workflow = ChunkingWorkflow(spark, "example_workflow")
    
    # Execute workflow with fixed-size chunking
    result = workflow.execute(
        df=df,
        chunking_strategy=fixed_size_chunking,
        strategy_params={"chunk_size": 1000},
        processing_func=my_processing_function,
        output_path="/tmp/chunking_output"
    )
    
    print("\nProcessed data sample:")
    result.show(5)
    
    return result

# PATTERN 1: PURE COLUMN STORE PATTERN
# ============================================================================
"""
Pure Column Store Pattern:
- Stores each column independently in separate files/partitions
- Optimizes for analytical queries that access specific columns
- Reduces I/O by reading only required columns
- Best for OLAP workloads with selective column access
"""

class PureColumnStore:
    """
    Implements pure columnar storage where each column is stored separately.
    This pattern maximizes compression and minimizes I/O for column-specific queries.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, base_path: str):
        self.base_path = base_path
    
    def write_column_store(self, df, table_name: str):
        """
        Write each column to a separate Parquet file for pure columnar storage.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            table_name: Name of the table/dataset
        """
        print(f"\n{'=' * 80}")
        print(f"PATTERN 1: PURE COLUMN STORE - Writing {table_name}")
        print(f"{'=' * 80}")
        
        # Store metadata about columns
        metadata = {
            "table_name": table_name,
            "columns": df.columns,
            "row_count": df.count(),
            "schema": df.schema.json()
        }
        
        # Write each column separately
        for col_name in df.columns:
            col_path = f"{self.base_path}/{table_name}/columns/{col_name}"
            
            # Select only the column with row_id for reconstruction
            df.withColumn("row_id", monotonically_increasing_id()) \
                .select("row_id", col_name) \
                .write \
                .mode("overwrite") \
                .parquet(col_path)
            
            print(f"✓ Written column: {col_name} to {col_path}")
        
        # Write metadata
        metadata_path = f"{self.base_path}/{table_name}/metadata.json"
        spark.sparkContext.parallelize([json.dumps(metadata)]) \
            .saveAsTextFile(metadata_path)
        
        print(f"✓ Metadata written to {metadata_path}")
        return metadata
    
    def read_columns(self, table_name: str, columns: List[str]):
        """
        Read only specified columns from column store.
        
        Args:
            table_name: Name of the table
            columns: List of column names to read
        
        Returns:
            DataFrame with requested columns
        """
        print(f"\n{'=' * 80}")
        print(f"PATTERN 1: PURE COLUMN STORE - Reading columns: {columns}")
        print(f"{'=' * 80}")
        
        # Read first column with row_id
        result_df = spark.read.parquet(
            f"{self.base_path}/{table_name}/columns/{columns[0]}"
        )
        
        # Join remaining columns
        for col_name in columns[1:]:
            col_df = spark.read.parquet(
                f"{self.base_path}/{table_name}/columns/{col_name}"
            )
            result_df = result_df.join(col_df, "row_id")
        
        # Drop row_id and return
        result_df = result_df.drop("row_id")
        
        print(f"✓ Successfully read {len(columns)} columns")
        return result_df
    
    def analyze_storage(self, table_name: str):
        """Analyze storage efficiency of pure column store."""
        print(f"\n{'=' * 80}")
        print(f"PATTERN 1: STORAGE ANALYSIS")
        print(f"{'=' * 80}")
        
        # This would analyze actual file sizes in production
        print(f"Column-wise storage allows:")
        print(f"  • Reading only required columns (reduced I/O)")
        print(f"  • Better compression per column type")
        print(f"  • Optimal for analytical queries")
        print(f"  • Parallel column scanning")
