class SerializationTuningPattern:
    """
    Optimizes serialization for better performance and memory efficiency.
    
    Serialization Options:
    - Java Serialization (default, slower)
    - Kryo Serialization (faster, more efficient)
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_serialization_optimized_session(app_name="SerializationTuningDemo"):
        """Creates Spark session with optimized serialization"""
        
        spark = SparkSession.builder \
            .appName(app_name) \
            .config("spark.serializer", "org.apache.spark.serializer.KryoSerializer") \
            .config("spark.kryo.registrationRequired", "false") \
            .config("spark.kryoserializer.buffer.max", "512m") \
            .config("spark.kryoserializer.buffer", "64k") \
            .config("spark.rdd.compress", "true") \
            .config("spark.shuffle.compress", "true") \
            .config("spark.io.compression.codec", "snappy") \
            .config("spark.sql.inMemoryColumnarStorage.compressed", "true") \
            .config("spark.sql.inMemoryColumnarStorage.batchSize", "10000") \
            .getOrCreate()
        
        return spark
    
    @staticmethod
    def demonstrate_serialization_optimization():
        """Demonstrates serialization optimization techniques"""
        
        spark = SerializationTuningPattern.create_serialization_optimized_session()
        
        print("=== Serialization Tuning Pattern ===")
        
        # Create complex data structure
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", LongType(), True),
            StructField("name", StringType(), True),
            StructField("details", StructType([
                StructField("age", IntegerType(), True),
                StructField("city", StringType(), True),
                StructField("scores", ArrayType(DoubleType()), True)
            ]), True)
        ])
        
        # Generate sample data
        data = []
        for i in range(100000):
            data.append((
                i,
                f"User_{i}",
                (i % 100, f"City_{i % 50}", [float(i % 10), float(i % 20), float(i % 30)])
            ))
        
        df = spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        
        # Technique 1: Compare serialization methods
        print("\n1. Serialization Performance Comparison:")
        SerializationTuningPattern.compare_serialization(spark, df)
        
        # Technique 2: Optimize UDF serialization
        print("\n2. Optimized UDF with Kryo:")
        SerializationTuningPattern.demonstrate_udf_serialization(spark, df)
        
        # Technique 3: Columnar compression
        print("\n3. Columnar Compression:")
        SerializationTuningPattern.demonstrate_columnar_compression(spark, df)
        
        spark.stop()
    
    @staticmethod
    def compare_serialization(spark, df):
        """Compares different serialization approaches"""
        
        # Cache with different storage levels
        start_time = time.time()
        df.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_ONLY)
        count1 = df.count()
        time1 = time.time() - start_time
        df.unpersist()
        
        start_time = time.time()
        df.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_ONLY_SER)
        count2 = df.count()
        time2 = time.time() - start_time
        df.unpersist()
        
        print(f"MEMORY_ONLY: {time1:.2f}s")
        print(f"MEMORY_ONLY_SER (Kryo): {time2:.2f}s")
        print(f"Performance improvement: {((time1 - time2) / time1 * 100):.2f}%")
    
    @staticmethod
    def demonstrate_udf_serialization(spark, df):
        """Demonstrates UDF with optimized serialization"""
        
        from pyspark.sql.functions import udf
        from pyspark.sql.types import DoubleType
        
        # Define UDF
        @udf(returnType=DoubleType())
        def calculate_score(details):
            if details and details.scores:
                return sum(details.scores) / len(details.scores)
            return 0.0
        
        # Apply UDF
        result = df.withColumn("avg_score", calculate_score(col("details")))
        
        result.select("id", "name", "avg_score").show(5)
    
    @staticmethod
    def demonstrate_columnar_compression(spark, df):
        """Demonstrates columnar compression benefits"""
        
        # Cache as columnar format
        df.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_ONLY)
        
        # Perform columnar operations
        result = df.select(
            col("id"),
            col("name"),
            col("details.age").alias("age"),
            col("details.city").alias("city")
        ).filter(col("age") > 50)
        
        print(f"Filtered result count: {result.count()}")
        
        df.unpersist()

class IOTuningPattern:
    """
    Optimizes I/O operations for better read/write performance.
    
    Key Areas:
    - File format optimization
    - Compression strategies
    - Partition strategies
    - Read/write parallelism
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_io_optimized_session(app_name="IOTuningDemo"):
        """Creates Spark session with optimized I/O configuration"""
        
        spark = SparkSession.builder \
            .appName(app_name) \
            .config("spark.sql.files.maxPartitionBytes", "134217728") \
            .config("spark.sql.files.openCostInBytes", "4194304") \
            .config("spark.sql.parquet.compression.codec", "snappy") \
            .config("spark.sql.parquet.mergeSchema", "false") \
            .config("spark.sql.parquet.filterPushdown", "true") \
            .config("spark.sql.parquet.enableVectorizedReader", "true") \
            .config("spark.sql.orc.compression.codec", "snappy") \
            .config("spark.sql.orc.filterPushdown", "true") \
            .config("spark.sql.orc.enableVectorizedReader", "true") \
            .config("spark.hadoop.mapreduce.fileoutputcommitter.algorithm.version", "2") \
            .config("spark.speculation", "true") \
            .config("spark.speculation.interval", "100ms") \
            .config("spark.speculation.multiplier", "1.5") \
            .getOrCreate()
        
        return spark
    
    @staticmethod
    def demonstrate_io_optimization():
        """Demonstrates I/O optimization techniques"""
        
        spark = IOTuningPattern.create_io_optimized_session()
        
        print("=== I/O Tuning Pattern ===")
        
        # Generate sample data
        large_df = spark.range(0, 1000000).selectExpr(
            "id",
            "concat('user_', id) as user_name",
            "id % 100 as category",
            "rand() * 1000 as value",
            "current_timestamp() as timestamp"
        ).withColumn("date", to_date(col("timestamp")))
        
        # Technique 1: File format comparison
        print("\n1. File Format Comparison:")
        IOTuningPattern.compare_file_formats(spark, large_df)
        
        # Technique 2: Compression comparison
        print("\n2. Compression Comparison:")
        IOTuningPattern.compare_compression(spark, large_df)
        
        # Technique 3: Partitioning strategies
        print("\n3. Partitioning Strategies:")
        IOTuningPattern.demonstrate_partitioning_strategies(spark, large_df)
        
        # Technique 4: Predicate pushdown
        print("\n4. Predicate Pushdown:")
        IOTuningPattern.demonstrate_predicate_pushdown(spark)
        
        # Technique 5: Coalescing for write optimization
        print("\n5. Write Optimization:")
        IOTuningPattern.demonstrate_write_optimization(spark, large_df)
        
        spark.stop()
    
    @staticmethod
    def compare_file_formats(spark, df):
        """Compares different file formats"""
        
        import os
        
        formats = ['parquet', 'orc', 'avro', 'json', 'csv']
        
        for fmt in formats:
            path = f"/tmp/data_{fmt}"
            
            # Write
            start_write = time.time()
            df.write.mode("overwrite").format(fmt).save(path)
            write_time = time.time() - start_write
            
            # Read
            start_read = time.time()
            read_df = spark.read.format(fmt).load(path)
            count = read_df.count()
            read_time = time.time() - start_read
            
            # Get file size
            size = IOTuningPattern.get_directory_size(path)
            
            print(f"{fmt.upper():10} - Write: {write_time:.2f}s, "
                  f"Read: {read_time:.2f}s, Size: {size / (1024*1024):.2f}MB")
    
    @staticmethod
    def compare_compression(spark, df):
        """Compares different compression codecs"""
        
        codecs = ['uncompressed', 'snappy', 'gzip', 'lz4']
        
        for codec in codecs:
            path = f"/tmp/data_compressed_{codec}"
            
            # Write with compression
            start_time = time.time()
            df.write.mode("overwrite") \
                .option("compression", codec) \
                .parquet(path)
            write_time = time.time() - start_time
            
            # Get size
            size = IOTuningPattern.get_directory_size(path)
            
            print(f"{codec.upper():15} - Write: {write_time:.2f}s, "
                  f"Size: {size / (1024*1024):.2f}MB")
    
    @staticmethod
    def demonstrate_partitioning_strategies(spark, df):
        """Demonstrates different partitioning strategies"""
        
        # Strategy 1: No partitioning
        df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet("/tmp/no_partition")
        
        # Strategy 2: Single column partitioning
        df.write.mode("overwrite") \
            .partitionBy("category") \
            .parquet("/tmp/single_partition")
        
        # Strategy 3: Multi-column partitioning
        df.write.mode("overwrite") \
            .partitionBy("date", "category") \
            .parquet("/tmp/multi_partition")
        
        # Read and compare query performance
        no_part = spark.read.parquet("/tmp/no_partition")
        single_part = spark.read.parquet("/tmp/single_partition")
        multi_part = spark.read.parquet("/tmp/multi_partition")
        
        # Query with filter
        start = time.time()
        count1 = no_part.filter(col("category") == 50).count()
        time1 = time.time() - start
        
        start = time.time()
        count2 = single_part.filter(col("category") == 50).count()
        time2 = time.time() - start
        
        print(f"No partition query: {time1:.2f}s")
        print(f"Partitioned query: {time2:.2f}s")
        print(f"Improvement: {((time1 - time2) / time1 * 100):.2f}%")
    
    @staticmethod
    def demonstrate_predicate_pushdown(spark):
        """Demonstrates predicate pushdown optimization"""
        
        # Write partitioned data
        df = spark.range(0, 1000000).selectExpr(
            "id",
            "id % 10 as partition_col",
            "rand() * 1000 as value"
        )
        
        df.write.mode("overwrite") \
            .partitionBy("partition_col") \
            .parquet("/tmp/pushdown_test")
        
        # Read with predicate pushdown
        read_df = spark.read.parquet("/tmp/pushdown_test")
        
        # Filter will be pushed down to file scan
        filtered = read_df.filter(col("partition_col") == 5)
        
        print("Query plan with predicate pushdown:")
        filtered.explain(True)
        
        print(f"Filtered count: {filtered.count()}")
    
    @staticmethod
    def demonstrate_write_optimization(spark, df):
        """Demonstrates write optimization techniques"""
        
```python
        """Demonstrates write optimization techniques"""
        
        # Technique 1: Coalesce before write (reduce small files)
        print("\nWithout coalesce:")
        start = time.time()
        df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet("/tmp/without_coalesce")
        time1 = time.time() - start
        file_count1 = IOTuningPattern.count_files("/tmp/without_coalesce")
        print(f"Time: {time1:.2f}s, Files: {file_count1}")
        
        print("\nWith coalesce:")

    @staticmethod
    def get_directory_size(path):
        """Calculate total size of directory"""
        import os
        total_size = 0
        try:
            for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(path):
                for filename in filenames:
                    filepath = os.path.join(dirpath, filename)
                    if os.path.exists(filepath):
                        total_size += os.path.getsize(filepath)
        except:
            pass
        return total_size
    
    @staticmethod
    def count_files(path):
        """Count number of files in directory"""
        import os
        count = 0
        try:
            for dirpath, dirnames, filenames in os.walk(path):
                count += len([f for f in filenames if not f.startswith('.')])
        except:
            pass
        return count


# ============================================================================
# PERFORMANCE MONITORING AND UTILITIES
# ============================================================================

class PerformanceMonitor:
    """
    Utility class for monitoring and measuring Spark job performance.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def time_operation(operation_name):
        """Decorator to time operations"""
        def decorator(func):
            @wraps(func)
            def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
                print(f"\n{'='*60}")
                print(f"Starting: {operation_name}")
                print(f"{'='*60}")
                start_time = time.time()
                
                result = func(*args, **kwargs)
                
                elapsed_time = time.time() - start_time
                print(f"\n{'='*60}")
                print(f"Completed: {operation_name}")
                print(f"Time elapsed: {elapsed_time:.2f} seconds")
                print(f"{'='*60}\n")
                
                return result
            return wrapper
        return decorator
    
    @staticmethod
    def print_spark_config(spark):
        """Print important Spark configurations"""
        print("\n=== Current Spark Configuration ===")
        
        important_configs = [
            "spark.executor.instances",
            "spark.executor.cores",
            "spark.executor.memory",
            "spark.driver.memory",
            "spark.sql.shuffle.partitions",
            "spark.default.parallelism",
            "spark.serializer",
            "spark.sql.adaptive.enabled",
            "spark.memory.fraction",
            "spark.memory.storageFraction"
        ]
        
        conf = spark.sparkContext.getConf()
        for config in important_configs:
            value = conf.get(config, "Not Set")
            print(f"{config:40} = {value}")
    
    @staticmethod
    def analyze_dataframe_stats(df, name="DataFrame"):
        """Analyze and print DataFrame statistics"""
        print(f"\n=== {name} Statistics ===")
        print(f"Number of partitions: {df.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
        print(f"Schema:")
        df.printSchema()
        print(f"\nSample data:")
        df.show(5, truncate=False)
        
    @staticmethod
    def get_stage_metrics(spark):
        """Get metrics for completed stages"""
        print("\n=== Stage Metrics ===")
        
        status_tracker = spark.sparkContext.statusTracker()
        
        for stage_id in status_tracker.getStageIds():
            stage_info = status_tracker.getStageInfo(stage_id)
            if stage_info:
                print(f"\nStage {stage_id}:")
                print(f"  Number of tasks: {stage_info.numTasks}")
                print(f"  Number of active tasks: {stage_info.numActiveTasks}")
                print(f"  Number of completed tasks: {stage_info.numCompletedTasks}")
                print(f"  Number of failed tasks: {stage_info.numFailedTasks}")

            "concat('Product_', id) as product_name",
            "id % 10 as category_id",
            "rand() * 100 as unit_price"
        )
        
        PerformanceMonitor.analyze_dataframe_stats(sales_df, "Sales")
        
        # Step 2: Apply memory optimization
        print("\n[Step 2] Applying memory optimization...")
        sales_df.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_AND_DISK_SER)
        customers_df.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_ONLY)
        products_df.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_ONLY)
        
        # Trigger caching
        sales_df.count()
        customers_df.count()
        products_df.count()
        
        # Step 3: Optimized joins with broadcast
        print("\n[Step 3] Performing optimized joins...")
        
        # Broadcast small table
        enriched_sales = sales_df.join(
            broadcast(products_df),
            "product_id",
            "inner"
        )
        
        # Regular join for medium table
        final_df = enriched_sales.join(
            customers_df,
            "customer_id",
            "inner"
        )
        
        # Step 4: Optimized aggregations
        print("\n[Step 4] Performing optimized aggregations...")
        
        monthly_summary = final_df.groupBy(
            "year", "month", "region_id", "tier"
        ).agg(
            count("transaction_id").alias("transaction_count"),
            sum("amount").alias("total_sales"),
            avg("amount").alias("avg_transaction"),
            countDistinct("customer_id").alias("unique_customers")
        )
        
        # Step 5: Write optimized output
        print("\n[Step 5] Writing optimized output...")
        
        # Coalesce to reduce small files
        monthly_summary.coalesce(20).write \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .partitionBy("year", "month") \
            .option("compression", "snappy") \
            .parquet("/tmp/optimized_output")
        
        # Step 6: Verify and analyze results
        print("\n[Step 6] Verifying results...")
        
        result = spark.read.parquet("/tmp/optimized_output")
        
        print("\nFinal Results:")
        result.orderBy(desc("total_sales")).show(20)
        
        print(f"\nTotal records: {result.count()}")
        print(f"Output partitions: {result.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
        
        # Step 7: Performance metrics
        print("\n[Step 7] Performance Metrics:")
        PerformanceMonitor.get_stage_metrics(spark)
        
        # Cleanup
        sales_df.unpersist()
        customers_df.unpersist()
        products_df.unpersist()
        
        spark.stop()
        
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("COMPREHENSIVE DEMO COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY")
        print("="*80)

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, when, lit
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, IntegerType, DoubleType

def content_based_routing_pattern():
    """
    Content-Based Routing Pattern:
    Routes data to different destinations based on message content/attributes.
    Use case: Route customer orders to different processing queues based on order value.
    """
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("ContentBasedRoutingPattern") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    # Sample data: Customer orders
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("order_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("customer_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("product_category", StringType(), True),
        StructField("order_value", DoubleType(), True),
        StructField("region", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    data = [
        ("ORD001", "CUST001", "Electronics", 1500.00, "North"),
        ("ORD002", "CUST002", "Clothing", 250.00, "South"),
        ("ORD003", "CUST003", "Electronics", 5000.00, "East"),
        ("ORD004", "CUST004", "Food", 50.00, "West"),
        ("ORD005", "CUST005", "Electronics", 800.00, "North"),
        ("ORD006", "CUST006", "Furniture", 3000.00, "South"),
    ]
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
    
    # Content-based routing logic
    # Route based on order value and product category
    df_routed = df.withColumn(
        "routing_destination",
        when((col("order_value") >= 1000) & (col("product_category") == "Electronics"), 
             lit("premium_electronics_queue"))
        .when((col("order_value") >= 1000), 
              lit("premium_queue"))
        .when(col("product_category") == "Electronics", 
              lit("electronics_queue"))
        .when(col("product_category") == "Food", 
              lit("food_queue"))
        .otherwise(lit("standard_queue"))
    )
    
    print("=" * 80)
    print("CONTENT-BASED ROUTING PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    df_routed.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Route to different destinations (separate DataFrames)
    routes = {
        "premium_electronics": df_routed.filter(col("routing_destination") == "premium_electronics_queue"),
        "premium": df_routed.filter(col("routing_destination") == "premium_queue"),
        "electronics": df_routed.filter(col("routing_destination") == "electronics_queue"),
        "food": df_routed.filter(col("routing_destination") == "food_queue"),
        "standard": df_routed.filter(col("routing_destination") == "standard_queue")
    }
    
    # Display routed data
    for route_name, route_df in routes.items():
        count = route_df.count()
        if count > 0:
            print(f"\n{route_name.upper()} ROUTE ({count} records):")
            route_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Write to different outputs (simulated with different paths)
    for route_name, route_df in routes.items():
        if route_df.count() > 0:
            output_path = f"/tmp/content_routing/{route_name}"
            # route_df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(output_path)
            print(f"Routed {route_df.count()} records to {output_path}")
    
    spark.stop()

## 2. Rule-Based Routing Pattern

```python
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, when, lit, udf
from pyspark.sql.types import StringType, ArrayType
import json

def rule_based_routing_pattern():
    """
    Rule-Based Routing Pattern:
    Routes data based on predefined business rules stored in a configuration.
    Use case: Route insurance claims based on complex business rules.
    """
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("RuleBasedRoutingPattern") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    # Sample data: Insurance claims
    data = [
        ("CLM001", "Auto", 5000.00, "High", "CA", "Approved"),
        ("CLM002", "Health", 15000.00, "Critical", "NY", "Pending"),
        ("CLM003", "Home", 2000.00, "Low", "TX", "Approved"),
        ("CLM004", "Auto", 25000.00, "Critical", "FL", "Pending"),
        ("CLM005", "Health", 500.00, "Low", "CA", "Approved"),
        ("CLM006", "Home", 50000.00, "Critical", "NY", "Rejected"),
    ]
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(data, 
        ["claim_id", "claim_type", "claim_amount", "severity", "state", "status"])
    
    # Define routing rules (could be loaded from external config/database)
    routing_rules = [
        {
            "rule_id": "R1",
            "conditions": {"severity": "Critical", "claim_amount_gt": 10000},
            "destination": "senior_adjuster_queue",
            "priority": 1
        },
        {
            "rule_id": "R2",
            "conditions": {"claim_type": "Health", "claim_amount_gt": 5000},
            "destination": "medical_specialist_queue",
            "priority": 2
        },
        {
            "rule_id": "R3",
            "conditions": {"severity": "Critical"},
            "destination": "urgent_queue",
            "priority": 3
        },
        {
            "rule_id": "R4",
            "conditions": {"claim_amount_gt": 20000},
            "destination": "high_value_queue",
            "priority": 4
        },
        {
            "rule_id": "R5",
            "conditions": {"status": "Approved", "severity": "Low"},
            "destination": "auto_process_queue",
            "priority": 5
        }
    ]
    
    # Apply rules using UDF
    def apply_routing_rules(claim_type, claim_amount, severity, status):
        """Apply routing rules and return destination based on priority"""
        matched_rules = []
        
        for rule in routing_rules:
            conditions = rule["conditions"]
            match = True
            
            # Check each condition
            if "severity" in conditions and conditions["severity"] != severity:
                match = False
            if "claim_type" in conditions and conditions["claim_type"] != claim_type:
                match = False
            if "status" in conditions and conditions["status"] != status:
                match = False
            if "claim_amount_gt" in conditions and claim_amount <= conditions["claim_amount_gt"]:
                match = False
            
            if match:
                matched_rules.append((rule["priority"], rule["destination"], rule["rule_id"]))
        
        # Return highest priority rule (lowest priority number)
        if matched_rules:
            matched_rules.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
            return f"{matched_rules[0][1]}|{matched_rules[0][2]}"
        
        return "default_queue|R0"
    
    routing_udf = udf(apply_routing_rules, StringType())
    
    # Apply routing
    df_routed = df.withColumn(
        "routing_info",
        routing_udf(col("claim_type"), col("claim_amount"), col("severity"), col("status"))
    )
    
    # Split routing info
    from pyspark.sql.functions import split
    df_routed = df_routed \
        .withColumn("routing_destination", split(col("routing_info"), "\\|").getItem(0)) \
        .withColumn("matched_rule", split(col("routing_info"), "\\|").getItem(1)) \
        .drop("routing_info")
    
    print("=" * 80)
    print("RULE-BASED ROUTING PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    df_routed.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Group by routing destination
    print("\nRouting Summary:")
    df_routed.groupBy("routing_destination", "matched_rule").count().show(truncate=False)
    
    spark.stop()

```

## 3. Dynamic Routing Pattern

```python
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, when, lit, current_timestamp, hour, rand
from datetime import datetime

def dynamic_routing_pattern():
    """
    Dynamic Routing Pattern:
    Routes data dynamically based on runtime conditions like system load, 
    time of day, or available resources.
    Use case: Load balancing across multiple processing clusters.
    """
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("DynamicRoutingPattern") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    # Sample data: API requests
    data = [
        ("REQ001", "user_service", "GET", 100, "2024-01-15 08:30:00"),
        ("REQ002", "payment_service", "POST", 500, "2024-01-15 14:45:00"),
        ("REQ003", "order_service", "GET", 200, "2024-01-15 09:15:00"),
        ("REQ004", "user_service", "PUT", 300, "2024-01-15 22:30:00"),
        ("REQ005", "payment_service", "POST", 450, "2024-01-15 13:00:00"),
        ("REQ006", "order_service", "POST", 800, "2024-01-15 23:45:00"),
        ("REQ007", "analytics_service", "GET", 1000, "2024-01-15 10:00:00"),
        ("REQ008", "user_service", "GET", 150, "2024-01-15 15:30:00"),
    ]
    
    from pyspark.sql.types import TimestampType
    df = spark.createDataFrame(data, 
        ["request_id", "service_name", "method", "processing_time_ms", "timestamp"])
    
    # Convert timestamp string to timestamp type
    from pyspark.sql.functions import to_timestamp
    df = df.withColumn("timestamp", to_timestamp(col("timestamp")))
    
    # Simulate system load metrics (in real scenario, fetch from monitoring system)
    cluster_loads = {
        "cluster_a": 0.3,  # 30% load
        "cluster_b": 0.7,  # 70% load
        "cluster_c": 0.5,  # 50% load
    }
    
    # Dynamic routing based on multiple factors
    df_routed = df.withColumn("hour_of_day", hour(col("timestamp")))
    
    # Routing logic considering:
    # 1. Time of day (peak vs off-peak)
    # 2. Request complexity (processing time)
    # 3. Load balancing (random distribution for similar requests)
    df_routed = df_routed.withColumn("random_factor", rand(seed=42))
    
    df_routed = df_routed.withColumn(
        "routing_cluster",
        when(
            # Peak hours (8-18) and heavy requests -> dedicated cluster
            (col("hour_of_day").between(8, 18)) & (col("processing_time_ms") > 500),
            lit("cluster_heavy_peak")
        ).when(
            # Off-peak heavy requests -> can use any cluster with low load
            (~col("hour_of_day").between(8, 18)) & (col("processing_time_ms") > 500),
            when(col("random_factor") < 0.5, lit("cluster_a"))
            .otherwise(lit("cluster_c"))
        ).when(
            # Payment service always goes to secure cluster
            col("service_name") == "payment_service",
            lit("cluster_secure")
        ).when(
            # Load balancing for normal requests
            col("random_factor") < 0.33,
            lit("cluster_a")
        ).when(
            col("random_factor") < 0.66,
            lit("cluster_b")
        ).otherwise(
            lit("cluster_c")
        )
    )
    
    # Add routing metadata
    df_routed = df_routed.withColumn(
        "routing_reason",
        when(
            (col("hour_of_day").between(8, 18)) & (col("processing_time_ms") > 500),
            lit("peak_heavy_load")
        ).when(
            col("service_name") == "payment_service",
            lit("security_requirement")
        ).otherwise(
            lit("load_balancing")
        )
    )
    
    print("=" * 80)
    print("DYNAMIC ROUTING PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    df_routed.select(
        "request_id", "service_name", "method", "processing_time_ms", 
        "hour_of_day", "routing_cluster", "routing_reason"
    ).show(truncate=False)
    
    # Show routing distribution
    print("\nRouting Distribution by Cluster:")
    df_routed.groupBy("routing_cluster", "routing_reason").count() \
        .orderBy("routing_cluster").show(truncate=False)
    
    # Simulate dynamic re-routing based on cluster health
    print("\nSimulating Dynamic Re-routing:")
    
    # If cluster_b is overloaded, re-route its traffic
    df_rerouted = df_routed.withColumn(
        "final_cluster",
        when(
            (col("routing_cluster") == "cluster_b") & (lit(cluster_loads["cluster_b"]) > 0.6),
            when(lit(cluster_loads["cluster_a"]) < lit(cluster_loads["cluster_c"]), 
                 lit("cluster_a_failover"))
            .otherwise(lit("cluster_c_failover"))
        ).otherwise(col("routing_cluster"))
    )
    
    df_rerouted.groupBy("final_cluster").count().show(truncate=False)
    
    spark.stop()

```

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, explode, array, lit, struct

def multicast_routing_pattern():
    """
    Multi-Cast Routing Pattern:
    Routes the same message to multiple destinations simultaneously.
    Use case: Send order confirmation to multiple systems (inventory, shipping, analytics).
    """
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("MultiCastRoutingPattern") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    # Sample data: Customer orders
    data = [
        ("ORD001", "CUST001", "Premium", 1500.00, "Electronics", "Completed"),
        ("ORD002", "CUST002", "Standard", 250.00, "Clothing", "Completed"),
        ("
```python
("ORD003", "CUST003", "Premium", 5000.00, "Electronics", "Completed"),
        ("ORD004", "CUST004", "Standard", 50.00, "Food", "Pending"),
        ("ORD005", "CUST005", "Premium", 800.00, "Furniture", "Completed"),
    ]
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(data, 
        ["order_id", "customer_id", "customer_tier", "order_value", "category", "status"])
    
    # Define multicast destinations based on order attributes
    # Each order may go to multiple destinations
    def get_destinations(customer_tier, order_value, category, status):
        """Determine all destinations for an order"""
        destinations = []
        
        # All completed orders go to these systems
        if status == "Completed":
            destinations.append(("inventory_system", "update_stock"))
            destinations.append(("shipping_system", "prepare_shipment"))
            destinations.append(("analytics_system", "record_sale"))
        
        # Premium customers - additional notifications
        if customer_tier == "Premium":
            destinations.append(("crm_system", "update_customer_profile"))
            destinations.append(("loyalty_system", "add_points"))
        
        # High value orders - fraud check and approval
        if order_value > 1000:
            destinations.append(("fraud_detection_system", "verify_transaction"))
            destinations.append(("finance_system", "record_revenue"))
        
        # Category-specific routing
        if category == "Electronics":
            destinations.append(("warranty_system", "register_product"))
        
        # Pending orders need approval
        if status == "Pending":
            destinations.append(("approval_system", "request_approval"))
        
        return destinations
    
    from pyspark.sql.types import ArrayType, StructType, StructField
    from pyspark.sql.functions import udf
    
    # Define return schema for UDF
    destination_schema = ArrayType(
        StructType([
            StructField("destination_system", StringType(), True),
            StructField("action", StringType(), True)
        ])
    )
    
    get_destinations_udf = udf(get_destinations, destination_schema)
    
    # Apply multicast routing
    df_multicast = df.withColumn(
        "destinations",
        get_destinations_udf(
            col("customer_tier"), 
            col("order_value"), 
            col("category"), 
            col("status")
        )
    )
    
    print("=" * 80)
    print("MULTI-CAST ROUTING PATTERN - Orders with Destinations")
    print("=" * 80)
    df_multicast.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Explode to create individual routing records
    df_routed = df_multicast.withColumn("destination", explode(col("destinations"))) \
        .select(
            col("order_id"),
            col("customer_id"),
            col("customer_tier"),
            col("order_value"),
            col("category"),
            col("status"),
            col("destination.destination_system").alias("destination_system"),
            col("destination.action").alias("action")
        )
    
    print("\nMulti-Cast Routing - Exploded View (Each destination):")
    df_routed.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Count destinations per order
    print("\nDestination Count per Order:")
    df_multicast.selectExpr(
        "order_id",
        "size(destinations) as destination_count"
    ).show(truncate=False)
    
    # Group by destination system to see workload
    print("\nWorkload by Destination System:")
    df_routed.groupBy("destination_system", "action").count() \
        .orderBy("destination_system", "action").show(truncate=False)
    
    # Simulate writing to multiple destinations
    print("\nSimulating Multi-Cast Delivery:")
    destinations = df_routed.select("destination_system").distinct().collect()
    
    for dest_row in destinations:
        dest_system = dest_row["destination_system"]
        dest_data = df_routed.filter(col("destination_system") == dest_system)
        count = dest_data.count()
        
        print(f"\nRouting {count} messages to {dest_system}:")
        dest_data.show(5, truncate=False)
        
        # In real scenario, write to different outputs
        # dest_data.write.mode("append").parquet(f"/tmp/multicast/{dest_system}")
    
    spark.stop()

## 5. Conditional Routing Pattern

```python
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, when, lit, expr, coalesce
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, IntegerType, DoubleType, BooleanType

def conditional_routing_pattern():
    """
    Conditional Routing Pattern:
    Routes data based on complex conditional logic with fallback mechanisms.
    Use case: Route customer support tickets based on priority, SLA, and agent availability.
    """
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("ConditionalRoutingPattern") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    # Sample data: Customer support tickets
    data = [
        ("TKT001", "CUST001", "Technical", "Critical", True, 120, "VIP"),
        ("TKT002", "CUST002", "Billing", "High", False, 45, "Standard"),
        ("TKT003", "CUST003", "Technical", "Low", False, 10, "Standard"),
        ("TKT004", "CUST004", "Account", "Critical", True, 180, "VIP"),
        ("TKT005", "CUST005", "Technical", "Medium", False, 60, "Premium"),
        ("TKT006", "CUST006", "Billing", "High", True, 90, "Premium"),
        ("TKT007", "CUST007", "General", "Low", False, 5, "Standard"),
        ("TKT008", "CUST008", "Technical", "Critical", False, 150, "Standard"),
    ]
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(data, 
        ["ticket_id", "customer_id", "category", "priority", "sla_breach", 
         "wait_time_minutes", "customer_segment"])
    
    # Simulate agent availability (in real scenario, fetch from resource management system)
    agent_availability = {
        "vip_technical_team": True,
        "vip_general_team": True,
        "technical_specialists": False,  # Not available
        "billing_specialists": True,
        "general_support_team": True,
        "escalation_team": True,
        "overflow_team": True
    }
    
    # Add availability as broadcast variable (simulated as columns)
    from pyspark.sql.functions import lit
    for team, available in agent_availability.items():
        df = df.withColumn(f"avail_{team}", lit(available))
    
    # Complex conditional routing with multiple fallback levels
    df_routed = df.withColumn(
        "routing_team",
        # Level 1: VIP customers with critical issues
        when(
            (col("customer_segment") == "VIP") & 
            (col("priority") == "Critical") & 
            (col("category") == "Technical") &
            col("avail_vip_technical_team"),
            lit("vip_technical_team")
        )
        # Level 2: VIP customers (any issue)
        .when(
            (col("customer_segment") == "VIP") & 
            col("avail_vip_general_team"),
            lit("vip_general_team")
        )
        # Level 3: SLA breach - immediate escalation
        .when(
            (col("sla_breach") == True) & 
            col("avail_escalation_team"),
            lit("escalation_team")
        )
        # Level 4: Critical technical issues
        .when(
            (col("priority") == "Critical") & 
            (col("category") == "Technical") &
            col("avail_technical_specialists"),
            lit("technical_specialists")
        )
        # Level 5: Billing specialists for billing issues
        .when(
            (col("category") == "Billing") & 
            (col("priority").isin(["High", "Critical"])) &
            col("avail_billing_specialists"),
            lit("billing_specialists")
        )
        # Level 6: High priority to general support
        .when(
            (col("priority").isin(["High", "Critical"])) &
            col("avail_general_support_team"),
            lit("general_support_team")
        )
        # Level 7: Premium customers
        .when(
            (col("customer_segment") == "Premium") &
            col("avail_general_support_team"),
            lit("general_support_team")
        )
        # Level 8: Long wait times
        .when(
            (col("wait_time_minutes") > 60) &
            col("avail_overflow_team"),
            lit("overflow_team")
        )
        # Fallback: Overflow team
        .when(
            col("avail_overflow_team"),
            lit("overflow_team")
        )
        # Final fallback: Queue for later
        .otherwise(lit("queued_for_next_available"))
    )
    
    # Add routing metadata
    df_routed = df_routed.withColumn(
        "routing_priority",
        when(col("routing_team") == "vip_technical_team", lit(1))
        .when(col("routing_team") == "vip_general_team", lit(2))
        .when(col("routing_team") == "escalation_team", lit(3))
        .when(col("routing_team") == "technical_specialists", lit(4))
        .when(col("routing_team") == "billing_specialists", lit(5))
        .when(col("routing_team") == "general_support_team", lit(6))
        .when(col("routing_team") == "overflow_team", lit(7))
        .otherwise(lit(99))
    )
    
    df_routed = df_routed.withColumn(
        "routing_reason",
        when(
            (col("customer_segment") == "VIP") & (col("priority") == "Critical"),
            lit("VIP_CRITICAL_PRIORITY")
        ).when(
            col("sla_breach") == True,
            lit("SLA_BREACH_ESCALATION")
        ).when(
            col("priority") == "Critical",
            lit("CRITICAL_PRIORITY")
        ).when(
            col("wait_time_minutes") > 60,
            lit("LONG_WAIT_TIME")
        ).when(
            col("customer_segment").isin(["VIP", "Premium"]),
            lit("PREMIUM_CUSTOMER")
        ).otherwise(
            lit("STANDARD_ROUTING")
        )
    )
    
    # Add estimated handling time based on routing
    df_routed = df_routed.withColumn(
        "estimated_resolution_minutes",
        when(col("routing_team").contains("vip"), lit(15))
        .when(col("routing_team") == "escalation_team", lit(30))
        .when(col("routing_team").contains("specialist"), lit(45))
        .when(col("routing_team") == "general_support_team", lit(60))
        .otherwise(lit(90))
    )
    
    print("=" * 80)
    print("CONDITIONAL ROUTING PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Select relevant columns for display
    df_display = df_routed.select(
        "ticket_id", "customer_id", "category", "priority", 
        "sla_breach", "wait_time_minutes", "customer_segment",
        "routing_team", "routing_priority", "routing_reason",
        "estimated_resolution_minutes"
    )
    
    df_display.orderBy("routing_priority", "wait_time_minutes").show(truncate=False)
    
    # Routing statistics
    print("\nRouting Distribution by Team:")
    df_routed.groupBy("routing_team", "routing_reason") \
        .count() \
        .orderBy("routing_team") \
        .show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\nPriority Distribution:")
    df_routed.groupBy("priority", "routing_team") \
        .count() \
        .orderBy("priority", "routing_team") \
        .show(truncate=False)
    
    # Simulate conditional re-routing based on team capacity
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("CONDITIONAL RE-ROUTING SIMULATION")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # If VIP team is at capacity, re-route to escalation team
    team_capacity = {
        "vip_technical_team": 2,
        "vip_general_team": 3,
        "escalation_team": 10
    }
    
    from pyspark.sql.window import Window
    from pyspark.sql.functions import row_number
    
    # Add row number within each team
    window_spec = Window.partitionBy("routing_team").orderBy("routing_priority", "wait_time_minutes")
    df_with_position = df_routed.withColumn("position_in_queue", row_number().over(window_spec))
    
    # Re-route if team is over capacity
    df_rerouted = df_with_position.withColumn(
        "final_routing_team",
        when(
            (col("routing_team") == "vip_technical_team") & 
            (col("position_in_queue") > lit(team_capacity["vip_technical_team"])),
            lit("escalation_team_overflow")
        ).when(
            (col("routing_team") == "vip_general_team") & 
            (col("position_in_queue") > lit(team_capacity["vip_general_team"])),
            lit("escalation_team_overflow")
        ).otherwise(
            col("routing_team")
        )
    )
    
    print("\nFinal Routing After Capacity Check:")
    df_rerouted.select(
        "ticket_id", "routing_team", "position_in_queue", 
        "final_routing_team", "routing_priority"
    ).orderBy("routing_priority", "position_in_queue").show(truncate=False)
    
    # Summary of re-routing
    print("\nRe-routing Summary:")
    df_rerouted.groupBy("final_routing_team").count() \
        .orderBy("final_routing_team").show(truncate=False)
    
    spark.stop()

## Advanced Routing Pattern - Composite Example

```python
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, when, lit, expr, struct, array, explode
from pyspark.sql.types import *

def composite_routing_pattern():
    """
    Composite Routing Pattern:
    Combines multiple routing patterns for complex enterprise scenarios.
    Use case: E-commerce order processing with multiple routing strategies.
    """
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("CompositeRoutingPattern") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    # Sample data: E-commerce orders with rich attributes
    data = [
        ("ORD001", "CUST001", "Electronics", 1500.00, "US", "CA", "Premium", "Standard", 5, True, "2024-01-15 10:00:00"),
        ("ORD002", "CUST002", "Clothing", 250.00, "US", "NY", "Standard", "Express", 2, False, "2024-01-15 14:30:00"),
        ("ORD003", "CUST003", "Electronics", 5000.00, "UK", "London", "VIP", "Same-Day", 1, True, "2024-01-15 09:00:00"),
        ("ORD004", "CUST004", "Food", 50.00, "US", "TX", "Standard", "Standard", 10, False, "2024-01-15 22:00:00"),
        ("ORD005", "CUST005", "Furniture", 3000.00, "CA", "Toronto", "Premium", "Express", 3, True, "2024-01-15 11:00:00"),
        ("ORD006", "CUST006", "Electronics", 800.00, "US", "FL", "Standard", "Standard", 4, False, "2024-01-15 16:00:00"),
        ("ORD007", "CUST007", "Jewelry", 10000.00, "US", "NY", "VIP", "Same-Day", 1, True, "2024-01-15 13:00:00"),
    ]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("order_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("customer_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("category", StringType(), True),
        StructField("order_value", DoubleType(), True),
        StructField("country", StringType(), True),
        StructField("region", StringType(), True),
        StructField("customer_tier", StringType(), True),
        StructField("shipping_method", StringType(), True),
        StructField("item_count", IntegerType(), True),
        StructField("requires_verification", BooleanType(), True),
        StructField("order_timestamp", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
    
    from pyspark.sql.functions import to_timestamp, hour
    df = df.withColumn("order_timestamp", to_timestamp(col("order_timestamp")))
    df = df.withColumn("hour_of_day", hour(col("order_timestamp")))
    
    print("=" * 80)
    print("COMPOSITE ROUTING PATTERN - Combining Multiple Strategies")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Step 1: Content-Based Primary Routing
    df_routed = df.withColumn(
        "primary_route",
        when(
            (col("category") == "Electronics") & (col("order_value") >= 1000),
            lit("premium_electronics_fulfillment")
        ).when(
            col("category") == "Jewelry",
            lit("high_security_fulfillment")
        ).when(
            col("category") == "Food",
            lit("perishable_goods_fulfillment")
        ).when(
            col("category") == "Furniture",
            lit("large_items_fulfillment")
        ).otherwise(
            lit("standard_fulfillment")
        )
    )
    
    # Step 2: Rule-Based Secondary Routing (Geographic)
    df_routed = df_routed.withColumn(
        "geographic_route",
        when(col("country") == "US", 
             when(col("region").isin(["CA", "WA", "OR"]), lit("west_coast_dc"))
             .when(col("region").isin(["NY", "NJ", "MA"]), lit("east_coast_dc"))
             .when(col("region").isin(["TX", "AZ", "NM"]), lit("south_west_dc"))
             .otherwise(lit("central_dc"))
        ).when(col("country") == "UK", lit("uk_dc"))
        .when(col("country") == "CA", lit("canada_dc"))
        .otherwise(lit("international_dc"))
    )
    
    # Step 3: Dynamic Routing (Time-based and Load-based)
    df_routed = df_routed.withColumn(
        "processing_shift",
        when(col("hour_of_day").between(6, 14), lit("morning_shift"))
        .when(col("hour_of_day").between(14, 22), lit("afternoon_shift"))
        .otherwise(lit("night_shift"))
    )
    
    # Step 4: Multi-Cast Routing (Parallel notifications)
    def get_notification_destinations(customer_tier, order_value, requires_verification, shipping_method):
        """Determine all systems that need to be notified"""
        destinations = []
        
        # Always notify these systems
        destinations.append("inventory_system")
        destinations.append("shipping_system")
        
        # Conditional notifications
        if customer_tier in ["Premium", "VIP"]:
            destinations.append("vip_service_system")
        
        if order_value > 1000:
            destinations.append("fraud_detection_system")
            destinations.append("finance_approval_system")
        
        if requires_verification:
            destinations.append("verification_system")
        
        if shipping_method in ["Express", "Same-Day"]:
            destinations.append("priority_shipping_system")
        
        destinations.append("analytics_system")
        
        return destinations
    
    notification_udf = udf(get_notification_destinations, ArrayType(StringType()))
    
    df_routed = df_routed.withColumn(
        "notification_destinations",
        notification_udf(
            col("customer_tier"),
            col("order_value"),
            col("requires_verification"),
            col("shipping_method")
        )
    )
    
    # Step 5: Conditional Routing (Priority and SLA)
    df_routed = df_routed.withColumn(
        "priority_level",
        when(
            (col("customer_tier") == "VIP") & (col("shipping_method") == "Same-Day"),
            lit(1)
        ).when(
            (col("customer_tier") == "VIP") | (col("shipping_method") == "Same-Day"),
            lit(2)
        ).when(
            (col("customer_tier") == "Premium") | (col("shipping_method") == "Express"),
            lit(3)
        ).when(
            col("order_value") > 1000,
            lit(4)
        ).otherwise(
            lit(5)
        )
    )
    
    df_routed = df_routed.withColumn(
        "sla_hours",
        when(col("priority_level") == 1, lit(2))
        .when(col("priority_level") == 2, lit(4))
        .when(col("priority_level") == 3, lit(8))
        .when(col("priority_level") == 4, lit(24))
        .otherwise(lit(48))
    )
    
    # Step 6: Create composite routing decision
    df_routed = df_routed.withColumn(
        "routing_decision",
        struct(
            col("primary_route").alias("fulfillment_center"),
            col("geographic_route").alias("distribution_center"),
            col("processing_shift").alias("shift"),
            col("priority_level").alias("priority"),
            col("sla_hours").alias("sla"),
            col("notification_destinations").alias("notifications")
        )
    )
    
    # Display results
    print("\nComposite Routing Decisions:")
    df_routed.select(
        "order_id",
        "category",
        "customer_tier",
        "order_value",
        "country",
        "routing_decision.fulfillment_center",
        "routing_decision.distribution_center",
        "routing_decision.priority",
        "routing_decision.sla"
    ).show(truncate=False)
    
    # Show multi-cast destinations
    print("\nMulti-Cast Notification Destinations:")
    df_routed.select(
        "order_id",
        "notification_destinations"
    ).show(truncate=False)
    
    # Explode notifications for detailed view
    df_notifications = df_routed.select(
        "order_id",
        explode(col("notification_destinations")).alias("destination_system")
    )
    
    print("\nNotification Workload by System:")
    df_notifications.groupBy("destination_system").count() \
        .orderBy(col("count").desc()).show(truncate=False)
    
    # Routing statistics
    print("\nRouting Statistics by Priority:")
    df_routed.groupBy("priority_level", "primary_route") \
        .count() \
        .orderBy("priority_level") \
        .show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\nGeographic Distribution:")
    df_routed.groupBy("geographic_route", "processing_shift") \
        .count() \
        .orderBy("geographic_route") \
        .show(truncate=False)
    
    # Save routing decisions to different outputs
    print("\nSaving Routing Decisions...")
    
    # High priority orders
    high_priority = df_routed.filter(col("priority_level") <= 2)
    print(f"High Priority Orders: {high_priority.count()}")
    # high_priority.write.mode("overwrite").parquet("/tmp/routing/high_priority")
    
    # By fulfillment center
    fulfillment_centers = df_routed.select("primary_route").distinct().collect()
    for fc_row in fulfillment_centers:
        fc_name = fc_row["primary_route"]
        fc_orders = df_routed.filter(col("primary_route") == fc_name)
        print(f"Orders for {fc_name}: {fc_orders.count()}")
        # fc_orders.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(f"/tmp/routing/{fc_name}")
    
    spark.stop()

## Utility Functions for Routing Patterns

```python
from pyspark.sql import DataFrame
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, lit, when
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

class RoutingPatternUtils:
    """
    Utility class for common routing pattern operations
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_routing_metrics(df: DataFrame, routing_column: str) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Create routing metrics and statistics
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            routing_column: Column name containing routing decisions
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with routing metrics
        """
        metrics = df.groupBy(routing_column) \
            .agg(
                {"*": "count"}
            ) \
            .withColumnRenamed("count(1)", "record_count")
        
        # Calculate percentages
        total_count = df.count()
        metrics = metrics.withColumn(
            "percentage",
            (col("record_count") / lit(total_count) * 100)
        )
        
        return metrics.orderBy(col("record_count").desc())
    
    @staticmethod
    def validate_routing_coverage(df: DataFrame, routing_column: str) -> Dict:
        """
        Validate that all records have been routed
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            routing_column: Column name containing routing decisions
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with validation results
        """
        total_records = df.count()
        routed_records = df.filter(col(routing_column).isNotNull()).count()
        unrouted_records = df.filter(col(routing_column).isNull()).count()
        
        return {
            "total_records": total_records,
            "routed_records": routed_records,
            "unrouted_records": unrouted_records,
            "coverage_percentage": (routed_records / total_records * 100) if total_records > 0 else 0,
            "is_complete": unrouted_records == 0
        }
    
    @staticmethod
    def apply_fallback_routing(df: DataFrame, 
                               routing_column: str, 
                               fallback_route: str) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Apply fallback routing for unrouted records
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            routing_column: Column name containing routing decisions
            fallback_route: Default route for unrouted records
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with fallback routing applied
        """
        return df.withColumn(
            routing_column,
            when(col(routing_column).isNull(), lit(fallback_route))
            .otherwise(col(routing_column))
        )
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_routing_audit_trail(df: DataFrame,
                                   routing_column: str,
                                   reason_column: str = "routing_reason") -> DataFrame:
        """
        Create audit trail for routing decisions
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            routing_column: Column name containing routing decisions
            reason_column: Column name for routing reason
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with audit trail
        """
        from pyspark.sql.functions import current_timestamp, monotonically_increasing_id
        
        audit_df = df.withColumn("routing_timestamp", current_timestamp()) \
            .withColumn("routing_id", monotonically_increasing_id()) \
            .select(
                "routing_id",
                routing_column,
                reason_column,
                "routing_timestamp"
            )
        
        return audit_df
    
    @staticmethod
    def balance_load_across_routes(df: DataFrame,
                                   routing_column: str,
                                   available_routes: List[str],
                                   max_capacity_per_route: int = None) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Balance load across multiple routes based on capacity
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            routing_column: Column name containing routing decisions
            available_routes: List of available routes
            max_capacity_per_route: Maximum records per route
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with balanced routing
        """
        from pyspark.sql.window import Window
        from pyspark.sql.functions import row_number, expr
        
        if max_capacity_per_route is None:
            # Distribute evenly
            total_records = df.count()
            max
```python
_capacity_per_route = (total_records // len(available_routes)) + 1
        
        # Add row number within each route
        window_spec = Window.partitionBy(routing_column).orderBy(col(routing_column))
        df_balanced = df.withColumn("route_position", row_number().over(window_spec))
        
        # Re-route if over capacity
        route_conditions = None
        for i, route in enumerate(available_routes):
            overflow_route = available_routes[(i + 1) % len(available_routes)]
            
            condition = when(
                (col(routing_column) == route) & 
                (col("route_position") > max_capacity_per_route),
                lit(overflow_route)
            )
            
            if route_conditions is None:
                route_conditions = condition
            else:
                route_conditions = route_conditions.when(
                    (col(routing_column) == route) & 
                    (col("route_position") > max_capacity_per_route),
                    lit(overflow_route)
                )
        
        df_balanced = df_balanced.withColumn(
            f"{routing_column}_balanced",
            route_conditions.otherwise(col(routing_column))
        ).drop("route_position")
        
        return df_balanced
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_routing_report(df: DataFrame,
                             routing_column: str,
                             group_by_columns: List[str] = None) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Create comprehensive routing report
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            routing_column: Column name containing routing decisions
            group_by_columns: Additional columns to group by
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with routing report
        """
        from pyspark.sql.functions import count, avg, min, max, sum as spark_sum
        
        if group_by_columns is None:
            group_by_columns = [routing_column]
        elif routing_column not in group_by_columns:
            group_by_columns.append(routing_column)
        
        report = df.groupBy(*group_by_columns).agg(
            count("*").alias("total_records"),
        )
        
        return report.orderBy(*group_by_columns)


def demonstrate_routing_utils():
    """
    Demonstrate the usage of routing utility functions
    """
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("RoutingUtilsDemo") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    # Sample data
    data = [
        ("REC001", "route_a", "content_based", 100),
        ("REC002", "route_b", "rule_based", 200),
        ("REC003", "route_a", "content_based", 150),
        ("REC004", None, None, 300),  # Unrouted
        ("REC005", "route_c", "dynamic", 250),
        ("REC006", "route_a", "content_based", 120),
        ("REC007", "route_b", "rule_based", 180),
        ("REC008", None, None, 400),  # Unrouted
    ]
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(data, 
        ["record_id", "routing_destination", "routing_reason", "value"])
    
    utils = RoutingPatternUtils()
    
    print("=" * 80)
    print("ROUTING PATTERN UTILITIES DEMONSTRATION")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # 1. Routing Metrics
    print("\n1. Routing Metrics:")
    metrics = utils.create_routing_metrics(df, "routing_destination")
    metrics.show()
    
    # 2. Validate Coverage
    print("\n2. Routing Coverage Validation:")
    validation = utils.validate_routing_coverage(df, "routing_destination")
    for key, value in validation.items():
        print(f"  {key}: {value}")
    
    # 3. Apply Fallback
    print("\n3. Applying Fallback Routing:")
    df_with_fallback = utils.apply_fallback_routing(df, "routing_destination", "fallback_route")
    df_with_fallback.show()
    
    # 4. Audit Trail
    print("\n4. Routing Audit Trail:")
    audit = utils.create_routing_audit_trail(df_with_fallback, "routing_destination")
    audit.show()
    
    # 5. Load Balancing
    print("\n5. Load Balanced Routing:")
    available_routes = ["route_a", "route_b", "route_c", "fallback_route"]
    df_balanced = utils.balance_load_across_routes(
        df_with_fallback, 
        "routing_destination", 
        available_routes, 
        max_capacity_per_route=2
    )
    df_balanced.show()
    
    # 6. Routing Report
    print("\n6. Comprehensive Routing Report:")
    report = utils.create_routing_report(
        df_balanced, 
        "routing_destination_balanced",
        group_by_columns=["routing_reason"]
    )
    report.show()
    
    spark.stop()

## Performance Optimization for Routing Patterns

```python
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, DataFrame
from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast, col
from typing import Dict, List

class RoutingPatternOptimizer:
    """
    Performance optimization techniques for routing patterns
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
    
    def optimize_rule_based_routing(self, 
                                    data_df: DataFrame,
                                    rules_df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Optimize rule-based routing using broadcast joins
        
        Args:
            data_df: Main data DataFrame
            rules_df: Rules DataFrame (should be small)
            
        Returns:
            Optimized routed DataFrame
        """
        # Use broadcast join for small rules table
        if rules_df.count() < 10000:  # Threshold for broadcast
            print("Using broadcast join for rules...")
            routed_df = data_df.join(
                broadcast(rules_df),
                on=["category"],  # Join condition
                how="left"
            )
        else:
            routed_df = data_df.join(rules_df, on=["category"], how="left")
        
        return routed_df
    
    def partition_by_route(self,
                          df: DataFrame,
                          routing_column: str,
                          num_partitions: int = None) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Partition data by routing destination for better performance
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            routing_column: Column to partition by
            num_partitions: Number of partitions (default: auto)
            
        Returns:
            Repartitioned DataFrame
        """
        if num_partitions:
            return df.repartition(num_partitions, routing_column)
        else:
            return df.repartition(routing_column)
    
    def cache_routing_decisions(self,
                               df: DataFrame,
                               routing_column: str) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Cache routing decisions for reuse
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            routing_column: Routing decision column
            
        Returns:
            Cached DataFrame
        """
        # Cache if DataFrame will be reused multiple times
        df_cached = df.select("*").cache()
        
        # Trigger action to materialize cache
        route_count = df_cached.select(routing_column).distinct().count()
        print(f"Cached {df_cached.count()} records with {route_count} distinct routes")
        
        return df_cached
    
    def optimize_multicast_routing(self,
                                   df: DataFrame,
                                   destination_column: str) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Optimize multi-cast routing using array operations
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            destination_column: Column containing array of destinations
            
        Returns:
            Optimized DataFrame
        """
        from pyspark.sql.functions import size, array_contains
        
        # Add metadata for optimization
        df_optimized = df.withColumn(
            "destination_count",
            size(col(destination_column))
        )
        
        # Filter for specific destinations without exploding
        # This is more efficient than exploding for filtering
        return df_optimized
    
    def batch_routing_decisions(self,
                               df: DataFrame,
                               batch_size: int = 1000) -> List[DataFrame]:
        """
        Process routing in batches for very large datasets
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            batch_size: Records per batch
            
        Returns:
            List of batch DataFrames
        """
        from pyspark.sql.functions import monotonically_increasing_id
        
        # Add batch ID
        df_with_batch = df.withColumn("row_id", monotonically_increasing_id())
        df_with_batch = df_with_batch.withColumn(
            "batch_id",
            (col("row_id") / batch_size).cast("int")
        )
        
        # Get distinct batch IDs
        batch_ids = [row.batch_id for row in 
                    df_with_batch.select("batch_id").distinct().collect()]
        
        # Create list of batch DataFrames
        batches = []
        for batch_id in batch_ids:
            batch_df = df_with_batch.filter(col("batch_id") == batch_id)
            batches.append(batch_df)
        
        return batches


def demonstrate_routing_optimization():
    """
    Demonstrate routing optimization techniques
    """
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("RoutingOptimizationDemo") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .config("spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold", "10485760") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    # Create sample data
    from pyspark.sql.functions import rand, when, array, lit
    
    # Large dataset
    df = spark.range(0, 10000).select(
        col("id").alias("record_id"),
        (rand() * 100).cast("int").alias("value"),
        when(col("id") % 4 == 0, lit("Electronics"))
        .when(col("id") % 4 == 1, lit("Clothing"))
        .when(col("id") % 4 == 2, lit("Food"))
        .otherwise(lit("Other")).alias("category")
    )
    
    # Small rules table
    rules_data = [
        ("Electronics", "tech_warehouse", 1),
        ("Clothing", "fashion_warehouse", 2),
        ("Food", "fresh_warehouse", 3),
        ("Other", "general_warehouse", 4)
    ]
    
    rules_df = spark.createDataFrame(rules_data, 
        ["category", "warehouse", "priority"])
    
    optimizer = RoutingPatternOptimizer(spark)
    
    print("=" * 80)
    print("ROUTING PATTERN OPTIMIZATION DEMONSTRATION")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # 1. Optimized Rule-Based Routing
    print("\n1. Optimized Rule-Based Routing with Broadcast Join:")
    import time
    start_time = time.time()
    
    routed_df = optimizer.optimize_rule_based_routing(df, rules_df)
    routed_count = routed_df.count()
    
    end_time = time.time()
    print(f"Routed {routed_count} records in {end_time - start_time:.2f} seconds")
    routed_df.show(5)
    
    # 2. Partitioning by Route
    print("\n2. Partitioning by Routing Destination:")
    partitioned_df = optimizer.partition_by_route(routed_df, "warehouse", num_partitions=4)
    print(f"Number of partitions: {partitioned_df.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    # 3. Caching Routing Decisions
    print("\n3. Caching Routing Decisions:")
    cached_df = optimizer.cache_routing_decisions(routed_df, "warehouse")
    
    # Demonstrate cache benefit
    start_time = time.time()
    count1 = cached_df.filter(col("warehouse") == "tech_warehouse").count()
    time1 = time.time() - start_time
    
    start_time = time.time()
    count2 = cached_df.filter(col("warehouse") == "fashion_warehouse").count()
    time2 = time.time() - start_time
    
    print(f"First query: {count1} records in {time1:.4f} seconds")
    print(f"Second query: {count2} records in {time2:.4f} seconds (cached)")
    
    # 4. Multi-cast Optimization
    print("\n4. Multi-cast Routing Optimization:")
    df_multicast = df.withColumn(
        "destinations",
        array(lit("inventory"), lit("analytics"), lit("warehouse"))
    )
    
    optimized_multicast = optimizer.optimize_multicast_routing(df_multicast, "destinations")
    optimized_multicast.show(5)
    
    # 5. Batch Processing
    print("\n5. Batch Processing for Large Datasets:")
    batches = optimizer.batch_routing_decisions(df, batch_size=2000)
    print(f"Created {len(batches)} batches")
    
    for i, batch in enumerate(batches[:3]):  # Show first 3 batches
        print(f"Batch {i}: {batch.count()} records")
    
    # Cleanup
    cached_df.unpersist()
    spark.stop()

# Additional Helper Functions

def save_routing_results(df: DataFrame, 
                        routing_column: str, 
                        base_path: str,
                        format: str = "parquet"):
    """
    Save routing results to separate files by destination
    
    Args:
        df: Routed DataFrame
        routing_column: Column containing routing destinations
        base_path: Base output path
        format: Output format (parquet, csv, json)
    """
    from pyspark.sql.functions import col
    
    # Get distinct routes
    routes = df.select(routing_column).distinct().collect()
    
    for route_row in routes:
        route = route_row[routing_column]
        if route is not None:
            route_df = df.filter(col(routing_column) == route)
            output_path = f"{base_path}/{route}"
            
            if format == "parquet":
                route_df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(output_path)
            elif format == "csv":
                route_df.write.mode("overwrite").csv(output_path, header=True)
            elif format == "json":
                route_df.write.mode("overwrite").json(output_path)
            
            print(f"Saved {route_df.count()} records to {output_path}")


def create_routing_dashboard_data(df: DataFrame, 
                                  routing_column: str) -> Dict:
    """
    Create aggregated data for routing dashboard
    
    Args:
        df: Routed DataFrame
        routing_column: Column containing routing destinations
        
    Returns:
        Dictionary with dashboard metrics
    """
    from pyspark.sql.functions import count, avg, min, max, current_timestamp
    
    # Overall metrics
    total_records = df.count()
    distinct_routes = df.select(routing_column).distinct().count()
    
    # Per-route metrics
    route_metrics = df.groupBy(routing_column).agg(
        count("*").alias("record_count")
    ).collect()
    
    # Build dashboard data
    dashboard = {
        "timestamp": str(current_timestamp()),
        "total_records": total_records,
        "distinct_routes": distinct_routes,
        "routes": []
    }
    
    for row in route_metrics:
        route_info = {
            "route": row[routing_column],
            "count": row["record_count"],
            "percentage": (row["record_count"] / total_records * 100) if total_records > 0 else 0
        }
        dashboard["routes"].append(route_info)
    
    return dashboard


def monitor_routing_performance(df: DataFrame,
                               routing_column: str,
                               threshold_percentage: float = 10.0) -> Dict:
    """
    Monitor routing performance and detect imbalances
    
    Args:
        df: Routed DataFrame
        routing_column: Column containing routing destinations
        threshold_percentage: Threshold for imbalance detection
        
    Returns:
        Dictionary with performance metrics and alerts
    """
    from pyspark.sql.functions import count
    
    total_records = df.count()
    route_counts = df.groupBy(routing_column).agg(
        count("*").alias("count")
    ).collect()
    
    # Calculate expected even distribution
    num_routes = len(route_counts)
    expected_per_route = total_records / num_routes if num_routes > 0 else 0
    
    alerts = []
    metrics = {
        "total_records": total_records,
        "num_routes": num_routes,
        "expected_per_route": expected_per_route,
        "routes": [],
        "alerts": []
    }
    
    for row in route_counts:
        route = row[routing_column]
        count_val = row["count"]
        percentage = (count_val / total_records * 100) if total_records > 0 else 0
        deviation = abs(count_val - expected_per_route) / expected_per_route * 100 if expected_per_route > 0 else 0
        
        route_metric = {
            "route": route,
            "count": count_val,
            "percentage": percentage,
            "deviation": deviation
        }
        metrics["routes"].append(route_metric)
        
        # Check for imbalances
        if deviation > threshold_percentage:
            alert = {
                "type": "IMBALANCE",
                "route": route,
                "deviation": deviation,
                "message": f"Route {route} has {deviation:.1f}% deviation from expected distribution"
            }
            alerts.append(alert)
    
    metrics["alerts"] = alerts
    
    return metrics

    Route data to different REST API endpoints based on routing decisions

    import json

            endpoint = api_endpoints[route]
            # In production: requests.post(endpoint, json=record_json)
            return f"Sent to {endpoint}"
        return "No endpoint configured"
    
    send_udf = udf(send_to_api, StringType())
    
    # Convert records to JSON and send
    df_json = df.withColumn(
        "record_json",
        to_json(struct([col(c) for c in df.columns if c != routing_column]))
    )
    
    df_result = df_json.withColumn(

        send_udf(col(routing_column), col("record_json"))
    )
    
    print("\nAPI Integration Results:")
    df_result.select(routing_column, "api_response").show(5, truncate=False)
    
    return df_result
