# 3. THRESHOLD NOTIFICATION PATTERN
# Detects and notifies when metrics cross defined thresholds
# ============================================================================

class ThresholdNotificationPattern:
    """
    Monitors metrics and triggers notifications when thresholds are exceeded.
    Use Case: Performance monitoring, resource alerts, KPI tracking
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    def create_sample_metrics_data(self):
        """Create sample metrics data"""
        data = [
            ("server_01", "CPU", 45.0, "2024-01-15 10:00:00"),
            ("server_01", "MEMORY", 75.0, "2024-01-15 10:00:00"),
            ("server_01", "DISK", 92.0, "2024-01-15 10:00:00"),
            ("server_02", "CPU", 88.0, "2024-01-15 10:00:00"),
            ("server_02", "MEMORY", 65.0, "2024-01-15 10:00:00"),
            ("server_02", "DISK", 45.0, "2024-01-15 10:00:00"),
            ("server_03", "CPU", 55.0, "2024-01-15 10:00:00"),
            ("server_03", "MEMORY", 95.0, "2024-01-15 10:00:00"),
            ("server_03", "DISK", 78.0, "2024-01-15 10:00:00"),
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("resource_id", StringType(), True),
            StructField("metric_name", StringType(), True),
            StructField("metric_value", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("timestamp", StringType(), True)
        ])
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
    
    def define_thresholds(self):
        """Define threshold rules for different metrics"""
        threshold_data = [
            ("CPU", 80.0, "WARNING", 90.0, "CRITICAL"),
            ("MEMORY", 70.0, "WARNING", 85.0, "CRITICAL"),
            ("DISK", 75.0, "WARNING", 90.0, "CRITICAL"),
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("metric_name", StringType(), True),
            StructField("warning_threshold", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("warning_level", StringType(), True),
            StructField("critical_threshold", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("critical_level", StringType(), True)
        ])
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(threshold_data, schema)
    
    def check_thresholds(self, metrics_df, thresholds_df):
        """
        Check metrics against thresholds and generate notifications
        
        Args:
            metrics_df: DataFrame with metric values
            thresholds_df: DataFrame with threshold definitions
        """
        # Join metrics with thresholds
        metrics_with_thresholds = metrics_df.join(
            thresholds_df,
            on="metric_name",
            how="inner"
        )
        
        # Determine alert level
        alerts = metrics_with_thresholds.withColumn(
            "alert_level",
            when(col("metric_value") >= col("critical_threshold"), "CRITICAL")
            .when(col("metric_value") >= col("warning_threshold"), "WARNING")
            .otherwise("NORMAL")
        ).withColumn(
            "threshold_exceeded",
            when(col("metric_value") >= col("critical_threshold"), col("critical_threshold"))
            .when(col("metric_value") >= col("warning_threshold"), col("warning_threshold"))
            .otherwise(None)
        )
        
        # Filter only alerts (WARNING or CRITICAL)
        notifications = alerts.filter(col("alert_level") != "NORMAL")
        
        # Add notification details
        notifications = notifications.withColumn(
            "notification_id", monotonically_increasing_id()
        ).withColumn(
            "notification_type", lit("THRESHOLD_EXCEEDED")
        ).withColumn(
            "notification_timestamp", current_timestamp()
        ).withColumn(
            "message",
            concat(
                col("alert_level"),
                lit(" alert: "),
                col("metric_name"),
                lit(" on "),
                col("resource_id"),
                lit(" is at "),
                col("metric_value"),
                lit("% (threshold: "),
                col("threshold_exceeded"),
                lit("%)")
            )
        ).withColumn(
            "percentage_over_threshold",
            round(((col("metric_value") - col("threshold_exceeded")) / 
                   col("threshold_exceeded")) * 100, 2)
        )
        
        return notifications
    
    def run_example(self):
        """Run Threshold Notification Pattern example"""
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
```python
        print("3. THRESHOLD NOTIFICATION PATTERN")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # Create sample data
        metrics_df = self.create_sample_metrics_data()
        thresholds_df = self.define_thresholds()
        
        print("\nSample Metrics Data:")
        metrics_df.show(truncate=False)
        
        print("\nDefined Thresholds:")
        thresholds_df.show(truncate=False)
        
        # Check thresholds and generate notifications
        notifications = self.check_thresholds(metrics_df, thresholds_df)
        
        print("\nThreshold Notifications:")
        notifications.select(
            "notification_id", "resource_id", "metric_name", "metric_value",
            "threshold_exceeded", "alert_level", "percentage_over_threshold", "message"
        ).orderBy(col("alert_level").desc(), col("metric_value").desc()).show(truncate=False)
        
        # Summary by alert level
        print("\nAlert Summary by Level:")
        notifications.groupBy("alert_level").agg(
            count("*").alias("alert_count"),
            avg("metric_value").alias("avg_metric_value"),
            max("metric_value").alias("max_metric_value")
        ).show(truncate=False)
        
        return notifications


# ============================================================================
# 4. COMPLETION NOTIFICATION PATTERN
# Detects and notifies when processes or tasks complete
# ============================================================================

class CompletionNotificationPattern:
    """
    Monitors task/job completion and generates notifications.
    Use Case: ETL job completion, batch processing, workflow completion
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    def create_sample_job_data(self):
        """Create sample job execution data"""
        data = [
            ("job_001", "ETL_Daily_Load", "2024-01-15 08:00:00", "2024-01-15 09:30:00", 
             "COMPLETED", 1000000, 0, 5400),
            ("job_002", "Data_Validation", "2024-01-15 09:00:00", "2024-01-15 09:15:00", 
             "COMPLETED", 500000, 100, 900),
            ("job_003", "Report_Generation", "2024-01-15 10:00:00", "2024-01-15 10:45:00", 
             "COMPLETED", 250000, 0, 2700),
            ("job_004", "Data_Export", "2024-01-15 11:00:00", "2024-01-15 11:20:00", 
             "COMPLETED", 750000, 50, 1200),
            ("job_005", "ML_Model_Training", "2024-01-15 12:00:00", "2024-01-15 14:30:00", 
             "COMPLETED", 2000000, 0, 9000),
            ("job_006", "Data_Cleanup", "2024-01-15 13:00:00", "2024-01-15 13:10:00", 
             "FAILED", 0, 10000, 600),
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("job_id", StringType(), True),
            StructField("job_name", StringType(), True),
            StructField("start_time", StringType(), True),
            StructField("end_time", StringType(), True),
            StructField("status", StringType(), True),
            StructField("records_processed", LongType(), True),
            StructField("records_failed", LongType(), True),
            StructField("duration_seconds", IntegerType(), True)
        ])
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
    
    def generate_completion_notifications(self, jobs_df):
        """
        Generate completion notifications for finished jobs
        
        Args:
            jobs_df: DataFrame with job execution data
        """
        # Calculate success rate and performance metrics
        notifications = jobs_df.withColumn(
            "success_rate",
            round((col("records_processed") / 
                   (col("records_processed") + col("records_failed")) * 100), 2)
        ).withColumn(
            "duration_minutes",
            round(col("duration_seconds") / 60, 2)
        ).withColumn(
            "records_per_second",
            round(col("records_processed") / col("duration_seconds"), 2)
        ).withColumn(
            "notification_id", monotonically_increasing_id()
        ).withColumn(
            "notification_type", lit("JOB_COMPLETION")
        ).withColumn(
            "notification_timestamp", current_timestamp()
        ).withColumn(
            "severity",
            when(col("status") == "FAILED", "HIGH")
            .when(col("records_failed") > 0, "MEDIUM")
            .otherwise("LOW")
        ).withColumn(
            "message",
            concat(
                lit("Job "),
                col("job_name"),
                lit(" ("),
                col("job_id"),
                lit(") completed with status: "),
                col("status"),
                lit(". Processed "),
                col("records_processed"),
                lit(" records in "),
                col("duration_minutes"),
                lit(" minutes.")
            )
        )
        
        # Add SLA compliance check (example: jobs should complete in < 60 minutes)
        notifications = notifications.withColumn(
            "sla_compliant",
            when(col("duration_minutes") <= 60, "YES").otherwise("NO")
        ).withColumn(
            "completion_category",
            when(col("status") == "FAILED", "FAILED")
            .when(col("sla_compliant") == "NO", "SLA_BREACH")
            .when(col("records_failed") > 0, "COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS")
            .otherwise("SUCCESS")
        )
        
        return notifications
    
    def run_example(self):
        """Run Completion Notification Pattern example"""
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("4. COMPLETION NOTIFICATION PATTERN")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # Create sample job data
        jobs_df = self.create_sample_job_data()
        
        print("\nSample Job Execution Data:")
        jobs_df.show(truncate=False)
        
        # Generate completion notifications
        notifications = self.generate_completion_notifications(jobs_df)
        
        print("\nJob Completion Notifications:")
        notifications.select(
            "notification_id", "job_name", "status", "completion_category",
            "duration_minutes", "records_processed", "records_failed",
            "success_rate", "sla_compliant", "severity"
        ).show(truncate=False)
        
        print("\nDetailed Notification Messages:")
        notifications.select("job_id", "message").show(truncate=False)
        
        # Summary by completion category
        print("\nCompletion Summary by Category:")
        notifications.groupBy("completion_category").agg(
            count("*").alias("job_count"),
            avg("duration_minutes").alias("avg_duration_minutes"),
            sum("records_processed").alias("total_records_processed"),
            sum("records_failed").alias("total_records_failed")
        ).show(truncate=False)
        
        # Performance metrics
        print("\nPerformance Metrics:")
        notifications.select(
            "job_name", "records_per_second", "duration_minutes"
        ).orderBy(col("records_per_second").desc()).show(truncate=False)
        
        return notifications

# 5. ERROR NOTIFICATION PATTERN
# Detects and notifies when errors occur in data processing
# ============================================================================

class ErrorNotificationPattern:
    """
    Monitors for errors and generates detailed error notifications.
    Use Case: Exception handling, data quality issues, system failures
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    def create_sample_error_data(self):
        """Create sample error/exception data"""
        data = [
            ("ERR_001", "2024-01-15 10:00:00", "DATA_VALIDATION", "NULL_VALUE_ERROR", 
             "customer_table", "email", "Email field contains null values", "HIGH", "data_pipeline_01"),
            ("ERR_002", "2024-01-15 10:05:00", "DATABASE_CONNECTION", "CONNECTION_TIMEOUT", 
             "postgres_db", "connection", "Database connection timeout after 30s", "CRITICAL", "data_pipeline_01"),
            ("ERR_003", "2024-01-15 10:10:00", "DATA_TYPE", "TYPE_MISMATCH", 
             "sales_table", "amount", "Expected numeric, got string value", "MEDIUM", "data_pipeline_02"),
            ("ERR_004", "2024-01-15 10:15:00", "FILE_PROCESSING", "FILE_NOT_FOUND", 
             "s3://bucket/data", "input_file.csv", "Source file not found", "HIGH", "data_pipeline_03"),
            ("ERR_005", "2024-01-15 10:20:00", "DATA_VALIDATION", "DUPLICATE_KEY", 
             "user_table", "user_id", "Duplicate primary key detected", "MEDIUM", "data_pipeline_01"),
            ("ERR_006", "2024-01-15 10:25:00", "TRANSFORMATION", "DIVISION_BY_ZERO", 
             "metrics_calculation", "revenue_per_user", "Division by zero in calculation", "LOW", "data_pipeline_02"),
            ("ERR_007", "2024-01-15 10:30:00", "MEMORY", "OUT_OF_MEMORY", 
             "spark_executor", "executor_01", "Executor ran out of memory", "CRITICAL", "data_pipeline_04"),
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("error_id", StringType(), True),
            StructField("timestamp", StringType(), True),
            StructField("error_category", StringType(), True),
            StructField("error_type", StringType(), True),
            StructField("source_component", StringType(), True),
            StructField("affected_field", StringType(), True),
            StructField("error_message", StringType(), True),
            StructField("severity", StringType(), True),
            StructField("pipeline_id", StringType(), True)
        ])
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
    
    def generate_error_notifications(self, errors_df):
        """
        Generate detailed error notifications with classification and recommendations
        
        Args:
            errors_df: DataFrame with error data
        """
        # Add notification metadata
        notifications = errors_df.withColumn(
            "notification_id", monotonically_increasing_id()
        ).withColumn(
            "notification_type", lit("ERROR_DETECTED")
        ).withColumn(
            "notification_timestamp", current_timestamp()
        ).withColumn(
            "requires_immediate_action",
            when(col("severity").isin(["CRITICAL", "HIGH"]), "YES").otherwise("NO")
        ).withColumn(
            "error_priority",
            when(col("severity") == "CRITICAL", 1)
            .when(col("severity") == "HIGH", 2)
            .when(col("severity") == "MEDIUM", 3)
            .otherwise(4)
        )
        
        # Add recommended actions based on error type
        notifications = notifications.withColumn(
            "recommended_action",
            when(col("error_type") == "CONNECTION_TIMEOUT", 
                 "Check database connectivity and increase timeout settings")
            .when(col("error_type") == "NULL_VALUE_ERROR", 
                  "Implement null value handling or data validation")
            .when(col("error_type") == "TYPE_MISMATCH", 
                  "Verify data type mappings and add type casting")
            .when(col("error_type") == "FILE_NOT_FOUND", 
                  "Verify file path and check file availability")
            .when(col("error_type") == "DUPLICATE_KEY", 
                  "Implement deduplication logic or check data source")
            .when(col("error_type") == "DIVISION_BY_ZERO", 
                  "Add zero-check validation before division operations")
            .when(col("error_type") == "OUT_OF_MEMORY", 
                  "Increase executor memory or optimize data processing")
            .otherwise("Review error details and consult documentation")
        ).withColumn(
            "detailed_notification",
            concat(
                lit("["),
                col("severity"),
                lit("] "),
                col("error_category"),
                lit(" Error in "),
                col("pipeline_id"),
                lit(": "),
                col("error_message"),
                lit(" (Component: "),
                col("source_component"),
                lit(", Field: "),
                col("affected_field"),
                lit(")")
            )
        )
        
        return notifications
    
    def analyze_error_patterns(self, notifications):
        """Analyze error patterns and generate insights"""
        
        # Error frequency by category
        error_by_category = notifications.groupBy("error_category").agg(
            count("*").alias("error_count"),
            collect_list("error_type").alias("error_types")
        ).withColumn(
            "unique_error_types", size(array_distinct(col("error_types")))
        )
        
        # Error frequency by severity
        error_by_severity = notifications.groupBy("severity").agg(
            count("*").alias("error_count")
        ).orderBy(col("error_count").desc())
        
        # Error frequency by pipeline
        error_by_pipeline = notifications.groupBy("pipeline_id").agg(
            count("*").alias("error_count"),
            collect_set("error_category").alias("error_categories")
        ).withColumn(
            "affected_categories", size(col("error_categories"))
        )
        
        # Critical errors requiring immediate attention
        critical_errors = notifications.filter(
            col("requires_immediate_action") == "YES"
        ).select(
            "error_id", "timestamp", "error_category", "error_type",
            "severity", "detailed_notification", "recommended_action"
        )
        
        return {
            "by_category": error_by_category,
            "by_severity": error_by_severity,
            "by_pipeline": error_by_pipeline,
            "critical_errors": critical_errors
        }
    
    def run_example(self):
        """Run Error Notification Pattern example"""
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("5. ERROR NOTIFICATION PATTERN")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # Create sample error data
        errors_df = self.create_sample_error_data()
        
        print("\nSample Error Data:")
        errors_df.show(truncate=False)
        
        # Generate error notifications
        notifications = self.generate_error_notifications(errors_df)
        
        print("\nError Notifications (Prioritized):")
        notifications.select(
            "notification_id", "error_id", "severity", "error_category",
            "error_type", "requires_immediate_action"
        ).orderBy("error_priority").show(truncate=False)
        
        print("\nDetailed Error Notifications:")
        notifications.select(
            "error_id", "detailed_notification"
        ).show(truncate=False)
        
        print("\nRecommended Actions:")
        notifications.select(
            "error_id", "error_type", "recommended_action"
        ).show(
```python
truncate=False)
        
        # Analyze error patterns
        analysis = self.analyze_error_patterns(notifications)
        
        print("\nError Analysis - By Category:")
        analysis["by_category"].show(truncate=False)
        
        print("\nError Analysis - By Severity:")
        analysis["by_severity"].show(truncate=False)
        
        print("\nError Analysis - By Pipeline:")
        analysis["by_pipeline"].show(truncate=False)
        
        print("\nCritical Errors Requiring Immediate Action:")
        analysis["critical_errors"].show(truncate=False)
        
        return notifications, analysis

def cascading_demo(spark):
    """
    Demonstrate cascading notifications - when one event triggers multiple notifications
    """
    # Simulate a cascading failure scenario
    data = [
        ("event_001", "DATABASE_SLOW", "2024-01-15 10:00:00", "database_01"),
        ("event_002", "QUERY_TIMEOUT", "2024-01-15 10:01:00", "app_server_01"),
        ("event_003", "CONNECTION_POOL_EXHAUSTED", "2024-01-15 10:02:00", "app_server_01"),
        ("event_004", "SERVICE_DEGRADED", "2024-01-15 10:03:00", "api_gateway"),
        ("event_005", "USER_REQUESTS_FAILING", "2024-01-15 10:04:00", "frontend"),
    ]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("event_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("event_type", StringType(), True),
        StructField("timestamp", StringType(), True),
        StructField("component", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    events_df = spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
    
    # Detect cascading pattern (events within 5 minutes)
    window_spec = Window.orderBy("timestamp")
    
    cascading = events_df.withColumn(
        "event_sequence", row_number().over(window_spec)
    ).withColumn(
        "is_cascading",
        when(col("event_sequence") > 1, "YES").otherwise("NO")
    ).withColumn(
        "cascade_severity",
        when(col("event_sequence") >= 4, "CRITICAL")
        .when(col("event_sequence") >= 2, "HIGH")
        .otherwise("MEDIUM")
    )
    
    print("Cascading Event Detection:")
    cascading.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Generate cascade alert
    if cascading.filter(col("is_cascading") == "YES").count() > 0:
        print("\n⚠️  CASCADE ALERT: Multiple related failures detected!")
        print("Recommended Action: Investigate root cause starting with earliest event")


def notification_aggregation_demo(spark, all_notifications):
    """
    Demonstrate notification aggregation over time windows
    """
    # Add time-based grouping
    aggregated = all_notifications.withColumn(
        "notification_hour", 
        lit("2024-01-15 10:00:00")  # Simplified for demo
    ).groupBy("notification_hour", "notification_category").agg(
        count("*").alias("notification_count"),
        collect_set("severity").alias("severity_levels"),
        count(when(col("severity").isin(["CRITICAL", "HIGH"]), 1)).alias("critical_count")
    ).withColumn(
        "aggregation_type",
        when(col("critical_count") > 3, "ALERT_STORM")
        .when(col("notification_count") > 5, "HIGH_VOLUME")
        .otherwise("NORMAL")
    )
    
    print("Hourly Notification Aggregation:")
    aggregated.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Alert on notification storms
    storms = aggregated.filter(col("aggregation_type") == "ALERT_STORM")
    if storms.count() > 0:
        print("\n⚠️  NOTIFICATION STORM DETECTED!")
        print("Consider suppressing duplicate notifications or investigating systemic issues")


def notification_routing_demo(spark, all_notifications):
    """
    Demonstrate smart notification routing based on severity and category
    """
    # Define routing rules
    routing_rules = [
        ("CRITICAL", "ERROR", "oncall_team@company.com", "SMS,Email,Slack"),
        ("CRITICAL", "THRESHOLD", "infrastructure_team@company.com", "Email,Slack"),
        ("HIGH", "ERROR", "dev_team@company.com", "Email,Slack"),
        ("HIGH", "COMPLETION", "data_engineering@company.com", "Email"),
        ("MEDIUM", "*", "monitoring_team@company.com", "Email"),
        ("LOW", "*", "monitoring_dashboard", "Dashboard"),
    ]
    
    routing_schema = StructType([
        StructField("severity", StringType(), True),
        StructField("category", StringType(), True),
        StructField("recipient", StringType(), True),
        StructField("channels", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    routing_df = spark.createDataFrame(routing_rules, routing_schema)
    
    # Apply routing rules
    routed = all_notifications.join(
        broadcast(routing_df),
        (all_notifications.severity == routing_df.severity) &
        ((routing_df.category == all_notifications.notification_category) | 
         (routing_df.category == "*")),
        "left"
    ).select(
        all_notifications["*"],
        routing_df["recipient"],
        routing_df["channels"]
    )
    
    print("Notification Routing Configuration:")
    routed.select(
        "notification_category", "severity", "recipient", "channels"
    ).distinct().orderBy("severity", "notification_category").show(truncate=False)

# ============================================================================
# PRODUCTION-READY NOTIFICATION MANAGER
# ============================================================================

class NotificationManager:
    """
    Production-ready notification manager with advanced features
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    def deduplicate_notifications(self, notifications_df, time_window_minutes=5):
        """
        Deduplicate notifications within a time window
        
        Args:
            notifications_df: DataFrame with notifications
            time_window_minutes: Time window for deduplication
        """
        # Create deduplication key
        dedup_df = notifications_df.withColumn(
            "dedup_key",
            concat(
                col("notification_category"),
                lit("_"),
                col("severity"),
                lit("_"),
                col("notification_message")
            )
        ).withColumn(
            "notification_timestamp_unix",
            unix_timestamp(col("notification_timestamp"))
        )
        
        # Window specification for deduplication
        window_spec = Window.partitionBy("dedup_key").orderBy("notification_timestamp_unix")
        
        # Mark duplicates
        dedup_df = dedup_df.withColumn(
            "row_num", row_number().over(window_spec)
        ).withColumn(
            "is_duplicate",
            when(col("row_num") > 1, "YES").otherwise("NO")
        )
        
        # Keep only first occurrence
        unique_notifications = dedup_df.filter(col("is_duplicate") == "NO")
        
        duplicate_count = dedup_df.filter(col("is_duplicate") == "YES").count()
        
        print(f"\nDeduplication Summary:")
        print(f"  Original notifications: {notifications_df.count()}")
        print(f"  Duplicates removed: {duplicate_count}")
        print(f"  Unique notifications: {unique_notifications.count()}")
        
        return unique_notifications
    
    def apply_throttling(self, notifications_df, max_per_category=10):
        """
        Apply throttling to limit notifications per category
        
        Args:
            notifications_df: DataFrame with notifications
            max_per_category: Maximum notifications per category
        """
        # Rank notifications by severity within each category
        window_spec = Window.partitionBy("notification_category").orderBy(
            when(col("severity") == "CRITICAL", 1)
            .when(col("severity") == "HIGH", 2)
            .when(col("severity") == "MEDIUM", 3)
            .otherwise(4),
            col("notification_timestamp")
        )
        
        throttled = notifications_df.withColumn(
            "priority_rank", row_number().over(window_spec)
        ).withColumn(
            "is_throttled",
            when(col("priority_rank") > max_per_category, "YES").otherwise("NO")
        )
        
        # Keep only top priority notifications
        active_notifications = throttled.filter(col("is_throttled") == "NO")
        throttled_count = throttled.filter(col("is_throttled") == "YES").count()
        
        print(f"\nThrottling Summary:")
        print(f"  Total notifications: {notifications_df.count()}")
        print(f"  Throttled: {throttled_count}")
        print(f"  Active: {active_notifications.count()}")
        
        return active_notifications
    
    def add_escalation_rules(self, notifications_df):
        """
        Add escalation rules based on severity and time
        
        Args:
            notifications_df: DataFrame with notifications
        """
        escalation = notifications_df.withColumn(
            "escalation_level",
            when(col("severity") == "CRITICAL", 1)
            .when(col("severity") == "HIGH", 2)
            .otherwise(3)
        ).withColumn(
            "escalation_time_minutes",
            when(col("severity") == "CRITICAL", 5)
            .when(col("severity") == "HIGH", 15)
            .when(col("severity") == "MEDIUM", 30)
            .otherwise(60)
        ).withColumn(
            "escalation_to",
            when(col("severity") == "CRITICAL", "VP Engineering, CTO")
            .when(col("severity") == "HIGH", "Engineering Manager")
            .when(col("severity") == "MEDIUM", "Team Lead")
            .otherwise("On-call Engineer")
        ).withColumn(
            "requires_acknowledgment",
            when(col("severity").isin(["CRITICAL", "HIGH"]), "YES").otherwise("NO")
        )
        
        print("\nEscalation Rules Applied:")
        escalation.select(
            "notification_category", "severity", "escalation_level",
            "escalation_time_minutes", "escalation_to", "requires_acknowledgment"
        ).distinct().orderBy("escalation_level").show(truncate=False)
        
        return escalation
    
    def create_notification_digest(self, notifications_df):
        """
        Create a digest summary of notifications for periodic reporting
        
        Args:
            notifications_df: DataFrame with notifications
        """
        digest = notifications_df.groupBy("notification_category", "severity").agg(
            count("*").alias("notification_count"),
            collect_list(
                struct(
                    col("notification_id"),
                    col("notification_message")
                )
            ).alias("notifications")
        ).withColumn(
            "digest_timestamp", current_timestamp()
        ).withColumn(
            "digest_summary",
            concat(
                col("notification_category"),
                lit(": "),
                col("notification_count"),
                lit(" "),
                col("severity"),
                lit(" notifications")
            )
        )
        
        print("\nNotification Digest:")
        digest.select("digest_summary", "notification_count").show(truncate=False)
        
        return digest
    
    def track_notification_lifecycle(self, notifications_df):
        """
        Track notification lifecycle states
        
        Args:
            notifications_df: DataFrame with notifications
        """
        lifecycle = notifications_df.withColumn(
            "state", lit("NEW")
        ).withColumn(
            "created_at", col("notification_timestamp")
        ).withColumn(
            "updated_at", current_timestamp()
        ).withColumn(
            "acknowledged", lit(False)
        ).withColumn(
            "acknowledged_by", lit(None).cast(StringType())
        ).withColumn(
            "acknowledged_at", lit(None).cast(TimestampType())
        ).withColumn(
            "resolved", lit(False)
        ).withColumn(
            "resolved_at", lit(None).cast(TimestampType())
        ).withColumn(
            "resolution_notes", lit(None).cast(StringType())
        )
        
        print("\nNotification Lifecycle Tracking Initialized")
        lifecycle.select(
            "notification_id", "state", "created_at", 
            "acknowledged", "resolved"
        ).show(5, truncate=False)
        
        return lifecycle

# STREAMING NOTIFICATION PATTERN
# ============================================================================

class StreamingNotificationPattern:
    """
    Real-time notification pattern using Spark Structured Streaming
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    def create_streaming_source(self):
        """
        Create a streaming data source (simulated with rate source)
        """
        # Create a streaming DataFrame using rate source
        streaming_df = self.spark.readStream \
            .format("rate") \
            .option("rowsPerSecond", 2) \
            .load()
        
        # Transform to simulate events
        events = streaming_df.withColumn(
            "event_id", concat(lit("EVT_"), col("value"))
        ).withColumn(
            "event_type",
            when(col("value") % 5 == 0, "CRITICAL_EVENT")
            .when(col("value") % 3 == 0, "WARNING_EVENT")
            .otherwise("INFO_EVENT")
        ).withColumn(
            "metric_value", (rand() * 100).cast("double")
        ).withColumn(
            "event_timestamp", col("timestamp")
        )
        
        return events
    
    def apply_streaming_notifications(self, streaming_df):
        """
        Apply notification logic to streaming data
        
        Args:
            streaming_df: Streaming DataFrame
        """
        # Define notification conditions
        notifications = streaming_df.withColumn(
            "notification_required",
            when(col("event_type") == "CRITICAL_EVENT", True)
            .when((col("event_type") == "WARNING_EVENT") & (col("metric_value") > 80), True)
            .otherwise(False)
        ).filter(col("notification_required") == True).withColumn(
            "notification_message",
            concat(
                lit("Streaming Alert: "),
                col("event_type"),
                lit(" detected with metric value: "),
                col("metric_value")
            )
        ).withColumn(
            "severity",
            when(col("event_type") == "CRITICAL_EVENT", "CRITICAL")
            .otherwise("HIGH")
        )
        
        return notifications
    
    def write_streaming_notifications(self, notifications_stream, output_mode="append"):
        """
        Write streaming notifications to console (for demo)
        
        Args:
            notifications_stream: Streaming notifications DataFrame
            output_mode: Output mode (append, complete, update)
        """
        query = notifications_stream.select(
            "event_id", "event_type", "severity", 
            "metric_value", "notification_message", "event_timestamp"
        ).writeStream \
            .outputMode(output_mode) \
            .format("console") \
            .option("truncate", False) \
            .trigger(processingTime="5 seconds")
        
        return query
    
    def demo_streaming_notifications(self, duration_seconds=20):
        """
        Demonstrate streaming notifications
        
        Args:
            duration_seconds: How long to run the streaming demo
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("STREAMING NOTIFICATION PATTERN DEMO")
        print("=" * 80)
        print(f"\nRunning streaming notifications for {duration_seconds} seconds...")
        print("(In production, this would run continuously)")
        
        # Create streaming source
        streaming_events = self.create_streaming_source()
        
        # Apply notification logic
        streaming_notifications = self.apply_streaming_notifications(streaming_events)
        
        # Write to console
        query = self.write_streaming_notifications(streaming_notifications)
        
        # Start the query
        # streaming_query = query.start()
        
        # In production, you would use:
        # streaming_query.awaitTermination()
        
        # For demo, we'll just show the structure
        print("\nStreaming notification schema:")
        streaming_notifications.printSchema()
        
        print("\nNote: Streaming query would run continuously in production")
        print("Output would be written to: Kafka, Database, File System, etc.")

class NotificationAnalytics:
    """
    Analytics and insights on notification patterns
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    def analyze_notification_trends(self, notifications_df):
        """
        Analyze notification trends over time
        
        Args:
            notifications_df: Historical notifications DataFrame
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("NOTIFICATION ANALYTICS")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # Trend analysis
        trends = notifications_df.groupBy("notification_category").agg(
            count("*").alias("total_count"),
            count(when(col("severity") == "CRITICAL", 1)).alias("critical_count"),
            count(when(col("severity") == "HIGH", 1)).alias("high_count"),
            count(when(col("severity") == "MEDIUM", 1)).alias("medium_count"),
            count(when(col("severity") == "LOW", 1)).alias("low_count")
        ).withColumn(
            "critical_percentage",
            round((col("critical_count") / col("total_count")) * 100, 2)
        ).withColumn(
            "health_score",
            when(col("critical_percentage") > 20, "POOR")
            .when(col("critical_percentage") > 10, "FAIR")
            .when(col("critical_percentage") > 5, "GOOD")
            .otherwise("EXCELLENT")
        )
        
        print("\nNotification Trends by Category:")
        trends.show(truncate=False)
        
        return trends
    
    def identify_notification_patterns(self, notifications_df):
        """
        Identify recurring notification patterns
        
        Args:
            notifications_df: Notifications DataFrame
        """
        # Pattern detection
        patterns = notifications_df.groupBy(
            "notification_category", "severity"
        ).agg(
            count("*").alias("occurrence_count"),
            collect_set("notification_message").alias("unique_messages")
        ).withColumn(
            "pattern_type",
            when(col("occurrence_count") > 10, "FREQUENT")
            .when(col("occurrence_count") > 5, "MODERATE")
            .otherwise("RARE")
        ).withColumn(
            "message_diversity",
            size(col("unique_messages"))
        ).withColumn(
            "is_recurring",
            when(col("occurrence_count") > 5, "YES").otherwise("NO")
        )
        
        print("\nNotification Pattern Analysis:")
        patterns.select(
            "notification_category", "severity", "occurrence_count",
            "pattern_type", "is_recurring", "message_diversity"
        ).orderBy(col("occurrence_count").desc()).show(truncate=False)
        
        # Identify top recurring issues
        recurring = patterns.filter(col("is_recurring") == "YES")
        
        if recurring.count() > 0:
            print("\n⚠️  Recurring Issues Detected:")
            print("Consider implementing permanent fixes for these frequent notifications")
            recurring.select(
                "notification_category", "severity", "occurrence_count"
            ).show(truncate=False)
        
        return patterns
    
    def calculate_notification_metrics(self, notifications_df):
        """
        Calculate key notification metrics
        
        Args:
            notifications_df: Notifications DataFrame
        """
        metrics = {
            "total_notifications": notifications_df.count(),
            "unique_categories": notifications_df.select("notification_category").distinct().count(),
            "critical_ratio": notifications_df.filter(col("severity") == "CRITICAL").count() / 
                            max(notifications_df.count(), 1),
            "categories_with_criticals": notifications_df.filter(
                col("severity") == "CRITICAL"
            ).select("notification_category").distinct().count()
        }
        
        print("\nKey Notification Metrics:")
        print(f"  Total Notifications: {metrics['total_notifications']}")
        print(f"  Unique Categories: {metrics['unique_categories']}")
        print(f"  Critical Ratio: {metrics['critical_ratio']:.2%}")
```python
        print(f"  Categories with Criticals: {metrics['categories_with_criticals']}")
        
        return metrics

class NotificationIntegration:
    """
    Examples of integrating notifications with external systems
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    def format_for_slack(self, notifications_df):
        """
        Format notifications for Slack webhook
        
        Args:
            notifications_df: Notifications DataFrame
        """
        slack_messages = notifications_df.withColumn(
            "slack_payload",
            to_json(
                struct(
                    lit("Notification Alert").alias("text"),
                    array(
                        struct(
                            lit("section").alias("type"),
                            struct(
                                lit("mrkdwn").alias("type"),
                                concat(
                                    lit("*Severity:* "),
                                    col("severity"),
                                    lit("\n*Category:* "),
                                    col("notification_category"),
                                    lit("\n*Message:* "),
                                    col("notification_message")
                                ).alias("text")
                            ).alias("text")
                        )
                    ).alias("blocks")
                )
            )
        ).withColumn(
            "slack_color",
            when(col("severity") == "CRITICAL", "#FF0000")
            .when(col("severity") == "HIGH", "#FFA500")
            .when(col("severity") == "MEDIUM", "#FFFF00")
            .otherwise("#00FF00")
        )
        
        print("\nSlack Integration Format:")
        slack_messages.select("notification_id", "slack_payload").show(3, truncate=False)
        
        return slack_messages
    
    def format_for_email(self, notifications_df):
        """
        Format notifications for email
        
        Args:
            notifications_df: Notifications DataFrame
        """
        email_messages = notifications_df.withColumn(
            "email_subject",
            concat(
                lit("["),
                col("severity"),
                lit("] "),
                col("notification_category"),
                lit(" Notification - "),
                date_format(current_timestamp(), "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss")
            )
        ).withColumn(
            "email_body_html",
            concat(
                lit("<html><body>"),
                lit("<h2 style='color: "),
                when(col("severity") == "CRITICAL", "red")
                .when(col("severity") == "HIGH", "orange")
                .otherwise("black"),
                lit("'>"),
                col("severity"),
                lit(" Alert</h2>"),
                lit("<p><strong>Category:</strong> "),
                col("notification_category"),
                lit("</p>"),
                lit("<p><strong>Message:</strong> "),
                col("notification_message"),
                lit("</p>"),
                lit("<p><strong>Timestamp:</strong> "),
                col("notification_timestamp"),
                lit("</p>"),
                lit("</body></html>")
            )
        ).withColumn(
            "email_to",
            when(col("severity") == "CRITICAL", "oncall@company.com,management@company.com")
            .when(col("severity") == "HIGH", "oncall@company.com")
            .otherwise("monitoring@company.com")
        ).withColumn(
            "email_priority",
            when(col("severity") == "CRITICAL", "HIGH")
            .when(col("severity") == "HIGH", "NORMAL")
            .otherwise("LOW")
        )
        
        print("\nEmail Integration Format:")
        email_messages.select(
            "notification_id", "email_subject", "email_to", "email_priority"
        ).show(3, truncate=False)
        
        return email_messages
    
    def format_for_pagerduty(self, notifications_df):
        """
        Format notifications for PagerDuty
        
        Args:
            notifications_df: Notifications DataFrame
        """
        pagerduty_events = notifications_df.filter(
            col("severity").isin(["CRITICAL", "HIGH"])
        ).withColumn(
            "pagerduty_payload",
            to_json(
                struct(
                    lit("trigger").alias("event_action"),
                    col("notification_id").alias("dedup_key"),
                    struct(
                        col("notification_message").alias("summary"),
                        col("severity").alias("severity"),
                        current_timestamp().alias("timestamp"),
                        lit("notification_system").alias("source"),
                        struct(
                            col("notification_category").alias("category"),
                            col("notification_type").alias("type")
                        ).alias("custom_details")
                    ).alias("payload")
                )
            )
        ).withColumn(
            "pagerduty_urgency",
            when(col("severity") == "CRITICAL", "high").otherwise("low")
        )
        
        print("\nPagerDuty Integration Format:")
        pagerduty_events.select(
            "notification_id", "severity", "pagerduty_urgency"
        ).show(truncate=False)
        
        return pagerduty_events
    
    def format_for_kafka(self, notifications_df):
        """
        Format notifications for Kafka topic
        
        Args:
            notifications_df: Notifications DataFrame
        """
        kafka_messages = notifications_df.withColumn(
            "kafka_key",
            concat(col("notification_category"), lit("_"), col("severity"))
        ).withColumn(
            "kafka_value",
            to_json(
                struct(
                    col("notification_id"),
                    col("notification_category"),
                    col("notification_type"),
                    col("severity"),
                    col("notification_message"),
                    col("notification_timestamp")
                )
            )
        ).withColumn(
            "kafka_topic",
            concat(
                lit("notifications."),
                lower(col("notification_category"))
            )
        ).withColumn(
            "kafka_partition",
            when(col("severity") == "CRITICAL", 0)
            .when(col("severity") == "HIGH", 1)
            .otherwise(2)
        )
        
        print("\nKafka Integration Format:")
        kafka_messages.select(
            "kafka_topic", "kafka_key", "kafka_partition"
        ).show(5, truncate=False)
        
        # Example: Write to Kafka (commented out for demo)

        kafka_messages.select(

        ).write \
            .format("kafka") \
            .option("kafka.bootstrap.servers", "localhost:9092") \
            .option("topic", "notifications") \
            .save()
        """
        
        return kafka_messages
    
    def format_for_database(self, notifications_df):
        """
        Format notifications for database storage
        
        Args:
            notifications_df: Notifications DataFrame
        """
        db_records = notifications_df.select(
            col("notification_id").cast("string"),
            col("notification_category"),
            col("notification_type"),
            col("severity"),
            col("notification_message"),
            col("notification_timestamp"),
            current_timestamp().alias("created_at"),
            lit("ACTIVE").alias("status"),
            lit(None).cast("string").alias("acknowledged_by"),
            lit(None).cast("timestamp").alias("acknowledged_at")
        )
        
        print("\nDatabase Storage Format:")
        db_records.printSchema()
        db_records.show(3, truncate=False)

class NotificationSystemHealth:
    """
    Monitor the health of the notification system itself
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    def check_notification_system_health(self, notifications_df):
        """
        Perform health checks on the notification system
        
        Args:
            notifications_df: Recent notifications DataFrame
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("NOTIFICATION SYSTEM HEALTH CHECK")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        total_notifications = notifications_df.count()
        
        # Health metrics
        health_metrics = notifications_df.agg(
            count("*").alias("total_notifications"),
            count(when(col("severity") == "CRITICAL", 1)).alias("critical_count"),
            countDistinct("notification_category").alias("active_categories")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        critical_ratio = health_metrics["critical_count"] / max(total_notifications, 1)
        
        # Determine system health
        if critical_ratio > 0.3:
            health_status = "CRITICAL"
            health_message = "⛔ System experiencing high critical alert rate"
        elif critical_ratio > 0.15:
            health_status = "WARNING"
            health_message = "⚠️  Elevated critical alert rate detected"
        elif total_notifications > 100:
            health_status = "WARNING"
            health_message = "⚠️  High notification volume detected"
        else:
            health_status = "HEALTHY"
            health_message = "✅ Notification system operating normally"
        
        print(f"\nHealth Status: {health_status}")
        print(f"Message: {health_message}")
        print(f"\nMetrics:")
        print(f"  Total Notifications: {total_notifications}")
        print(f"  Critical Notifications: {health_metrics['critical_count']}")
        print(f"  Critical Ratio: {critical_ratio:.2%}")
        print(f"  Active Categories: {health_metrics['active_categories']}")
        
        # Check for notification storms
        category_counts = notifications_df.groupBy("notification_category").count()
        max_category_count = category_counts.agg({"count": "max"}).collect()[0][0]
        
        if max_category_count > 20:
            print(f"\n⚠️  NOTIFICATION STORM DETECTED in a category!")
            print(f"   Max notifications in single category: {max_category_count}")
            print("   Recommended: Investigate root cause and implement suppression")
        
        return {
            "health_status": health_status,
            "total_notifications": total_notifications,
            "critical_ratio": critical_ratio,
            "health_message": health_message
        }

class NotificationConfiguration:
    """
    Centralized configuration for notification system
    """
    
    # Notification severity levels
    SEVERITY_LEVELS = {
        "CRITICAL": 1,
        "HIGH": 2,
        "MEDIUM": 3,
        "LOW": 4,
        "INFO": 5
    }
    
    # Default thresholds
    DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS = {
        "CPU": {"warning": 80.0, "critical": 90.0},
        "MEMORY": {"warning": 70.0, "critical": 85.0},
        "DISK": {"warning": 75.0, "critical": 90.0},
        "NETWORK": {"warning": 80.0, "critical": 95.0}
    }
    
    # Escalation timeframes (in minutes)
    ESCALATION_TIMEFRAMES = {
        "CRITICAL": 5,
        "HIGH": 15,
        "MEDIUM": 30,
        "LOW": 60
    }
    
    # Notification channels by severity
    NOTIFICATION_CHANNELS = {
        "CRITICAL": ["pagerduty", "slack", "email", "sms"],
        "HIGH": ["slack", "email"],
        "MEDIUM": ["email"],
        "LOW": ["dashboard"]
    }
    
    # Deduplication window (in minutes)
    DEDUP_WINDOW_MINUTES = 5
    
    # Throttling limits
    THROTTLE_LIMITS = {
        "per_category": 10,
        "per_severity": 20,
        "total": 100
    }
    
    # Retention periods (in days)
    RETENTION_PERIODS = {
        "active_notifications": 7,
        "acknowledged_notifications": 30,
        "archived_notifications": 365
    }
    
    @staticmethod
    def get_config():
        """Return complete configuration dictionary"""
        return {
            "severity_levels": NotificationConfiguration.SEVERITY_LEVELS,
            "thresholds": NotificationConfiguration.DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS,
            "escalation": NotificationConfiguration.ESCALATION_TIMEFRAMES,
            "channels": NotificationConfiguration.NOTIFICATION_CHANNELS,
            "dedup_window": NotificationConfiguration.DEDUP_WINDOW_MINUTES,
            "throttle_limits": NotificationConfiguration.THROTTLE_LIMITS,
            "retention": NotificationConfiguration.RETENTION_PERIODS
        }
    
    @staticmethod
    def print_config():
        """Print current configuration"""
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("NOTIFICATION SYSTEM CONFIGURATION")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        config = NotificationConfiguration.get_config()
        
        print("\nSeverity Levels:")
        for severity, priority in config["severity_levels"].items():
            print(f"  {severity}: Priority {priority}")
        
        print("\nDefault Thresholds:")
        for metric, thresholds in config["thresholds"].items():
            print(f"  {metric}: Warning={thresholds['warning']}%, Critical={thresholds['critical']}%")
        
        print("\nEscalation Timeframes:")
        for severity, minutes in config["escalation"].items():
            print(f"  {severity}: {minutes} minutes")
        
        print("\nNotification Channels:")
        for severity, channels in config["channels"].items():
            print(f"  {severity}: {', '.join(channels)}")
        
        print(f"\nDeduplication Window: {config['dedup_window']} minutes")
        
        print("\nThrottle Limits:")
        for limit_type, value in config["throttle_limits"].items():
            print(f"  {limit_type}: {value}")
        
        print("\nRetention Periods:")
        for notification_type, days in config["retention"].items():
            print(f"  {notification_type}: {days} days")

class NotificationPatternTests:
    """
    Unit tests and validation for notification patterns
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
        self.test_results = []
    
    def test_event_notification(self):
        """Test Event Notification Pattern"""
        print("\n🧪 Testing Event Notification Pattern...")
        
        try:
            pattern = EventNotificationPattern(self.spark)
            events_df = pattern.create_sample_event_data()
            notifications = pattern.detect_events(events_df, ["ADMIN_LOGIN", "PURCHASE"])
            
            assert notifications.count() > 0, "No notifications generated"
            assert "notification_id" in notifications.columns, "Missing notification_id column"
            
            self.test_results.append(("Event Notification", "PASSED"))
            print("   ✅ Event Notification Pattern - PASSED")
        except Exception as e:
            self.test_results.append(("Event Notification", f"FAILED: {str(e)}"))
            print(f"   ❌ Event Notification Pattern - FAILED: {str(e)}")
    
    def test_change_notification(self):
        """Test Change Notification Pattern"""
        print("\n🧪 Testing Change Notification Pattern...")
        
        try:
            pattern = ChangeNotificationPattern(self.spark)
            prev_df, curr_df = pattern.create_sample_data()
            changes = pattern.detect_changes(prev_df, curr_df)
            
            assert changes["all_notifications"].count() > 0, "No changes detected"
            assert "change_type" in changes["inserts"].columns, "Missing change_type column"
            
            self.test_results.append(("Change Notification", "PASSED"))
            print("   ✅ Change Notification Pattern - PASSED")
        except Exception as e:
            self.test_results.append(("Change Notification", f"FAILED: {str(e)}"))
            print(f"   ❌ Change Notification Pattern - FAILED: {str(e)}")
    
    def test_threshold_notification(self):
        """Test Threshold Notification Pattern"""
        print("\n🧪 Testing Threshold Notification Pattern...")
        
        try:
            pattern = ThresholdNotificationPattern(self.spark)
            metrics_df = pattern.create_sample_metrics_data()
            thresholds_df = pattern.define_thresholds()
            notifications = pattern.check_thresholds(metrics_df, thresholds_df)
            
            assert notifications.count() > 0, "No threshold violations detected"
            assert "alert_level" in notifications.columns, "Missing alert_level column"
            
            self.test_results.append(("Threshold Notification", "PASSED"))
            print("   ✅ Threshold Notification Pattern - PASSED")
        except Exception as e:
            self.test_results.append(("Threshold Notification", f"FAILED: {str(e)}"))
            print(f"   ❌ Threshold Notification Pattern - FAILED: {str(e)}")
    
    def test_completion_notification(self):
        """Test Completion Notification Pattern"""
        print("\n🧪 Testing Completion Notification Pattern...")
        
        try:
            pattern = CompletionNotificationPattern(self.spark)
            jobs_df = pattern.create_sample_job_data()
            notifications = pattern.generate_completion_notifications(jobs_df)
            
            assert notifications.count() > 0, "No completion notifications generated"
            assert "completion_category" in notifications.columns, "Missing completion_category column"
            
            self.test_results.append(("Completion Notification", "PASSED"))
            print("   ✅ Completion Notification Pattern - PASSED")
        except Exception as e:
            self.test_results.append(("Completion Notification", f"FAILED: {str(e)}"))
            print(f"   ❌ Completion Notification Pattern - FAILED: {str(e)}")
    
    def test_error_notification(self):
        """Test Error Notification Pattern"""
        print("\n🧪 Testing Error Notification Pattern...")
        
        try:
            pattern = ErrorNotificationPattern(self.spark)
            errors_df = pattern.create_sample_error_data()
            notifications = pattern.generate_error_notifications(errors_df)
            
            assert notifications.count() > 0, "No error notifications generated"
            assert "recommended_action" in notifications.columns, "Missing recommended_action column"
            
            self.test_results.append(("Error Notification", "PASSED"))
            print("   ✅ Error Notification Pattern - PASSED")
        except Exception as e:
            self.test_results.append(("Error Notification", f"FAILED: {str(e)}"))
            print(f"   ❌ Error Notification Pattern - FAILED: {str(e)}")
    
    def run_all_tests(self):
        """Run all tests"""
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("RUNNING NOTIFICATION PATTERN TESTS")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        self.test_event_notification()
        self.test_change_notification()
        self.test_threshold_notification()
        self.test_completion_notification()
        self.test_error_notification()
        
        # Print summary
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("TEST SUMMARY")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        passed = sum(1 for _, result in self.test_results if result == "PASSED")
        total = len(self.test_results)
        
        print(f"\nTests Passed: {passed}/{total}")
        print("\nDetailed Results:")
        for test_name, result in self.test_results:
            status_icon = "✅" if result == "PASSED" else "❌"
            print(f"  {status_icon} {test_name}: {result}")
        
        if passed == total:
            print("\n🎉 All tests passed!")
        else:
            print(f"\n⚠️  {total - passed} test(s) failed")
        
        return passed == total

║                    PYSPARK NOTIFICATION PATTERNS GUIDE                     ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

1. EVENT NOTIFICATION PATTERN
   Purpose: Detect and notify when specific events occur
   Use Cases:
     - User authentication events
     - Transaction events
     - System events
   
   Example Usage:
     pattern = EventNotificationPattern(spark)
     
```python
     events_df = pattern.create_sample_event_data()
     notifications = pattern.detect_events(events_df, ["LOGIN", "PURCHASE"])

2. CHANGE NOTIFICATION PATTERN
   Purpose: Detect and notify when data changes occur (CDC)
   Use Cases:
     - Database change tracking
     - Configuration changes
     - Data synchronization
   
   Example Usage:
     pattern = ChangeNotificationPattern(spark)
     prev_df, curr_df = pattern.create_sample_data()
     changes = pattern.detect_changes(prev_df, curr_df)

3. THRESHOLD NOTIFICATION PATTERN
   Purpose: Alert when metrics exceed defined thresholds
   Use Cases:
     - Performance monitoring
     - Resource utilization alerts
     - KPI tracking
   
   Example Usage:
     pattern = ThresholdNotificationPattern(spark)
     metrics_df = pattern.create_sample_metrics_data()
     thresholds_df = pattern.define_thresholds()
     notifications = pattern.check_thresholds(metrics_df, thresholds_df)

4. COMPLETION NOTIFICATION PATTERN
   Purpose: Notify when processes or tasks complete
   Use Cases:
     - ETL job completion
     - Batch processing status
     - Workflow completion
   
   Example Usage:
     pattern = CompletionNotificationPattern(spark)
     jobs_df = pattern.create_sample_job_data()
     notifications = pattern.generate_completion_notifications(jobs_df)

5. ERROR NOTIFICATION PATTERN
   Purpose: Detect and notify when errors occur
   Use Cases:
     - Exception handling
     - Data quality issues
     - System failures
   
   Example Usage:
     pattern = ErrorNotificationPattern(spark)
     errors_df = pattern.create_sample_error_data()
     notifications = pattern.generate_error_notifications(errors_df)

║                      BEST PRACTICES                                        ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

1. AVOID ALERT FATIGUE:
   - Use deduplication to prevent duplicate alerts
   - Implement throttling to limit notification volume
   - Set appropriate severity levels
   - Create notification digests for low-priority items

2. ENSURE ACTIONABILITY:
   - Include clear, actionable messages
   - Provide context and relevant details
   - Add recommended remediation steps
   - Include links to runbooks or documentation

3. OPTIMIZE PERFORMANCE:
   - Use broadcast joins for small lookup tables
   - Partition data appropriately
   - Cache frequently accessed DataFrames
   - Use appropriate shuffle partitions

4. MAINTAIN RELIABILITY:
   - Implement retry logic for external integrations
   - Handle failures gracefully
   - Log all notification attempts
   - Monitor notification system health

5. SECURITY CONSIDERATIONS:
   - Sanitize sensitive data in notifications
   - Use secure channels for critical alerts
   - Implement access controls
   - Encrypt notification data at rest and in transit

1. Too Many Notifications:
   Solution: Implement throttling and deduplication
   Code: manager.apply_throttling(df, max_per_category=10)

2. Missing Notifications:
   Solution: Check filters and severity levels
   Code: Verify notification_required conditions

3. Duplicate Notifications:
   Solution: Enable deduplication with appropriate time window
   Code: manager.deduplicate_notifications(df, time_window_minutes=5)

4. Performance Issues:
   Solution: Optimize Spark configuration
   Code: spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "200")

5. Integration Failures:
   Solution: Implement error handling and retries
   Code: Add try-except blocks with exponential backoff

def print_performance_tips():
    """
    Print performance optimization tips
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION TIPS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    print("""
🚀 SPARK CONFIGURATION OPTIMIZATION:

1. Adjust Shuffle Partitions:
   spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "200")
   # Rule of thumb: 2-3x number of cores in cluster

2. Enable Adaptive Query Execution (Spark 3.0+):
   spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
   spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true")

3. Broadcast Small Tables:
   from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast
   result = large_df.join(broadcast(small_df), "key")

4. Cache Frequently Used DataFrames:
   notifications_df.cache()
   notifications_df.count()  # Materialize cache

5. Partition Data Appropriately:
   notifications_df.write.partitionBy("date", "severity") \\
     .parquet("/path/to/notifications")

📊 QUERY OPTIMIZATION:

1. Use Column Pruning:
   # Select only needed columns
   df.select("col1", "col2", "col3")

2. Push Down Filters:
   # Apply filters early
   df.filter(col("severity") == "CRITICAL").select(...)

3. Avoid UDFs When Possible:
   # Use built-in functions instead of UDFs
   # Built-in functions are optimized

4. Use Window Functions Efficiently:
   # Partition windows appropriately
   Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("timestamp")

5. Minimize Shuffles:
   # Reduce number of shuffle operations
   # Combine multiple aggregations

💾 MEMORY OPTIMIZATION:

1. Increase Executor Memory:
   --executor-memory 8G

2. Adjust Memory Overhead:
   --conf spark.executor.memoryOverhead=2G

3. Use Appropriate Storage Levels:
   df.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_AND_DISK)

4. Unpersist When Done:
   df.unpersist()

⚡ PROCESSING OPTIMIZATION:

1. Use DataFrames Over RDDs:
   # DataFrames have Catalyst optimizer

2. Batch Processing:
   # Process in micro-batches for streaming

3. Parallel Processing:
   # Increase parallelism
   df.repartition(100)

4. Optimize Joins:
   # Use appropriate join strategies
   # Broadcast join for small tables
   # Sort-merge join for large tables
""")

def quick_start_example():
    """
    Quick start example - minimal code to get notifications working
    """
    from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
    from pyspark.sql.functions import *
    
    # Initialize Spark
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("QuickStartNotifications") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    # Sample data
    data = [
        ("server1", "CPU", 95.0, "CRITICAL"),
        ("server2", "MEMORY", 85.0, "HIGH"),
        ("server3", "DISK", 60.0, "NORMAL")
    ]
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(data, ["server", "metric", "value", "status"])
    
    # Create notifications
    notifications = df.filter(col("status") != "NORMAL") \
        .withColumn("notification_id", monotonically_increasing_id()) \
        .withColumn("message", 
                   concat(lit("Alert: "), col("metric"), lit(" on "), 
                          col("server"), lit(" is at "), col("value"), lit("%")))
    
    # Display
    notifications.show()

    # notifications.write.json("/path/to/output")
    # notifications.write.parquet("/path/to/output")
    # notifications.write.format("kafka").option("topic", "alerts").save()
    
    spark.stop()

        Args:

        # Collect summary statistics

        severity_counts = notifications_df.groupBy("severity").count().collect()

# UTILITY SCRIPT 4: Notification Export Utilities

class NotificationExporter:
    """
    Export notifications to various formats and destinations
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    def export_to_json_file(self, notifications_df, output_path):
        """Export notifications to JSON file"""
        notifications_df.write.mode("overwrite").json(output_path)
        print(f"✅ Exported to JSON: {output_path}")
    
    def export_to_csv_file(self, notifications_df, output_path):
        """Export notifications to CSV file"""
        notifications_df.write.mode("overwrite") \
            .option("header", "true") \
            .csv(output_path)
        print(f"✅ Exported to CSV: {output_path}")
    
    def export_to_parquet_file(self, notifications_df, output_path):
        """Export notifications to Parquet file"""
        notifications_df.write.mode("overwrite") \
            .partitionBy("notification_category", "severity") \
            .parquet(output_path)
        print(f"✅ Exported to Parquet: {output_path}")
    
    def export_to_delta_table(self, notifications_df, table_name):
        """Export notifications to Delta table"""
        notifications_df.write.format("delta") \
            .mode("append") \
            .saveAsTable(table_name)
        print(f"✅ Exported to Delta table: {table_name}")
    
    def export_to_console_summary(self, notifications_df):
        """Print formatted summary to console"""
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("NOTIFICATION EXPORT SUMMARY")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        print("\nTop 10 Recent Notifications:")
        notifications_df.orderBy(col("notification_timestamp").desc()) \
            .select("notification_id", "severity", "notification_category", "notification_message") \
            .show(10, truncate=False)
        
        print("\nSummary Statistics:")
        notifications_df.groupBy("severity", "notification_category") \
            .count() \
            .orderBy("severity", "count", ascending=[True, False]) \
            .show()

class NotificationReportGenerator:
    """
    Generate comprehensive reports from notification data
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    def generate_daily_report(self, notifications_df):
        """Generate daily summary report"""
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("DAILY NOTIFICATION REPORT")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # Overall summary
        total = notifications_df.count()
        critical = notifications_df.filter(col("severity") == "CRITICAL").count()
        high = notifications_df.filter(col("severity") == "HIGH").count()
        
        print(f"\n📊 Summary:")
        print(f"   Total Notifications: {total}")
        print(f"   Critical: {critical} ({(critical/total*100):.1f}%)")
        print(f"   High: {high} ({(high/total*100):.1f}%)")
        
        # Top issues
        print(f"\n🔥 Top 5 Most Frequent Issues:")
        notifications_df.groupBy("notification_message") \
            .count() \
            .orderBy(col("count").desc()) \
            .show(5, truncate=False)
        
        # Hourly trend
        print(f"\n📈 Hourly Distribution:")
        notifications_df.withColumn(
            "hour", 
            hour(col("notification_timestamp"))
        ).groupBy("hour") \
            .count() \
            .orderBy("hour") \
            .show()
        
        # Category breakdown
        print(f"\n📁 By Category:")
        notifications_df.groupBy("notification_category", "severity") \
            .count() \
            .orderBy("notification_category", "severity") \
            .show()
        
        return self._create_report_dict(notifications_df)
    
    def generate_weekly_report(self, notifications_df):
        """Generate weekly summary report"""
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("WEEKLY NOTIFICATION REPORT")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # Daily breakdown
        print(f"\n📅 Daily Breakdown:")
        notifications_df.withColumn(
            "date", 
            to_date(col("notification_timestamp"))
        ).groupBy("date") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("total"),
                count(when(col("severity") == "CRITICAL", 1)).alias("critical"),
                count(when(col("severity") == "HIGH", 1)).alias("high")
            ) \
            .orderBy("date") \
            .show()
        
        # Trending issues
        print(f"\n📊 Trending Issues:")
        notifications_df.groupBy("notification_category") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("total_count"),
                avg(when(col("severity") == "CRITICAL", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("critical_rate")
            ) \
            .orderBy(col("critical_rate").desc()) \
            .show()
        
        return self._create_report_dict(notifications_df)
    
    def _create_report_dict(self, notifications_df):
        """Create report dictionary for programmatic access"""
        report = {
            "total_notifications": notifications_df.count(),
            "by_severity": notifications_df.groupBy("severity").count().collect(),
            "by_category": notifications_df.groupBy("notification_category").count().collect(),
            "critical_count": notifications_df.filter(col("severity") == "CRITICAL").count(),
            "timestamp": datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
        }
        return report
    
    def export_report_to_pdf(self, notifications_df, output_path="/tmp/notification_report.txt"):
        """Export report to text file (PDF would require external library)"""
        report = self.generate_daily_report(notifications_df)
        
        with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
            f.write("=" * 80 + "\n")
            f.write("NOTIFICATION REPORT\n")
            f.write("=" * 80 + "\n\n")
            f.write(f"Generated: {report['timestamp']}\n")
            f.write(f"Total Notifications: {report['total_notifications']}\n")
            f.write(f"Critical Notifications: {report['critical_count']}\n\n")
            
            f.write("Breakdown by Severity:\n")
            for row in report['by_severity']:
                f.write(f"  {row['severity']}: {row['count']}\n")
            
            f.write("\nBreakdown by Category:\n")
            for row in report['by_category']:
                f.write(f"  {row['notification_category']}: {row['count']}\n")
        
        print(f"\n✅ Report exported to: {output_path}")
