def scenario_e_commerce_monitoring(spark):
    """
    Real-world scenario: E-commerce platform monitoring
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("SCENARIO: E-COMMERCE PLATFORM MONITORING")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Simulate e-commerce events
    events_data = [
        ("order_001", "ORDER_PLACED", "2024-01-15 10:00:00", 150.00, "success"),
        ("order_002", "PAYMENT_FAILED", "2024-01-15 10:05:00", 200.00, "failed"),
        ("cart_001", "CART_ABANDONED", "2024-01-15 10:10:00", 350.00, "abandoned"),
        ("order_003", "ORDER_PLACED", "2024-01-15 10:15:00", 450.00, "success"),
        ("payment_001", "PAYMENT_GATEWAY_TIMEOUT", "2024-01-15 10:20:00", 0.00, "error"),
        ("inventory_001", "LOW_STOCK_ALERT", "2024-01-15 10:25:00", 0.00, "warning"),
        ("order_004", "ORDER_PLACED", "2024-01-15 10:30:00", 275.00, "success"),
    ]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("event_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("event_type", StringType(), True),
        StructField("timestamp", StringType(), True),
        StructField("amount", DoubleType(), True),
        StructField("status", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    events_df = spark.createDataFrame(events_data, schema)
    
    # Generate notifications based on business rules
    notifications = events_df.withColumn(
        "severity",
        when(col("event_type").contains("TIMEOUT"), "CRITICAL")
        .when(col("event_type").contains("FAILED"), "HIGH")
        .when(col("event_type").contains("ABANDONED"), "MEDIUM")
        .when(col("event_type").contains("LOW_STOCK"), "HIGH")
        .otherwise("LOW")
    ).withColumn(
        "notification_message",
        when(col("event_type") == "PAYMENT_FAILED",
             concat(lit("Payment failed for order: "), col("event_id"), 
                   lit(" - Amount: $"), col("amount")))
        .when(col("event_type") == "CART_ABANDONED",
             concat(lit("Cart abandoned - Potential revenue loss: $"), col("amount")))
        .when(col("event_type") == "PAYMENT_GATEWAY_TIMEOUT",
             lit("CRITICAL: Payment gateway not responding - Immediate action required"))
        .when(col("event_type") == "LOW_STOCK_ALERT",
             lit("Low stock alert - Reorder required"))
        .otherwise(concat(lit("Event: "), col("event_type")))
    ).withColumn(
        "action_required",
        when(col("severity").isin(["CRITICAL", "HIGH"]), "YES").otherwise("NO")
    ).filter(col("severity") != "LOW")
    
    print("\n🛒 E-commerce Notifications:")
    notifications.select(
        "event_id", "event_type", "severity", "notification_message", "action_required"
    ).show(truncate=False)
    
    # Calculate business impact
    print("\n💰 Business Impact Analysis:")
    impact = notifications.agg(
        sum(when(col("event_type") == "PAYMENT_FAILED", col("amount")).otherwise(0)).alias("lost_revenue_failed"),
        sum(when(col("event_type") == "CART_ABANDONED", col("amount")).otherwise(0)).alias("potential_lost_revenue"),
        count(when(col("severity") == "CRITICAL", 1)).alias("critical_issues")
    )
    impact.show()


def scenario_iot_device_monitoring(spark):
    """
    Real-world scenario: IoT device fleet monitoring
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("SCENARIO: IOT DEVICE FLEET MONITORING")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Simulate IoT sensor data
    sensor_data = [
        ("sensor_001", "temperature", 85.5, "factory_floor", "2024-01-15 10:00:00"),
        ("sensor_002", "humidity", 75.0, "warehouse", "2024-01-15 10:00:00"),
        ("sensor_003", "temperature", 95.0, "factory_floor", "2024-01-15 10:05:00"),
        ("sensor_004", "pressure", 120.0, "production_line", "2024-01-15 10:10:00"),
        ("sensor_001", "temperature", 92.0, "factory_floor", "2024-01-15 10:15:00"),
        ("sensor_005", "vibration", 8.5, "machinery", "2024-01-15 10:20:00"),
    ]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("sensor_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("metric_type", StringType(), True),
        StructField("value", DoubleType(), True),
        StructField("location", StringType(), True),
        StructField("timestamp", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    sensors_df = spark.createDataFrame(sensor_data, schema)
    
    # Define IoT-specific thresholds
    thresholds = {
        "temperature": {"warning": 85.0, "critical": 90.0},
        "humidity": {"warning": 70.0, "critical": 80.0},
        "pressure": {"warning": 110.0, "critical": 120.0},
        "vibration": {"warning": 7.0, "critical": 9.0}
    }
    
    # Generate IoT notifications
    notifications = sensors_df.withColumn(
        "threshold_warning",
        when(col("metric_type") == "temperature", lit(85.0))
        .when(col("metric_type") == "humidity", lit(70.0))
        .when(col("metric_type") == "pressure", lit(110.0))
        .when(col("metric_type") == "vibration", lit(7.0))
    ).withColumn(
        "threshold_critical",
        when(col("metric_type") == "temperature", lit(90.0))
        .when(col("metric_type") == "humidity", lit(80.0))
        .when(col("metric_type") == "pressure", lit(120.0))
        .when(col("metric_type") == "vibration", lit(9.0))
    ).withColumn(
        "alert_level",
        when(col("value") >= col("threshold_critical"), "CRITICAL")
        .when(col("value") >= col("threshold_warning"), "WARNING")
        .otherwise("NORMAL")
    ).withColumn(
        "notification_message",
        concat(
            lit("IoT Alert - "),
            col("sensor_id"),
            lit(" at "),
            col("location"),
            lit(": "),
            col("metric_type"),
            lit(" = "),
            col("value"),
            when(col("alert_level") == "CRITICAL", lit(" (CRITICAL - Immediate action required)"))
            .otherwise(lit(" (WARNING - Monitor closely)"))
        )
    ).filter(col("alert_level") != "NORMAL")
    
    print("\n🔧 IoT Device Notifications:")
    notifications.select(
        "sensor_id", "location", "metric_type", "value", "alert_level", "notification_message"
    ).show(truncate=False)
    
    # Device health summary
    print("\n📊 Device Health Summary:")
    sensors_df.groupBy("location", "metric_type") \
        .agg(
            avg("value").alias("avg_value"),
            max("value").alias("max_value"),
            count("*").alias("reading_count")
        ).show()


def scenario_financial_transaction_monitoring(spark):
    """
    Real-world scenario: Financial transaction fraud detection
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("SCENARIO: FINANCIAL TRANSACTION MONITORING")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Simulate financial transactions
    transactions_data = [
        ("txn_001", "user_123", 50.00, "US", "2024-01-15 10:00:00", "approved"),
        ("txn_002", "user_123", 5000.00, "US", "2024-01-15 10:05:00", "approved"),
        ("txn_003", "user_123", 3000.00, "CN", "2024-01-15 10:10:00", "flagged"),
        ("txn_004", "user_456", 100.00, "UK", "2024-01-15 10:15:00", "approved"),
        ("txn_005", "user_123", 2000.00, "RU", "2024-01-15 10:20:00", "flagged"),
        ("txn_006", "user_789", 10000.00, "US", "2024-01-15 10:25:00",
```python
        ("txn_006", "user_789", 10000.00, "US", "2024-01-15 10:25:00", "flagged"),
    ]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("transaction_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("user_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("amount", DoubleType(), True),
        StructField("country", StringType(), True),
        StructField("timestamp", StringType(), True),
        StructField("status", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    transactions_df = spark.createDataFrame(transactions_data, schema)
    
    # Calculate user transaction patterns
    window_spec = Window.partitionBy("user_id").orderBy("timestamp")
    
    transaction_analysis = transactions_df.withColumn(
        "prev_amount", lag("amount").over(window_spec)
    ).withColumn(
        "prev_country", lag("country").over(window_spec)
    ).withColumn(
        "amount_spike",
        when(col("prev_amount").isNotNull(),
             (col("amount") / col("prev_amount")) > 10).otherwise(False)
    ).withColumn(
        "country_change",
        when(col("prev_country").isNotNull(),
             col("country") != col("prev_country")).otherwise(False)
    ).withColumn(
        "high_amount",
        col("amount") > 5000
    )
    
    # Generate fraud detection notifications
    fraud_notifications = transaction_analysis.withColumn(
        "risk_level",
        when((col("amount_spike") == True) & (col("country_change") == True), "CRITICAL")
        .when(col("high_amount") & (col("country_change") == True), "HIGH")
        .when(col("amount_spike") == True, "MEDIUM")
        .when(col("status") == "flagged", "MEDIUM")
        .otherwise("LOW")
    ).withColumn(
        "fraud_indicators",
        concat_ws(", ",
            when(col("amount_spike") == True, lit("Amount Spike")).otherwise(lit("")),
            when(col("country_change") == True, lit("Country Change")).otherwise(lit("")),
            when(col("high_amount") == True, lit("High Amount")).otherwise(lit(""))
        )
    ).withColumn(
        "notification_message",
        concat(
            lit("Fraud Alert ["),
            col("risk_level"),
            lit("]: Transaction "),
            col("transaction_id"),
            lit(" for user "),
            col("user_id"),
            lit(" - Amount: $"),
            col("amount"),
            lit(" in "),
            col("country"),
            lit(" - Indicators: "),
            col("fraud_indicators")
        )
    ).filter(col("risk_level") != "LOW")
    
    print("\n🚨 Fraud Detection Notifications:")
    fraud_notifications.select(
        "transaction_id", "user_id", "amount", "country", 
        "risk_level", "fraud_indicators"
    ).show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\n📊 Risk Summary:")
    fraud_notifications.groupBy("risk_level") \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("alert_count"),
            sum("amount").alias("total_amount_at_risk")
        ).show()

class NotificationPerformanceBenchmark:
    """
    Benchmark notification pattern performance
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    def benchmark_pattern(self, pattern_name, pattern_function, data_sizes=[1000, 10000, 100000]):
        """
        Benchmark a notification pattern with different data sizes
        
        Args:
            pattern_name: Name of the pattern
            pattern_function: Function to benchmark
            data_sizes: List of data sizes to test
        """
        import time
        
        print(f"\n{'=' * 80}")
        print(f"BENCHMARKING: {pattern_name}")
        print(f"{'=' * 80}")
        
        results = []
        
        for size in data_sizes:
            print(f"\nTesting with {size:,} records...")
            
            start_time = time.time()
            
            # Execute pattern
            try:
                result_df = pattern_function(size)
                result_count = result_df.count()
                
                end_time = time.time()
                duration = end_time - start_time
                
                throughput = size / duration if duration > 0 else 0
                
                results.append({
                    "size": size,
                    "duration": duration,
                    "throughput": throughput,
                    "result_count": result_count
                })
                
                print(f"  ✓ Completed in {duration:.2f}s ({throughput:.0f} records/sec)")
                
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  ✗ Error: {str(e)}")
                results.append({
                    "size": size,
                    "duration": None,
                    "throughput": None,
                    "result_count": None,
                    "error": str(e)
                })
        
        # Display results
        print(f"\n{'=' * 80}")
        print("BENCHMARK RESULTS")
        print(f"{'=' * 80}")
        print(f"{'Size':<15} {'Duration (s)':<15} {'Throughput (rec/s)':<20} {'Results':<15}")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        for result in results:
            if result.get('error'):
                print(f"{result['size']:<15} ERROR: {result['error']}")
            else:
                print(f"{result['size']:<15} {result['duration']:<15.2f} "
                      f"{result['throughput']:<20.0f} {result['result_count']:<15}")
        
        return results

## 1. Bulkhead Pattern

```python
"""
Bulkhead Pattern: Isolates resources to prevent cascade failures
Separates critical operations into isolated resource pools
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, lit, current_timestamp
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
from typing import List, Dict, Any
import logging
from datetime import datetime

# Configure logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class BulkheadPattern:
    """
    Implements bulkhead pattern by isolating different workloads
    into separate resource pools to prevent resource exhaustion
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        # Create separate thread pools for different workload types
        self.critical_pool = ThreadPoolExecutor(
            max_workers=5, 
            thread_name_prefix="critical-"
        )
        self.normal_pool = ThreadPoolExecutor(
            max_workers=10, 
            thread_name_prefix="normal-"
        )
        self.batch_pool = ThreadPoolExecutor(
            max_workers=3, 
            thread_name_prefix="batch-"
        )
        
    def process_critical_data(self, data_path: str) -> bool:
        """
        Process critical data with dedicated resources
        Isolated from other workloads to ensure availability
        """
        try:
            logger.info(f"Processing critical data from {data_path}")
            
            # Use separate Spark configuration for critical workloads
            critical_spark = SparkSession.builder \
                .appName("CriticalBulkhead") \
                .config("spark.executor.memory", "4g") \
                .config("spark.executor.cores", "2") \
                .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "50") \
                .getOrCreate()
            
            df = critical_spark.read.parquet(data_path)
            
            # Process with dedicated resources
            result = df.filter(col("priority") == "HIGH") \
                      .withColumn("processed_at", current_timestamp()) \
                      .cache()
            
            result.write.mode("overwrite").parquet("/tmp/critical_output")
            
            logger.info(f"Critical data processed: {result.count()} records")
            return True
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Critical processing failed: {str(e)}")
            return False
    
    def process_normal_data(self, data_path: str) -> bool:
        """
        Process normal priority data with standard resources
        Isolated from critical workloads
        """
        try:
            logger.info(f"Processing normal data from {data_path}")
            
            df = self.spark.read.parquet(data_path)
            
            result = df.filter(col("priority") == "NORMAL") \
                      .withColumn("processed_at", current_timestamp())
            
            result.write.mode("overwrite").parquet("/tmp/normal_output")
            
            logger.info(f"Normal data processed: {result.count()} records")
            return True
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Normal processing failed: {str(e)}")
            # Failure here doesn't affect critical processing
            return False
    
    def process_batch_data(self, data_path: str) -> bool:
        """
        Process batch data with limited resources
        Isolated to prevent resource starvation of other workloads
        """
        try:
            logger.info(f"Processing batch data from {data_path}")
            
            # Use limited resources for batch processing
            df = self.spark.read.parquet(data_path)
            
            result = df.filter(col("priority") == "BATCH") \
                      .repartition(10) \
                      .withColumn("processed_at", current_timestamp())
            
            result.write.mode("overwrite").parquet("/tmp/batch_output")
            
            logger.info(f"Batch data processed: {result.count()} records")
            return True
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Batch processing failed: {str(e)}")
            return False
    
    def execute_bulkhead_processing(self, data_paths: Dict[str, str]):
        """
        Execute all processing tasks in isolated bulkheads
        """
        futures = []
        
        # Submit tasks to appropriate bulkheads
        if "critical" in data_paths:
            futures.append(
                self.critical_pool.submit(
                    self.process_critical_data, 
                    data_paths["critical"]
                )
            )
        
        if "normal" in data_paths:
            futures.append(
                self.normal_pool.submit(
                    self.process_normal_data, 
                    data_paths["normal"]
                )
            )
        
        if "batch" in data_paths:
            futures.append(
                self.batch_pool.submit(
                    self.process_batch_data, 
                    data_paths["batch"]
                )
            )
        
        # Wait for completion
        results = {}
        for future in as_completed(futures):
            try:
                result = future.result(timeout=300)
                results[future] = result
            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(f"Bulkhead task failed: {str(e)}")
                results[future] = False
        
        return results
    
    def cleanup(self):
        """Clean up thread pools"""
        self.critical_pool.shutdown(wait=True)
        self.normal_pool.shutdown(wait=True)
        self.batch_pool.shutdown(wait=True)


# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("BulkheadPattern") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    bulkhead = BulkheadPattern(spark)
    
    # Process different workloads in isolated bulkheads
    data_paths = {
        "critical": "/data/critical",
        "normal": "/data/normal",
        "batch": "/data/batch"
    }
    
    results = bulkhead.execute_bulkhead_processing(data_paths)
    print(f"Bulkhead processing results: {results}")
    
    bulkhead.cleanup()
```

## 2. Fail-Fast Pattern

```python
"""
Fail-Fast Pattern: Detect and report failures immediately
Prevents wasting resources on operations that will eventually fail
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, when
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, IntegerType
import logging
from typing import Optional, Tuple

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class FailFastPattern:
    """
    Implements fail-fast pattern to detect failures early
    and avoid wasting resources on doomed operations
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
    
    def validate_input_immediately(self, data_path: str) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        """
        Validate input data before processing
        Fail immediately if validation fails
        """
        try:
            # Check if path exists
            try:
                self.spark.read.parquet(data_path).limit(1).count()
            except Exception as e:
                error_msg = f"Data path does not exist or is not accessible: {data_path}"
                logger.error(error_msg)
                raise ValueError(error_msg)
            
            # Validate schema immediately
            df = self.spark.read.parquet(data_path)
            required_columns = ["id", "name", "value", "timestamp"]
            
            missing_columns = set(required_columns) - set(df.columns)
            if missing_columns:
                error_msg = f"Missing required columns: {missing_columns}"
                logger.error(error_msg)
                raise ValueError(error_msg)
            
            # Validate data types
            schema = df.schema
            for field in schema.fields:
                if field.name == "id" and field.dataType != IntegerType():
                    error_msg = f"Invalid data type for 'id': expected IntegerType"
                    logger.error(error_msg)
                    raise TypeError(error_msg)
            
            # Check for empty dataset
            if df.count() == 0:
                error_msg = "Dataset is empty"
                logger.error(error_msg)
                raise ValueError(error_msg)
            
            logger.info("Input validation passed")
            return True, "Validation successful"
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Fail-fast validation failed: {str(e)}")
            raise
    
    def validate_business_rules(self, df) -> bool:
        """
        Validate business rules before processing
        Fail fast if rules are violated
        """
        try:
            # Check for null values in critical columns
            null_counts = df.select(
                [col(c).isNull().cast("int").alias(c) 
                 for c in ["id", "name", "value"]]
            ).groupBy().sum().collect()[0].asDict()
            
            critical_nulls = {k: v for k, v in null_counts.items() if v > 0}
            if critical_nulls:
                error_msg = f"Null values found in critical columns: {critical_nulls}"
                logger.error(error_msg)
                raise ValueError(error_msg)
            
            # Check for negative values
            negative_count = df.filter(col("value") < 0).count()
            if negative_count > 0:
                error_msg = f"Found {negative_count} negative values"
                logger.error(error_msg)
                raise ValueError(error_msg)
            
            # Check for duplicates
            duplicate_count = df.groupBy("id").count().filter(col("count") > 1).count()
            if duplicate_count > 0:
                error_msg = f"Found {duplicate_count} duplicate IDs"
                logger.error(error_msg)
                raise ValueError(error_msg)
            
            logger.info("Business rule validation passed")
            return True
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Business rule validation failed: {str(e)}")
            raise
    
    def process_with_fail_fast(self, data_path: str, output_path: str) -> bool:
        """
        Process data with fail-fast validation at each stage
        """
        try:
            # Stage 1: Validate input immediately
            logger.info("Stage 1: Validating input")
            self.validate_input_immediately(data_path)
            
            # Stage 2: Load data
            logger.info("Stage 2: Loading data")
            df = self.spark.read.parquet(data_path)
            
            # Stage 3: Validate business rules immediately
            logger.info("Stage 3: Validating business rules")
            self.validate_business_rules(df)
            
            # Stage 4: Validate resources before processing
            logger.info("Stage 4: Validating resources")
            available_memory = self.spark.sparkContext._jsc.sc().getExecutorMemoryStatus()
            if not available_memory:
                raise RuntimeError("No executors available")
            
            # Stage 5: Process only if all validations pass
            logger.info("Stage 5: Processing data")
            result = df.withColumn(
                "validated",
                lit(True)
            ).withColumn(
                "processed_at",
                current_timestamp()
            )
            
            # Stage 6: Validate output before writing
            logger.info("Stage 6: Validating output")
            if result.count() == 0:
                raise ValueError("Processing resulted in empty dataset")
            
            # Write output
            result.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(output_path)
            
            logger.info("Processing completed successfully with fail-fast pattern")
            return True
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Fail-fast processing aborted: {str(e)}")
            # Clean up partial results
            try:
                self.spark.read.parquet(output_path)
                logger.info("Cleaning up partial results")
                # In production, you would delete the partial output
            except:
                pass
            raise
    
    def validate_configuration(self, config: dict) -> bool:
        """
        Validate configuration before starting any processing
        """
        required_configs = [
            "spark.executor.memory",
            "spark.driver.memory",
            "spark.sql.shuffle.partitions"
        ]
        
        for config_key in required_configs:
            if config_key not in config:
                error_msg = f"Missing required configuration: {config_key}"
                logger.error(error_msg)
                raise ValueError(error_msg)
        
        # Validate memory settings
        executor_memory = config.get("spark.executor.memory", "0g")
        memory_value = int(executor_memory.replace("g", ""))
        
        if memory_value < 2:
            error_msg = "Insufficient executor memory (minimum 2GB required)"
            logger.error(error_msg)
            raise ValueError(error_msg)
        
        logger.info("Configuration validation passed")
        return True


# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("FailFastPattern") \
        .config("spark.executor.memory", "4g") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    fail_fast = FailFastPattern(spark)
    
    try:
        # Validate configuration first
        config = {
            "spark.executor.memory": "4g",
            "spark.driver.memory": "2g",
            "spark.sql.shuffle.partitions": "200"
        }
        fail_fast.validate_configuration(config)
        
        # Process with fail-fast validation
        fail_fast.process_with_fail_fast(
            "/data/input",
            "/data/output"
        )
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Processing failed fast: {str(e)}")
        # Handle failure appropriately

## 3. Fail-Safe Pattern

```python
"""
Fail-Safe Pattern: Provides graceful degradation and fallback mechanisms
Ensures system continues operating even when failures occur
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, DataFrame
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, lit, when, coalesce, current_timestamp
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, IntegerType, DoubleType
import logging
from typing import Optional, List, Callable
from datetime import datetime

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class FailSafePattern:
    """
    Implements fail-safe pattern with multiple fallback mechanisms
    to ensure graceful degradation
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.fallback_data_sources = []
        self.default_values = {}
    
    def read_with_fallback(self, primary_path: str, 
                          fallback_paths: List[str]) -> Optional[DataFrame]:
        """
        Read data with fallback sources if primary fails
        """
        # Try primary source
        try:
            logger.info(f"Attempting to read from primary source: {primary_path}")
            df = self.spark.read.parquet(primary_path)
            logger.info("Successfully read from primary source")
            return df.withColumn("source", lit("primary"))
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning(f"
```python
            logger.warning(f"Primary source failed: {str(e)}")
        
        # Try fallback sources
        for idx, fallback_path in enumerate(fallback_paths):
            try:
                logger.info(f"Attempting fallback source {idx + 1}: {fallback_path}")
                df = self.spark.read.parquet(fallback_path)
                logger.info(f"Successfully read from fallback source {idx + 1}")
                return df.withColumn("source", lit(f"fallback_{idx + 1}"))
            except Exception as e:
                logger.warning(f"Fallback source {idx + 1} failed: {str(e)}")
                continue
        
        # All sources failed, return empty DataFrame with schema
        logger.error("All data sources failed, returning empty DataFrame")
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), True),
            StructField("name", StringType(), True),
            StructField("value", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("source", StringType(), True)
        ])
        return self.spark.createDataFrame([], schema)
    
    def process_with_default_values(self, df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Process data with safe default values for missing/invalid data
        """
        try:
            logger.info("Processing with default values for safety")
            
            # Define default values for each column
            defaults = {
                "name": "UNKNOWN",
                "value": 0.0,
                "status": "PENDING",
                "category": "UNCATEGORIZED"
            }
            
            # Apply default values for null columns
            result = df
            for column, default_value in defaults.items():
                if column in df.columns:
                    result = result.withColumn(
                        column,
                        coalesce(col(column), lit(default_value))
                    )
            
            # Handle invalid values with safe defaults
            result = result.withColumn(
                "value",
                when(col("value") < 0, lit(0.0))
                .when(col("value").isNull(), lit(0.0))
                .otherwise(col("value"))
            )
            
            logger.info("Default values applied successfully")
            return result
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Error applying defaults: {str(e)}")
            return df
    
    def execute_with_circuit_breaker(self, 
                                     operation: Callable,
                                     max_retries: int = 3,
                                     fallback_operation: Optional[Callable] = None) -> Optional[any]:
        """
        Execute operation with circuit breaker and fallback
        """
        retry_count = 0
        last_exception = None
        
        while retry_count < max_retries:
            try:
                logger.info(f"Executing operation (attempt {retry_count + 1}/{max_retries})")
                result = operation()
                logger.info("Operation succeeded")
                return result
            except Exception as e:
                retry_count += 1
                last_exception = e
                logger.warning(f"Operation failed (attempt {retry_count}): {str(e)}")
                
                if retry_count < max_retries:
                    # Wait before retry (exponential backoff)
                    import time
                    wait_time = 2 ** retry_count
                    logger.info(f"Waiting {wait_time} seconds before retry")
                    time.sleep(wait_time)
        
        # All retries failed, try fallback
        if fallback_operation:
            try:
                logger.info("Executing fallback operation")
                result = fallback_operation()
                logger.info("Fallback operation succeeded")
                return result
            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(f"Fallback operation failed: {str(e)}")
        
        logger.error(f"All attempts failed: {str(last_exception)}")
        return None
    
    def safe_write(self, df: DataFrame, output_path: str, 
                   backup_path: Optional[str] = None) -> bool:
        """
        Write data safely with backup and validation
        """
        try:
            # Validate data before writing
            if df.count() == 0:
                logger.warning("DataFrame is empty, writing to backup location")
                if backup_path:
                    df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(backup_path)
                return False
            
            # Create backup if path provided
            if backup_path:
                try:
                    logger.info(f"Creating backup at {backup_path}")
                    df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(backup_path)
                except Exception as e:
                    logger.warning(f"Backup creation failed: {str(e)}")
            
            # Write to primary location
            logger.info(f"Writing to primary location: {output_path}")
            df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(output_path)
            
            # Verify write
            verification_df = self.spark.read.parquet(output_path)
            if verification_df.count() != df.count():
                raise ValueError("Write verification failed: record count mismatch")
            
            logger.info("Safe write completed successfully")
            return True
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Safe write failed: {str(e)}")
            
            # Attempt recovery from backup
            if backup_path:
                try:
                    logger.info("Attempting to recover from backup")
                    backup_df = self.spark.read.parquet(backup_path)
                    backup_df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(output_path)
                    logger.info("Recovery from backup successful")
                    return True
                except Exception as backup_error:
                    logger.error(f"Backup recovery failed: {str(backup_error)}")
            
            return False
    
    def graceful_degradation_pipeline(self, 
                                     primary_path: str,
                                     fallback_paths: List[str],
                                     output_path: str) -> bool:
        """
        Complete pipeline with fail-safe mechanisms at each stage
        """
        try:
            # Stage 1: Read with fallback
            logger.info("Stage 1: Reading data with fallback")
            df = self.read_with_fallback(primary_path, fallback_paths)
            
            if df is None or df.count() == 0:
                logger.warning("No data available from any source")
                # Create minimal valid output
                df = self.spark.createDataFrame(
                    [(0, "NO_DATA", 0.0, "none")],
                    ["id", "name", "value", "source"]
                )
            
            # Stage 2: Process with safe defaults
            logger.info("Stage 2: Processing with safe defaults")
            processed_df = self.process_with_default_values(df)
            
            # Stage 3: Apply transformations with error handling
            logger.info("Stage 3: Applying transformations")
            try:
                result = processed_df.withColumn(
                    "processed_at",
                    current_timestamp()
                ).withColumn(
                    "status",
                    lit("SUCCESS")
                )
            except Exception as e:
                logger.warning(f"Transformation failed, using processed data: {str(e)}")
                result = processed_df.withColumn("status", lit("PARTIAL"))
            
            # Stage 4: Safe write with backup
            logger.info("Stage 4: Writing output safely")
            backup_path = f"{output_path}_backup"
            success = self.safe_write(result, output_path, backup_path)
            
            return success
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Pipeline failed with error: {str(e)}")
            # Even in catastrophic failure, create minimal output
            try:
                error_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(
                    [(0, "ERROR", 0.0, "error", str(e))],
                    ["id", "name", "value", "source", "error_message"]
                )
                error_df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(f"{output_path}_error")
                logger.info("Error state persisted")
            except:
                pass
            return False
    
    def safe_aggregation(self, df: DataFrame, 
                        group_columns: List[str]) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Perform aggregation with safe handling of edge cases
        """
        try:
            # Check if group columns exist
            missing_cols = set(group_columns) - set(df.columns)
            if missing_cols:
                logger.warning(f"Missing group columns: {missing_cols}")
                # Use available columns only
                group_columns = [c for c in group_columns if c in df.columns]
            
            if not group_columns:
                logger.warning("No valid group columns, returning original data")
                return df
            
            # Perform safe aggregation
            result = df.groupBy(group_columns).agg(
                {"value": "sum", "id": "count"}
            ).withColumnRenamed("sum(value)", "total_value") \
             .withColumnRenamed("count(id)", "record_count")
            
            # Handle empty results
            if result.count() == 0:
                logger.warning("Aggregation resulted in empty DataFrame")
                # Return schema-compatible empty result
                return result
            
            return result
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Aggregation failed: {str(e)}")
            # Return original data as fallback
            return df


# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("FailSafePattern") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    fail_safe = FailSafePattern(spark)
    
    # Execute pipeline with multiple fail-safe mechanisms
    success = fail_safe.graceful_degradation_pipeline(
        primary_path="/data/primary",
        fallback_paths=["/data/fallback1", "/data/fallback2", "/data/fallback3"],
        output_path="/data/output"
    )
    
    print(f"Pipeline completed with fail-safe: {success}")

## 4. Compartmentalization Pattern

```python
"""
Compartmentalization Pattern: Isolates different components to prevent
failure propagation across the system
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, DataFrame
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, lit, current_timestamp, sha2, concat_ws
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, IntegerType
import logging
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Any
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from enum import Enum

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class CompartmentStatus(Enum):
    """Status of each compartment"""
    HEALTHY = "HEALTHY"
    DEGRADED = "DEGRADED"
    FAILED = "FAILED"
    ISOLATED = "ISOLATED"


class Compartment(ABC):
    """
    Base class for isolated compartments
    Each compartment operates independently
    """
    
    def __init__(self, name: str, spark: SparkSession):
        self.name = name
        self.spark = spark
        self.status = CompartmentStatus.HEALTHY
        self.error_count = 0
        self.max_errors = 3
    
    @abstractmethod
    def process(self, data: Any) -> Optional[Any]:
        """Process data within this compartment"""
        pass
    
    def execute_safely(self, data: Any) -> Optional[Any]:
        """
        Execute processing with isolation
        Failures don't propagate outside compartment
        """
        try:
            if self.status == CompartmentStatus.ISOLATED:
                logger.warning(f"Compartment {self.name} is isolated, skipping")
                return None
            
            logger.info(f"Compartment {self.name}: Starting processing")
            result = self.process(data)
            
            # Reset error count on success
            self.error_count = 0
            self.status = CompartmentStatus.HEALTHY
            
            logger.info(f"Compartment {self.name}: Processing successful")
            return result
            
        except Exception as e:
            self.error_count += 1
            logger.error(f"Compartment {self.name} error ({self.error_count}/{self.max_errors}): {str(e)}")
            
            # Isolate compartment if too many errors
            if self.error_count >= self.max_errors:
                self.status = CompartmentStatus.ISOLATED
                logger.error(f"Compartment {self.name} ISOLATED due to repeated failures")
            else:
                self.status = CompartmentStatus.DEGRADED
            
            # Return None instead of propagating exception
            return None
    
    def get_health_status(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Get health status of compartment"""
        return {
            "name": self.name,
            "status": self.status.value,
            "error_count": self.error_count,
            "max_errors": self.max_errors
        }


class DataIngestionCompartment(Compartment):
    """Compartment for data ingestion operations"""
    
    def process(self, data_path: str) -> Optional[DataFrame]:
        """Ingest data with isolation"""
        logger.info(f"Ingesting data from {data_path}")
        
        # Read data with specific configuration for this compartment
        df = self.spark.read \
            .option("mode", "PERMISSIVE") \
            .option("columnNameOfCorruptRecord", "_corrupt_record") \
            .parquet(data_path)
        
        # Add compartment metadata
        result = df.withColumn("ingestion_compartment", lit(self.name)) \
                  .withColumn("ingested_at", current_timestamp())
        
        return result


class DataValidationCompartment(Compartment):
    """Compartment for data validation operations"""
    
    def process(self, df: DataFrame) -> Optional[DataFrame]:
        """Validate data with isolation"""
        logger.info("Validating data")
        
        # Validation logic isolated in this compartment
        validated = df.withColumn(
            "is_valid",
            when(
                (col("id").isNotNull()) & 
                (col("value") >= 0) &
                (col("name").isNotNull()),
                lit(True)
            ).otherwise(lit(False))
        )
        
        # Separate valid and invalid records
        valid_df = validated.filter(col("is_valid") == True)
        invalid_df = validated.filter(col("is_valid") == False)
        
        # Log validation results
        valid_count = valid_df.count()
        invalid_count = invalid_df.count()
        logger.info(f"Validation: {valid_count} valid, {invalid_count} invalid records")
        
        # Store invalid records separately (don't fail the pipeline)
        if invalid_count > 0:
            invalid_df.write.mode("append").parquet("/data/quarantine")
        
        return valid_df.withColumn("validation_compartment", lit(self.name))


class DataTransformationCompartment(Compartment):
    """Compartment for data transformation operations"""
    
    def process(self, df: DataFrame) -> Optional[DataFrame]:
        """Transform data with isolation"""
        logger.info("Transforming data")
        
        # Transformation logic isolated in this compartment
        transformed = df.withColumn(
            "value_normalized",
            col("value") / 100.0
        ).withColumn(
            "name_hash",
            sha2(col("name"), 256)
        ).withColumn(
            "transformation_compartment",
            lit(self.name)
        )
        
        return transformed

class DataEnrichmentCompartment(Compartment):
    """Compartment for data enrichment operations"""
    
    def __init__(self, name: str, spark: SparkSession, reference_data_path: str):
        super().__init__(name, spark)
        self.reference_data_path = reference_data_path
    
    def process(self, df: DataFrame) -> Optional[DataFrame]:
        """Enrich data with isolation"""
        logger.info("Enriching data")
        
        try:
            # Load reference data within this compartment
            reference_df = self.spark.read.parquet(self.reference_data_path)
            
            # Enrich with join (isolated operation)
            enriched = df.join(
                reference_df,
                on="id",
                how="left"
            ).withColumn(
                "enrichment_compartment",
                lit(self.name)
            )
            
            return enriched
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning(f"Enrichment failed: {str(e)}, continuing without enrichment")
            # Return original data if enrichment fails
            return df.withColumn("enrichment_status", lit("FAILED"))


class DataOutputCompartment(Compartment):
    """Compartment for data output operations"""
    
    def __init__(self, name: str, spark: SparkSession, output_path: str):
        super().__init__(name, spark)
        self.output_path = output_path
    
    def process(self, df: DataFrame) -> Optional[bool]:
        """Write data with isolation"""
        logger.info(f"Writing data to {self.output_path}")
        
        # Write with specific configuration for this compartment
        df.withColumn("output_compartment", lit(self.name)) \
          .withColumn("written_at", current_timestamp()) \
          .write \
          .mode("overwrite") \
          .parquet(self.output_path)
        
        # Verify write
        verification_count = self.spark.read.parquet(self.output_path).count()
        logger.info(f"Wrote {verification_count} records")
        
        return True


class CompartmentalizedPipeline:
    """
    Pipeline with compartmentalized components
    Each compartment can fail independently without affecting others
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.compartments: Dict[str, Compartment] = {}
        self.execution_results: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    
    def add_compartment(self, compartment: Compartment):
        """Add a compartment to the pipeline"""
        self.compartments[compartment.name] = compartment
        logger.info(f"Added compartment: {compartment.name}")
    
    def execute_pipeline(self, initial_data: Any) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Execute pipeline with compartmentalized processing
        Each compartment's failure is isolated
        """
        logger.info("Starting compartmentalized pipeline execution")
        
        current_data = initial_data
        results = {}
        
        for compartment_name, compartment in self.compartments.items():
            # Execute each compartment independently
            logger.info(f"Executing compartment: {compartment_name}")
            
            result = compartment.execute_safely(current_data)
            
            # Store result
            results[compartment_name] = {
                "status": compartment.status.value,
                "success": result is not None,
                "health": compartment.get_health_status()
            }
            
            # Continue with result if available, otherwise use previous data
            if result is not None:
                current_data = result
                logger.info(f"Compartment {compartment_name} succeeded")
            else:
                logger.warning(f"Compartment {compartment_name} failed, using previous data")
                # Pipeline continues with data from last successful compartment
        
        self.execution_results = results
        return results
    
    def get_pipeline_health(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Get overall health status of all compartments"""
        health_report = {
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "total_compartments": len(self.compartments),
            "compartments": {}
        }
        
        healthy_count = 0
        degraded_count = 0
        failed_count = 0
        isolated_count = 0
        
        for name, compartment in self.compartments.items():
            status = compartment.get_health_status()
            health_report["compartments"][name] = status
            
            if compartment.status == CompartmentStatus.HEALTHY:
                healthy_count += 1
            elif compartment.status == CompartmentStatus.DEGRADED:
                degraded_count += 1
            elif compartment.status == CompartmentStatus.FAILED:
                failed_count += 1
            elif compartment.status == CompartmentStatus.ISOLATED:
                isolated_count += 1
        
        health_report["summary"] = {
            "healthy": healthy_count,
            "degraded": degraded_count,
            "failed": failed_count,
            "isolated": isolated_count
        }
        
        return health_report
    
    def isolate_compartment(self, compartment_name: str):
        """Manually isolate a compartment"""
        if compartment_name in self.compartments:
            self.compartments[compartment_name].status = CompartmentStatus.ISOLATED
            logger.info(f"Compartment {compartment_name} manually isolated")
    
    def restore_compartment(self, compartment_name: str):
        """Restore an isolated compartment"""
        if compartment_name in self.compartments:
            self.compartments[compartment_name].status = CompartmentStatus.HEALTHY
            self.compartments[compartment_name].error_count = 0
            logger.info(f"Compartment {compartment_name} restored")


# Example usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("CompartmentalizationPattern") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    # Create compartmentalized pipeline
    pipeline = CompartmentalizedPipeline(spark)
    
    # Add compartments
    pipeline.add_compartment(
        DataIngestionCompartment("ingestion", spark)
    )
    pipeline.add_compartment(
        DataValidationCompartment("validation", spark)
    )
    pipeline.add_compartment(
        DataTransformationCompartment("transformation", spark)
    )
    pipeline.add_compartment(
        DataEnrichmentCompartment("enrichment", spark, "/data/reference")
    )
    pipeline.add_compartment(
        DataOutputCompartment("output", spark, "/data/output")
    )
    
    # Execute pipeline
    results = pipeline.execute_pipeline("/data/input")
    
    # Check health
    health = pipeline.get_pipeline_health()
    print(f"Pipeline Health: {health}")
    
    # Print execution results
    for compartment, result in results.items():
        print(f"{compartment}: {result}")

## 5. Sandbox Pattern

```python
"""
Sandbox Pattern: Provides isolated execution environment for untrusted
or experimental code/data to prevent system-wide impact
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, DataFrame
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, lit, current_timestamp, udf
from pyspark.sql.types import StringType, IntegerType, DoubleType
import logging
from typing import Optional, Dict, Any, Callable
import tempfile
import shutil
import os
from contextlib import contextmanager

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class ResourceLimits:
    """Define resource limits for sandbox"""
    
    def __init__(self,
                 max_memory_gb: int = 2,
                 max_cores: int = 2,
                 max_execution_time_seconds: int = 300,
                 max_rows: int = 1000000,
                 max_partitions: int = 10):
        self.max_memory_gb = max_memory_gb
        self.max_cores = max_cores
        self.max_execution_time_seconds = max_execution_time_seconds
        self.max_rows = max_rows
        self.max_partitions = max_partitions


class SandboxEnvironment:
    """
    Isolated sandbox environment for safe execution
    Prevents untrusted code from affecting the main system
    """
    
    def __init__(self, 
                 sandbox_name: str,
                 resource_limits: ResourceLimits,
                 base_spark: SparkSession):
        self.sandbox_name = sandbox_name
        self.resource_limits = resource_limits
        self.base_spark = base_spark
        self.sandbox_spark = None
        self.temp_dir = None
        self.execution_log = []
    
    def __enter__(self):
        """Set up sandbox environment"""
        logger.info(f"Creating sandbox: {self.sandbox_name}")
        
        # Create temporary directory for sandbox
        self.temp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=f"sandbox_{self.sandbox_name}_")
        logger.info(f"Sandbox temp directory: {self.temp_dir}")
        
        # Create isolated Spark session with resource limits
        self.sandbox_spark = SparkSession.builder \
            .appName(f"Sandbox_{self.sandbox_name}") \
            .config("spark.executor.memory", f"{self.resource_limits.max_memory_gb}g") \
            .config("spark.executor.cores", str(self.resource_limits.max_cores)) \
            .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", str(self.resource_limits.max_partitions)) \
            .config("spark.driver.memory", "1g") \
            .config("spark.sql.execution.arrow.pyspark.enabled", "false") \
            .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true") \
            .getOrCreate()
        
        logger.info(f"Sandbox {self.sandbox_name} created successfully")
        return self
    
    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb):
        """Clean up sandbox environment"""
        logger.info(f"Cleaning up sandbox: {self.sandbox_name}")
        
        # Stop sandbox Spark session
        if self.sandbox_spark:
            self.sandbox_spark.stop()
        
        # Remove temporary directory
        if self.temp_dir and os.path.exists(self.temp_dir):
            try:
                shutil.rmtree(self.temp_dir)
                logger.info(f"Removed sandbox temp directory: {self.temp_dir}")
            except Exception as e:
                logger.warning(f"Failed to remove temp directory: {str(e)}")
        
        logger.info(f"Sandbox {self.sandbox_name} cleaned up")
        
        # Don't suppress exceptions
        return False
    
    def load_data_safely(self, data_path: str) -> Optional[DataFrame]:
        """
        Load data into sandbox with size limits
        """
        try:
            logger.info(f"Loading data into sandbox from {data_path}")
            
            # Read data with row limit
            df = self.sandbox_spark.read.parquet(data_path) \
                .limit(self.resource_limits.max_rows)
            
            # Verify data size
            row_count = df.count()
            logger.info(f"Loaded {row_count} rows into sandbox")
            
            if row_count > self.resource_limits.max_rows:
                logger.warning(f"Data truncated to {self.resource_limits.max_rows} rows")
            
            # Add sandbox metadata
            sandboxed_df = df.withColumn("sandbox_name", lit(self.sandbox_name)) \
                            .withColumn("loaded_at", current_timestamp())
            
            self.execution_log.append({
                "action": "load_data",
                "path": data_path,
                "rows": row_count,
                "status": "success"
            })
            
            return sandboxed_df
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Failed to load data into sandbox: {str(e)}")
            self.execution_log.append({
                "action": "load_data",
                "path": data_path,
                "status": "failed",
                "error": str(e)
            })
            return None
    
    def execute_transformation(self,
                              df: DataFrame,
                              transformation_func: Callable[[DataFrame], DataFrame]) -> Optional[DataFrame]:
        """
        Execute transformation in sandbox with safety checks
        """
        try:
            logger.info("Executing transformation in sandbox")
            
            # Set execution timeout
            import signal
            
            def timeout_handler(signum, frame):
                raise TimeoutError("Transformation exceeded time limit")
            
            # Apply transformation with timeout
            signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, timeout_handler)
            signal.alarm(self.resource_limits.max_execution_time_seconds)
            
            try:
                result = transformation_func(df)
                signal.alarm(0)  # Cancel alarm
            except TimeoutError as e:
                logger.error(f"Transformation timed out: {str(e)}")
                self.execution_log.append({
                    "action": "transformation",
                    "status": "timeout"
                })
                return None
            
            # Validate result
            if result is None:
                raise ValueError("Transformation returned None")
            
            # Limit output size
            result = result.limit(self.resource_limits.max_rows)
            
            self.execution_log.append({
                "action": "transformation",
                "status": "success"
            })
            
            logger.info("Transformation completed successfully")
            return result
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Transformation failed in sandbox: {str(e)}")
            self.execution_log.append({
                "action": "transformation",
                "status": "failed",
                "error": str(e)
            })
            return None
    
    def execute_user_code(self,
                         df: DataFrame,
                         user_code: str) -> Optional[DataFrame]:
        """
        Execute user-provided code in isolated sandbox
        CAUTION: This is a simplified example. In production,
        use proper code sandboxing libraries
        """
        try:
            logger.info("Executing user code in sandbox")
            
            # Create restricted namespace
            restricted_globals = {
                '__builtins__': {
                    'len': len,
                    'str': str,
                    'int': int,
                    'float': float,
                    'list': list,
                    'dict': dict,
                    'print': print
                },
                'col': col,
                'lit': lit,
                'when': when,
                'DataFrame': DataFrame
            }
            
            restricted_locals = {'df': df}
            
            # Execute code with restrictions
            exec(user_code, restricted_globals, restricted_locals)
            
            # Get result
            result = restricted_locals.get('result', df)
            
            self.execution_log.append({
                "action": "user_code",
                "status": "success"
            })
            
            logger.info("User code executed successfully")
            return result
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"User code execution failed: {str(e)}")
            self.execution_log.append({
                "action": "user_code",
                "status": "failed",
                "error": str(e)
            })
            return None
    
    def validate_output(self, df: DataFrame) -> bool:
        """
        Validate output before allowing it to leave sandbox
        """
        try:
            logger.info("Validating sandbox
```python
            logger.info("Validating sandbox output")
            
            # Check row count
            row_count = df.count()
            if row_count > self.resource_limits.max_rows:
                logger.error(f"Output exceeds row limit: {row_count} > {self.resource_limits.max_rows}")
                return False
            
            # Check for malicious columns or data
            for column in df.columns:
                if column.startswith("_") or column.startswith("__"):
                    logger.error(f"Suspicious column name detected: {column}")
                    return False
            
            # Check schema
            if len(df.schema.fields) > 100:
                logger.error("Too many columns in output")
                return False
            
            # Sample data validation
            sample = df.limit(100).collect()
            for row in sample:
                # Check for suspicious patterns
                row_dict = row.asDict()
                for key, value in row_dict.items():
                    if isinstance(value, str) and len(value) > 10000:
                        logger.error(f"Suspicious large string value in column {key}")
                        return False
            
            logger.info("Output validation passed")
            self.execution_log.append({
                "action": "validate_output",
                "status": "success",
                "rows": row_count
            })
            
            return True
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Output validation failed: {str(e)}")
            self.execution_log.append({
                "action": "validate_output",
                "status": "failed",
                "error": str(e)
            })
            return False
    
    def export_from_sandbox(self, df: DataFrame, output_path: str) -> bool:
        """
        Export data from sandbox to main system after validation
        """
        try:
            if not self.validate_output(df):
                logger.error("Output validation failed, export aborted")
                return False
            
            logger.info(f"Exporting validated data from sandbox to {output_path}")
            
            # Write to sandbox temp directory first
            temp_output = os.path.join(self.temp_dir, "validated_output")
            df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(temp_output)
            
            # Read with main Spark session and write to final location
            validated_df = self.base_spark.read.parquet(temp_output)
            validated_df.withColumn("sandbox_validated", lit(True)) \
                       .withColumn("exported_at", current_timestamp()) \
                       .write.mode("overwrite").parquet(output_path)
            
            logger.info("Data exported successfully from sandbox")
            self.execution_log.append({
                "action": "export",
                "output_path": output_path,
                "status": "success"
            })
            
            return True
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Export from sandbox failed: {str(e)}")
            self.execution_log.append({
                "action": "export",
                "status": "failed",
                "error": str(e)
            })
            return False
    
    def get_execution_log(self) -> list:
        """Get execution log from sandbox"""
        return self.execution_log


class SandboxManager:
    """
    Manages multiple sandbox environments
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.active_sandboxes: Dict[str, SandboxEnvironment] = {}
        self.sandbox_history: list = []
    
    def create_sandbox(self,
                      sandbox_name: str,
                      resource_limits: Optional[ResourceLimits] = None) -> SandboxEnvironment:
        """
        Create a new sandbox environment
        """
        if resource_limits is None:
            resource_limits = ResourceLimits()
        
        logger.info(f"Creating sandbox: {sandbox_name}")
        
        sandbox = SandboxEnvironment(
            sandbox_name=sandbox_name,
            resource_limits=resource_limits,
            base_spark=self.spark
        )
        
        self.active_sandboxes[sandbox_name] = sandbox
        
        return sandbox
    
    def execute_in_sandbox(self,
                          sandbox_name: str,
                          data_path: str,
                          transformation_func: Callable[[DataFrame], DataFrame],
                          output_path: str) -> bool:
        """
        Execute complete workflow in sandbox
        """
        logger.info(f"Executing workflow in sandbox: {sandbox_name}")
        
        # Create sandbox with default limits
        resource_limits = ResourceLimits(
            max_memory_gb=2,
            max_cores=2,
            max_execution_time_seconds=300,
            max_rows=1000000
        )
        
        with SandboxEnvironment(sandbox_name, resource_limits, self.spark) as sandbox:
            # Load data
            df = sandbox.load_data_safely(data_path)
            if df is None:
                logger.error("Failed to load data into sandbox")
                return False
            
            # Execute transformation
            result = sandbox.execute_transformation(df, transformation_func)
            if result is None:
                logger.error("Transformation failed in sandbox")
                return False
            
            # Export validated results
            success = sandbox.export_from_sandbox(result, output_path)
            
            # Store execution history
            self.sandbox_history.append({
                "sandbox_name": sandbox_name,
                "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
                "success": success,
                "log": sandbox.get_execution_log()
            })
            
            return success
    
    def execute_untrusted_code(self,
                              sandbox_name: str,
                              data_path: str,
                              user_code: str,
                              output_path: str) -> bool:
        """
        Execute untrusted user code in isolated sandbox
        """
        logger.info(f"Executing untrusted code in sandbox: {sandbox_name}")
        
        # Use stricter limits for untrusted code
        resource_limits = ResourceLimits(
            max_memory_gb=1,
            max_cores=1,
            max_execution_time_seconds=60,
            max_rows=100000,
            max_partitions=5
        )
        
        with SandboxEnvironment(sandbox_name, resource_limits, self.spark) as sandbox:
            # Load limited data
            df = sandbox.load_data_safely(data_path)
            if df is None:
                return False
            
            # Execute user code
            result = sandbox.execute_user_code(df, user_code)
            if result is None:
                return False
            
            # Export if validation passes
            success = sandbox.export_from_sandbox(result, output_path)
            
            self.sandbox_history.append({
                "sandbox_name": sandbox_name,
                "type": "untrusted_code",
                "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
                "success": success,
                "log": sandbox.get_execution_log()
            })
            
            return success
    
    def test_experimental_feature(self,
                                 sandbox_name: str,
                                 data_path: str,
                                 experimental_func: Callable[[DataFrame], DataFrame]) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Test experimental features in sandbox without affecting production
        """
        logger.info(f"Testing experimental feature in sandbox: {sandbox_name}")
        
        resource_limits = ResourceLimits(max_rows=10000)  # Small sample for testing
        
        with SandboxEnvironment(sandbox_name, resource_limits, self.spark) as sandbox:
            # Load sample data
            df = sandbox.load_data_safely(data_path)
            if df is None:
                return None
            
            # Execute experimental function
            result = sandbox.execute_transformation(df, experimental_func)
            if result is None:
                return None
            
            # Collect metrics without exporting
            metrics = {
                "input_rows": df.count(),
                "output_rows": result.count(),
                "input_columns": len(df.columns),
                "output_columns": len(result.columns),
                "execution_log": sandbox.get_execution_log()
            }
            
            logger.info(f"Experimental feature test completed: {metrics}")
            
            return metrics
    
    def get_sandbox_history(self) -> list:
        """Get history of all sandbox executions"""
        return self.sandbox_history


# Example usage and test cases

"""
Complete example integrating all failure isolation patterns
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, lit
import logging

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def integrated_failure_isolation_example():
    """
    Demonstrates all failure isolation patterns working together
    """
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("IntegratedFailureIsolation") \
        .config("spark.executor.memory", "4g") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    # 1. BULKHEAD PATTERN: Separate resource pools
    bulkhead = BulkheadPattern(spark)
    
    # 2. FAIL-FAST PATTERN: Validate early
    fail_fast = FailFastPattern(spark)
    
    # 3. FAIL-SAFE PATTERN: Graceful degradation
    fail_safe = FailSafePattern(spark)
    
    # 4. COMPARTMENTALIZATION: Isolated components
    pipeline = CompartmentalizedPipeline(spark)
    pipeline.add_compartment(DataIngestionCompartment("ingestion", spark))
    pipeline.add_compartment(DataValidationCompartment("validation", spark))
    
    # 5. SANDBOX PATTERN: Isolated execution
    sandbox_manager = SandboxManager(spark)
    
    try:
        # Fail-fast validation
        logger.info("Step 1: Fail-fast validation")
        fail_fast.validate_input_immediately("/data/input")
        
        # Bulkhead processing
        logger.info("Step 2: Bulkhead processing")
        bulkhead_results = bulkhead.execute_bulkhead_processing({
            "critical": "/data/critical",
            "normal": "/data/normal"
        })
        
        # Compartmentalized processing
        logger.info("Step 3: Compartmentalized processing")
        comp_results = pipeline.execute_pipeline("/data/input")
        
        # Sandbox for experimental features
        logger.info("Step 4: Sandbox testing")
        sandbox_manager.test_experimental_feature(
            "experiment_1",
            "/data/sample",
            lambda df: df.filter(col("value") > 0)
        )
        
        # Fail-safe output
        logger.info("Step 5: Fail-safe output")
        fail_safe.graceful_degradation_pipeline(
            "/data/processed",
            ["/data/fallback1", "/data/fallback2"],
            "/data/final_output"
        )
        
        logger.info("All failure isolation patterns executed successfully")
        
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"Integrated execution failed: {str(e)}")
    finally:
        bulkhead.cleanup()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    integrated_failure_isolation_example()
